"Ghost Recon Wildlands" is a tactical shooter video game developed by Ubisoft Paris and published by Ubisoft. Released in 2017, it offers an open-world experience set in a fictionalized version of Bolivia, where players take on the role of elite special operations soldiers known as Ghosts. Here's an extensive review covering various aspects of the game:Gameplay: The gameplay of Ghost Recon Wildlands revolves around completing missions to dismantle the Santa Blanca drug cartel. Players have the freedom to approach objectives in a variety of ways, whether it's through stealthy infiltration, coordinated assaults, or utilizing vehicular warfare. The open-world design allows for exploration of diverse environments, from dense jungles to arid deserts, providing ample opportunities for strategic planning and dynamic encounters.

Mission Structure: Missions in Ghost Recon Wildlands are varied and engaging, offering a mix of main story missions, side missions, and dynamic events scattered throughout the vast open world. Each mission provides multiple objectives that can be tackled in any order, promoting player agency and strategic decision-making. The game also features a robust progression system, allowing players to unlock new skills, weapons, and equipment as they progress through the campaign.

Cooperative Gameplay: One of the standout features of Ghost Recon Wildlands is its cooperative multiplayer mode, which allows up to four players to team up and tackle missions together. The seamless integration of cooperative play enhances the experience, as players can coordinate tactics, share resources, and cover each other's backs in intense firefights. The synergy between players adds depth to the gameplay and encourages teamwork and communication.

Stealth Mechanics: Stealth plays a significant role in Ghost Recon Wildlands, offering players the option to approach missions with subtlety and precision. Utilizing drones for reconnaissance, synchronizing takedowns with teammates, and employing silenced weapons are just a few of the tactics available to stealth-oriented players. The game's AI system provides a reasonable challenge, with enemies reacting dynamically to the player's actions, making stealthy infiltration both satisfying and rewarding.Visuals and Atmosphere: Visually, Ghost Recon Wildlands impresses with its stunning depiction of the Bolivian landscape, featuring breathtaking vistas, detailed environments, and realistic weather effects. The game's attention to detail brings the world to life, from bustling cities to remote villages, creating an immersive and atmospheric experience. Dynamic day-night cycles and weather conditions further enhance the sense of realism, contributing to the game's overall immersion.

Replay Value: With its vast open world and multitude of missions, Ghost Recon Wildlands offers considerable replay value. Players can approach missions from different angles, experiment with various tactics, and explore every corner of the expansive map. Additionally, the game's cooperative multiplayer mode provides endless opportunities for teamwork and camaraderie, ensuring that players can continue to enjoy the experience long after completing the main campaign.

Critiques: While Ghost Recon Wildlands excels in many areas, it's not without its flaws. Some players may find the game's storyline and characters to be lacking in depth and complexity, detracting from the overall immersion. Additionally, certain aspects of the game, such as vehicle controls and enemy AI behavior, could be improved for a smoother and more polished experience. However, these issues are relatively minor compared to the game's overall strengths and do not significantly detract from the enjoyment of playing.

Conclusion: Overall, Ghost Recon Wildlands is a highly enjoyable and immersive tactical shooter that offers a vast open-world experience filled with action, strategy, and cooperative gameplay. With its diverse missions, engaging gameplay mechanics, and stunning visuals, it provides hours of entertainment for both solo players and cooperative teams alike. Despite a few minor shortcomings, it remains a standout title in the Ghost Recon series and a must-play for fans of tactical shooters and open-world games alike.

This game is seven years old now, and I've had it for... what, seven years almost?  Look at all that time I've spent playing.  I guess I liked it.

This game hit the weird sweet spot between Clancyisms and Ubisoftisms.  And that probably doesn't make sense so I gotta explain, and I will, in a little bit.

First, Tom Clancy was a writer known for writing jingoistic and military-tech-fetishizing novels.  Never cared for 'em, had no patience for it. In this game, at least the vanilla game, you're a member of a four-man Tom Clancy supersoldier squad.  No implants or nanotech or anything, just superior training and superior technology.  The jingoism has been dialled down to manageable levels, which is quite refreshing.

In this game, you're in a properly open world, probably 25 square kilometers if not more.  You can go anywhere, at any time.  The game helpfully tells you some areas are harder than others, but won't stop you from going straight to the hardest areas if you want to.

The characters do have levels, and skills are locked behind skill points and all that, but it's perfectly possible with skill and starter guns to go do the hardest areas.  I know.  I've done it myself.  So the levels make things smoother, give you a margin of error, but it's not as absurd as your typical RPG where high level areas crush you instantly and areas you've outlevelled are a squash match.  Take the guys with guns seriously.

Your super-tech advantage is a drone that can be used to tag enemies, and you have a bit of AR vision where you know where tagged opponents are.  Parts of this aren't future tech anymore.  And the rest of the game is skulking about in various provinces, gathering intel, locating bosses and disposing of them, with a cutscene or two along the way describing how horrible (or whatever) that particular opponent is.

What makes the game shine is that it's playable coop.  In single-player, the other three members of the squad are played by the computer, and can be ordered to kill enemies with haxxored wall-hack guns.  It's slow, tedious, and very easy.  But get another player in, and all the computer-controlled squadmates go away.  Now you have to communicate, coordinate, and nobody gets haxxored guns.  So my wife, when she's not farming turnips, likes to snipe fools while I skulk about with an SMG and knock out people at close range.  I'll mark enemies that are somewhere awkward, and she'll pick 'em off.  We're a well-oiled team, I tell you what.

But where the game gets kinda fun for us is once you've gotten all the skills, it starts getting into super-hard mode.  It takes away most of your advantages.  Enemies become harder to kill, have better accuracy, and can end you with one or two bullets.  You don't get any clue where the enemies are until you've scouted the area.  Intel becomes super-important!  Stealth and discretion become vital.  And that's where the game shines.  It's just best to slog through the levelling nonsense first so your drone can be kind of capable, since it is basically your biggest advantage.

Later on, they've added some DLCs.  I haven't played most of them, just "Narco Road", which is just remarkably bad.  It doesn't irony-wrap into being good, it just feels like it was written by a different team.  Likely the same Ubisoft team that takes a good IP and turns it into rubbish.  They've also added some free content to the game which, frankly, is stupid.  Fighting the Predator?  REALLY?  The Splinter Cell stuff?  Rainbow Six references?  And a hint around the edges of their utter flopsicle sequel, Wildlands Breakpoint.  Ignore all of it.  Cuss it out.  If you get annoyed enough, put yourself on easy mode just to be done with it.

I realize I didn't explain Ubisoftisms.  Ubisoft games make you go around and collect things, resources of various sorts.  They love gacha boxes.  Those are the only two big Ubisoftisms.  You need resources to buy skill upgrades, and later, marginally improve your weapons.  You can get a lot of resources with dynamic open-world missions, or just pick up boxes here and there.  It's not an especially onerous burden.  The gacha stuff gives you in-game clothing or weapon skins, basically, and you can get them by jumping through stupid hoops in-game (kill this many guys while sneaking, shoot this many gangers in the knob with a pistol, etc) so all that can be ignored, frankly.  (There's others, like a totally unrelated quest-giver who gives you totally different currency to buy game-busting weapons.  That's not here.)

So!  My wife and I have played it through like, three times or something.  And we've come back for a fourth, dragging a friend of ours along.  As a coop experience, once you get to the hard mode, stealth and coordination are critical.  The AI isn't infallible and kind of predictable at times, so it's not a mission-over state, but it does make it a lot harder.

This game is Top Tier. I like it a lot. It's like a mix of GTA, Day Z, Far Cry. 

1) The World. It's beatiful. It does really seem like a real world. The nature is just wonderful: there are different terrains and they are feel great. It feels beatiful, cozy, relaxing, interesting at the same time. I played Far Cry 5, 6, GTA, Day Z and some other games, but this one just has a special feel. Many time I wanted to stop and just enjoy the view alone.

2) The Plot. I think it's great. It has everything I wanted it have. Maybe the next step would be the world changing upon you completing mission rather than being in a kinda static shape. I didn't feel overwhelmed with story and I really digged it. I watch all the bosses video tapes as soon as I have access to them. I read all the notes and enjoy some history notes, some stories and especially recordings. I wish I knew Spanish in order to understand the balladas as well.

3) Gameplay. The best thing about this game in my opinion is a CO-OP experience. I don't think you actually need more than 2 people in your party. I played as a trio but it felt way too rushed for some reason. Two is just the best. 
This games knows what it's best at and thrives in it. The drone experience been so good that you start wondering why nobody else does that. All features are well thought balanced and easy to grasp. Driving cars could feel not as good but with some time you get used to it and don't even notice. The helicopter controls are very comfortable and make easy to do some hard moves. The best about heli is that you just float when you are not pressing any buttons unlike in other games. Your teammate can use a drone from the heli as well but it failed us couple times so if you are scared of blowing up and dying, probably avoid that. 
I started at medium difficulty defeated like 10 small bosses and then when I reached Tier 40 lvl the game had to be switched to hard diffuculty. It made my friend and totally re-evaluate our style. We have to be very tactical now, scout everything, don't let enemy surround us, think more about positions and wats to go back. 

It feels like this game is for the players. So many things that are made so easy to use that you wonder how the come up with this: 
1) You see all the guns in your inventory page and you can find the exact location(area) where the gun is and where are the parts you need for it. 
2) Unless you tp or die, you don't have any loading screens at all. AT ALL. That makes the gaming experience so smooth. You just go from location to location by foot, car, heli or plane. And where ever the mission, events take you, you just go from there. It made us discover a lot of map without actually completing anything. It does bring the open world feeling to it.


And special place for customisiation:
1) Looks. You can change your outfit at any time, you can save a couple of your outfits and change them every hour if you wish to. Super easy, a lot of items available from the very start. And you have 30+ colors for a lot of the items, so you can either make the whole thing from 1 camo type that you love or make cool mixes in between them.
2) Weapons. You can change the weapons at any time, change parts, change color. That helps a lot when you are doing different types of missions and you don't have to overthink it and can use any weapon at any time. 
3) Playthough. You can really start from any area or boss in this game and it doesn't feel wrong and you don't have to commit either. We walked to Libertad a 5 star area and it was overwhelming, so what did we do? Just went to the one nearby with 3 stars and didn't have to struggle though it.
4) Playstyle. You can go guns blazing on easier difficulties but even that is different from lets say far cry. You can be stealth or you can attack and drag the enemies in side your terrotory, blow them up with mines, granates, explosives, drones and kill them with the help of night vision, drone or thermoscope.

With all of that said, imho it deserves 5/5. I am happy I found this game with a help of a friend of mine cause unfortunately it doesn't appear on any co-op mutliplayer best/recommended game lists from the magority sites.

Wildlands is riddled, and i mean absolutely PACKED with game-breaking, mission-failing, challenge-failing, immersion-breaking and otherwise infuriating bugs, glitches and certain "design choices"; it will simply blow your mind. After 133 hours, I can confidently imagine that both frequency and severity of these issues will leave you speechless and wondering how a title can be in such a bad overall shape, so many years after its release. 

There's only so much you can take of all sorts of different stuff randomly exploding and blowing YOUR stealth cover, vehicles glitching out in the weirdest ways, NPCs miraculously knowing exactly where you are while you're hiding in prone position in a forest in the middle of the night, not having made any noise whatsoever and not having moved at all, just because an explosion on the other side of their base alerted them, having them CONSTANTLY spot and shoot you through solid foliage that you, the player, cannot see through, before realising that most of your playtime has been, in all honesty, quite the ****show.

Just now, I attempted a daily challenge that requires you to use sniper rifles only. As part of the mission, you have to interrogate an NPC. At the end of the interrogation, your character always knocks out the NPC. This is not optional and it is required to happen for mission progress. Knocking out the NPC makes you fail the challenge because it counts as not having used a sniper rifle. A google search showed: across forums, steam threads and youtube comments; seemingly everyone attempting that challenge experienced this and today, years later and after countless reports, it still remains that way. 
This is only one example and there is quite the list..

If that's the kind of game you wanna play, go right ahead and get Wildlands. For me personally, I won't have to think about getting Breakpoint - especially when many ppl consider this to be the better title. Looking back, I wish I had spent my time and money on something else.

Harder difficulties, taking off some hud elements and increasing enemy awareness makes encounters so much more challenging and very lethal. You have to play smart while thinking about every decision you take to even just take a handful of enemies unnoticed.

Overall, is fun, but it's no Masterpiece.

Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands takes the tactical shooter genre and gives it a spicy Latin American twist. The game is like a mix between an action-packed thriller and a comedy club – because when you're not taking down drug cartels, you're cracking jokes with your squad. The storyline is as intricate as a spider's web, and just like trying to untangle that web, you'll find yourself getting caught up in the twists and turns. It's like a telenovela with more explosions and fewer love triangles. But fear not, the game doesn't take itself too seriously, and neither should you. The more you embrace the chaos, the better the experience. Now, let's talk about the squad banter – the real MVP of Wildlands. The witty one-liners and hilarious exchanges between your Ghost teammates are like a breath of fresh air in the midst of a bullet storm. At times, it feels like you've stumbled upon a stand-up comedy show in the middle of a war zone. I half-expected one of my teammates to pull out a mic and start a roast battle with the cartel. The open-world setting is expansive, and there's a ludicrous amount of freedom to approach missions. Sure, you can go in guns blazing, but where's the fun in that? I found joy in hijacking a llama and using it as my unconventional getaway vehicle. The cartels had never seen anything like it, and neither had I. Speaking of unpredictability, the game's glitches add an unintentional layer of humor. From cars doing somersaults to enemies moonwalking through walls, you'll encounter some unintentional comedy gold. It's like the Ghosts decided to bring a bit of slapstick comedy to the deadly serious business of dismantling drug empires. Wildlands also deserves credit for its beautiful and diverse landscapes. One minute you're soaring over snowy mountains, and the next, you're trudging through a dense jungle. It's like a vacation package where the only payment is dealing with hostile enemies.

In conclusion, Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon® Wildlands is not just a game; it's a rollercoaster of laughter, explosions, and llama-fueled shenanigans. While it may have its serious moments, the game's ability to balance intensity with humor sets it apart. So, grab your squad, gear up, and get ready for a wild ride that'll have you laughing in the face of danger.

Only other Ghost Recon game I'd played as Advanced Warfighter when I was little, it went over my head as being too complicated (I was 10). This, fortunately, is not that.

It looks damn good considering it's 7 years old at this point. Though it hows it's age in some areas, thats pretty easily overlooked. 
The environment is varied, the world is huge but you get fast travel from the get go... and free and pretty easy access to helicopters from the start, less so to fixed wing aircraft. Don't go expecting fighter jets, they're little Cessnas, but good enough for getting around.

Combat is decent, go in trying to be quiet but if everything goes sideways, there's no penalties for going loud. That being said, there's something satisfying about taking out a Unidad base without being spotted. Pretty much all weapons can be fitted with suppressors from the start so that makes things a lot easier.

Story is typical Tom Clancy, kinda ludicrous but frames the action well enough to not feel aimless. But who really goes into this looking for a spellbinding story full of emotional depth? At least you're not fighting Communists and Arabian terrorists... for once.

Here's an odd comparison: it kinda feels like Just Cause 2, but switching out the OTT wackiness for decent combat and stealth mechanics. The environments feel somewhat similar (though not as repetitive, thank god), the cars handle in an arcade way (easy powerslides, kinda bouncy), helicopters feel a little sluggish to turn as they should, so if you're after a vehicle sim then this isn't it. The game's focus is in the stealth combat, something it does quite well.

The downsides:
- Weapons and the related customisation items can be a bit tedious to pick up, I find having a loadout or two that you like and picking options up for that is a good idea. I generally use a sniper rifle/FAL, an SMG, and a pistol, and that'll get you through pretty much anything.

- Levelling up can be a bit of a chore too, but you don't really need that many skills to get by.

- The store for all the lootbox crates and everything has shut down, which is fine by me, but you can't get rid of the options in the weapon selection windows. Essentially, you see a whole lot of weapons you cannot access anymore. A good 50% of them.
Good news is that you couldn't customise them anyway so you lose a lot of the utility, they're essentially pre-modded weapons with unique skins. Not losing much.

All in all, I'm pretty impressed with it. I'm loving my time in it, though I'm not sure how much reply value you'd get out of it once you've finished it. Again, don't get it at full price, sub-$40 is the butter zone.

This game is one of the most fun I've had with my friends in a long time. 
I never really got into any of the Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon games before Wildlands, so I was compeletely new to the special forces and their covert missions.
From the first trailer I was hooked. What an interesting villain (El Sueño) with a whole cartel of characters that are still memorable over 5 years later. 

Never before and never since have I enjoyed picking up a multitude of vehicles to drive or fly around to my missions. What other game lets you ride a tractor to battle? (except farming simulators...) 

The movement is smooth (vaulting over things, running, etc.) and satisfying. 

The map is divided into different sections that are controlled by parts of the cartel, that need to be taken down. Even though each part of the map has recurring missions that might sound tedious or repetitive, I never felt like I was simply grinding the missions to advance. I loved collecting things, helping people, killing bad guys (and girls) and sneak around. 

The whole world in Wildlands is beautiful, there's people and animals that you can interact with. Yes, if you leave your vehicle on the street a whole traffic jam will occur. You have an impact, you are a person in their world not just a player in a map. 
On top of all the regular missions there's secrets you learn by talking to NPCs. I still remember the town that is completely inhabited by only dogs or the legend of El Tio.

There's also a whole thing about weapons and customizations but I'm going to be honest, I did not care about weapons when playing. As long as I could kill the enemies, I did not care whether my gun was more or less accurate. To learn more about this, another review might be more helpful. 

I've already played 180 hours and I have not yet seen the end of the game. I can wholeheartedly recommend this game. You should play it with your friends and free Bolivia!

Very good game! interesting and amazing graphics.  Supports 32:9 Super Ultrawide 5120x1440, The best surround sound.

This game is graphically amazing. It supports super ultrawide monitors. The dynamic weather system as well as a day-night cycle are simply wonderful, and graphically, how the lighting reflections are done is also impressive. Additionally, after it rains, the roads are still wet, and there are tire tracks on the ground. It's great to play in the dark.

Surround sound is also amazing. When I drive past a car or a helicopter flies over my head, I can determine the helicopter's location by the sound. When I landed a helicopter near a river and one wheel sank into the mud, I was unable to take off because the wheel was stuck in the mud. I had to ram the helicopter out so that the wheel would come out of the mud. Then I was able to fly. There are NPC people in this game who live their own lives. They ride motorcycles, drive cars, or walk. They get into car and drive. They even could take your car :). They also eat, use restrooms, and live their lives. Sadly, it's not possible to adjust the number of NPCs. I would like to have more NPC people in the game. and for them to behave even more like they do in real life.

It's also cool how the enemies sleep at night, go somewhere to eat, watch TV, or perform other actions. I like that in this game, once you find your right weapon, you don't have to spend time searching for other weapons or collecting bonuses.

In short, it's a very cool game. You can just drive around, explore, and enjoy without having to stick to anything. It's a shame that some weapons are locked. It seems you have to buy them with real money, which I do not plan to do.

Wildlands was my favorite shooter of 2017, and no game since has quite hit the same niche of large-scale, 3rd-person, semi-stealth combat with a focus on gunplay and spotting. It encourages planned and carefully executed assaults in a way that most modern shooters fail to. You wanna pretend you're special forces without dealing with the intricacy of milsim shooters? This is the ticket. Also, Breakpoint sucks, so buy this instead on a sale.

The map is sprawling. It's chock-full of content that you can easily play for 100 hours without getting bored. Inserting in a heli, rucking over a hill to a sniper spot, and picking off sentries before moving in to loot a base is satisfying every time. The enemy AI become weirdly omniscient once you get detected, but your AI allies are wallhacking aimbots, so it all balances out. The game also has some things to say about American military and economic intervention in South America... but it doesn't commit to its messages very well. The story and dialogue are better than your average modern military shooter, but this is no "Spec Ops: The Line."

Just watch out--weapon stat cards lie, and Ubisoft's store and UPlay integration are terrible. Those can be ignored easily enough.

Combat is okay. Once alerted enemies always know your exact location and can shoot you through cover with near perfect accuracy. Ridiculous that ♥♥♥♥♥ out gangsters have better accuracy than your supposed elite operators. Once actual combat starts your AI companions are effectively worthless. The game is really balanced around having four players so solo play can be frustrating. 

The forced stealth sections of the game are infuriating. You can spend 15 minutes slowly creeping through a mission only to be forced to start over due to one mistake or just bad luck. Enemies can see you at huge distances any time they're facing you and can often see through solid cover. The lack of ability to move bodies so they aren't discovered turns these sections into a tedious waiting game for the enemies to slowly patrol out of the paths you need to cross.

Driving feels pretty good with many of the vehicles handling better than they probably should. Most vehicles are fun to drive with the exception of the armored SUV and APC. This is good because you're going to be spending a lot of time traveling to each objective. Once you do a few rebel operations you can unlock the ability to spawn a helicopter every minute or so which will greatly speed up your ability to go from objective to objective. The exception being some provinces which are so covered in SAM sites that any air travel is nearly impossible.

Progression wise if you seek out all the available skill point bonuses you'll usually be limited more by scavenged resources for upgrading skills. The random small caches are basically pointless after the early game and you'll primarily be hitting convoys to get the resources you need. These are a hassle until you upgrade the EMP drone that lets you easily stop a convoy and pick off the guards easily.

Overall, there's some fun to be had between long tedious sections and others that are infuriatingly unbalanced. A flawed buy playable game.

Ghost Recon Wildlands is an exceptional open-world game that offers an engaging and immersive experience, particularly in co-op and solo gameplay. Ubisoft has truly showcased the talent of its environment and asset designers, creating a vast and dynamic world that is breathtaking in its detail and diversity. From the lush jungles and towering mountains to the bustling cities and dusty rural settlements, every corner of Ghost Recon Wildlands is a pleasure to explore.

The game's weather and day-night cycle effects add another layer of realism and immersion, with rainstorms, fog, and varying light conditions that affect visibility and gameplay. The sound design is equally impressive, with realistic gunfire, ambient noise, and a stirring soundtrack that heightens the tension and excitement of each mission.

In terms of game design, Ghost Recon Wildlands is a high-quality experience that offers a compelling blend of stealth, shooter, and open-world gameplay. While some may find the gameplay to be repetitive at times, the advanced AI ensures that each encounter is challenging and engaging. Enemy soldiers react intelligently to the player's movements and actions, taking cover, calling for backup, and using tactical maneuvers to flush out the player. This level of detail and challenge makes each mission feel rewarding and satisfying.

The game's story is another highlight, offering a gritty and realistic portrayal of a drug cartel's stranglehold on a fictionalized Bolivia. The player takes on the role of a Ghost, an elite special forces operative tasked with dismantling the cartel's operations and bringing its leaders to justice. The story is well-written and well-acted, with a cast of memorable characters and a strong sense of moral ambiguity.

Overall, Ghost Recon Wildlands is a must-play for fans of stealth, shooter, or open-world games. Its stunning setting, engaging gameplay, and compelling story make it a standout title in the genre, and one that is well worth experiencing for yourself.

Upon initial glance I thought the game was going to be another bland open world shooter. After playing it for a few hours I can start to understand the appeal, and go to know certain mechanics in this game that work a lot better than other shooters. In short, this game is good (and even better with friends), but does have a few limitations that may put off potential players.

Ghost Recon Wildlands' (GRW) [b]gameplay[/b] is a lot more engaging that I initially assumed. In my opinion, the gun handling/shooting in this game far exceeds a lot of other shooters (and dare I say, Call of Duty). It's satisfying, it feels real, the impact feels proper, and bullet delivery (especially with snipers) feels like it was done right. Although this is the highlight of the game for me, there are other features that players may buy into. The open world concept is a little overwhelming at first. As the player does a few missions and begins to notice how the game is structured, completing missions and acquiring new abilities becomes a little easier. The user interface and menus try their best to break down what the player can or should do next. At first the game's missions may seem a little "easy" compared to the initial Ghost Recon I played back on the Xbox. As the game progresses, some of the missions begin to get difficult objectives which challenge the player. If you are playing this game yourself the AI soldiers actually provide a decent amount of support. Though, I don't understand how sometimes friendly soldiers can move in front of the enemy, even if it is behind a buildings shadow midday. There are a few vehicles to choose from in the game from cars, trucks, mounted trucks, helicopters, and planes.

The [b]visuals and graphics[/b] are pretty good for a game of its era. Although the landscape looks stunning (and shaders seem to be really well done to reflect its beauty) the minor animations seem to be there. NPCs are interacting with one another (to some degree), enemies are patrolling and sometimes engage with their environment. Even though this is a large map game it can make the player feel like they're right there in the village, simply looking around and exploring (or sneaking and hiding). The [b]sounds and music[/b] are satisfactory. The radio is a little in what in can play, but Spanish music can be heard blaring while rolling on four wheels. There is interaction between the soldiers (and sometimes NPCs). The voice acting itself is suitable to a triple A game (especially coming from an Early Access game). Both domains were done well (especially the visuals), but I feel the sounds department could've done a little more to immerse the player.

Overall, this is a pretty good game given certain circumstances. Playing solo can be fun for about ten hours before some missions can seem extremely difficult without the support of another player, and sometimes boring without friends to play with. I'm happy I purchased it on sale - and would recommend the same to the reader! The driving is a little wonky/blocky and other little small movements throughout the game share the same value.

If you're looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if you're looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.

Ingredients:

1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie

Directions:

1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

This is the first fps game I have gotten into, and I got the opportunity to play all of it and then some with a couple friends of mine, and I have to say this is by far the best starting point for anyone wanting to get into the genre. The open world feels responsive, dangerous, but at the same time relatively easy to get into.

There is always a purpose to go after, as the game is split into missions and regions, with a fairly simplistic but engaging story explaining why you're murdering a bunch of Bolivian thugs. I particularly like it because it never interferes with the game. It almost always gives you exposition through your comms, allowing you to continue playing while you're given information. Cut scenes are rare, and usually come at the end of missions, meaning that it is a good time to stop and breathe anyways.

The gunplay is straight up phenomenal, as it allows you and your friends to play it by stealth, with a ton of tools at your disposal for that, or to just go complete run and gun. As long as you don't play on the highest difficulty, both are absolutely valid options. I initially found myself having way more fun throwing caution to the wind and just running everywhere and lighting people up with an LMG and grenade launcher, but overtime found times where it is preferable to pop a silencer on depending on the circumstances. There will be times when missions require you to play it stealth, but it is surprisingly uncommon considering the whole theme of the game. 

The missions themselves are great, and often have unique mechanics and circumstances that will shake up the game a little bit more then just shooting people, but I honestly found the ones where the goal is to just kill the most fun, which is a testament to the most basic formula of the game working.

Side note: I love the fact that they allow you to destroy and murder everyone indiscriminately. The rebel support team that is everywhere and sometimes gets in the way? You can murder all of them. The random civilians that occasionally drive you over and make you lose your ghost mode save (yes that happened to me) you can murder them and blow up all their vehicles. Or steal them GTA style. Granted, the game will reasonably slap you on the wrist by making you respawn if you have too many casualties, but it is surprisingly generous. Not that I am complaining... 

The progression of the game is also amazing, as it features a skill tree with different categories that cost resources you find along the way or steal from various side missions as well as skill points that can be found in collectable form or acquired by levelling up. Experience is earned by doing most things, such as killing or destroying important components of the base, but most significantly from completing missions. The skill tree allows you to choose what you care about and what fits your playstyle, which further contributes to the ability to choose stealth or running and gunning depending on you and your friends preferences.

Finally, there is replayability and the post-game. After maxing out in experience levels, the game allows you to enable tier one mode, which basically turns experience into a new system that can unlock exclusive cosmetics and prestige credits. This gives you something to do while pursuing all the collectables once you've finished the story. It isn't anything crazy, but overtime it will force you to play on higher difficulties, which is kind of neat, and adds an additional challenge if you didn't already play on them. There is also the aforementioned ghost mode, which is basically the "hardcore difficulty" of this game. You can choose whatever difficulty but if you bleed out and die your save gets wiped. If you enjoyed the game a ton and like pain, it's a good excuse to replay the game for more exclusive cosmetics and prestige credits, but it can be quite frustrating at times with janky auto deaths from vehicles that could occasionally happen being way more punishing. 

The main thing I take issue with in this game is its completely stupid loot crates system. It really doesn't make sense to exist in a game like this, but leave it to ubisoft to mess something up. The previously mentioned prestige credits can be used to cash in prestige crates which will randomly reward vehicles, cosmetics, emotes, and weapons that cannot be acquired through playing the game. I suppose this would have been fine enough if there wasn't a couple of other crates that are primarily earned through microtransactions with a bunch of exclusives as well. For a completionist, this is just a massive f you. 

One other thing you should be made aware of is that if you are picking up this game to play with friends, you need a lot of patience for the multiplayer netcoding. Once it works, it works fantastically, but getting to that point may result in a lot of peril and swearing, so tuck in and maybe grab a drink beforehand.

Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildland's is the most interesting application of the Ubisoft formula to date. 

The plot surrounds a team of special operatives that go by the name Ghosts who can either be your AI companions or co-op friends. The Ghost's objective is to take down El Sueno and his cartel. 

The gameplay revolves around going to different provinces in real life Bolivia to liberate them with the help of the Rebels in the area who are fighting against the Cartel State alongside you. 

There are brilliantly crafted, fully animated cut-scenes that are fully optional (but totally worth it) and the game leaves a lot of freedom of how easy or hard, and immersive or arcade-y the player wants it to be. Settings such as removing crosshairs, more realistic AI, limited HUD, etc. can allow for the player to decide if they want something more akin to traditional Ubisoft shooters, or opt for a more realistic, tactical experience. 

The progression in the game is very satisfying and doing side content is incentivized with cosmetics, guns, attachments, and rebel assistance through drops and back up; all are fun and get rewarding content, but almost none are necessary to completing the game. 

I spent ~67 hours in game at the time of writing this review but I immediately moved on to the sequel after this, and will probably come back to Wildlands at some point, I can easily see myself putting 200+ hours into this game before I'm done with it.

This is one of the games where I'm really split. In the beginning i found it far too easy. It is more fun on the extreme setting and later in tier-mode.
+ One-shot kills
+ sensible weapon customization mechanics
+ missing "numbers game" (i.e. you need to wear down the enemey with ridiculous amounts of hits... (even pistol one-shot kills are possible on head-shots).
- loot-boxes (mostly for cosmetic stuff, but also for additional weapons and vehicles, esp. the vehicles change abilities in game, as you can not call in an armed helicopter as transport vehicle until you find it in a loot box)
- (esp in tier mode) unrealistic enemy behaviour. e.g. snipers see you within seconds when you enter their viewcone and cross the imaginary view area boundary, sometimes also outside of their viewcone (i.e. when stealth approaching from behind)
- impossible spawning behaviour (i.e. clearing and barring and area with mines after, but enemies spawn between the barrier and you after moving forward; enemies spawning in impossible locations that have been cleard and are basically dead-ends. This is esp. irksome as the game in it's setup (and the original Tom Clancys brand legacy (yes, which has been dilluted by the more recent entries since the UbiSoft era, i know) would be the perfect open world stealth game without this problem, take your time stealth clearing an area and carefully approaching an objective, taking out enemies that go clear of their buddies , only to be killed by reinforcments spawned in between your AI buddies or something.
- (esp in tier mode) sometimes impossibly fast detection by enemies (e.g. running around a corner, but immediately seing you hunkered down behind cover, only very partially visible or behind shrubberies, insta kill while the enemy is running.
- As soon as one enemy spots you, ALL enemies know where you are, even if you kill that enemy half a second later and he never would have had a chance to tell anyone (yes, I'm looking at you, stealth missions, short burst to the head of enemy 1, short burst to the head of enemy 2, but enemy 3 spots you a splitsecond before burst to his head. Yeah, you are done, mission restart.)
- there are some stealth missions, where you have a timer running, but are not allowed to kill enemies initially.  The randomly spawned enemies make this unnecessarily hard.

+/- don't play alone, best played with four additional actual human players (that you know, don't play public games). In Solo play your AI can revive you once (2 or 3 times with upgrade). In MP you can infitnitely heal and the mission is not completely restarted when someone dies, they get respawned somewhat close and have to reapproach. Which esp on longer missions with an attempted stealth approach is terribly annoying.

So yeah, It was some fun, but it also was very annoying (esp when playing solo).

Ghost Recon Wildlands, the tenth installment in the Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon series, takes players on a thrilling journey into the heart of the Bolivian drug trade. Released in 2017 by Ubisoft, this tactical shooter introduces a vast open-world setting, allowing players to immerse themselves in a gripping narrative while employing strategic gameplay.

The game's standout feature is its expansive open-world environment. Set in a stunningly detailed and diverse rendition of Bolivia, players are given the freedom to explore landscapes ranging from dense jungles to arid deserts. The sheer scale of the map provides an immersive playground for tactical operations, fostering a sense of realism and unpredictability in every mission.

In Ghost Recon Wildlands, players assume the role of an elite Ghost operative tasked with dismantling a powerful drug cartel. The narrative unfolds through a series of interconnected missions, each contributing to the overarching goal of destabilizing the cartel's operations. While the story may not break new ground, it serves as a compelling backdrop for the intense and strategic firefights that define the Ghost Recon experience.

The game's tactical gameplay mechanics shine in both single-player and cooperative modes. Players can choose to tackle missions solo with AI-controlled teammates or enlist the help of up to three friends for a cooperative multiplayer experience. The emphasis on careful planning, reconnaissance, and synchronized execution adds depth to the gameplay, rewarding those who approach missions with a thoughtful and strategic mindset.

Ghost Recon Wildlands boasts an impressive array of weaponry and equipment, allowing players to customize their loadouts to suit different playstyles. The game's skill tree system further enhances personalization, offering a sense of progression as players unlock new abilities and improve their Ghost's capabilities. This level of customization encourages experimentation, ensuring that no two players will approach missions in exactly the same way.

The visuals in Ghost Recon Wildlands are nothing short of breathtaking. The attention to detail in the game's environments, character models, and dynamic weather effects contributes to a visually stunning and immersive experience. From the sun-drenched landscapes to the tense night operations, the game's graphics play a pivotal role in conveying the atmosphere and tension of the covert operations.

While Ghost Recon Wildlands received praise for its engaging gameplay and expansive world, some critics noted occasional technical hiccups and repetitive mission structures. The AI, while generally competent, could at times exhibit inconsistencies in behavior. However, the game's post-launch support and updates addressed many of these issues, reflecting Ubisoft's commitment to refining and improving the player experience.

In conclusion, Ghost Recon Wildlands successfully marries the thrill of tactical military operations with the freedom of an open-world setting. Its vast landscapes, strategic depth, and cooperative gameplay make it a standout entry in the Ghost Recon series. Whether playing solo or with friends, Ghost Recon Wildlands offers an intense and rewarding experience for fans of tactical shooters and those seeking an immersive open-world adventure.

You might find a lot of people in this review section saying the game's main downside is the fact that Ubisoft made it, and I agree completely; it's the one factor that stops this game from being a fantastic open-world FPS.

Don't get me wrong, this is still an absolute banger, but it didn't go without it's bumps in the road. Upon release, many glitches were prominent, which definitely stabbed the game's performance early on where it's most critical. But as time goes on, things got fixed, and people moved on to the next thing as the game got its repairs. This left it to not really blow up as much as what could be expected. I mean you look at the game firsthand and you hear glitches and Ubisoft, already a no-go, right?

What the game lacks in some functionality it makes up for in visual beauty. Yeah, you do need a decent rig to run it smoothly, but it's absolutely worth it. It still stuns me now, and I've tried RTX Minecraft. The lush forests, barren saltflats, and changing weather really bring this game to life.
There's LOTS, and I mean LOTS of information in the game about Bolivia itself which I find to be extremely appealing to have. Many games will take place in like France or something and not give you ANY information about the culture. That doesn't slide here. In the game, you're an operative in a country that isn't immediately in the mainstream media, so if you aren't familiar, the game gives you trivia. Post-war Germans living in the country, Death Road, Jesús Malverde, and more stories are able to be found. There are also PLENTY of files and dialogue on the main game story as well in case that's what you want to pay attention to, but none of said files and trivia are required to continue on. It's a respectful thing to do, and it shows the developers really went out of their way to understand Bolivian culture; it shows how much they really cared about the game, so it's nice to see.

The stealth in this game is fairly good, def could be better but pretty good. The game lacks in being able to drag bodies which is a pretty big letdown, but usually the AI is pretty easy anyways. The easiness was actually a complaint early on for the game, so Ubisoft added Extreme mode and Ghost Mode. Extreme mode meaning your body would seize if you breathed too much, and Ghost Mode meaning basically 2 shots without a revive and you gotta start over. All the way over. Like, back to the part where you're landing in the country, over. Talk about being careful. Still, can't drag bodies which is annoying and I really wish being able to hide in bushes was a bit more functional than it is as of writing, but the enemy on the right difficulty can still be scary at times which makes it all the more satisfying to do things right. When playing with friends, I like to have my friends infiltrate compounds while I post up as a sniper correcting any mistakes they make from 400+ meters away.

It would be a crime to not talk about the guns in a gun game. The guns are great in their models and customization. You can paint your guns solid colors, official camos, funny camos, whatever suits you. Then you can modify it to just how you like. Every Buchon has a custom gun you unlock too that reflects their personality. For example, one guy you capture builds submarines, so naturally his unlock is a gun made from sub parts. The sniper rifles were done really well in my opinion because every rifle has quite a different bullet drop, and since the landscape is huge, you have to pay attention to it a lot. I found myself testing different scopes with different rifles to see which was best, and started remembering where the range was on each set. It's very satisfying to get it right and pull off a 500+ meter shot.

The customization on the clothes as well is really good. The game gives you hundreds of options if you want to go with tactical clothes or more civilian-style like Nomad's base character. Of course, there's like 70 something different colors you can do for basically half or more of those clothing options too. When you're done with that, you can choose what patches you want to do on your backpack, baseball cap, shoulder-armor, etc. "Made in the 757" is a personal fav.

I'm a motorhead, so obviously I want the driving mechanics to be good. This game did okaaaay with that, but honestly better quite a few other games out there. Steering is pretty annoying, but the transmission mechanic is really good. You can hear the RPM climbing and, if you're smart, tap the throttle before it shifts to get a premature gearshift in the car. I'm glad they paid attention to that. What didn't go so well was the flying mechanics. The flying, like driving, is okaaaay, at least in classic mode. If you want to hit something in classic mode with weapons, forget it. It's basically impossible. Ubisoft tried to fix this issue with new flying mechanics but they found a way to realllllly fumble it. It's REALLY bad. Driving = eh, not bad | flying = pretty trash depending on what you're doing.

People in this review section have been talking about connection issues. I got a feeling this is just something Ubisoft did to mess things up like usual, so I can't be mad at the game for it,

My final verdict: 8.02/10, just barely got the 8.
The culture attention and visuals are fantastic. Gunplay, character/weapon customization and difficulty are great. The driving, stealth, and story is pretty good. The flying and the networking is meh. The fact that this is a Ubisoft game, meaning lootboxes and network issues, is bad. Just bad.

From rebel friends running you over at light speed to helicopters deciding to commit suicide at takeoff or AI teammates T-bagging you while watching you die. This made me realize there are worse loading simulators than GTA 5.

If you like pain and suffering with occasional fun then this game is for you.

Overall I will give this game a 8/10.

I grew up playing the original Ghost Recon on the original Xbox with all its expansions, plus Ghost Recon 2 and Rainbow Six 3. I skipped the rest of the Ubi/Ghost Recon games until this one. This game was bastardized to be more mainstream or lack of buttons on controller. 

At the time of this posting, I bought the game on deep sale about a week ago. For the initial honeymoon phase of the first 10-20 hours in I was having a lot of fun in co-op and solo, but the more I played the more I dislike it. At the time of this at 78 hours in I'm slogging through it with repetitive side quests to improve my chances of success.  

For starters, 6 years after release and it still employs Denuvo with the capability to degrade performance with Easy Anti-Cheat on top? Why? Anyone that wanted to torrent the game already has years ago, not to mention doesn't have to deal with UPlay. 

There's no option to play fully in 1st person and no manual leaning system. There are FOV mods to mitigate this but no manual leaning system is a massive blow. I do understand that this is a stealth game and I can lean around corners and walls when I ADS, but I'm exposing myself to be shot at by more enemies in a weaker position. The older games on the original xbox from 15 years ago at the time of release had this feature. Why do I need to mash 4 to switch between half a dozen throwables? Why can't I split these grenades up on 5 through 0 on the keyboard? Or better yet categorizing them from flashbangs, frags, mines, and other explosives. 

Despite having the game on Ultra settings, enemies on solo disappear past 600 meters. What is the point in having these high power scopes when we can't even fully utilize them? In addition killing the cartel bosses makes no difference exploring the world. 

The friendly AI is both powerful and stupid all at the same time. You get access to the powerful sync shot with up to 3 charges. Inside vehicles they are fine and always ready to shoot back. But I've experienced a few times when we are in the middle of a fight the friendly AI(s) don't even acknowledge the enemy shooting at them, the same issue as in Ready or Not.

Tonight, the time has come to put an end to their reign of terror. I'm armed with my trusty M40A51, the cool metal grip reassuring in my hands. My comrades, Weaver, Holt, and Midas, have my back, and the thrill of coordinated teamwork is palpable. We're all players in a meticulously crafted symphony of destruction.

The base is sprawling, lit up like a Christmas tree. Our objective: eliminate the cartel boss and extract vital intel. I rely on my drone, a handy tool in our arsenal, to scout the enemy positions. As the night closes in around us, I mark enemy snipers, armored soldiers, and spot a mortar that could mean our end here. The cartel's defenses are no joke.

Silently, we move forward. The moonlight casts eerie shadows through the jungle canopy as we approach the base. The stealth aspect of our is where we truly shine. We take down a couple of guards with well-placed shots, their deaths shrouded in mystery. The tension mounts with each silent kill, and I can feel the adrenaline pumping through my veins.

However, the element of surprise is short-lived. Our stealthy approach inevitably devolves into chaos as our presence is detected. Bullets fly, explosions rock the base, and alarms blare. The base comes alive with cartel soldiers hunting us down like wild animals. The heat of the firefight is breathtaking, and the sound of bullets whizzing past and explosions is as exhilirating as it gets.

In the midst of the chaos, we locate our target - the cartel boss. The intense firefight becomes a game of cat and mouse as we hunt him down through the twisting labyrinth of shipping containers and buildings. It's a heart-pounding experience, each step more dangerous than the last.

After an intense firefight, the cartel boss falls, his reign of terror over. With his death, the base is practically ours. I can't help but feel a sense of accomplishment as we extract the vital intel we came for and help the allied rebels into the base."

If you love intense combat, a compelling story, and the thrill of battling the odds in a hostile, drug-fueled world, Wildlands is the game you've been waiting for.

This game just disappoints me. Seriously, it's just disappointing. I've played GR Future Soldier, Breakpoint and now this...

To explain the reason why I *HEAVILY* suggest against buying this game, I'll put my points as to what I liked, what I don't like, and my reaction to the positive reviews.

The good:

Vehicle driving feels more fun, being able to drift around corners and give chase to lieutenants can be exhilarating!

The variety in guns is acceptable

Being able to help the rebel resistance to gain access to support options like rebel mortar fire is really interesting and cool, allowing you to plan for bigger assaults

----------------------------------------

The mediocre:

Call me crazy, but I think the gun mechanics are very mediocre, it feels like most of the time, I'm slinging bits of hardened playdough at my enemies, not damage wise, but the feel of the gun feels off, like battlefield 4 kind of gunplay, where the guns don't feel satisfying to fire

Along with this, there is gun customisation, which is okay, however the actual customisation of guns is limited, for example, to get a grenade launcher, you need to... put skill points into it? It rubs me the wrong way and is more of a personal preference, however comparing it to previous games, the customisation feels mediocre, or even a couple steps back

Character movement in this game is passable, it's nice how fluid getting behind and coming out of cover can be, however most of the time it feels like you're running through wax and it never feels like you're getting anywhere fast enough

Lack of specialists means that everyone feels the same. There's no difference between two maxed out players apart from their weaponry, which just feels bland, especially compared to Breakpoint. It's not for everyone, but not having access to unique abilities or tradeoffs makes the game very stale.

The character customisation is flat as a pancake, you have a choice between seven different hairstyles which are shared between both genders, different faces that you can't change the colours of, so I ended up just making Foap from MW3

----------------------------------------

The Bad/Controversial:

You are a regular soldier. On the surface, this may be a bit baffling, however comparing Wildlands to Future Soldiers is like comparing a generic armyman to someone in the spec ops, you're meant to be top class soldiers with futuristic equipment on you, allowing you to take care of situations quietly or be able to assault in ways that completely overwhelms your enemies, instead you're just Joe. You have your rifle, secondary, pistol and drone, and that's it. No stealth technology, no door busting gadgets, not even a throwable scanner of some description, and it's just.. empty. If you're going into this game with the expectation of being an actual member of the Ghost Recon squad, I'm sorry to say, you're just some standard army riflemen.

The map... by god the map. Your minimap is something you'll look at, purely for the purpose of finding materials for the rebels or for collectibles. Is it above or below your location? I don't know, it's just there, which makes it frustrating. Does it tell you where possible entrances are? Nope. Maybe it can give hints as to nearby people who haven't been identified? Nope. This makes looking at the minimap pointless, unless you wish to run around to give the rebels some supplies, speaking of..

The rebels, this system, while cool in theory, is just wasted potential. Most of what they can do is specifically useful when you're assaulting an area loud, however, you're Ghodt Recon, you're meant to be stealthy, which throws all of the cool stuff such as the mortar barrage, squad of rebels, etc out the window because calling any of them in will blow your cover

Guns, their customisation, the lack of sorting options, just baffles me completely. Bearing in mind I have all the DLC, the most useful weapon I've had is the rapid fire crossbow, which will one shot anyone, pierces so you can do a 2 for 1 deal, is always silent and hardly has any drop, meaning you can go on entire mutder sprees considering it fires as fast as it reloads, whilst holding 60 bolts, I have never felt like it was good using a gun as the inaccuracy modifiers and recoil of the gun were too penalising compared to using the crossbow, nevermind the lack of customisation compared to Breakpoint, which came out before this

Vehicles suck, the only vehicle you'll ever need is the minigun helicopter as driving takes too long with all the mountains, and the minigun eill not alert enemies outside a certain bubble, so you can spray to your hearts content at all the little dots down below

The lack of life in this game feels cheap, sure people drive by or are walking by the road, however I have never once stopped by the road because something caught my eye, as you're fast travelling then just going from point A to point B, at least in Breakpoint there were constant patrols, items to collect, resources to gather, in Future Soldier exploring would reward you with collectibles, guns, what have you, but EVERYTHING you need to actually progress is highlighted in all the different towns, which just kills off anything outside them, sadly

There is backstory to the characters, but they purely come from the collectibles, so if you ignore collectibles and just go straight into killing the folk, you won't even know stuff about the people you killed, which changes... nothing, the fact that they don't taunt you, or know about your existence after dlaughtering their dedicated sector feels jarring and unreal, I'm more than certain if you wiped off an entire group from a real life cartel, they wouldn't take it lying down.

My biggest grudge against ANYONE who says that "Oh yeah, playing it with friends will make it better" Is just a blitering idiot. Any game with multiplayer instantly gets better when you can have friends in it, however, if the core game is such a terrible dtate of empty, then what reason would YOU have to continue? Compare this to deep rock galactic, in which yes, you can play this with friends, playing it solo feels great to play as well as coop, and sometimes EVEN BETTER!


So riddle me this Batman, if this game is bland, empty, a point to point mission slog, with a story that probably is better left uncared for than you actually paying attention to it, by playing 3rd person Call of Duty, why would you want this game? If you desperately need your open world multiplayer game itch scratched, go play breakpoint, it has a much, MUCH better system than Wildlands.

----------------------------------------

Tldr: Game has nothing of value to give, multiplayer games are always more fun with friends, if you want futuristic gadgets with a more fun combat system, go play Breakpoint, it's cheaper and doesn't require as hefty of a system to look as good :)

I picked up Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands during a Steam sale as a surprise gift for my friends, and it turned out to be one of the best gaming decisions I've ever made. This game is a treasure trove of unforgettable memories, and it's held up incredibly well over time.

Even in the gaming world where new titles constantly clamor for attention, Wildlands still shines. Its polished graphics and immersive open-world environment feel just as fresh today as when we first dove in. The attention to detail in the sprawling landscapes, from dense jungles to arid deserts, is simply stunning.

But what truly makes Wildlands a standout experience is its co-op play. Playing with friends turned the game into a rollercoaster of hilarity, tactical brilliance, and occasional friendly fire mishaps. Whether we were coordinating helicopter assaults on drug cartel compounds or hijacking convoys, every mission was an adventure.

The outposts and objectives could sometimes seem repetitive, but when you're laughing your head off with buddies while trying to stay stealthy, it hardly matters. And speaking of variety, the game's high weapon customizability and the abundance of character perks added depth and replayability, keeping us hooked for hours on end.

Ghost Recon Wildlands isn't just a game; it's a canvas for unforgettable co-op stories. It's a testament to the power of friendship, teamwork, and the joy of conquering challenging missions together. If you're looking for a game that stands the test of time and offers endless opportunities for cooperative fun, look no further than Ghost Recon Wildlands. It's an experience that I'll cherish for years to come.

Missions that are time dependant that can get very repetitive due to the insufficient amount of time give.  Missions that have three or four parts to them that have no save point, and return you to the first part if you end up killed.  it's a relief to get those missions out of the way - but there are not that many of them.

You can chose just which missions to take on that are not story related - side ops that contribute to your ability to expand your characters capabilities.  And there are hundreds of these - no way you need to complete them all.  I did a huge chunk of them, and ended up finishing the first complete run through of the game in over 250 hrs.  Again, it's not necessary, but you get the most out of the game if you take on rebel ops that increase your abilities.  

The missions generated are not boring or too similar.  With Far Cry 2, it became all too easy after a while, and the missions chosen looked all too familiar.  Not with Wildlands - the world is even bigger, but this time the missions - even the side missions - have real contrast.

It does become a little easier once you develop your character's abilities.  Vehicle drop offs are a must - and it becomes more helpful if you can ask for an armoured car or a helicopter for some missions.  Weapon upgrades - loads of them.  However, I did find that there were limited weapons that could have grenade launchers attached.  A weapon with a grenade launcher is going to make your life so much easier.  I've played this first run through with weapon suppressors on the sniper rifle, assault rife and handgun.  It makes sense - but the next challenge would be to try a run through with no silenced weapons.

There are two possible end cut scenes - you have to complete the game once to generate the second ending. 

On a down side, there is one really bad bug that has not been resolved since the game's launch.. The first El Gato mission is seriously bugged if you are playing as a single player - the bad guy just doesn't appear so you can't take him out and therefore you can't progress.  The only way I found to get around this is to play this one mission as a co-op mission - let your team mates do the necessary - the mission gets finished - then revert back to the single player mode.  I've discovered that this bug has been around for years now - and it's really disappointing to find that Ubisoft still haven't fixed it.

That aside, this is one of the few games around that are worth the purchase price.  Loads of gameplay, and real challenges.  For all the faults I've mentioned, it's worth it.  Enjoy.

[b] Overview [/b]

One of my favourite games, 9.5/10. Play through the game at your own pace, some of the best fun is learning to build effective and fun gear sets, and learning how to explore and traverse the map is another great part of learning the game. However, there is one thing you should do after learning how the game works and what play-style you enjoy… [b] Complete Remanzo EARLY[/b], as sometimes an objective won't spawn, sometimes deselecting the mission objective (gold crown), fast travelling away, returning to the mission area, and reactivating the mission using the pop-up (hold "m") will fix it, but if not restarting with a new save will be necessary. There can be some jank, but it's usually not an issue, and some reviews really oversell how glitchy the game can be. Ubisoft and U-play sucks. Easy Anti-Cheat can suck, make sure it's not being registered as malware by your security program of choice. There are micro-transactions, but they're not necessary, and can be circumvented through daily challenges and ghost mode (use the pause menu, in-game menu, or hot-key, k, to see them).

Sniping and stealth are extremely satisfying. This is a [strike] tactical [/strike] [b] tacti-cool [/b] game, so learning how you position yourself for your goal, how you approach your goal, when to adapt, use of the resources you have (drone, rebels, and vehicles), how the game reacts to your actions, and [u] looking as badass as possible [/u] are essential. Driving is fun (or jank), SAM launchers are death, flying is fast, helicopters with weapons are easy mode, and [b] NEVER [/b] use bikes in perma-death mode.

[b] When Going Loud [/b]

Rate of fire, cover, and range are king (M4 + GL supremacy) in gunfights. Some weapon attachments are pointless, while others are nearly required to stay alive on higher difficulties. More bullets (bigger magazine / higher rate of fire) = more dead enemies and less bullets that could kill you. Anti-material/heavier weapons melt anything they shoot or spray at. Although, the most badass approach is always best, and the best looking gun always wins the gunfight.

[b] Good luck ghosts and happy hunting! [/b]

If you're looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if you're looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.

Ingredients:

1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie

Directions:

1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

I don't think i've written a review before but this game had me wanting to write one the entire time. There are pro's and con's but man do the cons just suck sometimes a little too much. Overall I'm cheap when it comes to games for fear i'll waste the money. A fear of "well what if i buy the game and don't like it" sorta situation. As of now i don't feel the game was bad, but i doubt i'll put more time into it. 


PROS
- I bought the game for 10$ so I can't really complain about the enjoyment i got out of it. I had a lot of fun trying a different FPS out. A simple youtube search for a FPS with high weapon customization (I don't like the idea of Tarkov's gameplay, and I despise battle royals honestly) and this game came up. This game is my style in some form, reminds me of far cry but in a different way.


CONS
- The AI is just ridiculous sometimes. Hiding is impossible so don't try it, just run endlessly to get away. But by far the worst part of the game and AI. Is if you ever become hunted or a threat according to the minimap that shows like your stealth status. They will always 100% know, where you're at no matter where you're hiding. Missed a shot by a couple inches from 400 yards away on a cliff side hiding in between bushes in a rock crevice. Too bad, they know exactly where your shot came from and will aggro to include shooting pinpoint mortars on you. Forcing you to relocate. Sniped someone from the same location and someone witnesses the kill, same ordeal. 
Here's a different scenario that's even more far fetched. Place a C4 somewhere and go hide or camp on the otherside of a compound. In a tower. Wherever you like, once you activate the C4 and they AI start to hunt for you, they already know your last known location at the time of being hunted. So you're hiding in the tower, aggro into hunted from an explosion, they already know you're in the tower. So you gotta relocate from there even though theres no way they even knew you were there. 
- A somewhat different con but maybe i should say each to their own. This game has a definite style that you should play to play the game so to speak. And that's stealth. I played on extreme difficulty because I wanted a tad of realism and not feel like a bullet sponge while 1 tapping other enemies. But i feel like you cant play it any other way. If you try to take them all on you'll quickly die. There were multiple times i was stealth-ing through and got caught so i attempted to fight my way to a win. But died every time i think. There was even a case that a pinged enemy was running towards me, i knew i had the advantage because i would see him coming before turning the corner. And In a magical buggy way, he turned the corner. appeared further than where he stopped,and shot me instantly before i could possible even think about shooting back. And I knew he was coming! 
- I think lastly, driving controls are atrocious. I'm mouse and keyboard and i understand the issue that a keyboard is not analog input. But man everything sucks. Even if you just baby tap cars it still wants to fling left and right. You can adjust the camera so you cant hardly see anything. You have to constantly adjust the camera with your mouse instead. Flying controls are equally bad. The helicopter has an updated new controls that are easier for sure than what the classic controls. But still, with the mouse controls it feels impossible to control the gun. Yes you can adjust the sensitivity but it felt useless. Even on low sensitivity the helicopter would swing past further than where intended. Crank up the mouse sensitivity. And it's the same problem, just faster. 

Overall, do i recommend the game? Yes, I cant say I'm upset or anything. Whenever the cons would come up I would just think about them every time, and would just put it in the back of my mind, its the wildpoint gameplay. I would just do things differently if i had the choice to change things in game.

Ghost Recon Wildlands is an outstanding tactical shooter that delivers an immersive open-world experience. From the moment I started playing, I was hooked on its gripping storyline, vast landscapes, and thrilling gameplay. As a fan of the Ghost Recon franchise, Wildlands exceeded my expectations and solidified its place as one of the best games in the series.

The first thing that struck me was the game's breathtaking open-world environment. The fictionalized version of Bolivia is stunningly realized, with diverse landscapes ranging from dense jungles and towering mountains to sprawling salt flats and bustling cities. The attention to detail is exceptional, and the sheer scale of the world is awe-inspiring.

The gameplay mechanics are polished and offer players a wide range of options to tackle missions and objectives. The freedom of choice is one of the game's strongest aspects. You can approach missions stealthily, gathering intel and taking down enemies covertly, or go in guns blazing, causing chaos and explosions. The variety of weapons, equipment, and vehicles at your disposal is extensive, allowing for strategic planning and execution.

One of the highlights of Ghost Recon Wildlands is the seamless co-op experience. Playing with friends or joining a team online adds a new layer of excitement to the game. Coordinating tactics, executing synchronized takedowns, and working together to accomplish missions is incredibly satisfying. The teamwork required brings out the best of the tactical gameplay that the series is known for.

The story campaign is engaging and keeps you invested throughout your journey. Taking down the vicious drug cartel, Santa Blanca, feels like a monumental task, and each mission contributes to the overarching narrative. The game's writing and voice acting are top-notch, immersing you in a gritty world filled with interesting characters and high-stakes situations.

Moreover, the developers have consistently supported Ghost Recon Wildlands with updates, patches, and new content, ensuring a rich and evolving experience for players. The addition of the Ghost War PvP mode further extends the game's longevity, offering intense multiplayer matches that put your skills to the test against other players.

Lastly, the technical performance on Steam is excellent. The game runs smoothly, and the graphics are visually stunning, showcasing the beauty of the environment and the detailed character models.

In conclusion, Ghost Recon Wildlands is a masterpiece of tactical open-world gaming. With its captivating storyline, vast and immersive world, engaging gameplay, and robust co-op experience, it stands as a shining example of what a tactical shooter can achieve. If you're a fan of the genre or simply looking for an unforgettable gaming experience, I wholeheartedly recommend Ghost Recon Wildlands on Steam.
