I love it

This game is incredibly pretty, and I don't just mean the visuals which are also top notch but almost everything about it is really commendable if you are a fan of open world games that are shooters in nature, but slightly harder in some aspects than your average 3rd person open world ordeal that's lacking a sort of coherent and complex narrative. 

I found the game to be highly immersive and good, if not great except perhaps the clunky gameplay which I tend to think is because it's somewhat of an old game coming from 2017 because also games have become a lot smoother since then both in their graphical streaming and gameplay. Of course high graphical fidelity games that run super smooth have existed in the past but just not necessarily in such an extent as - for at least at the time of release of this game - their scope, and I believe that is one of the aspects where its clunkiness comes from, that it's an (Ubisoft) original. By that I don't mean a jab at, but rather to say: it's an original game for its size. Not many other games come to mind that are as big and wide as this one is but a few do come to mind and they usually come from Ubisoft as well.

A few games in recent times that I have played from that era were also kind of clunky in their execution while others certainly were not and beauty of games goes for me a long way back so the pure beauty of Wildlands isn't necessarily in what it shows and how it shows it; it's a "techno-thriller" action/adventure game / tactical experience with very true to life game mechanics like the one shot one kill / death mechanic which really goes back to original Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six games which at the time of their release were truly original games with original mechanics and so: ideas behind them; where most of the other games were sort of blends of Fantasy themes and not really ever high-detail mili-tech, and such games are not really replicated a lot in a slew of games since that time. That is one aspect I appreciate about Wildlands, one that I embrace and one that I miss often in others, despite that this sort of theme feels like a niche.

Its quote/unquote -realism- which can be found in many aspects beyond the damage model is what appeals to me really and honestly appeals to me most out of many other game related themes. World or the geography of the game's world would be another example as would be: the story as well. I find that a lot of these aspects are actually bound to this Tom Clancy methodology which also go back to the writer's books as a core foundation establishing a legacy of someone who sold insurance for a living and had nothing to do with neither books nor games but who would later expand into both and have I would say pretty big success with. This game extends and in some regards expands on that legacy.

Realism of Wildlands appears in many factors which makes the game unique in even Ubisoft's catalogue of Tom Clancy's games but I feel are not necessarily alien to the person themself.

Realism also comes back in a few more aspects than gameplay alone as I eluded to before in context of damage mechanics and gameplay in terms of dealing that damage and receiving it and this cat and mouse or predator and prey type of gameplay becomes really the core aspect of the game which to some like myself would be enough to enjoy a gaming experience but Wildlands does much more with that core, aspect of the core loop of the gameplay because it makes the whole experience interconnected together because it blends together with many immersive and personal experiences like: exploration, discovery, understanding, expectation, learning and trial and error of amongst whom the lore it exposes and realism it allows you to experience in an immersive and sometimes very hectic and exciting way stand out to a high degree. Pleasure and enjoyment included!

Things like vehicles, tools and gadgets and weapons enhance this immersion which I think for the developers might have been a bit of a gamble because next to the story's exposition Wildlands is very limited in the way it is scripted and all the action that happens in the game involving the player, the player themselves initiates which is also another aspect of realism that makes the game, compared to other games stand out in essence in a sort of elegant way due to the simplicity these elements that game's realism provide. No explosion will happen unless player choses it to happen. It's like, making a choice. If it's a good choice it will work and if the player has made a bad choice then they start over, which admittedly is not realistic as in the real world so much as it is in a gaming context where the sandbox is the playground and you play it your way, given the circumstance and given the tools and the means, you chose your way, and usually in a split second  i.e. you make the choices and the choices revolve around you who is responsible to evolve the game further… This seems simple and logical until you realize that you've spent playing the game for years now…

Something to savor?

Clunkiness of the game, makes the game harder than it has to be but also in a sense it makes you rely more on aspects found within it, like one thing that stands out is for instance the power of teammates and rebels who you deploy as in a sort of Guerilla warfare type of way against seemingly an overwhelming enemy but the enemy in the game isn't so much overwhelming as that they are precise. They usually come in small groups and it's an even playfield in terms of damage taking and dealing and in this sense the game makes you as the player attempt a different type of approach that you would, playing other games that involve bulletsponges and more fantastic elements for in here are no healing items (there is life regeneration albeit slow) and there are no power-ups. There is only skill that comes in and persists through experience and knowledge, not necessarily overpoweredness like just a sheer numbers advantage or reliance on heavy metal of various shapes forms and sizes like superior body armor, brute force of war machines like tanks or the brunt of a thousand missiles raining down through artillery and patience of a siege for this skill gathered through what seems to be years of experience comes through knowledge and understanding of your weaknesses and strong points which this game has an interesting way of implementing and leaving it up to you to figure out what to do with and how.

…

So by referring to "game's clunkiness" I might as well had been referring to my own self because there were countless instances of situations that kept repeating where I would die simply because the aimbot like aim of the opponents and my inability despite having high frames in game of not being able to react in time to have a fair fighting chance where the enemy would simply pawn me and rinse and repeat until I became better. Clunkiness of the game can appear through the fact that the game auto switches between third and first person while aiming, that this leaves you somewhat disoriented and not being able to aim well at the enemy after you auto-lean out of cover to shoot, and the fact that when aiming down the sights the FOV zooms in so reaction times as well as overall vision of what is in front of you become hindered, and truly because of this the importance of correct positioning and angles of view from out of cover that you have to make in order not to die a lot and through maneuvering from place to place in game and so effectively learning to play the game become more apparent. I have managed to become better at it so about towards the end but still I think that if the game had more refined gameplay like for instance is found in Breakpoint, it would have saved me a lot of if noting loading of previous saves because the difficulty is really up there.

I just wasted a chunk of my precious life playing Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands, and let me tell ya, it's as exciting as watching paint dry. This game claims to be all about tactical warfare, but it feels more like a snooze-fest on steroids.

First things first, the storyline is about as captivating as a limp lettuce leaf. I mean, seriously, who came up with this generic, cookie-cutter plot? It's like they threw in every cliché they could find and hoped for the best. Yawn.

And don't even get me started on the characters. They're about as memorable as that guy you met once at a party and forgot about immediately. The voice acting is so cringe-worthy that it made me want to stab my eardrums with a rusty spoon. Bravo, developers!

Now, let's talk about the gameplay. Sure, you can roam around this vast open world, but what's the point? The missions are repetitive as hell, and the AI is dumber than a bag of rocks. I've seen more intelligent behavior from a pigeon. It's like the developers took "tactical" and replaced it with "tacti-dull."

Oh, and the graphics? Mediocre at best. The environment looks like it was designed by an intern with a limited budget and a bad taste in colors. There's no wow factor here, folks. Just a whole lot of meh.

But hey, if you're into mind-numbingly dull gameplay, a forgettable story, and characters that you couldn't care less about, then go ahead and waste your hard-earned cash on this snooze fest. Personally, I'd rather watch paint dry or count the tiles on my bathroom floor. At least that would be more entertaining than Ghost Recon Wildlands.

Still fun though.

Note to self, do give a game a chance before making a review. I first reviewed this game after 10 hours and nearly gave up on it. And don't don't even try fast travel; its quicker to run to your destination than to wait for it to load. Secondly its almost impossible to be a ghost. The bad guys have 20-20 night vision and take about a second to spot you.  They can also hit you from 200 meters away with pinpoint accuracy.  In Normal mode this means you have a second to get out of the line of fire.  In advanced mode its be seen, be dead.  More often than not you move out of one line of fire directly into another.

They also let people creep up on you; they hardly ever watch your back.

And then some of the missions are just random.  Parachute into a base, kill all the bad guys without getting noticed, fly out with a helicopter and then suddenly have to fight  5 helicopters all of which can shoot you down in one shot. It tries to be Just Cause meets Sniper Ghost Warrier 2.  It fails on both counts.  In Just Cause the vehicles work.  In this game all vehicles are skittish and random. In Just Cause I almost never died.  You can always get out of trouble using the grappling hook then regroup and go again.  In this piece of trash if your vehicle dies then you are dead; If you get spotted by Unidad you are dead.

I have just gone back and done a "protect the radio" mission that was impossible 5 hours in and is now possible thanks to all of the upgrades. Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands is an action-packed, tactical shooter game that takes players on an adrenaline-fueled journey through the stunning and expansive open world of Bolivia. Developed by Ubisoft Paris and released in 2017, it offers an immersive experience filled with intense firefights, stealth missions, and breathtaking landscapes. As a fan of the Ghost Recon series, I found this installment to be a compelling addition to the franchise, although not without a few minor drawbacks.

One of the standout features of Ghost Recon Wildlands is its massive open world. Bolivia is beautifully rendered, offering diverse environments ranging from lush jungles to arid deserts, towering mountains to sprawling urban areas. The attention to detail is commendable, creating an atmosphere that feels alive and authentic. Exploring the vast landscape, players can choose to tackle missions in any order they please, providing a sense of freedom and agency rarely seen in similar games.

The gameplay in Wildlands strikes a perfect balance between tactical strategy and exhilarating combat. Players assume the role of a member of the elite Ghost Recon team, tasked with taking down a powerful drug cartel. Whether playing solo or in cooperative multiplayer with friends, the game offers a wide array of tools, weapons, and vehicles to accomplish missions in your own style. The tactical aspect is enhanced by the ability to mark enemies, coordinate synchronized shots with teammates, and execute carefully planned infiltration strategies.

In terms of visuals and audio design, Ghost Recon Wildlands delivers a high-quality experience. The attention to detail in the character models, weapon animations, and environmental effects is impressive. The sound design effectively captures the chaos of combat, and the dynamic day-night cycle and weather system contribute to the immersion. However, occasional visual glitches and repetitive character animations can momentarily detract from an otherwise polished presentation.

While the game's strengths lie in its cooperative multiplayer experience, the single-player campaign offers a solid and enjoyable experience as well. The AI teammates are competent and can be given simple commands, making solo play a viable option. However, their behavior can be predictable at times, and a deeper level of squad customization would have been a welcome addition.

One area where Ghost Recon Wildlands falls short is the narrative. Although the premise of taking down a drug cartel is intriguing, the story lacks depth and fails to develop memorable characters or a compelling plot. The game's focus is more on the gameplay and exploration, but a stronger narrative would have added an extra layer of immersion and motivation.

In conclusion, Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands offers an exhilarating and vast open-world experience that fans of tactical shooters will thoroughly enjoy. The game's attention to detail, engaging gameplay mechanics, and cooperative multiplayer elements make it a standout title in the genre. While it may have a few minor flaws, such as a lackluster narrative and occasional technical hiccups, these issues are outweighed by the sheer fun and excitement Wildlands has to offer. If you're looking for a thrilling adventure in a beautifully realized open world, this game is definitely worth exploring.

[code]Ghost Recon Wildlands offers a lot of open world content for fans of tactical shooters and is especially enjoyable as a coop game, however, it also gets repetitive very quickly and suffers from occasional technical problems[/code]

The best way to describe [i]Wildlands[/i] is probably this: It’s a typical modern Ubisoft game, with all the strengths and weaknesses that come attached with that. On the one hand, [i]Wildlands[/i] offers a vast open world with different environments, ranging from forests to deserts to mountains. Said open world, Bolivia in this case, is also filled to the brim with content, from story missions to side activities, which are cramming up your in-game map. And of course, there are lots and lots of ways to upgrade your character: level ups, skill trees, new weapons (& weapon parts for an in-game gunsmith) to find, rebel support upgrades, etc. – in short, [i]Wildlands[/i] gives you a lot of different opportunities to invest your time.

On the other hand, the sheer mass of content also means that the developers favor quantity over the quality of the individual activities. Many of the upgrades don’t really matter – a gun I received earl in the game was better than any other gun I found throughout the rest of it. The novelty of infiltrating bases, killing high value targets or escorting them quickly wears off once you discover that [i]Wildlands[/i] basically reuses the same few mission structures throughout the entire game. And considering that even though the environments look different, many of the bases, camps and hideouts do not, all of your infiltrations or shootouts will quickly turn into a blur. Even though I spent 54h in the game to tackle all of the available story missions, I won’t be able to name even one location that stood out to me – in fact, the many, many locations you visit are so generic that I wouldn’t be able to draw you a map of even one of them.

That said, especially in coop, the basic gameplay loop works solid enough that the generic locations won’t matter much at first. It’s fun to use the variety of gadgets & approaches [i]Wildlands[/i] offers in order to accomplish objectives just the way you want. You could use a helicopter and a parachute to drop into an enemy base, barge in with a tank or sneak your way in by stealthily eliminating guards in your way. Especially the missions tasking you with killing a specific target allow for different tactics – sometimes a well-timed sniper shot from a nearby mountain is all it takes, sometimes a full-on assault with allied rebel NPCs might be a better choice.

[i]Wildlands[/i] offers two enemy factions, the Santa Blanca cartel and Unidad, which sort of work like the police in the [i]Grand Theft Auto[/i] franchise. Both factions got normal goons with guns as well as special types (snipers, armored enemies). Sometimes you’ll also encounter enemy vehicles, like helicopters or tanks. However, as the enemy variety is pretty low and vehicles are only used in certain cases (e.g. enemy convoys), they’re rarely more than simple gunfodder. If you want to infiltrate a base you might want to take of snipers first, but you won’t have to change your approach because of certain enemy types - disappointing. It would have been nice to make plans based on the enemies present, not just on the location alone.

Speaking about the variety in approaching objectives I previously praised, I also have to point it that this sadly doesn’t last forever. Especially on higher difficulty (or the “Tier One”-mode available after reaching max level), [i]Wildlands[/i] becomes a much different game. Enemies can kill you almost immediately now and their locations aren’t hinted at on the map anymore, which basically makes stealth approaches the only viable option if you want to complete missions. Considering [i]Wildlands[/i] is a tactical shooter after all, this isn’t surprising, but I’m still mentioning it for those who don’t want to sneak around guards all the time.

My biggest gripe with the stealth approaches in [i]Wildlands[/i] concerns the enemy AI, which can ruin your well-planned approaches to a mission in more ways than you expect. Throughout most of the game, the AI is solid enough: enemies aren’t particularly smart, but they do take cover when shoot at from afar and call for help if needed. What makes them so annoying in terms of stealth approaches, however, is their unpredictable spotting. Sometimes enemies are able to spot you through walls or other solid structures (the snipers in particular), sometimes they don’t react to corpses of their friends but at other times they immediately sound the alarm instead. They’re also very good at “coincidentally” heading directly to your location when searching for you: One time I had an entire truck of reinforcements spawn directly behind me even though it was only my coop partner they spotted. These AI issues can make stealth approaches quite frustrating, especially as mission checkpoints can be quite bad as well.

Anyway, even while stealth doesn’t work as well as it should be, getting spotted is less frustrating when you got a coop partner to help you out: [i]Wildlands[/i] opens up a lot more if you got friends to play with. Especially on lower difficulty, you can simply go wild while approaching missions, which is a lot of fun. Maybe one of you is piloting a helicopter transporting another, who is using a sniper to take out a target from above. Or you’re participating in a great car chase, with one player driving while the other is trying to take down your pursuers. But even on higher difficulties it’s really entertaining to infiltrate a base with each player taking care of a different corner and I can’t think of many games allowing for all these moments at once.

That said, while the generic locations and missions as well as the general repetitiveness of [i]Wildlands[/i] don’t feel as bad if you play this game in coop and I highly recommend playing this game with friends, coop also comes with additional problems. These are mainly of the technical sort, like progress sometimes not being properly saved when finishing missions together. Especially the “Silent Spade” mission was bugged, with me receiving the rewards for finishing the mission together while my coop partner was stuck at an earlier checkpoint according to the game. Additionally, while the game ran fine once connected, we encountered many issues trying to join each other’s lobby. This might be thanks to Ubisoft Connect, which is required if you want to play this game – online or not.

Lastly, let’s talk about the story of [i]Wildlands[/i]. The basic set-up of [i]Wildlands[/i] is basically to take down a big bad cartel boss, however, in order to approach him you have to take down a dozen of his underlings first. Of course, it shouldn’t be surprising that the story of [i]Wildlands[/i] is quite cliched and doesn’t feel very coherent, as you can tackle the story missions in any order you want. Considering you also don’t encounter the big bad until the final mission, apart from a handful of previous voice lines, the big villain doesn’t receive much characterization beyond “he’s evil”. Frankly, the entire story set-up feels like it’s just window-dressing for the open world activities anyway, so don’t expect it to be more than that.

Concluding, [i]Wildlands[/i] does offer a solid gameplay loop that’s especially great when experienced with friends. But it also suffers from a problem of quantity over quality, which might lead to a few fun hours at first but a feeling of boredom later on. The longer you play, the more you realize that [i]Wildlands[/i] is lacking depth and some true variety. It’s fun but for a tactical shooter, it's also a bit mindless and might be best experienced with some long breaks between sessions.

Gameplay:
+ good gunplay
+ lots of gun and character customization and personalization
+ massive, diverse map
- distance between everything makes travel often tedious
- the grind is real - this game takes a _while_, even if you don't plan to 100% this game
- a few random missions are weirdly hard/unforgiving
+ civilians (and strict orders to not attack them) keeps gunplay interesting and careful, prevents turning the game into a shoot 'em up

Graphics/Sound:
+ gorgeous world
+ smooth, natural character animations
- this PC port doesn't feel too optimized. Even on a desktop RTX 3-series, I changed to lower settings and still had occasional stutter.
- some long load times (especially with Internet on - see my note at the end)
+ gun customization sounds are oh so satisfying
+ voices and ambient sounds enhance gameplay

Story:
+ good characterizations of enemies
- ...the protagonist, not so much
+ refreshing seeing "playing the long game" in stories, where results come with time
- in my personal experience, I felt little investment in cutscenes and individual characters
+ some fun cameos from the "Ubisoft cinematic universe"

Overall: great third-person RPG shooter that requires a lot of grind. If you have the time (and can figure out how to play with a friend), it's worth it.

Other notes:
- I only played offline - no friends connected, no co-op. I heard some had issues with it. Even then, the Internet connection makes load times longer. I just put the Ubisoft launcher in offline mode, that fixed it.
- this review is from someone who's only other Ghost Recon game played is "Advanced Warfighter 2" on the Xbox 360 (solid game btw). So I can't really rate it on whether it lives up to the rest of the series or not.
- high profanity warning - both in cutscenes and gameplay, your character swears often when things go wrong. The most you can do is mute _all_ voices, including cutscenes, enemies, other characters, etc. So if you are unsure about profanity, it's either all or nothing.

This is one of those games where it might be fun to play, but your time is better spent on so many other things. I played the main story from beginning to end. Got all the weapons, all the upgrades, reached max level, and I'm still playing one of the expansions. While there are some memorable missions and cool characters, at it's core, this game is more Ubisoft busywork, and the game is worse now than when it first came out (due to all the microtransactions and cosmetic loot crates in a supposedly strategic open world military game).

The good:

-Bolivia is beautiful and there's a huge amount of variation in the topography.
-Gunplay is solid and fun.
-Using rebel skills is fun.
-*Certain* missions are memorable (the final battle, Bookhart, the mission with the Unidad general, and the mission with Sueno's daughter to name a few). Ironically, the most fun missions for me were bonus missions completely unrelated to the story (the Predator, Sam Fisher, and the Breakpoint tie-in mission).

Cons:

-Pretty much everything in the game reminds me of another game that did a better job. Metal Gear Solid 5 has better stealth, Arma is more realistic, Hitman has more memorable missions, Far Cry has more eccentric and interesting characters. 
-The balance and the way damage is calculated is way off. Submachine guns and shotguns are just not that viable at higher difficulties. Assault rifles, LMGs, and snipers are better in 99/100 scenarios.
-Most of the special tools in the game are worthless. Lures are completely outclassed by flares, flashbangs are never more useful than frag grenades, and frag grenades themselves are outclassed by mines and C4. 


The "stupidly big but empty map full of busywork" has been done to death, I'm sick of it, and the work never really pays off. Take your money elsewhere. Also, stay away from the sequel. It's somehow even worse than this game.

Great tactical stealth shooter. To succeed you need to plan ahead, recon the area thoroughly with the drone, watch patrol routes, take out lone enemies first so as not to attract attention. You have a lot of freedom to approach missions in the way you want thanks to the many vehicles you can drive or pilot and the vast open world. It's true that side missions lack variety - there are a set range of side missions and they are essentially repeated with minor variations in each province. However, the main story missions I found to be very compelling and varied, and the moment-to-moment stealth gameplay is addictive and satisfying. The storyline is predictable and cookie-cutter, with highly questionable ethics, but if you can disconnect that part of your brain and focus on the high quality tactical combat in a beautiful open world you will definitely have a blast with this.

I havent played military shooters in a while, got burned out during the 360/PS3 days. But i was looking for another open world game, killing dudes, upgrading, finding the things etc. Since this game was 80% off i figured why not. And this game delivers. There actually may be *too* many things to do in this game. I spent a good portion just doing side missions, exploring and doing some of the main quests. But then it started to feel too repetitive but in a negative way. Not sure why. Thankfully though, the main story missions are pretty damn good, same with the voice work. 

As a fan of Far Cry, i wanted more of that feel here. So i played in Arcade (easy) difficulty, which isnt exactly easy but is way more forgiving. However, if you want the full tactical experience you can ramp up the difficulty and turn off the hud, waypoints, and more if you wish. You can play with an AI squad which is what i did, but you can also remove them completely and go solo which i thought was a nice feature. But there's some big downsides to that too. You cant get revived, and you lose the ability to have your squad mark targets and kill them instantly with a perk called sync shot in which they do it silently and is very helpful and fun because they do it silently. 

Anyways, i had only about 3 or 4 generals(?) to kill before killing the main bad guy. I decided to wrap things up and beat the final boss and got what i suppose is the "bad" ending, but i thought it was pretty good. Then in typical open world fashion you get booted back to the game to continue on if you wish with a notification that i beat 80% of the bosses and if i do them all i'll get a different ending. So I figured why not and spent a few more hours killing all of them and then the main bad guy. The ending was different, but tbh i kinda liked the other one better. Alternatively, if you do things a certain way you can actually kill the main bad guy pretty early on if you want as well, although all the cutscenes afterward will still go on as though he never died which sorta ruins consistency, so dont do that. 

Theres tons and tons of weapons, parts and things to find. The weapon parts annoyed me the most though because a weapon part is only good for ONE specific weapon instead of its class. So you can go on for dozens and dozens of hours collecting parts for weapons you either dont want to use or for a weapon you dont even have. Plus, you can only carry two weapons and your side pistol. No upgrades for an extra weapon slot or two which was a bummer. I got to the point where i found a good assualt rifle and sniper rifle both with suppressors and i was doing just fine with them and never bothered with looking for all the other crap out there. 

Upgrades are good, but i wish there were more, especially considering theres SO much you can do in this game. It got to the point where i upgraded everything i wanted to and didnt care much to upgrade anything else.  Side missions will reward you with one of four types of resources that you need to upgrade a certain skill. Since i upgraded what i want enough i stopped doing side missions and banked over 65 skill points which i couldnt use at all. It would have been nice to use them for something extra like a 1% bonus to something like in the AC Origins/Odyssey games.

Overall though it was a decent shooter.

Let's get the bad out of the way:
- Game came out in 2017, in 2023 still having server issues.
- Occasional crashes caused by unoptimized performance, surprisingly taxing even on RTX 3080 hardware.

Ok, now to the meat of the game:

This is one of those rare games where I can and have to wholeheartedly recommend that you play co-op either with strangers, or better yet, with friends. Why?

If you play alone, it's standard Ubisoft open-world fare: massive areas, paper-thin exploration, outposts to clear, loot to collect and forget about yada-yada...There are interesting repeatable tasks such as convoy ambush, rebel support, and multiple approaches you can take to complete them, which is very neat. Most of the items in game you can earn by completing missions, doing challenges, so no real money required - which is very strange for Ubisoft.

HOWEVER, with friends, that's where the game truly shines: tactical mishaps, failure of coordination, helicopter crashes, accidental killings of VIPs...Wait, you might be asking: why is this guy listing stupid stuff that you generally would hate in a co-op environment? Trust me: failures are fun, because with a team of functional primates, you will learn - get better - and once you and your teammates get the hold of things, it gets really, and I mean REALLY badass. Like movie-level badass.

But uh, servers still suck though.

BACK STORY:
To be honest, I used to hate Ghost Recon. When it was first announced in 2015, it just didn't appeal to me, and I kept confusing it with other Tom Clancy games like Rainbow Six Siege and The Division, trust me it was the Tom Clancy name, lol. I know it sounds embarrassing, but I just couldn't get excited about it. At the time, everything was turning into an open-world game, and Ghost Recon just didn't seem to fit that mold. 

 Around the time Rainbow Six Siege was releasing, I found myself coming up with numerous excuses as to why I wouldn't get the game. I would purposely confuse the game with Ghost Recon, a completely different game. My friends would attempt to correct me, but I stubbornly clung to my delusions. I vividly recall saying things like, "Rainbow Six Siege is an open-world shooter, I'm not interested in that kind of game." To which my friends would say, "No, that's Ghost Recon! You should really give Siege a chance, it's going to be so much fun, just buy the game."I was too insecure to admit that I didn't have a next-gen console and was only debating with them to hide that fact

I would eventually get a PS4 in 2017. In the years that followed, Ubisoft would drop banger after banger. From Far Cry 5 to Assassin's Creed Odyssey, and even made a comeback with games like Siege and For Honor, The amount of hours I spent playing those games was insane, with Odessey being the peak of my enjoyment. I would eventually platinum it and move on. 
That's when my friend would recommend Ghost Recon Wildlands as our next playthrough. I really treasured our friendship but I was opposed to the idea. After some thought, I agreed, because this was the same friend who game-shared me Odessey, and man, did I love that game. So in return, I bought the game and game-shared him. We would play it but never really got into it, going as far as the end of the tutorial mission. Our lives would move on, with him and work and me and school. Unfortunately, our friendship would eventually fade when Covid hit the globe. 

Fast forward to 2021, and I'm a workaholic who plays Rainbow Six Siege in my free time. Long story short, turns out playing Siege with brain-dead teammates was taking a toll on my mental health, so I took a break from gaming and started working out. That's when I got in touch with that old friend from 2019 who I used to play with. We caught up, and he told me he was getting married. We played a game of GTA Online together before going our separate ways. Grieving with nostalgia I looked at my game library. From GTA 5, Injustice 2, Fortnite, R6 Siege, Assassins Creed, and Ghost Recon Wildlands. Ghost Recon? I couldn't help but notice that Ghost Recon was the odd one out. I had no memory of playing it with him, so I downloaded it and gave it a try.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

REVIEW:
I don't know if it was my disdain for what Siege had become, but man did I fall in love with Wildlands. The story hooked me from the start, the UI was clean, and the game had such a deep and well-crafted weapon and cosmetic selection. In the past, I've played tactical games like Operation Flashpoint and Insurgency Sandstorm, but Wildlands felt real. it was modern, tactical, and clean. And the gameplay and story just further enhanced this


Gameplay:
The guns and gunplay for the most part are consistent. The guns sound and feel great, I only wish the game gave them more scopes. The way our character moves and interacts with the world is amazing as well. From having deep convos with the crew, hit firing when taking cover, removing/adding the suppresser, and shooting from their back while prone. I just love and appreciate the attention to detail that when into the gameplay. (There's a lot I'm leaving out but you get the gist)

Story:
You could definitely still feel that Ubisoft formula in the story but it somehow just works. I got fully immersed in the game's story, primarily because of Bowman, loved her character. The story combined with the world felt real and the way the music complimented everything was just amazing. 

But what really made it all a blast was the co-op. I played it with my brother, and we had a great time customizing our characters to suit each biome, grinding the skill tree, stealth infiltrations, role-playing, and just messing around and having fun. Unfortunately, all good things come to an end, and my brother eventually drifted away from the game. Ghost Recon Wildlands stands out as a pinnacle of tactical gaming, offering players a compelling blend of stealth, action, and exploration within the vast expanse of Bolivia's open world. At its core, the game's stealth mechanics provide a challenging and immersive experience, allowing players to infiltrate enemy territories with precision and strategy. Whether executing silent takedowns with a karambit or coordinating covert operations with a squad, the stealth gameplay keeps players engaged and on the edge of their seats as they navigate through hostile environments.

Yet, Ghost Recon Wildlands doesn't shy away from heart-pounding moments of loud, explosive action. The game seamlessly transitions from stealth to intense firefights, often accompanied by the unmistakable sound of an Apache helicopter roaring overhead. These adrenaline-fueled encounters offer a stark contrast to the quieter moments of infiltration, ensuring that players are constantly faced with thrilling challenges and varied gameplay experiences.

In addition to its dynamic gameplay mechanics, Ghost Recon Wildlands offers extensive customization options for both weapons and characters. Players can choose from a diverse selection of firearms, each with its own set of attachments and modifications, allowing for personalized loadouts tailored to individual preferences. Furthermore, the game's photo mode provides a creative outlet for players to capture and share their most epic moments, further enhancing the immersive experience of exploring Bolivia's stunning landscapes. With its combination of strategic depth, exhilarating action, and robust customization features, Ghost Recon Wildlands offers an unforgettable gaming experience that is sure to captivate players for hours on end.


There are several drawbacks to note in this game. Firstly, the reliance on the Ubisoft Connect launcher can be a hassle for some players, disrupting the seamless gaming experience. Additionally, co-op play may encounter occasional errors, detracting from the overall enjoyment of team-based gameplay. Another issue arises with the game's AI, as allied bots may appear unresponsive or ineffective during crucial moments, leading to frustration. Furthermore, enemy AI accuracy occasionally feels overly precise, making encounters feel disproportionately challenging. Moreover, the inclusion of microtransactions for desirable cosmetics and vehicles, such as the Apache helicopter, APCs, and Gold Lamborghini, can detract from the immersion of the game world. Additionally, there's a need to restart the game after completing DLC content to return to the main menu, which disrupts the flow of gameplay. Lastly, the Tier 1 mode's demanding grind can feel excessively time-consuming, potentially deterring players seeking a more accessible experience. 

Beside the drawbacks, it is one of the best FPS tactical game i ever played.

A game where, at the beginning is an essence of a classic Tom Clancy game (AI that is dumber than rocks but kills your entire team within seconds, a game style that revolves around making the perfect plan, and US troopers some backwaters somewhere within the Eastern Europe or Central Asia/Counter-Terror unit hunting some big name Terrorist), becomes something different at the end of the 2000s; more akin to a pseudo-sci-fi military shooter that is en vogue during those times.

Obviously, Wildlands is a departure from that formulae; since now its a standard Ubisoft sandbox but with third-person shooter mechanics. You have your choices of stealth (at higher levels, its mandatory) or loud (means you screwed yourself). The story itself is, uh.... something. It's obvious that aside from novels written by the late Tom Clancy himself, the games that are made with his name aren't exactly the pinnacle of storytelling. Ghost Recon Wildlands isn't an exception. Sure, it's fun hearing Diana Burnwood swear every other sentences, and hearing Male Nomad (whom, if I remember, is a Major and should be in his mid to late 30s) sounding like a teenager who learned every single swear word in the vocabulary and combining them to become cooler (♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥) is always funny for me.

The actual story itself, while simple, isn't the main drive of it. I don't think it is. The main drive is with the gameplay loop. Yes, it's as standard as apple pie with Ubisoft for putting Combat Outposts like its candy, but the fun part begins on how you tackle 'em. Nomad moves pretty well, any weapons you use is an auto-kill when hidden, and at higher levels; the game becomes your little plaything, especially when you have all the tools at hand (which you will need on some locations). Some weapons are build equally, others aren't. Shotguns are really bad in this game; since SMGs fill their role better and can hit targets above 50 meters. LMGs are always a treat to carry on loud missions, but they took forever to load, and using a M4A1/TAR-21/Famas with 50 round mag is better at that case.

There are many other complaints I would give. The car and bike physics felt like the cars have their tires sanded out, and the bike felt like driving with a very obese man on the back with how erratic it responded sometimes. But, my biggest complaint yet is with Unidad.

In the game, there's three factions: Kataris, Santa Blanca and Unidad. Kataris is the rebels you're working (and throwing their people into fire if you play 'em like me) with, Santa Blanca is the funny cartel people with the world's most annoying DJ and Mrs."IF YOU'RE NOT BOSSY, YOU GET WHAT YOU DESERVE" (Perico can you stop putting Nidia every 5 minutes you simp, I wish I actually shot her instead of dragging her into a chopper so Bowman has a Bosslady to Bosslady talk to her), and Unidad. Full stop.

If there's words I can describe Unidad is "swarms of rats". GTA V cops ain't got anything with these people. They have essentially a wanted mechanic, where if they spot you for more than 30 seconds, they will send a patrol at you. If that doesn't work: 2 patrols. No? APCs. "Oh, is that all", you may ask? If that's all, then it shouldn't be a problem! Sadly, the one thing that LSPD doesn't have with Unidad is the SHEER QUANTITY that they can throw at you. During one of the missions in Media Luna (the penultimate one), they send an entire platoon at me. Sure, you can just walk around 'em (and in fairness, that's what you should do), and you SHOULD have an Anti-Materiel Rifle at the ready for helicopters (if you don't, then you're screwed), but it does get really annoying at times when their patrols spotted you and you have to do the whole song and dance.
Don't get me started about the only-Unidad territories (Media Luna and Fior de Oro), those are an exercise of pain, patience and "AGAIN?" once you get spotted by a Unidad patrol and you didn't kill 'em fast enough. Admittedly, Fior de Oro has the best Assault Rifle in the game for me (M4A1 my beloved).

Sometimes, it's good that the AI is dumb as rocks. They only have two moods when spotting you: Laser-accurate shooting while in cover, or RUSH. Like, they will rush exactly at your location where you shoot 'em. Not even a 10 meters or two of deviation. Funnily enough, that's exactly how I take care of Unidad bases at that point. Since they're tankier than the average Sicario, the grunts are gonna rush in willy-nilly half of the time. So, you set up traps and mines for 'em. If not, and you already spotted 'em, just walk around and shoot 'em in the back. Sometimes, their cheating helps you since, like a Tactical Shooter AI, they're dumb as rocks.

While you may play the game without even leveling up or getting any weapons/attachment you want in the map is fine (P416, MP5 and M40A5 are solid weapons), the games does feel like it builds on the idea that you slowly build your Nomad to become a maniac with enough explosives to level an entire city, and carrying an entire arsenal that fits to their situation. Like, leveling up all your stuff to level 1 is a must for me, since you get all the tools you needed. When you reach to the point where you deal with Unidad, hopefully you already have a good LMG, Anti-Materiel Rifle and enough levels on Vehicular destruction. If not, then, uh, well, ♥♥♥♥.

The customization in this game is uh... something. I kinda wish Nomad gets more than just four hairs, 12 faces and more gear that doesn't look off; but that's life.I guess that's on the sequel.

Either way, this game is worth playing.... on a discount. Don't buy it full price, you're an absolute buffoon if you do that.

Ghost Recon Wildlands is an open-world third-person shooter game developed by Ubisoft Paris and published by Ubisoft. Released in 2017, the game is set in a fictionalized version of Bolivia, where players take on the role of a special forces team tasked with taking down a drug cartel.

One of the standout features of Ghost Recon Wildlands is its massive open world, which offers players a vast and diverse environment to explore. The game's world is filled with different landscapes, including mountains, forests, deserts, and cities, each with its unique challenges and opportunities.

The game's tactical gameplay mechanics are also noteworthy, as they allow players to approach missions and combat situations in various ways. Players can choose to take a stealthy approach, using silenced weapons and carefully planning their actions, or opt for a more aggressive playstyle, using heavy firepower and vehicles to take down enemies.

Another aspect of the game that stands out is its multiplayer mode, which allows players to team up with friends or other players online to complete missions and take on the cartel together. The game's co-op mode adds to the game's overall replayability and provides players with a fun and challenging experience.

However, the game's story and characters are somewhat forgettable, and the game can feel repetitive at times, with many of the missions feeling similar to one another.

Overall, Ghost Recon Wildlands is an enjoyable open-world shooter game that offers a vast and diverse environment to explore and fun tactical gameplay mechanics. While the game's story and characters may not be its strongest point, the game's co-op mode and replayability make it worth checking out for fans of the genre.

TL;DR. If you get this 80% off, and have friends to play it with, it's worth it. At full price it is not. Game has bugs, micro transactions, and loot boxes. And an uninspiring and at times incoherent story. In general, I enjoyed this game. However, that comes with a few caveats. Firstly, I got this when it was 80% off. There is no chance that this game would be even nearly worth it at its full price of $75 AUD.For the base price of $75, you’re not even given everything, in true Ubisoft fashion there is still loot boxes and micro transactions. Also requires the Ubisoft game launcher (which can be quite annoying).Also, this is one of those games that requires mates to play with. In single player the AI companions are annoying at best and a big hinderance at worst. Fortunately, you can disable them in the settings menu, but be prepared for a difficulty spike over playing co-op.The story is also uninspiring and bland. If you want something story rich, maybe look somewhere else. On top of that some of the character's voice acting in a few places could use some, [i]work[/i]. Though for most characters the voice acting is pretty good. But the excessive use of 'tango' does annoy me. I get the use of it, being an elite recon team, but hearing it a hundred times in a single encounter, it's a bit over done.On top of micro-transactions and loot box mechanics, even after the age of this game, bugs are still everywhere. Gotta love falling through the map after exiting a helicopter and dying, getting spotted through vehicles, or failing a stealth mission because the rebels decided to start a faction warfare. But probably the most annoying is how inconsistent inviting people to your lobby is. My mate and I typically spend 15 min restarting the game trying to get the invite to work. A constant loop of 'in menus (unavailable)', and other features that are just broken. E.g., the prompt asking if you want to rejoin a game after crashing or quitting is broken, and always results in a message saying Ubisoft services are down, along with a couple other game joining features.Also falls into the common [i]go stealth or go loud[/i] games where if your going stealth, and the enemy is alerted (e.g., finds dead body), they can magically know where you are. Nothing is more annoying than being up on a massive hill sniping, someone finds a dead body, and then a few min later a patrol is just magically behind you. While this isn't game breaking, it is very annoying and is something you should be aware of.Also, toward the end of the game upgrading can get a bit grindy and tedious, constantly running around trying to get enough resources to unlock the next tier of a single skill. And of course you can also use micro transactions to skip the grind, thanks Ubisoft.Though overall I did enjoy the game, I still don't recommend it at it's full listed price.

Like a gob of sh* thrown on the Mona Lisa, this game's beautiful open world is utterly ruined by escalating difficulty and painfully long reloading times (the game, not your guns in game). I've played ghost recon and splinter cell from the beginning. I was excited to play a stealth action game after the seeming death of the genre (although the original Ghost Recon was more strategy than stealth). This game however, is just not fun. It's amazing aesthetics and customization only raise your expectations to be utterly crushed.

I've maxed out my stealth abilities and tooled out my silent weapons and there's seemingly no difference in detection times or ability to stay stealthy. I completed the missions to get the stealth optic camouflage and it doesn't make a difference to anything. Enemies will still see you and alert the entire base in a second. I even turned down the difficulty to 'Arcade', the game's easiest setting, and there's no discernible difference.

For the enemy AI being so incredible at homing in on you and shooting you with extreme precision, your squad-mates' AI is hot garbage. They are constantly losing marks and getting caught by the enemy, often times costing you missions... which is made worse by the game's reload times. I can get up and go make some coffee while the game reloads. Even with my rig above recommended specs and Ethernet hard-lined in. Now I understand why old-school stealth games just had the enemies resume their regular patrol routes so fast.     
-That was a meme but here it would be welcome so we wouldn't have to reload the whole damn game.

You get some cool gadgets that just end up being worthless junk. You can't use mines because civilians run over them constantly. Kinda weird how an alerted armored enemy is almost as tough as a vehicle, but you can one-shot them when firing from stealth.

Overall, this game is so close to being a beautiful masterpiece that could breath life into the now extinct stealth action genre, it just pisses you off they could fumble it so bad. It should be re-named "Souls-Recon: A Fromsoftware wannabe."

Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands is a well-crafted tactical shooter that offers a vast and immersive open-world environment for players to explore. The game's storyline is interesting, with players tasked with taking down a powerful drug cartel operating in Bolivia. The game's graphics are also impressive, with stunning visuals that add to the realism and atmosphere of the game.

One of the highlights of the game is its cooperative multiplayer mode, which allows players to team up with up to three other players to complete missions and take down the cartel. This mode adds a lot of replayability to the game and makes it a great option for those who enjoy team-based gameplay.

The game's weapon customization and upgrade system is also well-designed, allowing players to tailor their weapons to their playstyle and become more effective in combat. The game's vehicles and gadgets also add to the variety of gameplay options available to players.

However, the game's open-world environment can feel overwhelming at times, with a large number of side missions and activities to complete. The game's AI can also be frustrating at times, with enemies sometimes behaving in unrealistic ways or being too easy to take down.

Overall, Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands is a great game for fans of tactical shooters and open-world gameplay. While it has some minor flaws, its cooperative multiplayer mode, customization options, and immersive world make it a worthwhile game to check out.

There is roughly 80 hours of content in the base game should you take your time to complete everything the game has to offer. There are multiple side objectives to complete and collectables to find, with a large number of which providing accurate historical and cultural information regarding Bolivia's real-world customs and beliefs. The weapons on offer are all extremely satisfying to use, with attachments and new firearms requiring one to find them throughout the world. There are also rebel-assistive perks that can expand your options for tackling any situation, such as the command to request rebel infantry support, vehicle drop-offs and even mortar fire on a designated location. The process of scouting out enemy positions is conducted through the use of your personal drone, which can also be upgraded to become a portable EMP, a noise emitter or even a remote control bomb.

Highly recommend to anyone who enjoys open-world games that encourage stealthy approaches to combat, yet are not punished for taking gunfights head-on.

This is possibly my favorite game of all time, and anyone looking for an immersive, tactical, squad-based shooter should look no further.

First of all, the game is beautiful to look at, even six years after release. You'll explore Bolivia's salt flats, dominating snow-capped mountains, swamps, lakes, and fields of the infamous coca plant as you take down outposts, destroy convoys for precious loot, and pursue missions that have a decent variety that keep you intrigued. The open world is dynamic, though perhaps feels a bit empty, but if you stick to your modus operandi of striking unwitting opponents and disappearing before anyone was the wiser, it will suffice.

There are a variety of ways to handle each enemy encounter, but I find stealth to be this game's strong suit. Much has been made of the inability to move/hide bodies (a detail fixed in the sequel, Ghost Recon Breakpoint), but I love the increased difficulty this can add to the game's stealth encounters. What really unlocks this game's full potential is the "Ghost Mode," or permadeath mode you can play with your friends. It amps up the tension, and is absolutely a serious challenge for gamers.

This game's strongest weaknesses lie with the AI, both your AI teammates and the enemies can be pretty bone-headed at times, and their behavior can be predictable. But, due to reinforcements coming if you alert the base, every encounter is difficult enough to take seriously. The story is also laughably jingoistic and ridiculous; don't come to Wildlands for a page-turner. But that's okay when you can get immersed in the world on your own, and get lost in the wildlands of Bolivia.

I love this game, I've probably sunk more hours into it than any game I've ever played, and I hope many more people can experience what it has to offer.

This game is a masterpiece. If you like tactical shooters and open world, there is no better game (even its sequel Breakpoint is not as good).

The gameplay is fantastic: A huge campaign with parallel missions (in fact this is a tree you can solve in any order), taking place in a gigantic, credible open world. Everything is possible from your gun to flying helicopter. You can even play the campaign in coop, up to 4 players!

The graphics are superb. Its sequel Breakpoint is a notch higher, however, the feeling of being in a foreign country with all its colors and culture is incredibly well rendered in Wildlands.

The audio is great as well: from all tactical stuff to inhabitants dancing on the main square, celebrating stuff in towns. You really feel you are here.

Indeed, unlike 99% of other open world games, this one is really immersive: It feels like you are in a real country with real civilian people doing their stuff. While the bad guys are just a small part of the population. 

You can customize the difficulty to your liking. I played without any help (no HUD), just two weapons, “realistic” clothes, and all, and it was fun to drive down the roads, listening to the radio, reading the map, to know where to turn to reach the next town where my target was.

This game is half arcade, half simulation. Weapons are from real life. However, they are (un)balanced for gameplay. No weapon is really better than another, and they do not necessarily match their real-life characteristics. Now, that said, they are great fun. You can customize them to death, same for your outfit and loadout.

It is great to play coop, one player infiltrating with his gun and knife, while a sniper is covering him from afar. Even in solo, the bots, while not great, are fine. They can’t break your missions, and do whatever you ask of them.

To date, this is the best open world tactical shooter I have played in a long time. While Breakpoint is a notch higher technically. Wildland campaign, characters and overall gameplay is better. I like how the world is full or real civilian people, not just bad guys, and stupid drones…

Buy it, even at full price, this game is a gem.

A pretty good game. Stealth is handled pretty well, shooting feels good, and the atmosphere of the world and story is done very well.

Some of the things it could improve on are the movement mechanics and mission design. The movement is very context-dependent like in other Ubisoft games. i.e. you can't jump unless there is an obstacle that you can press A on to activate the jumping animation. This works fine for the most part, but there are some obstacles in the open world which appear easily passable but that you cannot press A on. This can be really disappointing when it ruins your carefully planned stealth approach. As for mission design, there are some missions where enemies just spawn out of nowhere. This just seems like a lazy way to create a sense of urgency, and clashes with the stealthy and precise tone of the game. The convoy missions are another irritation. If I can shoot out the driver, it is very satisfying, but usually I can't do that. These missions often devolve into a goofy-ass car chase, which, again, clashes with the tone of the game. My final complaint is that the guns don't feel very unique from each other. There are several assault rifles that feel the same, and the same goes for smgs and snipers. I didn't find much use for shotguns. I guess the variety is just there for style/customization, which is fine I guess.

Worth it in 2023? Absolutely.

TOM CLANCY'S GHOST RECON: WILDLANDS - '' Some Are Soldiers, We Are Ghosts'' - 

1 ABOUT) -
Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands is a tenth installment of tactical shooter video game by Ubisoft and first game in the Ghost Recon series with open world. The game offer third-person perspective and optional first-person view for gun aiming. Unlike GR Wildlands predecessors, the game consist from main and side missions. After completing missions, players can reach the locations where the mission starts or where they want to go. The game offer you Classic campaigne mode, Guerrilla mode, Ghost mode and Ghost War mode with 2 DLC's, Narco Road and Fallen Ghosts (exclusive Predator event is no more supported).
2 GAMEPLAY ) -
Players can parachute from helicopters and planes, walk overland, driving vehicles towards their objectives. Also they can grab enemies at close range or use them like a human shield, gain experience points, also available is customization characters including their AI teammates, and more. Every weapon and gear can be upgraded. Wounded characters will be healed automatically and your dying teammates can be revived. The game can be played solo with AI teammates, which player can give orders or they can be disabled via  the game settings. GR Wildlands is playable like PVP and PVE, offer you many activities. In CO-OP mode players can be joined by other three players, to complete missions and explore the game's world together. 
3 PLOT ) -
Ghost Recon Wildlands take a place in Bolivia in 2019. The Sounth American country has become unstable after that brutal and religious drug cartel boss ''El Sueno'' and his ''Santa Blanca'' gains a control over several location in the Bolivia. Meanwhile the Bolivian government established ''La Unidad'' special semi-military forces for fighting with Santa Blanca's thugs. In the same time DEA agent Ricardo Sandoval has disappeared probably after his attempt to infiltrate El Sueno's cartel. Ghost Recon team is here deployed as a part of  special ''Operation Kingslayer'' joined by CIA, DEA, JSOC and Pac Katari's rebels. 
Aftermath of Operation Kingslayer the Bolivian government trying remnants of tactical police unit Unidad reformed into the ''Los Extranjeros'' which is corrupted and now take control of over cocaine's production.
Somewhere in Bolivia CIA trying reveal identity and find a location of Santa Blanca's head of smuggling network ''El Invisible'', they sent Ghost in undercover to find a clues of El Invisible's identity and stop activities of Santa Blanca's remnants. 
4 REVIEW) - 
For me is Ghost Recon: Wildlands the best part of franchise, which offer refined story, an action, a thrill, interesting locations and landscapes, battlefields, multiple weapons and gears. It's ultimate adventure with promise of never ending pleasure from playing. I think that Ghost Recon: Wildlands is really one of many Ubisoft's masterpieces and that's reason why I give it full 10/10 points. It's really a very good work.

This game is a good memory for me. Playing Breakpoint makes me remember how much more fun and diverse this game is. 

This game is so beautiful. Breakpoint is such a downgrade from this game. I found my mate and me were changing outfits to go with some of the different biomes (I say some but there are so many it's insane) and often times I decided not to take a vehicle into situations, but rather just take a stroll up the mountain. I feel bad for my characters calves. 

 The characters you pick up and extract are different and sometimes are fun to watch. While the story is one of the most generic American Intervention on a cartel story you will ever see, it's still much more alive than Breakpoint. KAREN BOWMAN really carries this game. You'll have one of the most vile human beings on the planet sitting in a room with you and KAREN BOWMAN. All she says is "You tell me where to find (person of interest) or you go to jail" and then every single one of these vile cartel members are like "Ok I'll tell you" with no fight. It's quite hilarious. 

I love the idea that this white woman in jeans is the master interrogator and you're just a pawn in the machine. 

I hate to compare Breakpoint so much, but this world feels so much more like it has a purpose than Breakpoints world.  It's not a story game and that's ok. For the story it has, you can suspend your disbelief and just have fun in the game. I've been walking through a town where I will see people playing music in a circle, dancing, eating, and doing things. I really enjoy the graffiti, the propaganda, the grand statues and buildings that the cartel are trying to build. It gives this game such a unique personality. With that being said, I think most of the AI is pretty dumb and I hate playing with AI teamates. Either find a friend to play the game with, or just play solo. (AI teamates are only good for sync shotting). There is also Wildlife and it's really cool. I like the part with the flamingos. I often hung out with those guys before a mission. (Also, be on the lookout for random explosions happening all over the world. Not sure why this happens, but it happens a lot) 

Guns are fun and unique (Crossbow gang for life) . You actually have to go out and unlock a gun which makes playing this game worthit. Are the bases Copy and Paste Ubisoft moment? Yes. What did you expect when you were downloading a tactical military shooter from Ubisoft. I don't care too much about Copy and Paste bases that much, I care about a bunch of enemies in a base that make it a real challenge for my friend and I to get through so we can unlock a new gun and use it. Some of the characters that you capture and deliver to our lord and savior KAREN BOWMAN will actually give you an exclusive gun. It's pretty cool.

Difficulty is weird. So basically you can make the game harder to level up and earn more LOOTBOXES (Among other things). We love lootboxes in this game. You can literally play as KAREN BOWMAN and I find that funny. (Our lord and savior from the Cartel). It's funny because the difficulty means that you just take more damage. Late game, there were many times where a single cartel member (Probably a 22 year old just trying to get by in the world) would murder the both of us in cold blood without a shirt on, equipped with 2 MAC-10s. Late game, if you do decide to keep going up a level, you will NOT be able to go guns blazing into a situation. As I said before, a shirtless man with 2 MAC 10's WILL rush into you with no care for their life at all and WILL kill you and your mates easily.

Buy the game. It has great meme potential and if you have friends, then this game is one of my favorite co-op experiences ever. (Prepare to yell at each other because one of you got spotted out of nowhere and now the entire cartel knows your exact location). Stop listening to the reviews that talk about performance issues with only 4 hours in the game. I didn't experience many performance issues when I played and I have a normie PC. Ubisoft does a great job in allowing you to customize your gaming experience. That is one thing that I think they do really well in every game they release. 

If I were to give this a review though, I'd probably give it 1 Karen Bowman out of 10 shirtless men dual wielding MAC 10's.

Every house has little assets here and there from candles to plates to just random clutter. That takes a long time considering how big the world is. Same with Bolivia. Every Sicario house you walk in looks authentic and believable. Every area you explore makes you feel like you are there. The game mechanics are familiar if you've played other tittles from Ubisoft, but there is a lot here you can play with. From having an up-gradable drone that you can use to pre-spot bases and hideouts and using it to distract enemies. You have a plethora of firepower from handguns to SMGs and LMGs, assault rifles and sniper rifles. Grenades, proximity mines, C4, regular mines, flashbangs and on top of all that, rebels that you can call in for back up, diversion or other tactics. This allows you to approach every fight in the manner that fits your play style. If you get the DLCs you can also get a knife so you can do stealthy take downs. The game is huge, the world is beautiful and very well crafted and the story is decent too. I think Ubisoft should stick to this formula, cause that Frontline battle royale idea they had is absolute garbage and will without a doubt ruin this franchise. I recommend this game, especially now that they are back on Steam and you'll most likely be able to pick it up on sale

I had fun in this game. There were definitely some great moments, and  the co-op is where most of the enjoyment was for me. But, objectively, this game is one of the least polished, most poorly made, and disappointing games I have ever played from a major studio. I am legitimately surprised that Ubisoft let the game go at this state. Well, maybe I shouldn't be.

Ignoring all the intentional decisions, one major issue with the game that you will likely notice is the impressive amount of bugs. I encountered some "minor" issues such as:

- Clipping textures
- Complete dialogue malfunctions (Voice lines playing from wrong character, wrong voice lines playing, same voice line playing multiple times, etc.)
- Needlessly far/oddly inconvenient vehicle spawns 
- Occasional stutters

And more. I can personally overlook bugs like those. What I can't overlook, though, is the absolutely mind-boggling amount of game-breaking bugs, glitches, and issues I encountered in my playthrough. These included:

- Missions disappearing from map
- Enemies detecting and shooting you through solid cover
- AI teammates/NPCs being stupid, (i.e. walking right in front of you while you are shooting)
- Vehicles exploding spontaneously, with no external damage

And many, many more. Unfortunately, my issues with the game don't end with the bugs (that are still not fixed, over 5 years after release). There are also some issues that come from conscious choices made during development, that reflect the lack of effort from Ubisoft to actually put real effort into this game.

The performance that I had playing this game on PC was laughable. Even on the lowest settings, I could only achieve 80-90 FPS maximum (In very rare cases) and in certain environments I would see frame drops down to the low 20s, with the stutters that I mentioned earlier. I had averages from 40-60 FPS, which is very low for my hardware when compared to other, similar games. Although I expected this game to be demanding, I see no reason that this runs so poorly even when compared to other Ubisoft games of similar (or better) visual quality.

The story of GRW I felt was very uninspired and generic. The characters can be forgettable, and the voice acting is HORRIBLE. Seriously. The main character sounds like a 17 year old doing his best "generic military guy" impression, complete with cringe-worthy humor. (If I hear the word "s***balls" come out of his mouth one more time, I think I might go insane)

The gameplay, while fun at times, really suffers from a lack of creativity. While you do technically have "hundreds of hours" of content in the game, it really only consists of hundreds of repetitive, mundane, and generic missions. Some of my least favorite were the stealth missions. You would think that the company responsible for Splinter Cell would have good ones, right? Well, I wholeheartedly believe that this game was just not made for stealth gameplay. Annoying enemy placement, bad AI, and no unique stealth mechanics make most of the stealth sections in this game either barely a challenge, or near impossible when combined with additional requirements like "Do not kill any enemies".

I also have to mention the multiplayer issues I faced. Due to Ubisoft's magnificent networking prowess, you will probably have better luck trying to scam Bill Gates with a phishing email than you will trying to get into a co-op session with your friend(s). We were CONSTANTLY plagued with random network errors every time we booted up the game, and short, 15 minute sessions quickly became 10 minutes of restarting the game and pressing random options, hoping the game would let us join each other. And that is assuming that Ubisoft servers are currently online, which itself is not guaranteed.

I can't end the review without at least a couple positives though. Ubisoft did an amazing job bringing such a large map to life, while still giving each section variety. I also do think that the "mexico cartel leader takedown" game format has a lot of potential and if adapted to be a more linear experience, (Maybe inspiration from Sicario?) could work very well.

Overall, even though I did have fun playing this game, I have to realize that it was probably only because I played the co-op campaign with a close friend. I have to think that if I had purchased this game for solo play only, I would have refunded it very quickly. For this reason, I can't recommend it to most people, especially at the insane normal pricing of $49.99. Get it on sale if you want some co-op fun with friends.

Oh boy where to begin this game could be so much, but it’s just bad, it feels like it was rushed out in almost every aspect. Idea is great and the game is looking fine at first but after playing you will start finding things that are bad or broken in almost every session. Keep in mind that I played on the hardest difficulty, in solo and without HUD.

Ubisoft connect - Yeah like all ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ games this one also needs Uplay to run the game. It’s not that bad but inviting friends or joining their games is a bit tricky and won’t go as fluently as in Steam. Also Ubisoft servers can be a pain in the ass sometimes. 

Graphics - The game looks amazing, nothing to complain about.

Customization - Woah there’s a lot to customize, you can modify a big variety of guns just the way you want, characters have a lot of different gear options, there’s included nice 5.11 gear as well. Most of the items you have to unlock thru playing or by opening “loot boxes”... yeah of course they have included those.

Ballistics - Some of the worst I have ever experienced, seems like devs just rushed the game out. Bullet flying speed is ridiculously slow, from 200m I can clearly see the bullet slowly flying towards the enemy, oh and the bullet drop…. I have no words, from 400m 7.62 drops like it should from 800m. There’s no difference where you hit, with a FAL bullet to the leg kills the bastard, no injuries, nothing. Someone once said that paintball guns have better ballistics than guns in this game.

AI - The AI is straight up stupid in this game. Some enemies don’t see dead bodies lying in front of them (oh and the bodies disappear for some reason), there are moments when snipers can’t spot you from their towers but a car which is passing by will spot you easily (have you ever tried to spot something from a moving car?), sometimes bandits get stuck and run on the same place. Oh and I killed a guy who was on a rooftop, noone heard anything but a guy who was sitting in a van which was parked by the building heard the shot and alerted the others, wtf he couldn’t even see to the rooftop. AI pretty much has wallhack and has accuracy levels beyond understanding. 

Story - nothing special, keeps you hooked up at first and little video briefings you get are nice. Missions on the other hand will get very repetitive very fast, go and interrogate that guy, kill those guys over there, steal that vehicle and so on. 

Environment - Bolivia looks very good and feels alive, streets have lots of locals, there are a big variety of cars driving around, choppers flying, even some planes, countryside is nice and the radio is good. It would be nice to have some wild animals not only animals in farms, no dogs or cats tho, all the villages should have dogs. 

Driving - First of all the map is so big that the only good option for travel is helicopter. Car, plane and helicopter controls are good, every vehicle feels a bit different and it seems that there was a lot of work done. Motorcycles on the other hand are a big mess, yeah they drive just fine but sometimes even from a small speed you can end up flying to death if you hit an obstacle but sometimes from a much greater speed I can ram buildings and nothing happens. Just avoid motorcycles otherwise you can end up dying from a little mistake.

Glitches - yeah there are a lot, some of my missions have glitched, sometimes when the enemy is behind the cover then bullets will fly thru their heads not harming them, I have fell thru the mountain, got stuck in rocks so the only option to escape was to blow myself up and so on.

TL;DR Rushed out game, if you are looking for realism keep far away from this crap, buy only if it’s on sale.
