This game is literally the quality of a pre-early-access title, but it's 5 years after launch. Every single system clashes with every other system. I'm 11 levels into the prestige system and I've been playing on the hardest difficulty with 1-3 other friends, so I've played a decent amount of solo and co-op at a 50-50 ratio almost.

I run the 50 cal sniper rifle from the fallen ghosts dlc, mk249 lmg, and a m1911 pistol, just so you have an idea of the playstyle I was using.

There is a huge focus on sniping but there is no consistency with what objects are penetrable with bullets. Some times I can shoot through a concrete wall of a bunker, but other times, the bullet will be totally stopped by something like a 1cm piece of rebar sticking out of a broken building or a sheet of tin you would find on a shack roof, maybe 3-4mm thick, totally stopping a .50BMG round... If the enemies just double-layered their wife beaters, they would be bulletproof.

Bullet travel time and drop are *insanely* bad. Bullets travel at like 100mph or 75 if you're using a silencer, even the highest-powered sniper rifles have massive bullet drop that comes out of nowhere at about 175m. Taking a shot over 250m is like watching a Bullet Bill chase you in Super Mario. Imagine a sniping game, but you cringe *every time* you take a shot that actually requires a sniper rifle's range.

IRL, the M82 has an effective range of 1,800 meters. You literally could not shoot half that in this game if you tried. The IRL muzzle velocity of the M82 is about 850m/s but in this game I find myself having to lead slow-walking, not alerted targets by about a foot at 100m away.

My longest headshot is over 400m, you have to aim like halfway down the range finder on the crosshairs and the bullet travel time is around 3.5 seconds, so this gun is actually shooting bullets at around 12% of its real muzzle velocity. If you snipe at someone over 50m who has detected you, they will duck to the side and dodge the shot like Neo in The Matrix. It's pathetic.

The enemies all wear white or black clothing, which would be great except the entire main color palette of the game is earthy neutrals, so I find myself entering a base and getting shot by some guy wearing all white standing up against a white concrete wall, or a guy wearing all black laying on a black military cot. I mean seriously, white is the lamest bad-guy color ever and this is a videogame, not a movie. It's just bad game design. 

The AI is absolutely god awful. I have like 850 games on steam/others, GRW has *the worst enemy AI I have ever seen in a game*. Half the time they know exactly where you are because some guy on the other side of the base heard a round ricochet and yelled "OMG" in Spanish, other times you'll kill 5 out of 6 people standing in a circle talking to each other and the 6th guy won't even react. 

Sometimes all the AI bum rush you in a horde, but usually they will trickle in 1-by-1. There's a particularly obnoxious behavior that commonly happens, where an enemy will detect you and just hide in cover no matter what, as all his allies are massacred, then when you start walking around the area, they will pop up already aiming at you and you had better hope you already got whatever unlock was in the base because you're about to be respawning.

The reinforcements can spawn anywhere you aren't currently looking at, so you can clear a base except for 1 guy and then turn around to face the base entrance and a car with 4 LMG troops will pop in behind you and instakill you. Another loading screen.

The loading screens are like "Witcher 3 on Xbox at initial release" levels of bad, my SSD is better than an Xbox Series X SSD and the load times can be 5+ minutes some times, no I am not kidding.

Multiple times I have been in a story mission that failed for some reason or another and then after a 5 min respawn, I load into the game and it instantly fails the mission for me again? Had a friend get stuck in that loop 10+ times last night so he just had to quit the game via Task Manager.

I have had *multiple* hostage extractions fail because the target I am carrying straight up disappears from the game right out of my character's hands and it tells me "target lost". Other times where the "do not kill the VIP" target will suddenly change (icon goes from gold to red) and they become a normal enemy who is shooting me. I had it happen once while the guy was inside my car with me mid conversation.

The enemies also from what I can tell from playing at 100% volume make *0 movement noises whatsoever*. Unless an enemy is yelling something, they are totally silent and you have to hope you have them spotted on your drone. #1 cause of death for me is definitely an enemy that I haven't spotted silently sprints up to me and fries me with dual skorpions.

I have been killed multiple times by the "friendly" rebels running up behind me and shooting through me at an enemy. The military AI faction is supposed to fight the cartel AI faction when they meet, but oftentimes I find them just grouping up and hunting me as a team.

The voice acting is terrible. The dialog is terrible and cringy, but the actual way the voice actors say the words is just... Bad. Like they were amateurs who were just doing their "regular voice", which IMO sounds like a cattle rancher who just moved to the city and is mildly dampening her accent because she's afraid the "city slickers" will judge her (for the female operator) or a FOX news stereotype of a hipster in San Francisco ordering a coffee (for the guys). Really, the only VA in this game that isn't so bad it seems like it was on purpose was Jon Bernthal's character.

There is a massive desync issue in co-op, some times I will find my teammates telling me they're standing next to me, but in the game, they are 1+KM away from me. Some times players will get downed and TP across the map, sometimes when you revive a teammate they revive kilometers away. 

The vehicles are the same, some times one of my squadmates will share their screen and a boat or a car is just bouncing all over the world on their game, even though for everyone else it isn't moving. The spazzed out vehicle can still kill the other teammates by smashing into them, they will just instantly go down with no hitmarker, this happens multiple times every single co-op play session I have had. Boats flying out of the water and smashing into your heli sounds funny but if you can't even see the bug, it's immediate cancer.

The gunplay isn't great either, all the automatics seem the same with just slightly different recoil. Semis all seem the same except for whatever their minimum fire rate is changes a bit per gun.

The vehicle AI is god awful as well, you can cheese any "stop the target from escaping" type of objective by just parking a car sideways in the road in front of a base, the enemy will floor their car and smash into it, causing theirs to catch on fire so they bail... And get another car, to drive it straight into the bonfire/pile up they just created. Earlier today I had an NPC do this with over 10 cars in a row, he ran out of cars parked nearby and started *carjacking the civilians, and then crashing their cars too*.

Oh yeah, the store works with minimal errors, though. Almost makes this game seem like a flaming dumpster fire of a cash grab.

I could keep making this list longer but the game is so bad it's already not been worth my time to type this much out, please avoid this game. I only took the time to write this much so people will realize I'm serious and not just raging out. Save your money, save your time, save your rage.

Ghost Recon Breakpoint Skipping Steam For Epic Store

Ghost Recon Breakpoint is to skip Steam in favor of an Epic Games Store-exclusive release, publisher Ubisoft says. The game will also come to Ubisoft's proprietary Uplay store, but will otherwise not be available digitally from alternative sources on PC.

The company confirmed the news to PCGamesN, but did not give a reason why it had decided to withhold Breakpoint from a Steam launch. Ubisoft's two most recent games, Anno 1800 and The Division 2, have also skipped Steam in favor of the Epic Store. GameSpot has contacted Ubisoft to ask why the company has made this decision.

A possible explanation is that Epic takes a much smaller share of revenue than Valve does on Steam, making the former an attractive proposition for developers and publishers. On the other hand, Steam has a significant install base and has been around for much longer, meaning it possesses features the Epic Store does not, including cloud saves, achievements, and more.

Other big games, such as Metro: Exodus and Detroit: Become Human, have also skipped Steam, as Epic continues its drive to secure exclusives. Epic has stated it will change its policy of chasing exclusives if Valve reduces the cut it takes from game sales on Steam

Ghost Recon Breakpoint was revealed just recently and will launch on October 4 for PS4, Xbox One, and PC. For more, check out our hands-on impressions and thoughts on why Ghost Recon Breakpoint is both promising and concerning.

Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands is a third-person tactical shooter video game developed by Ubisoft Paris in collaboration with Ubisoft Bucharest, Ubisoft Reflections, Ubisoft Montpellier, Ubisoft Annecy, Ubisoft Milan and Ubisoft Belgrade, and published by Ubisoft. It was released worldwide on March 7, 2017, for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 4 and Xbox One, as the tenth installment in the Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon franchise and is the first game in the Ghost Recon series to feature an open world environment.

The game moves away from the futuristic setting introduced in Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Advanced Warfighter[b] and instead features a setting similar to the original Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon. Ubisoft described it as one of the biggest open world games that they have published, with the game world including a wide variety of environments such as mountains, forests, deserts, and salt flats.

Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands received generally mixed to positive reviews from critics. A sequel, Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Breakpoint, was released on October 4, 2019.

The major issue with Wildlands is that it isn't a stealth shooter. Don't get me wrong, it has stealth shooter sections, and those are by far the best parts of the game, but that is fundamentally not how the developers intend for you to play.

There are simply too many story missions where you go in with stealth, and the game forcefully reveals you. Then you're shooting everything that moves, while every enemy is taking potshots at you from behind cover.

Often times when you die, you have to redo the first bit of a mission, then fly a helicopter in a straight line for 5 minutes to get back to the part you died at. I'm not sure if travelling long distances is supposed to build suspense, but it doesn't, it causes me to literally watch movies while holding a key down on my keyboard.

Then Unidad spawns infinite enemies because you had the gall to stand beside the road and change your gear, or check the map. This behavior should at least be restrained to villages, because with the amount of map traversal required I'm not going to be hiding in a bush every time someone drives by.

Not to mention, there are way too many escort and extraction missions.

All in all it is impossible for me to recommend this game. Go play Rainbow Six Vegas 2 if you want a good shoot-em-up game. If you like stealth, try Hitman. I used to recommend Ghost Recon Advanced Warfighter 2, but good luck getting that game to run on a modern PC. Or maybe just heavily mod Fallout 4 until it plays like a Ghost Recon game.

EDIT: Also, the ending is bugged. If you 100% the game, it will give you the bad ending and say something along the lines of "Congratulation, you've completed 100% of the game. Now complete 100% of the game for a different ending". Apparently the developers assumed no one would be stupid enough to 100% the game the first time around. You can replay the mission to get the correct ending, but that at point you might as well just watch the ending on youtube and save your time.

Wildlands looks beautiful with its stunning graphics and its huge open world. It provides the impression to be deep and realistic, when in fact it's rather shallow in both gameplay and lore. 

You are an elite soldier in a foreign country and your job is to either kill the bad guys or steal their stuff because... well, they are the bad guys who must be stopped. No need for diplomacy, no need for asking any more questions. 

Tactical combat play is solid, some nice features here like the drone exploration. Combine that with generic story, generic quests, generic characters, generic dialogues and a highly detailed world, which would have been a great opportunity to learn something about not so far Bolivia, its people, its culture on the fly, but no. Detailed environments are just non-interactive scenery for the "ultimate military shooter experience". And shooting, sneaking, driving, flying you can, "total freedom" they say and even physical limits are not unviolable. 

In sum though, at least for me, that's not enough to make for a remarkable game. Wildlands is not really bad when played with friends. But it's not good either. It's missing teeth, cleverness, empathy and charisma and while my mates are liking it, personally I've expected more.

[b]DISCLAIMER: THIS REVIEW DOES NOT EVALUATE MULTIPLAYER MODE DUE TO LOW PLAYER POPULATION.[/b]

[h1]Story[/h1]
Set in 2019, GRW sets itself in Bolivia after an incredibly powerful Mexican drug cartel has moved into the country.  Known as Santa Blanca, the cartel has systematically integrated itself so deeply into the nation that major sections of the government actively look the other way in the face of its operation for fear of the consequences; while others have made deals with or are under complete control of SB.  Players take control of one of four Ghosts, an elite squad of US military operators.  After a US undercover agent was killed and the embassy in Bolivia bombed, the Ghosts have been smuggled into the country to assist a rebel faction with the process of dismantling SB piece by piece.  Coordinated by a CIA agent named Karen Bowman, the story is delivered mostly in the form of video files that Karen uploads to give brief rundowns on each of the targets the Ghosts will go after as they work their way up the SB chain of command.  Defeating major SB players will also reveal video files from the boss of the organization.  At the head of Santa Blanca is a massive and imposing man named El Sueño, and his video files will reveal some of the inner turmoil the cartel faces with each hit the Ghosts make.  While the boss seems like he has the makings of an interesting and strange antagonist, he's never really explored as a character.  Unfortunately there's really not much interesting story telling here in general.  The Ghosts themselves are dry and uninteresting even when they banter and you'll be challenged to put a name to their faces.  The cartel bosses rarely stand out as anything more than first drafts and you'll never really see them as people but rather as just cardboard cutouts that a personality has been imposed onto.  And Bowman is by far the most obnoxious creature in the entire game; constantly swearing or saying edgy things as if she's a high schooler whose parents aren't around and she can finally say bad words for the first time.  It's a genuine shame too.  The ending even makes a valid attempt at some legitimate drama but it falls flat in the face of just how bland the entire game is before it.
The Ghost Recon also includes two side stories:
The first, Narco Road, is complete tonal whiplash.  Taking control of an unnamed Ghost working undercover for SB's smuggling operations with the intent of finding and taking down one of their top men by working jobs and gaining trust.  Where the main game was at least attempting to take its subject matter seriously, portraying the vile way that the cartel treats the people of Bolivia; NR plays out like some sort of wacky and goofy cartel fantasy where silly dudes drive fast monster trucks and say silly cartoony things.  This is especially jarring since it seemingly takes place just before or perhaps even during the main story AND it takes place in the same regions.  The villains aren't particularly interesting and their over the top nature often comes off as more annoying than funny; though two of their deaths were incredibly entertaining in the moment.  Much like the main game, the ending suddenly attempts to up the dramatic stakes out of nowhere and to no real effect.
Fallen Ghosts is the second story and takes place months after the main story.  The Ghosts are reinserted into Bolivia to extract US operatives in the wake of their identities being revealed and a well equipped mercenary group being sent after them.  Tonal whiplash sets in again where this time the villains are SO brutally vile that it often feels like you'll see more dead civilians than any given village could ever house; inside of a single building.  And these scenes litter the entire map.  There's not much story here.  Kill the bad guys and get out of Bolivia.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Wildlands is a third person shooter set in a massive open world environment with elements of stealth and very basic squad command.  Up to four players can cooperatively play the game as well.  The Ghosts have a massive variety of firearms and gadgets though frankly a basic assault rifle will get every single job done; even destroying helicopters and armored cars with ease.  A small drone can be used for scouting outposts before you attack and a Sync Shot mode allows your squad to drop multiple enemies at once.  The world is absolutely littered in supplies, weapons, parts, skill points, and other items but none of them are really necessary.  Skill points and supplies can be spent on improving the Ghosts' abilities though very few of these upgrades feel like actual game changers.  Every mission is basically the same form of going to a place and either killing/capturing someone or destroying/capturing something.  Sometimes you'll defend a position or be forced to follow someone around.  Sometimes you have to complete one of these tasks without raising the alarm.  To be frank, the gameplay in Wildlands is incredibly shallow.  Stealth is laughably easy as enemies won't even notice your loudly buzzing helicopter when it's less than a hundred meters away and even if you do get caught, combat is incredibly simple cover shooting against enemies who aren't particularly bright and whose positions are always revealed to you on the minimap.  You can also call for support from the rebel faction in the form of things like attack troops, mortar strikes, or requesting vehicles; though the vehicles are often dropped off so far away you'll wonder why you didn't just walk in the first place.  The game is also filled with all sorts of annoying quirks like bullet proof chain link fences and vehicle explosions affecting things half a block away despite the fireball barely being much bigger than the vehicle itself.
Narco Road doesn't do much to change any of this, merely putting an emphasis on the game's less than great vehicle handling.  Fallen Ghosts introduces some new enemy types like armored gunners and invisible snipers that really feel like they should have been in the main story to begin with as there are more types of enemy vehicles than there are enemy soldiers.  Both DLC's are rather lazy as both simply take place in truncated areas of the main game's map.
The game also includes a sort of horde mode called Guerilla, in case you really feel like you need even more generic area defense in your life.

[h1]Presentation[/h1]
If there's one thing Wildlands can be proud of, it's the overwhelming natural beauty of its fictionalized Bolivia.  From the massive snowy slopes of the mountains to the dense swampy jungles and flamingo swarmed lakes; GRW's environments are wonderfully rendered.  Vegetation is dense, detailed, and stretches off into the distance for miles in all directions and even reacts to overhead helicopters.  Mud is thick, reflectively wet, and smears across your character's belly when you crawl through it.  The lighting is fantastic if a bit buggy when underground but be it day or night, the world delivers on visual wonder rarely seen.  Ironically the world is so excellently rendered that everything else pales by comparison. Vehicles, characters, and structures don't look like the same standard of visual quality as the world they inhabit.  Animation is especially wooden although serviceable, but the lip sync in cutscenes is downright terrible.  The music isn't especially interesting but sometimes the gentle strings during quiet moments can add an extra layer to how serene the world is.

Ghost Recon Wildlands is a sprawling open-world tactical shooter that delivers an adrenaline-fueled experience set in the heart of a fictionalized Bolivia overrun by a powerful drug cartel. As a member of the elite Ghost Recon team, players are tasked with dismantling the cartel piece by piece, using any means necessary.

One of the game's standout features is its massive open world, which is beautifully realized and teeming with life. From dense jungles to barren deserts, each region feels distinct and offers a unique set of challenges. The sheer scale of the world is awe-inspiring, and players are free to explore it however they see fit.

The gameplay in Ghost Recon Wildlands is where the game truly shines. Whether playing solo or with friends in cooperative multiplayer, the tactical gunplay and strategic planning are incredibly satisfying. From carefully coordinating synchronized shots to executing daring helicopter assaults, the game offers a wide range of approaches to completing objectives.

Visually, Ghost Recon Wildlands is stunning, with breathtaking landscapes and realistic character models that bring the world to life. Whether you're traversing the rugged mountains or navigating the bustling streets of a cartel-controlled town, the game's attention to detail is impressive.

Overall, Ghost Recon Wildlands is a triumph of open-world gaming, offering a thrilling mix of action, exploration, and tactical gameplay. With its vast open world, deep customization options, and engaging cooperative multiplayer, it's a must-play for fans of the genre.

Wildlands is not like the earlier Ghost Recon games I played.  It’s more arcadey.  But that’s a good thing.  The original Ghost Recon was brutal with it’s difficulty.  Advanced Warfighter had a terrible checkpoint system.  Wildlands is just pure fun.  And you can ramp up the difficulty if you want it more challenging.  The gunplay is very well designed.  The map and environment is incredibly varied.  Vehicles are extremely fun to drive.

Story wise there is nothing special about the game.  But that’s a good thing.  Special Forces aren’t like Jack Bauer in 24 stopping nukes.  Most of the time they are Quiet Professionals doing something on the other side of the world to protect their country.  This story shows the Ghosts doing unappreciated but extremely dangerous work.  The local politics at play that the US interferes in with questionable motives.

The DLC is nice but not required.  Base weaponry is just as good as the downloadable guns.

Multiplayer is a blast.  Drop in coop.  Play with friends, achieve difficulty mission goals.  Or just mess around causing chaos for fun.  Solo missions are just as fun because your friendly AI is actually useful.

GRW is a solid, if not repetitive tactical shooter. The story content is relatively minimal, but it takes place in an alternate Bolivia, under the thumb of the ruthless Santa Blanca drug cartel, and your role as Nomad, leader of the Ghosts, is to dismantle the cartel one leader at a time. The cartel targets are pretty well thought out, with each one having their own purpose and personality, but other than that what little there is of the plot really just exists to contextualise the gameplay. Speaking of, the core mechanics are pretty great - you're given a selection of tools that allow you to plan and execute the various missions (mostly revolving around clearing out enemies from a location to access an objective), and the further you go into the game the more customisation options are available to you, both on the in-depth visual level and the far-reaching gameplay options you have to work with. By the end, the progression structure does feel very tired, due to its rigid "go here, do enough missions, take out the target" formula, to the point where the last few regions I had left on the map started to feel like a chore, especially due to the game's length. In terms of design, the game is nothing special - the world is good looking, but outside of a few small areas it all feels a little monolithic, and there isn't much to be said of a memorable soundtrack or visual style. Not a terrible game by any means, and the core gameplay is really great, but there just isn't much to it beyond that. Good for playing a little bit of at a time, and probably best with friends.

Ghost Recon Wildlands is one of the best coop shooter experiences I have ever had. The open world of a fictionalized Bolivia with psuedo realistic ballistics and near seamless drop-in-drop-out coop has been a staple of my gaming group's gameplay since we started online gaming together back in 2017. The collectibles are fun, the story is engaging (if disjointed) and the characters are interesting (even if they're not all voice acted very well). Customization depth ensures that all of our characters looked pretty different. It also has a perma-death mode with separate files, allowing for very harrowing moments. 

So why can't I recommend the game? Unfortunately, Ubisoft has either downgraded server support or the aging system is starting to break under the stress. Connecting online is a gamble, and frequently it just doesn't. Even using suggested tricks works perhaps one in five times, and my friends have had to give up and move on to something else, like Grand Theft Auto, Vermintide 2, or Second Extinction. Additionally, when we do actually get the game working, desync issues are constant and missions have broke simply because the players are locked in two separate states of the same mission.

According to a recent statement from Ubisoft, they are going to discontinue supporting old games that require online support. While Wildlands wasn't specifically listed as a game where the plug is being pulled, its clear they have no intention of fixing the severe server issues. It's functional if you play it single player, but do NOT buy this game for its online functionality. It will not work with any kind of reliability.

Purchase at your own risk.

In my humble opinion, Ghost Recon Wildlands is less Ghost Recon and more The Division. In my perspective, that is not so much a bad thing, that said though I miss the old Ghost Recon style. You can play Wildlands much more tactically like a Ghost Recon game, or you can go guns blazing, and even that creates some goofy and entertaining fun. The problem for me, I think, is the repetitive gameplay. There is so much to do. The map is littered with side missions like getting intel, supplies, rescuing rebels, etc. It just all feels the same. Sure, technically, all games are repetitive, especially in shooters like this. There just isn't much to grab onto. I could care less about my character or any other character for that matter which makes it hard for me to justify doing every mission. There is just a disconnect there. The game shines the most when playing with friends and NOT the AI buddies. We were able to get into some wacky situations. We also were able to coordinate tactical strikes and finish missions without being seen at all. We were ghosts, so to speak. :) In that sense, it gives you a feeling of accomplishment. The sync shots are really cool. This is when you have maybe 3 or 4 enemies standing around next to each other or far apart and call your shots. Maybe one friend gets one enemy, another friend gets another enemy, and so on and so forth. You all fire at the same time, and the enemies drop without alerting anyone nearby. I found, though, that going in guns blazing was much more fun for me, and the best part is the game doesn't feel like it's punishing you for doing it that way, mostly because of how well the game plays. Just for context's sake, I liked The Division way more. It kinda seems like, (with my friends anyway) that if you hated The Division you might really like Wildlands and if you loved The Division, you may not like Wildlands. Either way, I would probably wait on this one. At least until the price drops a little bit, or you can find a used .

This can be done silently or you can just go loud on yourself. There are huge selection of weapon available to you and offer different parameters of customization and usability. Player Character customization is also excellent and You tweak a look of charactor upto your satisfaction, given that you will be seeing the character right though it, from behind all the time and dont want a Eye sore. The Drone also makes tagging and enalyzing enemies and location easy and is fun to control. 

Game offers good number of Upgrades and Unlocks which makes the gameplay progressively immersive. Side quest gives various ingame resources which can be used to buy new upgrades and unlocks. Resources can also be collected manually and is spread thoughout whole game level. At some places this are slightly tricky to find but you can still find them.  

Obtaining almost all Upgrades and Unlock gives a good sance of achievement, given that this require a lot of side mission complition, which regulary spawn in game level. There are choices to use various types of vehicles to explore such huge openworld which You can also steel on roads. you might need help of such vehicles to defog the ingame map to get a sense of exploration.

The quests in the game involves completing verious objectives like eliminating a target, Item delievries and detroying stretagic entities. The game has Huge Quest Tree with various character associated with it and it unlockes progressively. A certain Goon must be eliminated before being able to obtain new quest objectives. A quest can be collected just by visting a area and activating a keypoint or by finding and talking some individuals.    

Graphics:

Graphics in this game is amazing. The Detailed Textures on Terrain, Road, Trees as well as many items adds to realism. It is not hidden that game uses huge graphic memory in gigabytes to depict such openworld detail. Terrain features realistic muddy surfaces on non highway roads. water patches on such areas feature realistic looking reflections. Regions outside cities feature good looking trees and leaves. You can notice shinnines on vegitation as well as wet ground. Lighting in the game is great and makes the details on object and surfaces relistice as the dents, cracks with wear and tear are distinguishable. Tessellation also adds to realism on surfaces with debris and stones. It is noticable when you go near to such areas of level. Farm and vegitation areas of game world contains beautiful weavy grass blades and foliage.
Areas containing water bodies and channels shows realistic water with good reflection, refraction and Foam.  

Draw distane is also amazing and you can view very far when on helicopters and planes, Almost full distant level is visible. Wheather system is also slightly integrated to game world and allows Rains, wet roads etc. 

Road network in the game level is most beautiful. These road offer great scening view on certain part of level when they run down the hill in a curvy pattern, adding to grand sense of atmosphere when viewed form a scenic view point. Almost all of the map is well connected with road network of various types, be it highways or Gravel road. Fun to drive vehicle into. 

Physics:

Vehicle physics in the game is good and vehicles handles realisticly. Vehicle loose certain of thier characteristic when damaged and good amount of smoke and effects does comes out. Explosion occures when a vehicle lost all of its health. 

Animation:

Character animation in the game is very realistic and movement does look life like and not fake. Enemies also stands, walks and run in a ways that doesnt break the immersion as if certain unrealistic thing has happened. Certainly no entity in game looks stupid and out of place. 

Sound:

Sound tracks featured is definately immersive. The weapons sounds great with all of fires and reloads. The music which is played on Driving a vehicles adds quality to experience. But most of the time we will hear Engine sounds and impacts of bad road conditons on vehicles. however the road vehicle engine sounds is not that great and feels very generic. It is just enough to hear that a vehicle is being driven. 

Enemies:

These entities in game is not so intelligent and almost looks clueless. They will surely search you when alarmed but even then they are easy to avoid. Their Aim on You however is quite accurate when exposed and it makes difficult some times to complete a level in one try because you die alot if not playing carefully. Headshots are always an answer for instant enemy elimination. They comes in groups and can hide behind a object to give you a challenge to seek them and kill. Fights in Vehicles on roads with them is also enaging and is integral part of various quests.

Story:

Honestly i was skipping all cutscenes and dialogs and was actually more involed in compliting a level. Still game has cutscenes that are dramatic and integrates with gameplay actions. Much of story is concerned with locating a boss of the boss and collecting clues by completing a mission.

This isn't necessarily a bad game, but it's a bad stealth game. Let me explain why:

The Hunted system is absolutely broken. The status of getting "Hunted" occurs once the enemies are aware of your presence, and once you're being "Hunted" then every single enemy within' the vicinity will begin heat seek to your exact position. This sounds fairly reasonable if you've been spotted by an enemy for a bit and they've seen where you've been and they're just checking that general area, but this can also occur when:

- A random faction war begins that you have absolutely no control over.
- A dead body is found, which become anchored to the ground and you cannot move (which should be expected for a stealth game made as recently as 2017).
- An explosion goes off, even if it went off miles away from your position and there should be no way enemies know where you are.
- An opposing faction spots you and suddenly all information from one faction is also magically transferred to the other even though they are opposing factions.
- A shot is heard (which makes sense obviously but this applies to suppressors too. The game gives no information regarding how the sound is traveling or how far away you need to be in order to not be heard. All they give is some arbitrary "Noise Reduction" bar that gives little to no useful information). This is also painfully inconsistent because sometimes you can shoot someone near someone else at point blank range and nobody will hear it and vice versa.

This doesn't necessarily seem that bad on paper but it becomes extremely annoying when every time something insignificant happens that shouldn't reveal your exact position occurs and suddenly every single enemy within' a 1 mile radius suddenly knows your exact position. And then you get sniped by some jackass dual wielding MAC-11s because enemies have perfect accuracy no matter what weapon they're using and no matter what range they're engaging you at. 

The missions are also indescribably dull and feel like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ chore to do. If I had to sum this game up it's just Third person Farcry 3. It doesn't try anything new or ground breaking, just the same old copy paste open world ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. If you're into that then this game is right up your alley, but I will not be returning to this game anytime soon... or at all for that matter.

One last thing. If you plan on getting this game with the intention of playing this with your friends... well all I can say is have fun getting disconnected every 5 minutes because the Ubisoft servers suck monkey tits.

Sometimes the in-game lobby (L menu) doesn't show any friends online. Sometimes it does. Sometimes the SHIFT-F2 Ubisoft overlay lets you see and invite friends. Sometimes it doesn't. The external Ubisoft Connect app almost always shows friends online, but good luck trying to invite/join from there. Often, when a player sends an invite the recipient never actually receives it, or only receives it after restarting the game. Once in a blue moon, everything works like you would expect, but that is a rare occurrence. The Ubisoft multiplayer networking functionality is wildly inconsistent, frustrating to work with, and cripples what could be a spectacular gaming experience.

So I've put in a lot of hours into this game. For the most part (85-90%) I've enjoyed it. It's a fun shooter/driver game with stealth elements that are USUALLY pulled off pretty well.

HOWEVER: There are some ... issues I've come across that lead me to believe that QC was not as thorough as it should have been, or that whoever was in charge didn't adequately explain that the game should not have 1995 hit boxes.

Issue: Hit boxes are TOO BIG. I stood on the road, in the opposing lane, with a convoy headed toward me and I sniped the driver of the convoy truck. The convoy stops, and I start lining up my next shot. A civilian vehicle passes me as I take my next shot and the vehicle blows up immediately. The vehicle was a good yard or to my side and ahead of me, I had very clear line of sight to my target, but the game blows up the civvy truck instead.

I go to take another shot over the hood of the truck i'm hiding behind, I again have a clear line of sight, and I shoot, and the truck in front of me takes the bullet and starts smoking immediately. WTF?!

In another scenario, I'm shooting up a hill. I can see the head of the enemy peaking over the hill, in line of sight. I aim and shoot, and the ground collision layer takes the bullet, The ground collision layer ends up being a protective barrier to the enemy for some stupid reason. Maybe they programmed the hill to do gravitational lensing on opponent heads, IDK.

In another scenario, I'm shooting at enemies across a field. I have clear line of sight, a rebel ally walks near me and stops a good yard or so away and a little in front of me (like...diagonally next to me) and I shoot, and somehow the rebel takes the bullet instead of the enemy. WTF?! 

Collision in this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥. They really need to not have hit boxes so big, and to fix their collision issues.

The BIGGEST ISSUE though I have is that...

At some point you unlock [spoiler] Optical Camo [/spoiler] and I thought, "Great! This will help me sneak better." Because it should be bloody obvious that this 'item/effect' would help with sneaking. BUT NO! It has NO effect in game other than visual. I've had enemies see me from 200 or so yards, on a mountainside, in tree cover and thick bushes. They know IMMEDIATELY where I am EXACTLY even tho I'm using a suppressed weapon, am far away, and my clothing is camouflaged to the environment despite the thing I got above.

I've also had helicopters ID me from distances and angles where I should be essentially invisible.

I understand that they want to make the game difficult, i get that... BUT When it comes at the cost of realism, that's when I have an issue. /sigh

Apart from these...issues... I've had fun playing the game. I DO Recommend it, in spite of it's annoying and frustrating issues. The landscape is Gorgeous and crazy well done, the stories and missions are okay, the gunplay is good, fighting is good. But it certainly has it's annoyances that will make you quit for a day or so when you get fed up with them. But the game has nice little details that help make the world feel more immersive, it's just too bad they skimped on the things that actually effect the game.

Wildlands is in a weird spot for me when it comes to recommending it or not. To sum it up right away, I would get it on sale and not spend anything over $30 for it.

Whenever I play a new Tom Clancy's game, I feel like I am almost obligated to compare it directly to the other games in the franchise, which I feel most others do as well. While this game has more open world exploration and story mode aspects, I would still choose The Division series over it. However - I do think this game does have elements that make it enjoyable. 

I am a big fan when it comes to customization, especially in an open game like this. I do think Wildlands does a good job of giving the player a wide variety of ways to make their character unique, but I do really wish you could edit the voice and other things cause I cant stand the voices in this game. I do also think the gun play and variety there is good, but the constant running around to different sections for certain gun pieces that only go on certain guns gets really old really fast. I would rather it have been rewards for actual story missions, since this map and overall game is quite large. I was not a fan of going of course so often. It also irritates me that every gun practically sounds the. For a game so centered around gun play and customization - I just wish they put more time into the sound design. 

One of the absolute worst aspects of this game is the driving controls. Every damn car I have driven in this game feels like the tires are constantly on ice. I really just don't get it, the thing slides around like crazy and is so hard to actually control in a realistic way. This may seem like a small issue, but when you are driving around this massive map all the time, it gets super annoying and I hate how bad it is. 

Another big issue for me is the story itself. While I like the idea of taking down all these region heads, it gets so repetitive and all you are doing is going to a new part of the map and doing the same thing you just did in the previous one. There is no sort of game-play changes or even an effort to make things fresh and new. I know its not easy to do in a more linear game like this, but it did not have to be much, just anything new would of been great. 

I eventually gave up on the story since it got so bad, and found the most fun out of making the game as realistic as possible for myself. I would set the time of day to night, turn off the HUD/map, and any indicators, and turn on night vision and go slow and steady. That's where this game exceeds for me, and the lack of this mechanic in the overall game is sad. 

I do think the game has some nice pros to it, but the cons are also right there. If you can get it for cheap, give it a go and try some of the things I mentioned, but I would not pay full price for this game.

Although repetitive, the game is pretty good. The entire game is basically shooting at bad guys but it's pretty well done considering I'm not tired of it 40 hours in. There are multiple ways to do missions in this game including stealth, which is sometimes mandatory. The stealth isn't as fleshed-out as in games like Hitman or Dishonored, and I'm pretty sure guards don't even spot out dead bodies. The game can still be challenging though. You can't run in guns blazing, because you WILL die pretty quickly. You have to use your brain, especially after you've tiered up.

Bolivia is stunning and varied. From swampy areas like Caimanes to the salt flats of Koani and canyons of Media Luna this game has a lot of biomes, all of which are awesome, though some can be annoying to traverse. Despite all of this, the world can feel very empty. There are maybe 4 or 5 towns/cities in the game, and most of the time when you're roaming you will be seeing bad guy bases or small villages.

Weapons and gunplay are pretty good. While playing on normal difficulty I felt like every weapon was viable, even if some are better than others. I assume that once you reach the tiers you will have to start using the meta weaponry. Also, they all one-shot in stealth, including pistols.

HOWEVER:

The game is still repetitive. If you're not a fan of doing the same things over and over this game is a hard pass. Especially solo.
Talking about solo, the servers are broken and it's hard to play with friends without getting disconnected (if you even connect to the servers).
The AI can be sucky. If one guy spots you the entire base will be hunting for you.
There are microtransactions which include weapons, however since it's PvE it's not too bothersome.

And last but not least, Ubisoft are just a terrible studio. Soon enough this will be the next game to have its online services "closed", which most likely means you will not be able to play co-op or play the two DLCs: Fallen Ghosts and Narco Road.

With all that in mind, this is still a good game which is unfortunately being crippled by the company behind it. Buy it on sale when it's at around 10 to 15 Euro if none of the issues above concern you.

EDIT: Also the game runs like ass. 60-70fps on medium preset with a ryzen 3600 + RX 5700 XT is unacceptable.

You may have heard some mediocre reviews from gaming publications which may have cautioned you from purchasing Ghost Recon: Wildlands. However, the game while it has it's flaws is tons of fun and well over 100+ hours worth of content, granted the same types of side missions repetitive sides missions fill much of that content but I personally don't mind and find it engaging. 

First there is nothing wrong with the AI teammates, the enemy AI can be oblivious to a fault, depending on the difficulty but again I found it more enjoyable with the fact that they are just smart enough to make it fun to play. secondly the game is generally well polished as with most Ubisoft games with some minor bugs where I got, on a rare occasion, stuck between some rocks on a cliff, train and a platform and other environmental objects which are mostly my only real complaint. 

The weapon parts, new medals, skill points, resources, rebel support ops and new guns are a good incentive to explore the map but I do feel that, like with other Ubisoft games, less "farming" for XP type of game play to unlock skills would have been nice. 
It adds filler to the game that doesn't do much for the already content filled game. 

which leads me to my next point...
It does suffer from the "Ubisoft formula" where there is little distinction between their titles, a problem that so many of their games suffer from. However, this formula is engaging fun and I don't see any other companies with the same quality consistency with the same level of polish so I don't have much to complain about as of now. 

The game to date is best Ghost Recon I've personally played aside from Future soldier which was better in terms of story, granted it does feel like a third person shooter rehash of Far Cry and the side mission can be repetitive but I find it enjoyable and fun and didn't mind it too much. 
It plays and works well in the open world setting but I do wish there was less travel times and actual epic boss fights and the lack thereof is underwhelming. 
You'll spend a lot of time traveling in vehicles in this large open map setting since that is the best means to navigate this huge map of fictional Bolivia. 

If you like Far Cry and Assassins Creed you'll like this game too. 

I suggest getting this game on when it's on sales. 
Perhaps my review is more lenient due to the fact I got it on Steam sales for about $13.00.

Suffers from some of the most braindead design flaws you could have in any kind of shooter. 
- Your companions are near useless, and only ever function right when you are directly commanding them and not focused on defending yourself.
- Enemy ability to detect you is near supernatural 
- You're a tier 1 spec ops operators that can't afford to start with rifle mags that can hold a standard 30 round capacity
- You can't use your parachute any time that it matters.
- Airplane missions are impossible because the controls are garbage and your companions can literally bump into the wing when exiting and make them explode (not an exaggeration, that's actually how poorly calibrated the physics and impact settings are). 
- All difficulty is cheaply artificial due to suicidal enemy AI, and them being able to spawn wherever they want. The rules of the game only really apply to you. 
- Ammo is plentiful to the point that I've never run out, making brute force almost always the best course of action. 

There is a good game buried deep deep beneath the absolute absence of quality control, but the problems with it surface so constantly that I've never been able to go a single day without being infuriated and having to take a break. I hit not recommended on this masterpiece of a game that I truly enjoy for one big reason, I wanted to make a statement on greed in the video gaming industry. Since Assassin’s creed Valhalla and Far Cry 6 aren’t on Steam yet, I didn’t really have any other game I could review that I could accurately use to convey my thoughts on how the mighty have fallen. You see right now there is a cancer, a disease, a malingnet growth that threatens the gaming industry and it’s only spreading in the video gaming industry, it’s a 5 letter word. It is greed. 

As much as I enjoy this masterpiece of a game, it’s breathtakingly gigantic and beautiful world space, it’s Easter eggs, and everything about it, I can’t help but feel some guilt. You see, every company that has been fully consumed with greed has a fallacy. It has one little quirk highlitighting it’s greediness. It’s not the microtransactions or loot boxes, it’s not the 14 year old boys using their mommy’s credit card, and it’s not the sacrifice of a single player experience to ♥♥♥♥♥ DLCs and multiplayer loot boxes. It’s something more unique. 

For Bethesda, it’s them re-releasing their cash cow Skyrim over and over again, for the creative assembly, it’s screwing over their original fan base and what made their series great, for paradox interactive, it’s lazily churning out large amounts of crappy DLC and screwing over modders, and for Ubisoft, it’s literally giving us the exact same cut and paste formula for single player campaigns in all games after this one as well as this one. 

It’s like they finally found a lazy cheap gameplay formula that works for their yearly releases and have just stuck with it. They left series like watchdogs and splinter cell because they wouldn’t fit with this formula. 

It’s a game map broken down into provinces each governed by a boss. You take out all the bosses before confronting the main villain. As a result, you will get bored, frustrated, and feel like it’s a grind rather than fun. Now in this game and games like AC Unity, it wasn’t as painfully noticeable because Ubisoft tried to their best to paper it over with the game’s story and gigantic map. 

In Far Cry 5, it was papered over with the incredible villains. But every Ubisoft game since, has just been this lazy plot and gameplay just pasted on a new setting in a different franchise. In pretty much every newer Ubisoft game, they try again to cover up the stale, boring, and tedious gameplay with the plot but by doing that, they make it less enjoyable and far harder to enjoy or understand the plot.

Also offtopic but a significant chunk of this game’s assets were reused for far cry 6. 

Ubisoft is lazy and fully infected with greed. It doesn’t help that they haven’t made any kind of push or effort to encourage or facilitate modding. Skyrim and pretty much every total war and paradox game would have died years ago without modding. I’m shocked that their unwillingness to facilitate modding hasn’t caused more problems for Ubisoft. 

Anyways, yes I enjoy this game, yes I’ve still played it through many times, yes I’ll still play it, but I can’t ignore it’s faults and the prediscent that it set. Plus it’s servers are basically dead so there isn’t a way to access the store in game. 

Overall, while I do recommend this game, I had to hit not recommended on this review because I cannot ignore how much it went toward Ubisoft and the video gaming industry as a whole’s greed.

I. Love. This. Game.

-Cringe dialogue 
-Your starting rifle is better then 70% of late game rifles
-Can only customize probably half of all rifles, handguns and machine guns
-Most enemy encampments have mile high walls surrounding the entire base perimeter so you basically have to kick down the front door, alert all the enemies, get spotted and then get funneled into a trap.

With all that negativity out of the the way, the game still has exceptional and addicting game play. Weapons feel great to use and dropping mortars on enemies never gets old. The original ghost recon games were great, I preferred them to Delta Force (no voxels), but the next two had a terrible interface that tried too hard to be like SWAT3's command system and failed. Wildlands has a simple, easy to use command system that doesn't get in the way. Driving is a pain (too twitchy), helicopters are a breeze, fixed wing are an even bigger pain. Boats are simple, but your idiot gang can only disembark by jumping in the water, even if you are alongside the dock.

Pros:
Your character and even the AI team-mates can be customised (gender, appearance) but the changes are purely cosmetic: wearing body armour has no more protection than a tee shirt.

As a sandbox, the game is great. Graphics are smooth even on my crappy system, and you can fly from one end of the map to the other with no pausing for disc loads. The attention to detail in terrain building is outstanding. Bolivia is actuially about 50 times larger in all directions, but the game world  feels real.

Cons: AI characters freeze occasionally and don't even try to follow; the bad guys appear to have unlimited troops and helos (I shot down over twenty Apaches in one mission and still they kept sending more.)
Story is cliched and obviously gung-ho (it is a TC title) but there is enough variation to keep your interest.
The thing that bugs me the most is that taking out the bosses has no real effect in the game: I thought that taking out the security boss first (including the army chief) would reduce the strength of your enemies, but no, there is no change.
Vehicles, even the armoured APC can plough through small brick walls but crash if they hit a lowly telegraph pole.

For those who enjoy sniping, the bullet drop mechanics mean the rangefinder on scopes can actually come in use while making every long-range shot all the more satisfying (and risky if you miss). Ghost mode makes it an intense with permadeath, yet enjoyable experience where you play the cautious stealth game where possible, but when all hell breaks loose you find yourself rushing the enemy with all resources at your disposal, because you sure as hell don't want to go back to killing La Yuri and El Polito all over again. Word of advice, don't get stranded up mountains without a chopper or you might just fall to a dumb death like I did where your teammates can't reach you to revive you.

One thing I really wish is that they'd bring in a first-person POV option. It would make the game so much more immersive and going from over-the-shoulder to first-person sights is disorientating as hell.

Last bit of advice, DON'T GET THE DLCs. Even if on sale, just go read the reviews to find out why not.

If you're looking for an adrenaline-fueled gaming experience, Ghost Recon Wildlands is a must-buy.

One of the standout features of Ghost Recon Wildlands is the freedom it grants players. The game presents a massive open-world environment filled with diverse landscapes, bustling cities, and dangerous cartel-controlled territories. The sheer size and scope of the world offer endless opportunities for exploration and discovery. Whether you prefer to complete missions stealthily or engage in intense shootouts, the game allows you to tackle objectives in your own style.

The gameplay mechanics of Ghost Recon Wildlands strike the perfect balance between tactical strategy and exhilarating action. As a member of an elite Ghost Recon team, you'll embark on thrilling covert missions, infiltrating enemy compounds, and taking down high-value targets. The game encourages player creativity, allowing you to approach each mission from multiple angles and employ a wide array of weapons, gadgets, and vehicles to accomplish your objectives.

The cooperative multiplayer mode adds another layer of excitement to the gameplay. Join forces with friends or other players online and coordinate your actions to take down the ruthless Santa Blanca drug cartel. Working together as a team brings a new level of immersion and intensity to the game, enhancing the overall experience and fostering unforgettable moments of camaraderie.

Visually, Ghost Recon Wildlands shines with its stunning graphics and attention to detail. The picturesque landscapes, bustling towns, and intricate enemy bases are rendered with impressive realism, immersing you in a visually captivating world. The dynamic weather system and day-night cycle further enhance the immersive experience, adding an extra layer of depth to the game's atmosphere.

In conclusion, Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands is a thrilling and action-packed open-world adventure that offers countless hours of entertainment. Whether you prefer stealthy approaches or intense shootouts, the game provides a wide range of gameplay options to suit your playstyle. The vast open-world, cooperative multiplayer, and stunning visuals make it a standout title in the genre. If you're seeking an adrenaline rush and an immersive gaming experience, don't hesitate to embark on this unforgettable journey. Get ready to sneak, shoot, and have a blast in the wild world of Ghost Recon Wildlands.

[b]If you have played other recent Ubisoft's open world games you probably know what to expect from "Ghost Recon - Wildlands". Yet, although I 've played few of them I was never expecting this level of boringness and repetitiveness. The game is visually gorgeous with a big, convincing world, great sound design and a pretty rich characters' and weapons' customization/upgrading system. But everything else is just a mess. The story and world seem to be awkwardly familiar and most of its assets are copied from previous Ubisoft's games. The open world logic of moving between dots on the map is well worn. Missions, enemies and combat gameplay are awfully repetitive and not intriguing at all. On top of all these it is full of silly bugs and glitches. A game that doesn't give you the motivation to continue playing it after the first few hours.


Manometer: 3/10[/b]


The good
- It is gorgeous visually with great graphics, nice chromatic palette and atmospheric lighting.
- Big, well designed and convincing world. Nice sceneries of natural environment to go with small villages and military bases. The world feels alive with people, vehicles and animals roaming around. There are some nice touches and details here and there too.
- Rich sound design with tons of natural, ambient, gunshot sounds. It feels realistic most of the time.
- Above average NPCs' AI. They react to your actions realistically. Enemies also seem to be pretty clever during the combat following tactics and without exposing themselves too much.
- Decent co-op implementation. Waypoints, missions and accomplishments are visible to every team member and there are also some nice tools of communication.

The bad
- Well worn open world logic that offers nothing new. You just have to go mechanically from a mark on the map to another without a certain reason. You are the military errand boy that follows orders and wanders endlessly without a certain purpose. Also it's crazy of how many hours you will spend driving from one place to another. After a few hours there is no motivation to go on.
- Missions that all look alike each other. Combat's pace is mediocre and the gameplay doesn't give you the tools or the motivation to try different approaches. Everything feels repetitive. Missions should have specific scenarios that force you through their objectives to try things and use all your skillset.
- It is full of bugs and glitches. Physics are not completed. NPCs tend to get invisible, teleported, stretched or floated up in the air. Explosions often occur weird effects around them. There are often disconnections and some random problems that needed game's restart to get addressed. The game is a mess and so many years after its release it 's unacceptable that it remains at this state.
- The well known, boring mafia-cartel story with the paranoid boss we 've met in most of "Far Cry" kai "Ghost Recon" games. Uninteresting plot, mediocre cut scenes. After a while you forget that the story is actually there and you are not eager to learn more.
- Although the world is visually gorgeous it is awkwardly similar to other open world Ubisoft's games like "Far Cry". I mean they are not only aesthetically identical but at many occasions they have copied the same aspects again and again. Some more creativity would be nice.
- Respawn system after you get killed doesn't work well. Most of the time it doesn't resurrect you near the teammate you chose. Sometimes you will get respawned miles away from the action and some others among ten enemies and with two helicopters above your head with a result of immediately dying again. Respawn points are an important shooters' element that should be implemented more carefully.
- They designed only two or three kinds of enemies and threw them around the entire world. It would be less boring if each area had a specific identity with its special units and NPCs.
- Police spawning system at points of interest, fortresses or during missions is silly. No matter how many and how fast you kill them, cops keep coming. It seems fake. If you 're fast enough it should give you small time windows to fulfil your objectives or escape between the waves.
- Problematic collisions. Climbing sometimes doesn't work even if the obstacle has average height. You will often get stuck under rock complexes or inside narrow spaces. NPCs will annoyingly block your way sometimes too.

Excellent arcadey mil-sim outpost takedown co-op FPS* (third person until ADS) strategy game, and can get unbearably difficult if you want that sort of thing. There's tons of guns. I feel like I have half of them, however many of them were behind a paywall and the ones I don't have, I have no idea how to get unless from a crate (you earn in game credits for crates infrequently, and the crate is a random item out of 200+). Flying is the biggest highlight for me, in both helicopters and small prop planes, with plenty of SAM sites to keep you on your toes with their missiles/rockets. There is also plenty of character progression, and eventually you will be forced to play on the hardest difficulty (but not the permadeath mode mentioned below) if you want your character's level to keep progressing. There are save slots for 3 characters.

Expect many, many bugs. It's entertaining seeing a new one each play session, and typically they don't break the game necessarily, however it makes trying to do the hardest difficulty (permadeath with only 1 gun and pistol sidearm) literally not worth your effort. You'll get killed by a random NPC getting spooked and running you over. Or, you'll get stuck in mid-air because your parachute works a little too well (stuck in place). Or, Unidad (think federal police) will be on patrol in a buggy with a minigun and mow down your whole team in less than a second while you're fighting someone else.

When the game works, and even when it's bugging out, it is so much fun, and matchmaking is pretty good. 90% of randoms have been great and typically everyone will add you if you just play with purpose. It's very, very satisfying when 4 people spend 10 minutes on just one outpost and clear it together (harder areas on harder difficulties will have 20+ enemies, active drone jammers, multiple alarms, multiple sniper enemies with long vision and good vantage points, manned MGs, etc).

I can't recommend this game anymore, though, simply because it doesn't run well, at all. It's a laggy, stuttery mess, from main menu, to in game, to tabbing out of the game, and God forbid you have anything running in the background (Spotify for me), because the anti-cheat system will crash the game and take a while just to do that. There have been many times that I have given up trying to play it because it is just too damn stuttery and desyncs from teammates. It's never in a state that makes you feel like things are going to go well. It's stressful enough dying to the very competent enemies, without the headache of just trying to move about the map as a group. But it is fun, and scratches an itch different from others in the genre. I think of it like MGS:V, without the supernatural stuff, and easier to just run and gun and not care about the consequences. If you die in the normal mode, your AI or online teammates can revive you, or after a short time you'll respawn nearby with no penalty. *There are a few missions that require maximum stealth, and will restart at a checkpoint if you fail, and those are rough because the enemies can become bugged and already aware of your presence and seeking you out when you re-load the checkpoint, getting you stuck in an endless loop of re-loading and no time to exit the game the right way before it fails you again.

I want this game to be better, but in the month or so that I've been playing, I haven't seen anything to suggest the game is still being worked on or maintained by anyone. Everyone accepts it as is, for better or worse. If you ever see it free or discounted, absolutely try it out. Can't recommend it, though.

There’s so much fun to be had here, and the co-op is probably the best I’ve seen in a long time. The country of Bolivia is massive and fun to explore, with plenty to do and visuals that never fail to impress. But, since I like this game a lot, I have to go over its shortcomings.

At start it's somewhat generic 3rd person shooter. It is fun solo, but the real fun starts in co-op.

The Bolivian setting is impressive and beautiful, with a diverse biome world to explore. The environments feel properly dense with all kinds of growth. However, gruesomely repetitive missions can hinder your gameplay, there really is no fun to be had in all that, unless you're a digital game world photography enthusiast, or a digital game world hiking/tourism lover, then i'm sure you'll be having the time of your life with Wildlands.

The "shooty shooty" mechanics are quite competent with it's 1st-3rd person shooter hybrid mechanics, guns feel decent to use and have satisfying sound effects. The character, gear customization is well done too with quite a lot of options to deck out your character. There's a good amount of weapon choice as well. Also props to Ubisoft for including bullet drop and prone mechanics, not many AAA mass market oriented games include those, especially 3rd person perspective driven games. The tactical gameplay aspects barely feel like they're even there, they are very bare bones and worse, feel like they don't even need to be used. The cluttered HUD is also painful, there is very little challenge in fighting enemies since they get auto tagged and become visible through walls and crap, so yes – disable HUD elements to increase immersion and realism. However, by disabling HUD elements, the game becomes unbalanced because it was clearly meant to be played with the hand holding mechanics enabled. The synchronized execution mechanic is also half broken, because your AI team mates can shoot through solid rock to execute their targets.

Then comes the driving, Wildlands has one of the worst feeling driving i have ever experienced in a game, the cars are weightless, they feel like paper boxes on wheels. Nailing the driving model should've been a core focus for the developers, since you spend so much time driving in this thing, instead the numb driving played a significant role in my abandonment of the game. The flying feels better, but not by much, it also is quite dumbed down, with very little fear factor of screwing up.

I will still recommend the game, since I had too much fun and would be insincere otherwise. There is lot of cool freedom in that game, you just have to use it. Many possibilities to do things in unusual way thanks to the open world structure. I'll give 2 examples. First is a mission where you have to drop off a truck in enemy base and leave without raising any alarms. You can do that normal way and try to sneak out or take down all enemies quietly. Alternatively, you can sneak into a nearby building, get to the top and base jump out of the base. Second example is mission to interrogate base commander. You can get in normal way, or get a friend to fly you in a helicopter over the base, jump on a parachute on top of the building he's in and after interrogation have you friend pick you up with the same helicopter. The quantity over quality approach is the most detrimental aspect of nearly every modern Ubisoft game. it really hurts to grind basically same content over and over, however it is my guilty pleasure to role-play specialist and explore the vastly different biome world solo or with friends.

[h1] [i] A deeply flawed, gorgeous and ultimately enjoyable experience [/i] [/h1]

Wildlands managed to divide fans of both tactical TPS/FPS and of Ghost Recon franchise. While some exalted the new mechanics and the direction the developers decided to head towards, not everyone was happy. Some disliked, what they have seen as oversimplification with many important tactical elements being removed, replaced or straight up dumbed down, all of that set in one of the prettiest and best crafted worlds that ends up feeling barren and non-interesting with a lukewarm story to help you navigate it. I am somewhere in between both camps – while I am more than happy to acknowledge that Wildlands has myriad of flaws and issues and understand people saying that it is not a Ghost Reckon game anymore, I can’t deny the fact that I have enjoyed the game, for the most part. Some of its aspects incredibly poorly realized (such as driving) but overall, I liked the feeling of beautiful world, moving around in it, completing missions and objective and alternating between stealthy and loud approach to each situation.

In the end, I do completely understand why someone might decide to pass on the game, particularly if they were fans of the previous GR games, I just can not say I haven’t enjoyed the experience I have had – that would be a lie. I do, however, definitely wish the game was less flawed.

[b] [i] Positives [/i] [/b]

+ Without a doubt, one of the best looking and most well-crafted game worlds of all time – the Bolivian environment looks amazing realized in the Ubisoft’s AnvilNext’s 2.0 engine and the feeling is only bolstered by incredible weather effects, wind and dynamic day/night cycle. Whoever has done the work on this has made immense effort that paid off.
+ Level design - there are so many regions in the game, each with a unique feeling to them
+ Some parts of the story, particularly the backstories of the villains that have really well done cutscenes combining real life-like imagery with game assets
+ Competent voice acting and mo-cap
+ Overall gameplay – shooting mechanics and weapon selection, stealth mechanics (drone, spotting...) are decent
+ Length of the game, even if its bloated and repetitive in some parts
+ Good co-op

[b] [i] Negatives [/i] [/b]

- Typical Ubisoft open world games problems – the world is filled to the brim with things to do but those do ultimately feel pointless and unnecessary, not to mention repetitive.
- Most event/crossover missions are utter and broken trash, either being a dysfunctional mess or being nonsensically difficult (hello Operation Watchman)
- Awful driving mechanics - who the hell designed that? The movement is choppy and unnatural, the handling of vehicles is often unresponsive and hard to get used to. Choppers fare a bit better but overall, vehicle gameplay is truly one of the worst in open-world games.
- Disappointing DLCs that range from okay-ish (Fallen Ghosts) to outright horrible (Narco Road - how the hell did the devs find the idea of concentrating on driving mechanics which is objectively the worst part of the game) - do not buy any Season Passes, it's a waste of money for this game
- A lot of content in the store that you have to buy with real money if you really want it which is stupid in a single-player/co-op game
- Story, although having some bright parts, is fairly boring and sidequests are repetitive and uninspired

I came into this game with low expectations.  I picked it up as a quick Co-op shooter to play with my friends.  It had a surprisingly high steam rating and seemed like a more tactical GTA.  On top of this, I’m one of the chumps who actually enjoyed games like Assassin’s Creed Odyssey and Watch_Dogs.  But, to reiterate, I still had pretty low expectations for this game.  That being said I still think the game is well below average.

To be fair for the first 10 hours or so it’s pretty fun in a sandbox sort of way, especially with friends.  But so is Dead Island so putting into the equation on whether the game itself is any good, I feel, is unfair.

I can sort this into 2 major problems I have.  There are other gripes like how mediocre the story is, even for a Ubisoft game, or how the driving is complete garbage, or how the resource system is poorly implemented and didn’t make me want to get more skills but rather made me mostly ignore the skill tree altogether.  These are smaller problems that do wear down the game but I don’t want to write a 10 page thesis on this.

1: The gameplay loop is counter-intuitive

The whole gimmick of this game is the high tactical gameplay with an emphasis on stealth and tactics.  The problem is it’s just way more efficient to just run in and kill everyone.  When I got the skill that makes your running silent the game was over.  I could just run around murdering and still not alert anyone.

Now I can already hear you crying “no wonder you didn’t enjoy yourself you didn’t play the game right!’  Or something.  If they wanted a bigger emphasis on stealth they should have either improved the AI or made going loud more dangerous.  It’s a basic human function to find the most efficient way to do something and when they find it they will exploit it.  It’s what we do.  Look at a game like Assassin’s Creed, the older ones.  The combat in those games, especially 2, kind of sucked.  It was janky and slow, it was literally more efficient to stealth your way through.  But making a hard hitting stealth system would take to much work or something so they skipped it.

2: Bloat

How we define a game’s length and whether it’s too long varies.  For instance, I put 83 hours into Red Dead Redemption 2 or I put 81 into the Witcher 3.  I wouldn’t call these games too long.  They are long but they aren’t so long they overstay their welcome.  It comes down to the gameplay loop and story to carry a game.  A 20 hour game with a good game loop or story will feel much shorter than a game with neither.  Unfortunately, Wildlands falls into the latter.

I played the game for 23 hours and as I said in the beginning the first 10 were enjoyable at the very least.  The next 13 felt like a month.  There is just not enough variety in the missions nor a real pushing factor behind you to motivate you.  It just shows you a list of bad guys and tells you to go kill them.  It makes the game feel more like a checklist you’re filling out than plaything through a story.

Not to mention I only killed half of the guys on the map so I didn’t get the true ending but, frankly, I couldn’t be bothered.  I called it done and uninstalled.

I think this game could have been good, or even great if they had done more with the story.  The problem is it doesn’t really know what it wants to be, especially in tone.  I can’t tell if it wants to be an over the top action shooter like Call of Duty or a serious gritty military shooter like Spec Ops: The Line.  It tries to tow this weird line in between the two which leaves everyone unsatisfied.  Having some actual consequences for your actions or really showing the horrors of war could have heightened the game a lot but instead it’s happy to bathe in its own mediocrity.

4/10 - A boring, uninspired “tactical” shooter.  It’ll do little more than waste your time.
