I like this game, and hate it.
The game is not bad, gameplay is pretty alright and quite fun, and I see myself going back to it quite often.
But the game is riddled with many small problems that make it hard if not impossible to recommend this game.
The story, is pretty bland and generic, the missions are very repetitive and get boring after a very short time playing it.
The map feels needlessly large, which is a recurrent problems is games in recent open-world games, and although it is quite beautiful (the game sometimes really looks amazing and you should definitely try to take some nice screenshots) the map is really just a whole lot of nothing, lifeless, and doesn't make you want to travel in it. Even less with the awful driving mechanics of the game.

But buy far my largest problem with the game, is the AI, and how straight-up unfair and impossible the game sometimes can be on higher difficulties. I tend to play on second hardest difficulty, with a lot of HUD options disabled and on Tier mode (which increases difficulty).
On higher difficulties the game tries to make itself harder in very terrible ways, like spawning enemies behind you, or spawning infinite enemies reinforcements.

On another note, there are many things that could have been great to have in the game, 1st person comes to mind, I would love to play this game and do stealth missions in first person, and although you can sort of have 1st person (by aiming) that really doesn't cut it.
But overall, the UI of the game is pretty good, and the controls are some of the best I've ever had in a game like that.

So basically, the game is good, but has some strong flaws.
If you want to have fun, play with a friend in coop on intermediate difficulties, doing mission in coop is very enjoyable, or play super realistic in hard difficulties all HUD off.
And try to enjoy the view, especially in the mountains, the game is very nice looking.

Ghost Recon Wildlands is the reboot of the Ghost Recon franchise and this time it takes on the open world stealth genre. 

Story:

You play as Nomad (gender is chosen by the player), who is a part of the Ghost squad. You and your squad are sent to Bolivia after a dangerous Santa Blanca cartel bomb the US embassy and kill a CIA agent. Your mission is simple, teaming up with the local rebels, you have to destroy every chain of the cartel and then take out its leader, the notorious El Sueño all while fighting against it's devout members and the ruthless police force Unidad. 

The story in Ghost Recon Wildlands is weak to say the least. The idea itself is solid as hell, taking down a ruthless cartel by taking down its members seems ripe for a good story, but the game doesn't simply use its full potential. The main story of the US embassy bombing is quickly dropped and only brought back near the end of the game, where I completely forgot that it even happened.
 
I'll admit however some writing is pretty good and some of the cartel members are pretty interesting. They range from normal people joining the cartel to make money or absolutely crazy people. There are video profiles for each one of them, when you start their region, so you know who you're dealing with. 

Graphics.

One thing that is impossible to deny is that Ghost Recon Wildlands looks absolutely stunning. Bolivia is an absolutely amazing location and it's incredibly varied.It ranges from cities, deserts, mountains, jungles and salt flats. It's all pretty amazing stuff and honestly this feels like a live and breathing world, even though most of the locations feel abandoned. 

There's a lot of attention to detail in the world and I really loved exploring Bolivia and seeing the sights. So now about everything else, the character models for the main characters are decent and they look distinct, but everyone else looks the same. Cartel minions, unidad, rebels and civilians all have a few distinct looks and so it feels like a massive clone army.

Guns look decent and look like their real life counterparts, there's a lot customizing options so you can design most guns to your liking, even choosing what type of camo you want on them. 

And of course there's vehicles, but there's not that many types of them, so you see the same colored trucks and sedans on the road over and over, maybe a sports car every so often.

Audio:

The audio design in Wildlands is decent, but there's quite a few things I don't like about it. First of all I'll start with the good. The voice acting is really good and honestly everyone does a decent job, every character has a distinct voice and some of them really play their parts well, like a douchebag cartel DJ. Also the surrounding ambiance of the world is great, like rain hitting the ground, birds chirping and stuff like that.

However there's a few other things I don't like and these. One of the biggest things I don't like is how most guns sounds too similar to one another, even you slap on an silencer other guns of the same caliber sound pretty much identical.

Gameplay:

When playing a Ghost Recon game, most people expect a tactical experience and while Wildlands has some tactical missions, it's nowhere near as much as the older games. If I had to describe the gameplay, it would be Far Cry in third person.

Your basic goal is pick any region in Bolivia, gather information by collecting intel and then trying to take out that particular region boss. The missions are basically on a cycle, it's always go to someplace and either A) Kill someone B) Destroy something and or C) Collect something on a repeat and then once you're done with that region the boss emerges from hiding and you either kidnap them or kill them.

In the first hours of the game it's really fun and taking on waves of cartel members is fun, but sadly it quickly becomes boring to the point, when you reach the final few regions, you just want to get it over with as soon as possible.  

The basic gameplay is fun enough, most of the time you have an option of either go loud or go quiet. Stealth is rather fun, but most of the time, you can't keep it up for long, because something might go wrong and that is out of your control. For example you might be clearing a big outpost of cartel members quietly and all of a sudden another cartel minion from a nearby outpost wanders into your location and spots a body which alerts everyone else. It gets pretty annoying, pretty fast. 

Also the game has another type of enemy which is the Unidad. Unidad is the police of Wildlands and they are a much tougher enemy than the Santa Blanca cartel. When fighting them, the bigger fight you put up, the bigger the punch back they will throw towards you. So if you stand your ground and fight, they might start sending choppers to your location and armored trucks to chase you down. They are at first a dangerous enemy and fun enemy, but quickly end up becoming really annoying. In some missions where you invade their bases they never stop spawning and dealing with them becomes a pain. 

Verdict:

While I don't absolutely hate Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands, I don't love it either. In my opinion this game is too much like Far Cry with not much different factors. It's still a fun game, but honestly the mission structure could have more variety cause it becomes pretty boring doing the same missions over and over again. On a sale this game is a great experience, but for full price it's not worth it.

Final Rating:
6.5/10

If you're on the fence about Ghost Recon Wildlands, let me give you a friendly nudge – in a stealthy way, of course! This game is like an all-you-can-eat buffet of tactical fun, and I’m the hungry gamer diving into every digital taco and burrito! From the breathtaking landscapes of Bolivia to the exhilarating gameplay that keeps you on the edge of your seat (or sofa, no judgment here), it’s a full-on adrenaline fiesta! I mean, where else can you blow up a drug cartel while sipping an imaginary piña colada? What a daydream!

But seriously, if you enjoy sneaking around in camo while planning the perfect heist, then grab your controller and prepare for some shenanigans. The squad mechanics are a conspiracy theorist’s dream, with tons of ways to strategize your moves. Whether you're going in guns blazing like a caffeine-fueled action figure or opting for the stealth mode where you pretend to be a ninja – let’s be honest, you will NEVER be a ninja – the freedom this game offers is unparalleled! Plus, nothing says "team bonding" quite like accidentally blowing up your friend's helicopter just as they were about to land. Oops!

The cherry on top? The game is truly a haven for those of us who relish chaos wrapped in a tactical bow. I wholeheartedly recommend Ghost Recon Wildlands to anyone who enjoys the genre – or just seeks to unleash their inner Rambo while taking endless selfies with their drone (pro tip: remember to take the selfies after the mission, not during). So suit up, grab your buddies, and get ready to save the world one hilarious misstep at a time. You won't regret it — unless you forget to bring snacks!

Where do i even start. 

I'm torn that i'm only given a thumbs up or thumbs down decision on this game. This game pivots on the edge of the extremely bad and the extremely good more so then any other game i've played in recent memory. Depending on your skill-level, method of playing the game, and the aspects of the game you're most interested in this game either has what your looking for or falls short. 

Firstly just as a little preamble here, i'm a single-player gamer, because of this i admittedly feel that i'm not completely using the full extent of the game and it's campaign and i can easily imagine the gameplay would be considerably better with other players to help apply tactics without having to cross your fingers that the Squad AI doesn't ruin your entire plan of attack. I'm a long time Tom Clancy fan and a military enthusiast. 

*Gameplay*

The gameplay itself again is a hit or a miss depending on what aspect you're looking at, vehicles for example are complete trash that mostly just operate as transports for long distances while the gunplay is pretty entertaining and on point, the game does feels to have a bias to mid-range stealth shooting which is fun enough but if you wanted to go with a different discipline say an LMG you'd better be ready to realize the game is about to not know how to handle you and will either throw everything at you full force or get rofl-stomped. 

Scenarios either you come across organically or missions constructed for you all pretty much follow the same theme, you have a heavily guarded well defended position be it a town, a camp, a FOB, or any other instillation, and then you are infiltrators who slowly pick away at their perimeter until you're either detected and forced to "Go Loud" or have eliminated all hostiles. This is very entertaining the first four our five times, and then still as the game goes on still hold's it charm but is repetitive and makes up the vast majority of the game experience. 

As stated above the AI is much to be desired, i feel like Ubisoft's answer to the reality that AI will never function as effectively as we believe it should was to make the laws of physics and logic simply suspend whenever AI is challenged. This kind of works, though it makes you squadmates unpredictable and not particularly reliable and act more as satellites to the player then an actual squad, i think the best example of logic simply suspending itself was i got bum-rushed by some heavies (because i wasn't paying attention) and got downed (you can go down once in a firefight, if you go down again game over) and my squad mate took his sweet time to get to me meanwhile the enemy-AI all charged my location, instead of the the allied AI eliminating the hostiles they were 'off their radar' totally ignored as they ran up to revive me (in the middle of 6 hostiles) without eliminating any of them leading to me being revived and then instantly killed. Though it works, i found the entire squad system completely lacking, and the potential for a really interesting gameplay dynamic squandered.

The environment and map design of the game is probably it's most redeeming quality, its stunning and diverse, it makes sense and immerses you into the world but it too has it's short comings. I cannot tell you how many times i've glitched though or become stuck in the terrain of this game, and with no real check-point system you can't simply revert to an autosave, if you become stuck while in combat well then you have to backout of the game to reset. Though doesn't happen all that often (more often then in other games) it is extremely annoying when it does. 

*The Niche* 

Lets be honest, most people who are interested in this game are interested because of the Tom Clancy logo, and the style that comes with that franchise and in that regard this a very solid experience for young military enthusiasts, casual shooters looking for something a little more substantive then most run-an-gun games without going too hardcore like some other titles, or fans (like myself) of the greater franchise. 

I wasn't 100% sold i was going to address this, but as i'm writing this i feel like i have to because this a Tom Clancy title : The politics of this game is pretty messed up at best, and Racist at worst. Now i feel like everything now a days has gotten unnecessarily political and as i mentioned above i only feel compelled to mention this because it's a Tom Clancy game, and geopolitics plays a significant roll in most if not all of the entries into that franchise and does so in this title as well. It is the manner of the politics in this game that is so offensive, not because any controversy but because of it's sinful simplicity; it boils down too "Americans Good! Narcos Bad!" while completely ignoring the USA's (Particularly the CIA) extremely complicated history in Latin America and any depth into the equally complicated and dynamic state of Latin American politics. Instead what is portrayed is a US-Spec Ops team as a universal good while depicting the Bolivian people (A Real People) as insane zealots of a narco-prophet in a very weird disingenuous take on the religious nature of their culture while propping up an allied counter-culture faction that just exists like a 'Tio Tomas' for the player's perception of the population. With utterly no story, depth, or background Bolivians are portrayed as murderous Maniacs committing inhumane acts of depravity, or valiant revolutionary american-puppets with frankly is just very poor writing and world building. At times the game tries to take a satirical look at situations in places like Bolivia but fails to do anything meaningful and plays like a Just Cause game and yet is just still too serious to laugh at and too out of touch to be intriguing. Best way i can describe it is that this game is like explaining counter-insurgency to children, they don't get it, they have no idea whats going on, but they can pretty accurately tell who the "Good Guys" and the "Bad Guys" are, and as a fan of the franchise, i expected better then this.

But if you're looking for a game that focuses on applied infantry tactics, strategy, analysis, planning and execution of that plan to accomplish objectives like you would expect from a game that sells you as a team of CIA-Backed Operators in Narco-Bolivia, then this is Not the game for you. If you want a casual military-esque shooter that focuses on ruining some Sicario's days with your sneaky shenanigans then you should seriously pick up this game, you wont not regret it.

Honestly one of the best games I've played in a while! Yes, there's some bugs here and there (what'd you expect, it's Ubi...), but it's an amazing game. The graphics are great, which help bring alive this amazing, and huge, open world with loads of varying terrain! Snowy mountains, dessert, jungle, swamp and more! Character customizability is okay, I wish you had a few more options, many of the clothing options are through in-game purchases which is sad. Weapon customizability is great though, loads of options there. Mind you, you will have to find these weapons and accessories on the map first. The story missions are quite varied. I like the fact that you're able to do the missions in any order you want. For me the missions felt well balanced, they gave me a challenge but they remained doable; on the advanced difficulty setting with AI Squadmates turned off. Just don't bother using the rebel support, and don't open up their cells when you're trying to play stealthily. They'll mess with your mission, and they'll usually end up getting you killed. I personally played without the AI Squad from the start because I liked the lonewolf idea. This is definitely doable in terms of difficulty. Do keep in mind that the AI's voice-lines will remain for the story side of things which takes a bit away from the immersiveness. Your own character's voice-lines can be VERY repetitive, especially when spotting: "Sniper, top of the tower" "I got a sniper, top of the tower" "Sniper, top of the tower" "I got a small group of tangos" "I got a small group of tangos" "I got a small group of tangos". 
The game isn't perfect, but sure is a lot of fun! Clearing large UNIDAD outposts while remaining undetected, blowing up a cocaine stash in a hidden warehouse. The story makes sense and if you watch the video's the game prompts you to watch actually pretty good. If you're looking for a real story game, don't buy this. If you're looking for a game with a lot of gameplay, very little handholding but at least a story to guide you, then this could very well be one of the funnest games you've played in a while. 

(Oow, and if one or more of your friends buy the game you can play co-op, which works actually really well and is a lot of fun!)

Having played Ghost Recon Wildlands with friends, I can say that it's moderately fun, but if you plan on playing singleplayer only, definitely don't buy it. Ghost Recon is a game about the US sending the Ghosts, the best of the best of their special forces in order to stop a drug cartel that's taken over the country of Bolivia. However, there are a lot of bumps and hiccups on the way, both in-game and in a metaphorical sense.

Ghost Recon looks fantastic. You are scarcely left with anything bad to say about the graphics after traversing the flatlands, forests and mountains of Bolivia, and everything looks the part. This is probably the only part where the game shines - despite being visually impressive, there's not much to it.

In terms of gameplay, Ghost Recon's been going down the drain. The installment after this one, Breakpoint, has even less substance than Wildlands, and even this is pretty bad. Sure, you have your cool military tech and tactics, but that just amounts to drones and trying to coordinate moves with your AI companions who are, mostly, only useful for that and nothing else. You constantly feel distanced from the game world, and the repetitiveness and monotony of the multiple fetch-quests that take you across Bolivia is mind-numbing. The missions don't even vary that much, and you have to do a ton of them just to bring down ONE branch of the cartel.

The characters are just... there. There's not much characterization, and I couldn't even remember the name of the bad guy. Dialogue is scarce, and none of your teammates have any personality to them. The gameplay and the story don't help each other one bit, each one being boring and repetitive. The story tries to change some things up sometimes by having different targets, but everything you have tho do to get them is the same. Hell, probably the best character in this game is the radio DJ that occasionally actually cracks some funny things that satirize the situation or are just good jokes.

The AI is incredibly dumb. Your AI companions often get you into trouble, no one knows anything about tactics or shooting, and you're just left with a sense of complete disbelief at just how bad the game is and how it handles the AI. As said before, the only thing good about the AI is that it can be used to line up free shots on highlighted enemies.

As for the sound, Wildlands is a bit gamey, with bullet noises being a bit bad. The good thing is that this, compared to Breakpoint, actually has a radio station, and the music really builds up the ambiance and the tone of being in Bolivia. There's really not much else, but music and sound are some of the only things that kept me from dying of boredom.

Ghost Recon Wildlands is a whole open world of absolutely nothing. Despite its multiple regions, characters, and missions, it's as repetitive as a game can be and is really a good example of the general decline in quality of Ubisoft open worlds into becoming mind-numbing icon-filled same-y maps that fill the game up so that it can reach more hours of gameplay. Buy this game on sale if you're planning to play it with friends; otherwise, don't buy it at all.

Tom Clancy’s Ghost Recon Wildlands review by Kurz

For Onono - Gamers Connect.
All reviews is also available at: https://www.onono.no/


10/10


Introduction

Tom Clancy’s Ghost Recon Wildlands, by Ubisoft Paris and published by Ubisoft, was released on March 7, 2017. Wildlands is the 10th game in the series but the first Ghost Recon game to go with the open world concept. It is one of the biggest open world maps that Ubisoft has ever created.


Gameplay

The game starts off in the high mountains of Bolivia. At first, you get drawn into the awesome graphics that surround you, complete with detailed and nicely made terrain, trees, grass, and so on. It’s purely breathtaking. When you start off, you get three bots to play with, or you can choose to play with friends in co-op. If you choose to play in coop, the bots will disappear.
Ghost Recon Wildlands is played in a 3rd person perspective, but you have the option of taking on a first person view as well. You play as a member of the Delta Company, and your task is to retake control of Bolivia. Your target is the druglord El Sueño, who is running the biggest drug cartel in the world, and it’s up to you and or your friends to take him Down.

There are different difficulties you can put on to make the game easy or extremely challenging. I would recommend putting it has high as you can tolerate, since it will increase the amount of fun you have in the game. There is nothing like sneaking up to a base and silently take out the entire force who are armed with a high skill set. I would recommend if you are playing with friends that you put your difficulties at the same as your friends. That will force you to play the same tactics.

Doing missions in the dark compared to daytime makes a big difference in how you plan your entry. During the night, you have the advantage of stealth. Many of the soldiers are also sleeping during the night, making them an easy target.
Drones are your best friend in the game. You can easily scout an entire base within a minute to plan your attack. The first of the drones have fewer abilities, but as you progress and get the experience required, you can upgrade your drone to be quicker and stronger.

There is a wide variety of weapons, clothing, and ways to customize your equipment. Ghost Recon Wildlands uses weapons from different militaries around the world. As you progress in your game, you will find and unlock new guns, add-ons, clothing, and vehicles.
Helicopter is my main way of transportation, and the sweet thing is that you can spawn in any vehicle wherever you are on the map, making it easy to travel. You can also teleport to different locations you have unlocked on the map, or you can teleport to any of your friends.

The map is huge and is divided into 21 areas. The different areas have different difficulties, meaning it’s best to start out with the lower levels. When you enter a new area, you unlock new missions to complete. The missions in the different areas are controlled by a Buchon, and to progress towards eliminating them, you need to take out the underbosses.

Cutscenes for the story are well made, and Karen Bowman is as bad as you can get. Spoiler alert: pressuring cartel members to overdose on coke to makes them squeal.

Special Operations
Ubisoft has done a lot to support the game over the years. They have made several special operations to keep players like me playing the game continuously.

There are currently five special operations:

Predator
Operation Watchman
Operation Archangel
Operation Silent Spade
Operation Oracle


DLC

There are 2 DLCs for Ghost Recon Wildlands: Narco Road and Fallen Ghosts. They both take place on self-sustaining maps- both edited parts of the original map. The gameplay is a little bit different from the original game, but they both have some interesting new implements. For example, the way your vehicles and planes are made so much more arcade-like in Narco Road to the awesome new enemies you encounter in Fallen Ghost.
I would recommend them both, but I wish they had made the DLCs’ maps expand into the main map.


Conclusion

If you want to get an awesome shooter game with cooperative gameplay, there is no way around Ghost Recon Wildlands. It is the best Coop game out there to date, even if it’s some years old.
The world of Wildlands is so beautiful, you can just drive around enjoying the view. 10/10

Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands offers an expansive, open-world tactical shooter set in a fictionalized version of Bolivia, where players take on the role of elite soldiers tasked with dismantling a brutal drug cartel. Here's a breakdown of its pros and cons:

Pros:
Co-op Gameplay: Wildlands shines in its multiplayer co-op mode, where players can team up with friends to tackle missions together. The game emphasizes coordination and strategy, making it much more engaging when played with others. This feature is especially strong with the synchronizing shot mechanics that let you plan and execute coordinated takedowns with your squad.
Massive Open World: The game offers a vast, detailed environment to explore, featuring diverse landscapes and varied terrains. It offers a rich world to traverse, with the sense of a living, breathing place that offers plenty of opportunities for tactical play.
Weapon Customization: Players have the freedom to customize their arsenal, adjusting everything from optics to suppressors. This offers a satisfying level of depth for fans of tactical gameplay​.
Soundtrack and Atmosphere: The soundtrack blends South American influences with military rock, adding a unique touch to the game’s tone. The voice acting is generally solid, with the antagonist, El Sueño, being particularly well-received.

Cons:
Single-Player Experience: While multiplayer is a highlight, the single-player experience can feel lacking. AI teammates are underwhelming and often fail to contribute effectively to the mission. This makes solo play feel like a less enjoyable experience compared to the dynamic and collaborative nature of co-op.
Vehicle Controls: Many players find the vehicle controls cumbersome and unrealistic. The physics and handling of cars, helicopters, and planes feel clunky and frustrating, often detracting from the immersion.
Performance Issues: Even with a powerful PC setup, Wildlands can suffer from occasional stuttering and inconsistent performance, although patches have addressed some of these issues since launch.
Tonally Inconsistent: The game’s story and humor can be jarring at times. The attempts at satire and comedic elements often clash with the more serious and violent themes, making the overall tone feel inconsistent.

In conclusion, Ghost Recon Wildlands offers a great multiplayer experience with a massive open world, but its single-player experience, vehicle handling, and tonal dissonance may be off-putting to some. It’s ideal for players who enjoy tactical shooters in co-op settings.

This is one of my favorite games let me tell you why.

The Gist:
This game sees the player step into the shoes of Nomad, the leader of Ghost team. This time, the special forces group has been sent on a mission to Bolivia, as the combat element of Operation Kingslayer, a joint effort between JSOC and the CIA to take down the Santa Blanca Drug Cartel, who have created a narco-state. With the help of local rebels, the ghosts are tasked with dismantling the cartel piece by piece, through any means necessary.

The Good:
The story, although not entirely original, is still interesting enough to get invested in. It's more interesting than many of the cliched action movie plots that plague Hollywood in the current times. The characters are interesting, although a lot of the major cartel members don't really interact with the player at all. The characters of the other ghosts are also really fun, as they have lots of banter that shows how close they are as brothers in arms.

The game is set in what might be one of the best open worlds that Ubisoft has ever crafted. Its environments vary wildly by region, from snowcapped mountaintops to rocky deserts, from dense jungle to open salt flats. The world feels lived in as well. The world is populated by NPCs that have routines and schedules, and even when they don't really impact gameplay, they at least help create a superficial sense of immersion. None of the buildings feel out of place or copy-pasted, even the buildings that clearly reuse assets. Everything feels natural, and serves as an excellent backdrop for the events of the game.

The customization is top tier with this game. The faces and hairstyles are somewhat limited, but the gear selection is extremely in depth, with many options to choose from. From clothes to accessories, you can tailor your outfit to your specific sensibilities. Weapon customization is also extremely in depth, with many weapons to choose from, each with many different attachments available, which allows the player to tailor their loadout to their desired style of gameplay. The skill system also allows the player even more options to play the game their way.

The gameplay is what you'd expect out of the standard Ubisoft open world game. What sets it apart is the stealth sandbox element. The game's world is an extremely good playground to utilize different weapons and playstyles. The stealth feels satisfying, and the loud firefights have a sense of danger to them. There's almost no scripted events, either. Most of the things that happen in the game world are happening in-system. The gameplay loop of entering regions and reducing cartel influence within them is an extremely captivating element as well.

The Bad:
This game is not without issues. For starters the AI in this game is rather poor. Upon being seen, enemies will descend upon your location even if they shouldn't know where you are. Another thing that breaks immersion for me is how bodies are unable to be carried, and disappear after a certain amount of time. The open world gameplay can get pretty repetitive at times, as well. There is also a disappointing lack of options given to the player as to how to dismantle the cartel. The gameplay loop would be much more unique and satisfying if you got to pick how to remove each underboss from power.

The Verdict:
Overall, a decent military themed shooter whose problems can be tiring, but are ultimately overshadowed by the excellent gameplay and setting. If you're trying to decide between this game and its sequel, Breakpoint, just pick this one. It's a better use of not only your money, but your time.

A massive, open world, tactical shooter that can be enjoyed in single player or co-op with friends. 

The premise of the game is to play elite operatives dropped off in Bolivia with the purpose of dismantling the cartel. Customize your character with numerous customization options, collect guns and modifications, beef up your resistance forces. 

The game world is massive, but unfortunately it's not filled with much useful stuff. There is stuff to do here and there. Checkpoints, patrols, etc. Every region has a main boss which you are trying to get to. However, to get them, you need to first collect intel and weaken their resolve. This is done through missions which are unlocked by locating intel on computers, talking to informants, kidnapping cartel lieutenants, etc. 

This game is played in 3rd person mode, however, it is possible to change to first person when aiming down sights. The graphics are amazing. The world feels vivid and alive. When I first played this game I used to fly a helicopter everywhere and miss out on its beauty. Recently, I have been enjoying the company of my teammates while rolling through hills and valleys in normal vehicles and jamming to the propaganda radio stations. 

Like I previously mentioned, there is plenty of stuff to collect including supplies, which the resistance forces desperately need. Every enemy camp is going to have different quantities of supplies you can tag for pickup. Occasionally, there will be supply convoys you can hijack or transport helicopters you can hijack, etc. Supplies are used to upgrade various character skills. 

This game allows the player to mount and remove silencers on the go to make stealth approaches fun to play. It also provides access to binoculars to tag enemies and a drone to do the same with more efficiency. Night vision and thermal vision can be used to enable enemy spotting even more. While playing with AI teammates you can order them to select targets and then sync kill them to assist in quietly taking down multiple enemies without setting off alarms.

The further you progress into the game the harder it becomes. Small base camps become fortresses with sandbags, mine throwers, armored vehicles, sniper nests, light fixtures, signal jammers to prevent drone scouting, etc. 

All in all, it's a solid game and I do enjoy playing it. However, the campaign is nothing special and at the end of the day, it's more "meh" than anything. The game world is beautiful though. The design that went into it was fantastic. The guns are all cool and interesting to play around with. Character customization is satisfying, although there are plenty of micro-transactions if you want some of the cooler stuff.

The game has additional game modes to try including the infamous Ghost Mode, which allows you to replay the entirety of the game with the added difficulty of perma-death if you get killed. Better sit back and take things slow if you go that route. There are also PVP modes, but I have not given those enough time to warrant a fair review. 

If you are looking for a super competitive and fast paced shooter, this probably isn't it. But, if you are looking for an immersive world where you can create your agent and roleplay a highly trained operative that single handedly can debilitate an entire enemy base through high-tech tools and covert advantage. This may be just the game for you. 

Pros:
+ World Size
+ Graphics
+ Gun variety
+ Gun play (bullet drop/spread/effects/sound)
+ Cinematics
+ Options (binocs/drone/night vision/thermal vision)
+ Can drive vehicles (cars/boats/helicopters/planes)
+ Third person/ first person
+ Character Customization

Cons 
- Campaign
- Small scale PvP
- Vehicle controls
- Empty world
- Dumb AI
- Repetetive
- Microtransactions 

All in all, it's really not a bad game and quite fun. Definitely a pick up, especially on a sale.

育碧的幽灵行动荒野玩完了。不得不说这个游戏体现出了对现实非常好的反映。游戏中的四大行动部门基本上完整的考虑到了现实生活中一个毒贩组织的必要架构。每个部门的小首领也反映了哥哥行动的细节方面。游戏中的收音机看似只是一个好玩的元素，但是如果你仔细听一听他讲的英语就会发现其实和游戏剧情关联性极大。毒贩们反复给当地人民洗脑，反复宣传毒贩才是为人民生活谋福祉的组织。有时还对首领进行一些采访，又有时你完成了一个任务，广播里就会说某某某被抓了。体现的很真实。还有游戏打到一半的时候我在想为什么广播里不能播出一些反抗军的内容呢，果然游戏剧情就让你去找到广播电台的主播问他要来电台密码，然后就时常能在广播中听到反抗军首领充满激情的演说了。
 游戏中穿插的彩虹六号小队的剧情也是很有趣。这剧情看似是不相关，其实也相关。女鬼是巴西缉毒警察，玻利维亚是巴西的邻国，他跑到这里来也很合理。当然了这可以理解是育碧想做一个广告，“那里还有一个好的射击游戏，快去买呀！”
 游戏虽然结束了，但是结局也非常值得人思考。大使馆是谁炸的？是毒贩吗？答案是并不是，大使馆是美国特工炸的。为什么呢？因为这样我们才回去玻利维亚大力打击毒贩。因为这样他自己辛辛苦苦收集的情报才有价值。最后噩梦被抓了，他也供出了其他的毒贩头子。但是那样南美洲的毒贩贸易就终止了吗？也并不是，如果不能从源头上改变当地人的生活，不能从源头上切断毒品的需求，那么即便今天El Sueño surrender and even serve the americans to help fight cartel and drug use, tomorrow numerous can emerge. 游戏中完成任务的时候也多次提到：“你这么做当地人的生活可不好了。”为什么呢？因为你破坏了毒贩的生产系统那么许多当地人的就业就成了问题。前两天读到一些南美洲的人想要偷渡到美国要在墨西哥的落脚点现为毒贩打工才能赚到钱。恐怕育碧的游戏让我们认识到，即便是有神一般的部队的存在（你能无限次的复活还不是神吗？）你也不能从根本上解决这个问题。这也确实是这款游戏让人深思的地方。

With a large number of missions in total, but similar objectives, you CAN experiment with different tactics, weapon loadouts, etc.
It will become repetitive if YOU fail to think about how to better achieve the goals.
For example, "snatch" missions (where you take someone alive) can be done many many ways.
Eliminate all guards, eliminate no guards, with suppressors, without suppressors, alone, with AI team, etc.
But, if you use the same "recipe" every time you snatch someone then it will get boring quickly.
Therefore, the variety, or monotony, is up to you.  
The game supports a wide range of possibilities.

[h1] WHAT IS GHOST RECON WILDLANDS? [/h1]
Wildlands is a great big sandbox where you can tackle the missions any way you please, either using stealth or guns blazing, from land or sea or sky. It's basically Ubisoft's take on Narcos.

Wildlands is an open-world game in every sense of the word, with complete freedom of movement and frequent clashes with both cartel members and nefarious local law enforcement, which also happens to be extremely corrupt. You’re given total control to approach each objective the way you want, whether that means stealthily stalking a jungle hideout while sniping militants or driving a farm tractor into a military base and lobbing grenades at everything that moves. Sometimes stealth is necessary to survival, but other times doing your best impression of Rambo is not only extremely effective, but also a whole lot of fun.

[h1] COMPLETE CUSTOMIZATION [/h1]
The best part is that the cutscenes are rendered using your in-game characters, so watching my ponytailed gal talk shop with other deadly agents while gazing through a pair of shiny, pointless ski goggles really made the entire experience worthwhile. 

That level of customization extends to your weaponry. There are dozens and dozens of guns to find in the world and add to your loadout, and each of them has a number of different components that can be swapped out. New barrels, sights, scopes, triggers, grips, launchers, stocks, and other bits and pieces are littered throughout Bolivia, and if you’re a completionist you’re going to want to rethink things a bit. Oh, and each individual component can have its own color scheme, too, in addition to the full-gun paintjobs available to choose from. This is a very, very deep game.

[h1] WHAT'S THE GAME ABOUT? [/h1]
Like most of the Ghost Recon series, Wildlands throws you into a troubled, war-torn land that is absolutely overrun with bad guys who need to be dispatched as efficiently as possible. This time around the action takes place in the South American country of Bolivia. Plenty of artistic liberty has been taken with both the landscapes and politics of the region, but the game does its best to fit the story arc into something resembling modern-day world affairs. Thankfully, you’ll be too busy flying helicopters, rescuing rebels, and sniping heavily armed cartel members to care how well it pulls that off.

[h1] PROGRESSION IN THE GAME [/h1]
As you collect new guns and accessories and use them to take down terrible people you earn experience points which can then be spent, along with credits you get for aiding the friendly local rebels, on upgrades to your soldier. These can range from new abilities like a deployable parachute to more stamina and health. Many of the skills have several levels, but the skill tree itself is fairly short. That’s not really a drawback, however, as it allows any soldier to be good at just about everything, which is crucial during solo play. 

The sense of scale in Wildlands never ceases to impress, but that ambition can also cause some headaches. The world map is absolutely massive, and although the exact measurements haven’t been revealed, it’s clear that it puts Grand Theft Auto 5 to shame. That’s a heck of an accomplishment, especially when you get a glimpse of the variety of environments Ubisoft managed to cram into this make-believe Bolivia, There’s salt flats, jungle, desert, tundra, grasslands, and everything in between, with no loading screens or stops. Unfortunately, while the game looks really impressive, the framerate can get a bit choppy during particularly hectic scenes. Battling a dozen soldiers? Everything is smooth. Add in a couple of helicopter explosions, a few waves of reinforcements, and a herd of 30 llamas kicking up dust in the glare of car headlights and suddenly things start to slow down a bit.

[h1] TL;DR IS IT WORTH BUYING IT [/h1]
[b]ABSOLUTELY YES[/b]
There’s a reason while some fans and critics believe Wildlands is the best Ghost Recon game to date, as it successfully reinvigorated a dying franchise by returning to the tactical roots from which it came from and borrowing from other Ubisoft franchises. Like Far Cry and Assassin’s Creed, Wildlands gives its players options that suit a variety of playstyles. Fans can survey the terrain they’re in before approaching an enemy encampment in order to find the best way to take down everyone stealthily, or they can rush into an outpost with guns blazing.
[u]Diverse environments encourage fans to explore and experiment as they venture through the campaign solo or with a squad. Terrains help the franchise come alive in a way it hasn’t realized before and elevates the genre as a whole.[/u]

This game has had it's ups and downs. They had done a few updates that somehow broke the game entirely for me on several machines over time. There's lots of things about it that may be frustrating/grindy/greedy, but besides all that the game is really good. There's a lot of pros. I think it's really one of the most impressive games ever released. I should pick up the new one to see if it is half as good as this one but I haven't heard many good things, plus, there's so much to do in this game. 

    First of all, gameplay is king. Whether you are playing coop, solo with AI, or solo solo, the games mechanics are really good, and familiar to anyone playing similar kinds of games. The amount of player animations is great, and how those animations affect the flow of gameplay is incredibly well done. Controls are well done as well although precise aiming on controller really is a disadvantage as usual. It's not just about player actions tho, the ai mechanics are really well done as well. While some things are a bit wonky, this game and the latest farcry really handled AI companions probably better than anyone else. I wish they would have incorporated the AI's ability to drive and fly you like in Farcry, but the control over your people is done so well.

    You also have weapon customization done to a level of insane degree. What's great about it is the selection. You could be from 100 different countries and find you're favorite spec op weapon. There's a few OP, or underpowered weapons, that kinda prevent you from using what you want, but it's ok. What's compelling and torturous about it is you have to find the weapons and mods in the world, in various ways... with the exception of some that have to be unlocked either through cash or grinding... which is unfortunate, but I don't see a game this big getting made without some kinda monitization involved.

     I guess to close up, there's just a lot to do in this game, and I think the community will remain active for a while. While "tier" mode is a bit too unforgiving, the other modes are pretty damn compelling. It's Iron Man mode is really a lot of fun, with high stakes, but balanced depending on difficulty. Giving a reason to start over and go about the whole experience differently. I think the thing the game does best is giving the player just so many ways of approaching not just missions, but the entire story. It's a good game, and while I expect some other update in the future, I don't think it will be broken again.

There is soooooo much negative criticism surrounding this game, too much even. Some warranted, but mostly its all very knit picky. I think most of which came from a rough launch, but lets be real, if you buy a game a launch these days (even from some of the top developers) you're asking for trouble.

The story here is bland, but in context of playing a special forces operator it works fine. And once I immersed myself into the Bolivian world, I actually had a bit of fun hearing about all the different cartel members before taking them down.

The biggest draw here is the visuals. Even after a couple of years this is a stunning looking game, especially for the scale of the Bolivian map. I found it easy to get lost in the game-play because of the overall look and feel of the different “biomes” in-game.

The game-play of course is a massive departure from the originals. But it is so much fun! I played this a hell of a lot single-player and co-op, there was never a dull moment. Most criticism concerning the game-play can be mitigated by changing a lot of the settings, such as difficulty, highlighting enemy etc. Hell, even though I found the combat a wee bit easy, I did find it fun and challenging to try and stay as “tactical as possible”. 
Yes, there is a grind, but when the grind is fun with just enough variety between activities, it's not a bad thing. This game is all about “what you make it” at the end of the day.

Overall, don't come here for realism or a trip down Ghost memory lane. Come for some good old fashion “shooty shooty bang bang” fun, especially with some mates.

I don't see a lot of advertising for the the NPC culture of the world, or a lot of reviews covering it. It adds a beautiful and charming depth to the game. It took me many many hours to even realise they have their own little activities and responses. It all seems like meaningless chaos and destruction until you slow down enough to listen and watch.

Two examples:
The children sometimes play gun games with their hands as you run through a town to your next operation. It's a little dark and innocent at the same time. I wish I could join them sometimes just to take the pressure of the next mission off my mind.

I ran over a rebel once. They're not very smart so it happens sometimes. Apparently not to the civilians in the town. I was messing around in the town a bit and looked back to see a group of civilians around the dead rebel weeping and wailing over their fallen. I...don't really know why they included a mourning act for the NPCs. 

I started feeling a bit creeped out by these NPCs who had this secret...humanity. But not in the way that developers usually force the humanity of an NPC on a player (I'm looking at you Bethesda. Your NPCs need to STFU.), but in the background, in the aftermath, where a player is least likely to see it. It felt special to me. Like I was witnessing a part of the game not many people have.

Typical Ubisoft-like open world game. Why play it? Simple: the core mechanics are fun. It's fun to ride around. It's fun to sneak up to bad guys. It's fun when you ♥♥♥♥ up sneaking, alert them and they start shooting back. It's fun to open new abilities and use them, to open new weapons and new rides.

First of all, the visuals are remarkable. Including the mechanics from the older games of the franchise, like sync shots, one shot kill, cover mechanics, gun customization, using drones makes it more addictive. Character customization is over-emphasized other than taking cool snaps of them and the landscapes, with different conditions, using photo mode. The skill tree comes handy later on for taking down harder enemies and bosses as well as using allies for support. Making use of the environment to our tactics is well done. Vehicle mechanics are a bit sloppy, but aren't that bad at the same time. AI teammates on solo have pretty much no use other than reviving, having dialogues and for sync kills. The story is pretty straight forward, having to take down a drug cartel. But having it segregated into its own 4 separate operations, each with its own story involving half a dozen of characters is easier to grasp. Wish it had more Rainbow Six crossover missions and some Division connection. Sam Fisher mission is hell, having to not get detected nor kill enemies, only to kill them anyway and exfiltrate is hard and pointless. Trust me, playing that with friends is easier than AI, as that mission is needed to completed the game. The game felt more vivid and lively than what I experienced on The Division. The soundtracks are awesome and memorable. Even though it is possible to finish the entire game on Solo having to carry the team, Co-op is much more fun and reliable. Overall this game feels like a pretty strong and bold reboot for the franchise apart from Future Soldier.

[h1] Ghost Recon Wildlands Review [/h1]

Ubisoft has truly delivered an ultimate military shooter experience with Wildlands. I am a big time Tom Clancy fan and I have adored the games since I was a child. I remember playing Ghost Recon Advanced Warfighter as a kid and to play Ghost Recon again really hit me!

If you love tactical shooters and open world games then this is the perfect game for you. I must admit, the side missions can be repetitive, but while you are traveling on the map to and from locations they offer a more exciting ride. I often was side tracked by side missions, finding myself off course to complete one.

My favorite part of this game has to be the cross-over missions. I absolutely LOVED them. Each one hit me with major nostalgia. Fighting alongside Sam Fischer from Splinter Cell to running with Rainbow Six Siege. Fighting the Predator did throw me off a bit, but I thoroughly enjoyed it. I personally think these missions were more challenging then the main missions as well. 

Wildlands doesn't really have any non-lethal methods for enemy takedown, so stealth can be harder (especially for the beginning of the Splinter Cell Op with Sam), but as long as you remain quiet you can perform stealthy kills and takedowns, though honestly lets face it, I ran in guns blazing half the time.

I also love the story line very much. I don't always pay attention to lore, plot or story when it comes to games, but Bolivia and the Cartel intrigues me. I want to know more and nail more missions. Exploring Bolivia is extremely fun.

I have not put a ton of hours into the game yet, but I guarantee I will. I hope to buy the DLC too once I finish the rest of the game!

A big 10/10 from me! The game has a few minor issues I suppose, but it makes up for that. I am extremely satisfied and glad I bought this game when I did.

I highly recommend for you and a friend(s) if you enjoy tactical shooters. Just wait for a sale or buy from a third party (g2a, cd keys, etc)

Something about dismantling the cartel piece by piece in any order you choose, just adds to the overall experience and sense of achievement.

Graphics (9 of 10):  You feel like you're in Bolivia fighting the drug lords

Stability (0 of 10):  The game hard crashes my computer every time I try to run it.  After several hours of troubleshooting I no longer recommend this game.

Gameplay (8 of 10):  This is not a simulation shooter.  If you want an enjoyable arcade experience it is fantastic.  The vehicle steering is overpowering, good with a controller though. Vehicles have ungodly acceleration, good if you want a constant adrenaline rush, but being able to race, cross country... in a minibus is a bit silly.

Story and Progression (8 of 10):  There are a lot of levels of advancement for a variety of skills.  Many are relevant, though the advancement is ponderous at times.  The story is rich and varied with a clear plot and side plots.

Overall:

There's a lot to enjoy in this game, I'd go far as to say that it really is a blast sometimes. But other times it just really makes you question why you're still playing this game.

Starting out with Pros:
+ Sandbox is a huge playground
Possibly the largest open-world game I've played, and it's filled with a lot of fun side-activities and outposts to raid.

+ Fun stealth/infiltration style gameplay
It really feels like a puzzle game, where the pieces are your bullets, and the way to solve them is where you put those bullets. You have tons of toys to play around with and my personal favorite is the exploding drone. I just feel smart for successfully and quietly raiding a base. Or alternatively, blow everything up with C4, mines, and the drone.

The 'tactical' side of this game is mostly just interactions with your friends and marking out targets. It's still highly rewarding and enjoyable. Taking out generators and drone jammers to lower a base's defense is always fun. Removing strategic targets make you feel like a true commando in action. Plus if you play on singleplayer, you have a maximum of three free instant kills on selected enemies.

The support powers are also cool, it reminded me of Battlefield 2, the one from 2005 I mean, so they're not exactly new or groundbreaking but fun to play with nonetheless. And like BF2, the vehicles are also great fun, but most of the time you're going to want a helicopter more than anything else.

It's also just a huge laughter generator, especially with friends. So much ridiculous shenanigans and endless possibilities for unrestrained explosive fun.

+ Extensive character customization
If you want to look like your average The Division character, you can do that. Wanna look like a soldier that's all geared up? Yup. What about a dude on vacation with a polo shirt? That's all game. It's a shame this aspect is held back by one of the major cons, see below.

+ There's lots to do
People complain it's repetitive, then don't play the same game several days in a row. You get your money's worth activities-wise, just play in short-bursts with friends. Otherwise it will feel like a slog having to commute and doing the same types of missions.

+ Game just looks great
My PC has had its glorious days but even with modest settings, game looks really good. Most of everything is highly detailed, especially the outfits and guns.

+ Interesting lore and story
A super-powered drug cartel that bought out the government armed forces is genuinely a dangerous threat. Plus there are some colorful characters in there that intrigue.

As for the frustrations with Cons:
- There's no jump button or jumping of any sort
That means you're prone to getting stuck on the rough terrain or at the cliffside while you make your escape from the Bolivian armed forces. You have two options, you can one: kill yourself, or two: fast travel to a teammate. But that second option isn't always available when you're in combat.

- Direct confrontation is surprisingly not fun
Even with maxed out bullet resistance you still die in as little as 4 - 5 hits to your left pinky toe from a mile away. Enemies have extreme laser precision and have a better wall-hacking system that your supposed state of the art technology of tagging enemies. I get it, it's not the point, but there are times you can't avoid direct confrontation.

- Instant failure stealth missions
There's one particular mission I'm talking about, it's not the one with the mansion. You have to sneak into a heavily guarded base and meet with an agent. Simple right? Problem is, you're not allowed to kill any enemies, and you can't be spotted. It's instant game over. Fine, get lucky with RNG AI pathfinding, you get in and meet with agent. But then the next segment is guns-blazing, and as we've established, your armor is made of butter, and there are no checkpoints.

- Game is prone to crashing
Now I've tested this on three capable machines and all three of them have experienced at least 2 or 3 crashes. If you've played long enough, you're sure to crash more than 5 times.

- Frustrating bugs
There's a specific province with a specific mission where you need to rely on AI units to get into a van then guide you to the next part of the mission. My friend and I have restarted this several times on the beginning alone because the AI kept failing or getting stuck with pathfinding. There was even one time the AI got inside the van only to sit on the roof, THE ROOF OF THE VAN! (WHILE GETTING HIS ARMS STRETCHED ABNORMALLY).

There's another bug with the drone wherein if you get spotted and simultaneously use the detonate button, the drone won't explode, and you won't get your drone back until you reconnect to the game host. Sometimes you can get stuck using the drone until an enemy shoots you once. After activating Tier One, this bug happens a ton more frequently than you would expect, I heard it's a bug from 2017 and it still hasn't been patched out.

There's a separate bug wherein your drone payload flat out does not work but it will trigger the cooldown of that payload. This happens quite frequently and is equally frustrating. They won't patch this out, because a sequel for this game is coming.

There's a relatively uncommon chance for the coop session to become out of sync, causing players to not perform actions reflected on the client-side screen. There were two instances I got separated from my game host but at his screen he was flying the helicopter I was riding. So the one I was on appeared to be floating in mid-air with no sound, no animation, and no other player inside. Sometimes the player will reappear outside the helicopter and smash into the blades causing the heli to explode.

Do you like using grenade launchers? What about your game working consistently? You can promptly say goodbye to both if you do. Your grenade launchers have an extremely large chance of not working, you'll instead shoot a regular bullet, only after a three to five seconds later will they explode. You cannot use this attachment with intentionality. Again, old bug, not fixed.

Fairly often when joining a session, you will spawn in the middle of a firefight. And what have we established about health in this game? You're made of molten marshmallow. A single stray bullet can end the 4-man Bolivian tour group. I cannot for the life of me understand why it doesn't spawn you in a safer location.

- Uplay
Two clients running in the background for a video game and cloud saves. One of them is useless. It constantly stops working during updates, and conflicts with Hamachi. There's also a chance it won't sync your achievement rewards. Not to mention it's slower than a sloth. Yeah I think you've guessed what it is, it rhymes with pooplay.

- Microtransactions
I've got nothing else to add here. They are what they are.

- Super long loading times
Need to respawn right next your teammates in the same area? Wait 1 - 2 minutes. That's an eternity right there.

Conclusion:
I can't say this is something I can easily recommend, especially at full price and with its sequel coming out. This is my first shot at a Ghost Recon title, and I'm frankly disappointed.

This does not mean I hate the game. There are genuinely fun moments to be had when playing with a friend or a group of friends. But its problems are too large to ignore and they very quickly get in the way of everything. No amount of cool cameos from other titles and 80s references can save this game. Because for all the 'care' Ubisoft seems to show for this title seems to be the amount of loot types you'll get on random crates. Terrible unlock system, we don't deserve this, period.

If you really feel like getting it, wait for a big discount. Not that lame 20% off thing, I mean 60 - 75% off. Even then it's tough to kind of level the odds.

Recommended, but with major caveat — it is filled with extremely frustrating moments that only exist because of game mechanics. Probably the most enduring frustration of the game is the third-person perspective; it's impossible to smoothly sweep through a building interior because the first person aiming narrows the FOV too much and 3rd person over-the-shoulder has you seeing something different from what the player avatar and enemies see. This means that if you see an enemy and shoot, you might hit a wall or box or something that's in the way of the shot, but which you can see clearly. Conversely, sometimes you'll not be able to see an enemy, but the PC is in line of sight of the enemy despite a wall or object obscuring your view. Out in the open, it's rare and has little impact. Inside a building, it's almost as clunky as Arma.

The ballistics system is extremely dumb. As far as I can tell, the trajectory of all guns are the same, but the "range" statistic governs how fast bullets travel and how much damage is reduced. For short guns like pistols and SMGs, you can see the bullet go about as fast as a paintball would so you need to lead a moving enemy by about a foot to make a hit. Sniping is a chore because at 300 or so meters, the bullet will drop about 6 ft from point of aim. Just as well though, as the highest magnification in the game is 6X, which is a very modest magnification in the real world. It's a damn shame though, because the game has some excellent opportunities to play sniper. 

Another major recurring annoyance is the enemy shot spread. It's very narrow, even for enemies holding an SMG in each hand blasting in full auto. At lower difficulties, this isn't a problem because the PC can absorb hits, but at higher difficulties (which is required to get some of the collectibles) an enemy who sees you from 50 ft, alerted by a helicopter that inexplicably can see directly below itself, who blasts away with a full auto MAC-11, can quickly send you to the bleed-out stage. 

On missions that are setup to cause confrontation like that, it gets really old, really fast. 

Friendly AI is both overpowered and next to useless. They can be used to setup impossible shots which is helpful but cheesy, but they won't get your back in any way except to revive you after watching some gangster run up behind you and blast you in the back. It's really jarring to see 3 heavily armed teammates behind you, turn around, and then get shot by someone who ran right past those 3 heavily armed teammates. They have a magic stealth ability where they can walk right past enemies without being seen, but occasionally, during stealth-required missions, they'll somehow get detected and ruin the mission. These of course usually take the most time. 

Furthermore, there's an ending for if you get less than 100% completion, that's incredibly unsatisfying. If you get 100% mission completion, you can another ending, that's just as unsatisfying. Basically, it makes all the events feel like it doesn't matter, which is kind of a big deal for people who like the storytelling. And the end-game mission is completely stupid and makes no sense. I'll just say they really need to take Tom Clancy's name off of these games. 

In all, it was a fun game. Some really satisfying moments when you can pull off the plan in your head, but just as many really annoying and frustrating moments. For the most part I guess I liked the game, but for the annoyance and the hollow ending, I wish I hadn't taken the time to play it.

This game is enjoyable and worth a buy despite some flaws.

The story gets so hung up on good guy vs bad guy cliches that it cheeses you out of the milsim aspect a bit.

There is a lot to like about the gunplay, co-op functionality, gun collecting and base infiltration missions. Its easy to have a great time flying all sorts of aircraft and planning ways to approach different missions.

I would recommend skipping solo play and diving right into some co-op with other people. This is a good way to learn the ropes and level up. Plus it means you aren't the one stuck driving/flying everyone around all the time. Co-op players are often helpful and usually become new adds on your friends list. 

You will love this game if you enjoyed Phantom Pain as gameplay is similar, with better movement and gunplay. Speaking of which, it was a missed opportunity for Ubisoft to not allow some kind of option to build something with all these resources you collect. Sure, you level up your character and rebel assist options - but you never get an option to establish so much as a crummy looking FOB. You collect guns of all kinds along with their attachments, but you never have that hub to build on. I do understand that the concept is 'Ghosts', your character is aptly named 'Nomad', and this is not another sandbag laying simulator. Having the option to build in this world still would have been great.

You will also love this game if you enjoyed R6: Siege. They've incorporated some Siege characters into the game and their missions really mesh well.

The only other missed opportunity they had with this game was the PvP. 

Competitive modes are fun with their quickplay events and options, though you are limited to 4v4 GHOST matches. They would have been smarter instead to have built modes with bigger maps and higher player counts. The storyline of all out war breaking out in Bolivia could have easily passed and players would have had a blast duking it out over large areas in 50vs50 battles. I'd even settle for 20vs20, because that would at least allow all the PvP kits to truly shine with their utility options.

These are my criticisms and the game is still a blast worth placing many hours of time into.

If you take it as it is and got a friend to play it with, this title will give you some enjoyment. There is just one major factor that will ruin it all unless you have a sense of humor...

Speaking of driving...someone ship the development team to a 3rd world country. They really are completely out of touch with the kinds of cars being driven and the quality of roads. Come on, it's a joke.

That said, it's not a bad title. Just, understandable why it didn't get well received at first. If people paid full price for this, of course they'd be upset. If it's on sale, go for it. You'll likely enjoy enough out of it.

After playing 500+ hours, I'm still having a hard time formulating an opinion about this game.

On one hand, it's a fun and engaging tactical shooter that offers plenty of replay value, thanks to it's coop feature, wide range of character customization (so many role-playing options!) and a vast open world. It's a game that let's you make your own fun, and I think it's the main reason why I've played it so much.

On the other hand, I can't say it's a good Ghost Recon game. Ubisoft seems to be making a habit of pushing their flagship franchises through the same gameplay format, which is "big open world, filled with collectibles upgrades and boring codex entries". In short - Wildlands doesn't feel any different from Far Cry, Watchdogs, The Division or Assassin's Creed. It's a "You've seen one, you've seen them all" type of situation. I'd dare say that Wildlands has an identity crisis. It doesn't really know what it wants to be, especially with the Narco Road DLC (seriously, what the hell is even that?).

I expected this game to be a more casual version of ARMA, but it turned out to be a militaristic GTA, since most of the random players you'll come across will be playing it like that. No strategy, forward-planning or teamwork whatsoever. But if you find people, who actually try to approach each situation with strategy and cunning, you may have a lot of fun.

We all know the genre of this game, from the tags and description and also trailer and picture available right above here. So I'll just get to the point.
It's a Ubisoft game, so obviously, it still follows the Ubisoft formula. A bit parkour here, some broken scripts there and alike. Although is so much fun with your friends, it lacks the same experience alone [aka solo]. The AI are worse than ever and commanding them is also not useful and sometimes is even dangerous. The only useful command is sync shot that is not even balanced. If the selected target is in open area, no matter how difficult to reach, They can shoot from kilometers away; They don't even face the enemy or shoot straight at him when you look at them. however the AI teammates are cool and memorable characters, their dialogues are sometimes dark and hilarious.
The graphics....well, although the graphics are heavily un-optimized, the view of Bolivia is outstanding, I play on the lowest resolution [800x600 specifically] and graphics, the view still amazes me and I usually stop by to just watch the sundown or sunrise. The characters are very detailed and the field of view is also breathtaking.
Customization on the other hand, has its ups and downs. You are very limited in case of facial details, but the outfits options are massive, yet not enough. We can say it's better than Division in this case, but still it lack certain style of outfits or most importantly, haircuts. The outfits are great because they have no stats to limit you from how you want to look, unless some certain update accessories that will add new animations or stats. I can looks like a cowboy roaming around Bolivia, or I can be a USA infantry, and none of them change my health, stamina or damage.
There are lots of weapons available for you to use. Although the sounds or stats are not satisfying me [and many other], they are enough for you to choose how you play/improvise. you can be sniper, have a G28 with an HTI, or you can be a loud one, grabbing LMGs and Shotguns, or you can be silent, maybe even all of them in the same time. There's no restriction about what set of weapons you can grab. The game also has a very good and big set of weapon customization system; Dozens of skins with lots of different tools like Laser sights or muzzles.
The story has different aspects and stories but it's not a good linear, full of surprises story. It's really due to the fact of "Full Autonomy" promise they gave us. you can take down whoever you like in any order you like and in any way you like. This leads to freedom of play but a very meh story, since there's no connection between your actions except for head takedowns which will lead to El Sueno's reaction. Though you see every boss has its own story and origins, you won't find a very amazing story in it.
The gameplay which for some of you might be the most important aspect is like every Ubisoft games you [might] have played. Lots of bugs and broken scripts, and some annoying micro transactions. If you are looking for a real challenge, this game can put you to your limits. If you are just looking to slack off and have an easy gameplay, you are also in the right place. Turn of the tier and face the ultimate challenge in the game. although Tier mode doesn't look fair, it's a nice and rewarding challenge. Even turn off the HUD and get the full immersion out of it; Or you can just set it to arcade difficulty, and kill everyone like cutting the butter. The gunplay feels satisfying and fun and the variety of options really helps it, you have full freedom of engagement, jump over a fence, or go guns and blazing in the front door or even go far up a hill and takedown everyone with whatever sniper you like. Even though solo might get boring, it's a good way to get ready to play with your friends. No one will curse you if you screw a mission and you can patiently take your time and learn. Although the game offers Public Matchmaking, I don't recommend it to people who prefer stealth. Sadly there is no way you can customize what type of player you want to play with and most of the people [sadly] prefer direct assault over stealthy approaches.
and YES, the game offers PvP experience, however from where I am [which is middle-east and/or basically Asia], it's nearly dead and takes alot of time to join a match and you probably end up joining an existing match that has been going on before you join.

I have mixed feelings about Ghost Recon Wildlands. There are some parts that I really like and others that could be greatly improved. I'm going to start off with a general list of my pros and cons and go into more detail below.

Pros:
[list]
[*] Huge open world with a variety of different regions ranging from snowy mountains to jungles, swamps and deserts.
[*] Variety of weapon attachments to choose from (on most guns}.
[*] Different ways to approach missions.
[*] Character customization is okay. There is lots of clothing, vest, and headgear variety, but not many helmets.
[*] You don't need any DLC to enjoy the game.
[*] Co-op is fun with friends. I've only had bad experiences with randoms, but that's just me.
[/list]

Cons:
[list]
[*] The map feels empty of enemies, but there's civilians.
[*] Not much mission variety.
[*] Story is meh and you can see the ending coming from a mile away. There was only one twist that caught me off guard.
[*] The friendly and enemy AI isn't the smartest.
[*] Bullet velocity is pitiful, and the drop is atrocious. You can't shoot 200 meters away without aiming incredibly high.
[*] Most of the weapons and cosmetics are locked behind lootcrates / surprise mechanics.
[*] Vehicle handling is awful.
[*] There are still quite a few bugs.
[*] No new game plus.
[*] Daily challenges provides and endgame, but it's extremely repetitive and has you doing the same things over and over again.
[/list]

[b] World and Missions: [/b]

     The Map is absolutely stunning. There is lots of variation between the different regions and each offer their unique scenery. You have urban environments, jungles, forests, deserts, and snowy mountains. The game's version of Bolivia is so big that it takes a long time to drive from one end of the map to the other, which would be great if there was more to do. 

Don't get me wrong, the missions are fun to play, but that's it. Once those are done, there's rebel ops, special operations, collectibles and that's it. Post-game, all you can do is clear bases for fun. There's no enemies in the wilderness other than vehicle patrols and convoys on the roads, making the map devoid of enemy life anywhere but in bases.

The lack of a new game plus mode makes it harder to play the whole game again with what you've earned (outside of lootcrates). Missions (not rebel ops) aren't that much different. There's vehicle stealing missions, assassination/killing missions, capture missions, blow something up missions, gather intel missions and framing missions. The only variety is the enemies you fight and the location that the missions take place in. Often times, it feels like I'm doing the same thing, but in a different place. There are some different ways to approach missions like loud or stealth (for some of them), but there's also a choice on what direction you want to go to get to the objective, each offering their own pros and cons. That's about it. It's nothing like the level of choice they advertised during E3 a few years ago.

[b] Weapons: [/b]

      Weapons are unlocked by finding weapon crates scattered around the world, or by buying them with premium currency (you can get this for free if you work for it though). I think the weapons are alright, but it feels like you're shooting a paintball gun or something. The bullet drop is atrocious and travel time is insane and totally unrealistic. It's like weapons are zeroed to 50 meters, and you have to aim incredible high above the heads of enemies to hit them at 100-150+ meters. Long range sniping is really difficult without a friend to spot for you since enemies disappear after about 500-600 meters (unless you scope them in and walk backwards). Weapon customization extremely limited. I have no idea why it gets so much praise. Most of the attachments might as well be cosmetic, and there's no reason to run several combos.

[b] Customization and Lootcrates: [/b]

     You unlock a lot of the customization when you first play the game, but there are still quite a few things that are locked behind paywalls or grindwalls (crates and store bundles) I think what you start off with is great unless you want helmet mounted night vision or slightly better looking vests. The helmets are sad though. All you have is an Ops-Core FAST helmet and a High Cut helmet. The Ops-Core helmet can't even be brown because the colors on certain pieces of gear are so screwed up. Many of the camos are also off and extremely inaccurate to their real life counterparts. Some of them like AOR1 are so bright and look ugly on anything you put them on. No cosmetics provide any benefit or concealment. Camo doesn't even anything, and armor provides no benefit.

[b] Friendly and Enemy AI [/b]

     The AI in this game isn't absolutely horrible, it's just slightly above that. Your team AI takes out enemies and revives you most of the time, but Unidad (the game's heat system) can kill them so easily. You can upgrade them with skill points to kill enemies better and tank more bullets, but that's it. Their primary use is to do sync-shot kills for you, but even that is limited. They can't drive vehicles, and can't sync-shot enemies inside buildings or structures.

Rebel AI likes to run you over, but they can be good in a firefight if you fully upgrade them. Civilian AI also likes to run you over and jump in your stream of bullets. 

In terms of enemy AI, these guys all depend on the difficulty. When you're not being stealthy, Santa Blanca charges at you and sprays at you, and all of them have the same spotting distance (so snipers don't have more than a grunt). Tier 1 mode is a joke, making enemies become terminators. Essentially, they now have superhuman reflexes and pinpoint accuracy with two uzis from 300 meters away while you're in a fast moving vehicle going at an angle away from them. As for Unidad AI, these guys act somewhat more tactically, carefully advancing on your position, staying put and waiting for you to get out of cover, or spamming you with endless vehicles. These guys never stop coming and tier mode makes them Terminators too. Other than that, they aren't that smart.

[b] Bugs: [/b]

     Where do I begin?

[b] Final Notes: [/b]

     At the end of the day, I'm still going to have to give this game a positive rating. The world is nice, the missions are okay and this game is a blast with friends. Playing with minimal HUD on the maximum difficulty is also a great experience. This is certainly a good time waster but I would only recommend getting this when its on sale. Just remember that this game isn't for everybody.

    In all honesty, if you have a choice between this and Ghost Recon Breakpoint, go with Breakpoint. Most of the negative reviews are extremely out of date, and a lot of the issues are fixed. It's like Wildlands (with a choice between gear score enabled or disabled), but with improved gameplay mechanics, vehicle handling, and enemy variety and life. You can get it relatively cheap on sale, and there's loads of great content. Just know that the story isn't that good, but the open world is.
