[h1]Ghost Recon Wildlands, a very bad and unoptimized experience:[/h1]

I've been a fan of the Ghost Recon series by Tom Clancy for quite a while now (generally a Tom Clancy Fan boi).

I used to play Wildlands for the first time back when it had a free weekend, and my experience was actually really good, but not having the time or motivation at that point to buy the game I left it off with 12 play hours.

Now as it was on sale I went back to it and decided to buy it.

That was a mistake.

The game wasn't what it used to be, already bugs like vehicles glitching out and exploding in the intro cutscene or a helicopter visibly spawning in (this wasn't the worst though) gave me some bad thrills. It was after the first cutscene where the horror began. Instead of taking one of the standard giving vehicles I went straight ahead and stole me a good ol bike.
Which happened to immediatly make me fall through the map and having to restart.
Overall vehicles are just a janky mess, the controls are very nice, but the physics... Dear god... A bike wheel hitting a small gravel stone will result in your bike reaching a height of about 20 meters in an instant. Luckily without damage, as the damage system is really weird.

And if we already start talking about damage, the damage models of the vehicles are... weird to nonexistential. I managed to blow up a van just by shooting straight at it's window that refused to break.

The AI magically can find you when you enter a proximity, they don't care about dead bodies of their comrades laying around. 

Stealth is really meh, action play is even more meh... With the AI just seeming either confused or unable to navigate when I'm attacking the base is really a moment killer.

Did I start talking about the grind yet?

No?

Well, there's [b]alot[/b] of grinding in this one. If you don't have the time like I do, you should stay away from this as the grind is necessary to progress further in unlocking weapons and accessoires.

I could keep this rant up for quite some time, but to help [b]YOU[/b] alias "the buyer" I'm just going to tell you this straight away:

If you got friends to play this game, and alot of time, and you don't judge gameplay mechanics and details too much, this is your game, you can get some good time gone with it.

On the other side, I can not recommend to buy it.

If you are also looking for a possible stealth game that features coop, (also a Ubisoft title) I can only recommend taking a look at Watch_Dogs 2. It may not meet the requirement of tactical espionage but is going to give you a good story without alot of grind and really good gameplay.

They are JUST ASTONISHING, the graphics of this game are really one of a kind and if you are someone who seeks these kinds of things, this game is definetly for you! 
...........................................................THE GAMEPLAY .............................................................
Personally, I LOVED the gameplay as much as I loved the graphcis of the game .. I think the game aims to make you enjoy its gameplay no matter which style you choose to play it with , weather it was stealth, or all open chaos, it's always great ... here are some headlines I liked about the gameplay .
-The Stealth : Most of the time stealth is optional, you can use a drone to mark enemies, followed by killing or disabling your them with some perfectly done tactics!
-The Kit : This part doesn't differ from other games that much .. From your inventory , you can some sort of .. dissemble your weapon to replace specicifc parts such as scope, grip and stock! .
The game also gives you the ability to fully costumize anything in your kit weather it was your main firearm, or your sidearms .. Or your charachter himself .. 
The skill tree : I don't think there is anything particularly special about the skill tree, it's just like any other game skill tree :) .

.............................................................THE STORY ..................................................................
Although the story is not professionally written and is rather very "classic" I'd say , I still managed to really enjoy it thrughout the game .. It's fairy acceptable but not the best. 

.............................................................THE CO-OP ...................................................................
I would say this game really focuses on co op ... Each player can even do seperate mission from the other player .. So "for example" if your farming some resorces .. you can make the best of it if your co op player(s) each do seperate resourses-rewarding missions! and even in the same mission, You get multiple oppertunities to fit your style!

Overall, my experience with this game has been amazingly positive. The various difficulties are well-balanced to appeal to someone of basically any FPS experience, the world looks great, and between the ridiculous, saints-row-esque driving mechanics and the tendancy of enemies to spawn every 25 feet, along with the massively varied terrain, this is an open world game that doesn't struggle nearly as hard with "dead time" as most others I've played. The map is utilized to its fullest extent, as well - the few open areas of nothing still serve a purpose in some way, shape or form, even if that's just making a potential shortcut completely ridiculous to try and attempt.

That said, the game DOES need to be played with friends, and it DOES need to be played tactically to be enjoyed. Playing solo, the game sticks you with an annoying-ass AI team you can't turn off. Playing with randoms, you're probably either going to die every few minutes, or run over everything in the goofiest way possible. The game shines best when taking a slow, methodical, more roleplay-ish approach - identifying enemies, strategizing approaches, and working in tandem with your buds to cut down bad guys as quietly and methodically as possible.

My only real qualms with the game lie in limitations of the formula more than anything else. After a few dozen hours, you start to realize that there are only a few guns really worth using - the only real variety in your firepower is in the magazine size and effective range, and outside of the few best-ofs, "weapon variety" generally means "mediocre in slightly different ways."

Additionally, although the game provides a wonderfully refreshing, unrestricted freedom in how you approach basically any scenario, with very few (if any) mandated approaches to any encounter, the game could do for some more creative gadgetry to help you exploit that freedom to its fullest extent. Using the current selection of grenades, mines and other misc. doodads typically feels suboptimal for most scenarios.

Finally, like all Ubisoft open worlds, the game does tend to drag on a bit towards the end. Although the varied environments help keep things interesting, there is a point around halfway (25-30 hours) where you start to realize you've seen it all. In hindsight, I do wish that the developers had chosen to cut about the last 4th of the game away and instead use those resources to concentrate the remainder.

That all said, this is hands-down one of the best tactical shooters of the past 5-10 years, and the best tactical co-op experience I can remember. Would recommend to anyone looking for a good time with a pal.

Loading times are absolutely horrendous, but I guess that's what comes with an open world game. Still think Ubisoft could've done better to decrease the loading times when fast travelling, failing missions, dying etc.

TL;DR It's a decent game, I don't recommend getting the game at full price, wait for a sale and you'll be able to grab it for ~$20. ~Meaningless weapon customisation
save for magazine size, suppressor and scope, all other attachments just affect the stats of the weapons. More damage, longer range, more handling. In Tier Mode, you can upgrade your weapons but only the damage. But that honestly exists because the enemies have increased health. There are no other upgrade options. So why have that option at all? Why not keep the enemy health the same?

Some guns can shoot through brick walls. Some cant. Thats fine. But sometimes even the ones that can shoot through brick walls cannot shoot through sheet metal. Or a certain tree branch. To basejump, you need to need to sprint off the edge while holding down the climb button. while you are in freefall, if you press forward you dive stright down. So what happens when you sprint off the edge is that you dive straight down to your death because you were holding down the forward key and didnt let go of it immediately when you jumped off.

Vehicles take damage from everything. They take double damage from being shot in the tires. They take half damage from shooting the windows. Either case, they can be triggered to explode if you have depleted the vehicle health enough.  Helicopter I am riding in can be brought down if  a drone runs into the propeller. APCs can explode just from being shot with assault rifles.

I've played Ghost Recon Wildlands for near 150 hours at the time of writing this review, and I can say that it is definitely a must buy for those who like a more casual spin on combat sims. Ghost Recon Wildlands underpins its intriguing story about a Bolivian Cartel led by a nihilist with a god complex through superb customisation, both cosmetically and practically, along with an in-depth breathtaking environment which never fails to impress. Like some of my other reviews, I like to outline pros and cons then summarise them nicely at the end on why they justify a recommendation. So lets get into it!

Pros - This part lists the positives of the game and parts which I felt highlighted this game's ability to shine.
- Graphics are very well done.
- Environment boasts diversity and looks stunning!
- Codex and journal entries about Bolivian folklore, legends and history. (I found lots of it very fascinating)
- Process of dismantling a cartel seems well thought out and logical. 
- Customisation (Weapons) Weapons can be customised in such a way to suit a variety of playstyles. 
- Customisation (Cosmetics) You can customise what you wear throughout the game, some of which offers benefits such as the Optical Camouflage backpack, or the Predator Biomask offering infrared vision which is arguably better than thermal. 
- Adding side missions. Mainly nods to other Ubisoft titles, but I loved the Predator. 
- Kidnap people and put them in the boot of your car...

Cons - This is where we look at where the game falls short and feels somewhat like a missed opportunity in my own opinion. 
- Lack of air and sea vehicles, somewhat too much emphasis on land. Detracted from the environment diversity in some ways. 
- Loot boxes, no matter what these will always be a negative, this really took something away from the progression in the game and I felt that maybe cosmetics and weapons unlocked in these could have definitely contributed to the end game. 
- With a game like this where some missions require stealth or to be done in a certain way, multiplayer with randoms is not a good idea, best just to do them with AI teammates then go to multiplayer when you're not doing anything. 
- Terrible end game, get all the perks, complete the tier system, finish the campaign and you're done. I felt there really wasn't much to work towards. There definitely lacked some incentives to playing the tier system. (The tier system is a level up process which begins after you have finished the normal levels).
- DLC wasn't all that good either, just re-used content, with different enemies and more people to kill. 
- Changes to the environment based on your progress through dismantling the cartel and taking on the Unidad paramilitary were pretty much nonexistent. 

Summary - Overall I felt this deserved a recommendation as I felt the environment it drops you into with the turmoil, fear mongering and even civilian attitudes towards CIA operatives made it feel very alive and makes for great role playing! If anybody remembers the Crackdown games, which much like Half-Life, we will never see a third, reminds me of this. It is definitely worth picking up if you enjoy the idea of being one of the four most dangerous people alive, three of which are on your team. 

Thanks for reading! :D

- Driving is baddddddd, very slow, and feels like an after thought. It quickly becomes replaced with flying.

- Not optimized (only uses about 60%-70% of my CPU, 90% on one GFX card and 50-60% on the other) and I only get around an average of 60FPS on low settings. WHY IS THIS A THING!? Other thoughts: 
This game is a smash of Assassian's Creed, Just Cause, and a hint of Ghost Recon in one. Unfortunately, it doesn't work very well in the larger gameplay scheme. AC and JC are known for being grindy and repetitive, but then you combine the two, and it becomes super grindy (not in the fun way).

Wildlands is a phenomenal game with a decent story, outstanding gameplay, and a very well thought out late-game progression system. If you want a good "tactical" shooter that can be played with friends and has some of the best graphics on the market right now then Wildlands is for you. 
If you are looking for a game with more than surface level content, look elsewhere. The PVP is stale and dry with combat being repetitive and overall lacking in design. The "bosses" have no real challenge as they fall just as easily as any other enemy lacking any real flair or challenge. I killed once boss by grabbing a .50cal and sniping him from outside the entire base, waited until the enemies died down, then completed the mission without breaking a sweat. Turns out it was supposed to be a high-octance fight, sometimes railroads can be helpful. 

Overall, this game gets a solid 7.5/10 for me. It has everythign I want out of a game but a good PvP system, which is honestly a very minor complaint.

Microtransactions and anti-consumer practices coupled with a Dev team that has no passion for the realism or authenticity make this a relatively hard title to recommend.

The core gameplay is competent but lacks any amount of serious tactical depth. It's missing core components that add to a realistic tac-shooter - minimal squad commands, cosmetic only customization, non-dynamic campaign or enemy AI.

It's "Freedom" is meaningless...your actions have NO weight in the game world - the trailers fabricated it. All mission outcomes and objectives are Scripted...you just choose whether you shoot your way in or sneak in. If you've played any of the Far Cry games, you've played Wildlands.

I've sunk 300+ hours into the game - mostly because I roleplay (as much as the game allows) and spend a ♥♥♥♥ ton of time playing Barbie with the customization available (Which is admittedly cool). But do not let it be an indicator of how much I like the game...I've often spent hours on a title which isn't much fun, but I tinker around in it...so it's a personal idiosyncracy.

Do not purchase this game. I'd recommend you wait for a serious price drop next year....and even then, the obnoxious monetization practices in the game do not deserve your time or money.

Cons:
- Repetitive gameplay after mid game onwards
- Not made clear to new players on what to do next. Basically you can do any mission anytime you want. And sometimes you've got to unlock missions by getting Major Intels or exploring new regions. So new players might get lost if they're not used to these kind of objectives.
- Enemy AIs are not the best. They tend to be either really dumb, or really accurate when shooting, which makes them pretty predictable once you've gotten a grip on them and how they react.
- Stealth isn't exactly the kind of stealth you'd get from games like Metal Gear Solid. You can't hide or move bodies. It's more of killing when the enemy is away from other enemies, then the body disappears in a while, which makes the "stealth" really easy to execute, especially when you have max drone battery life (infinite duration) to mark targets and sync shots with your AI team mates.
- Sometimes camera angles can be bad.
- Sometimes saving onto UPlay Servers will fail, so don't do that.

Here's my tips to all new players:
[spoiler] Get drone with Explosives, then max out Battery life and Range. This can help you take out Mission Targets, Target Vehicles, or basically anything that requires you to kill or destroy. I accomplished many of such missions simply by flying the drone to the target and detonate, no effort at all and enemy AIs are pretty much blind to the drone unless its super close to their face.[/spoiler]

This game is kinda like if rainbow six / splinter cell (blacklist not chaos theory) had a baby with grand theft auto. 
Really neat open world with two main different enemy factions, and you can run and gun or stealth every scenario that you find yourself in. The open world adds a whole different layer of tactical fun, as you have the ability to approach any area you're about to infiltrate from any side, and if things get too hot you have lots of bolivian forests, buildings, vehicles, etc. to run off to and hide in. 

The weapons system isn't perfect in the way that it isn't true to life, but the customization is fun and unlocking items in the different areas of the massive map of bolivia really adds a fun element and a reason to play. 

There's an ability tree with lots of unlocks that add extra skills and items for your character to use, and none of it is pay to win which is a massive plus and almost a surprise in 2018. 

They teamed up with 5.11, so if you're into tacti-cool stuff IRL they might have some of your real gear to deck your character out in. 

The in game purchases are for the most part aesthetic and are in no way necessary, which is a very welcome bonus after playing stuff like siege where they force you into it. I'm very welcoming of this kind of purchase model, but even more welcome is the fact that there are less purchaseable items than items you have already or get by playing, and on top of that a lot of the purchaseable items are really dumb looking IMO which really provides no incentive to buy them. 

If it's on sale and you're into tom clancy games, buy it. You won't be disappointed.

[u][b]Pros:[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Good open-world design and size. Immersive environment from the start.
[*] Possibility of configure the desired gameplay style (from Hardcore with practically no HUD to something more Arcade).
[*] Varied character, inventory, and weapon part customization.
[*] With friends and good communication, it greatly enhances the immersion, and you can lose yourself in the game for hours.
[*] Configurable allied AI if one day you decide to continue the single-player campaign.
[*] For Side-Mission Hunters, the content guarantees many hours of gameplay, with nice surprises from other franchises.
[*] I highly praise the intention of bringing an arcade tactical style to an open world with an easy learning curve. The influence of ArmA is noticeable in certain aspects, and the idea of ​​bringing it to a less tense and complex setting, like a MilSim, is welcomed. If there's one feature to remember Wildlands by, it's this one.
[/list]

[u][b]Cons:[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Within a few hours, the repetitive pattern of the missions becomes apparent.
[*] Ubisoft. Not only because of what this company and its reputation represents with micro transactions and bloated menus in its games, but it also forces you to launch the Uplay launcher every time you run it from Steam.
[*] Sometimes, the immersion can be broken by the cheap lore of the missions; at times, the antagonists are bizarre stereotypes, and I wonder why it's named after Tom Clancy. Definitely don't play it for the story.
[*] The enemy AI is somewhat broken in one respect: when your presence or someone in your squad is detected, the entire settlement/facility immediately telepathically knows the location. It breaks the logic, but I recommend using it as an extra difficulty level to emphasize stealth.
[/list]

[h1]Decision:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Overall, recommended. It's worth the purchase, and if you get it on sale, it's a great value for money/hours of entertainment.
[/list]

Ghost Recon: Wildlands  is one extensive open world game. If you thought Grand Theft Auto 5 was the mother of all open world games, then this is even bigger, if not the biggest currently. The game developer, Ubisoft, has managed to get the environment spot on whether it’s the mountains, jungles, swamplands, desert, small rundown towns, salt flats or lakeside resorts. The graphics are so realistic that you feel that Ubisoft has managed to recreate a Bolivia of their own.

PvP mode is called Ghost War  It plays out as a third-person, 4v4 tactical team deathmatch, where you only get one life per match (unless a teammate is able to revive you) in best-of-three games.

Team deathmatch sounds like a really simple mode, but each game in Ghost War feels tactical and plays differently than the match before it. Matches often play out slowly, and you might find yourself going prone in tall grass on several occasions to listen for enemy footsteps. The maps are pretty open with varied terrain, so you might have some close-quarter combat inside buildings or long range fights across desert or jungle biomes.

It's a must-have game if you're a Ghost Recon fan or a shooter.

There's a way to play this game incorrectly. By rushing into every enemy outpost guns blazing you're limiting the experience that you can get. Story: Weak. You'll be hunting down and killing cartel members so you can hunt down this one bald guy. Not that the story matters in this kind of game anyway!

Vehicles: Oh boy. The driving physics are hilarious! Cars feel like they're constantly floating and sometimes you'll crash with your bike and fly 50 meters forward. Helicopters are pretty great though.

Sounds: The voice acting is hilariously bad. Your character will scream "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!" on the brink of death. Very emotional. Also the weapon sounds aren't very impactful but the silencers make each gun sound pretty cool.

Graphics: Actually a very nice looking game if you play on the highest graphics! The open world is very detailed which you can truly appreciate.

Repetition: I, for one, don't find this game that repetitive. If you rush through every mission with the same weapons and with no strategy whatsoever, then yes, you'll find yourself irritated fast. Change your loadout, customize your character, USE THE DRONE. Utilize all the different things the game offers to you, please!

Overall: Wildlands is a game that stealth fans will like. The game isn't really meant for aggressive rushing. There are no unique mechanics that'll make this game special but when you take out an enemy outpost without anyone realizing, you'll feel like you've really accomplished what the game aims for in the first place.

Different title, same old Ubisoft. My review is completely on solo play only because I cannot find anyone to play with online. Maybe its my region so I cannot comment much on the co-op part.

Wildlands puts into a remote country where it is governed or ruled by some really bad guy. This particular bad buy has lots of ally/lieutenant and also happen to have bought off the police, leaving a "handful" of locals trying rebel against the bad guys and you are there to help. Sounds exiting? Lets continue shall we. 

The world/map is huge and they are divided into sub areas. Each of these areas are pretty similar and your mission is to lure the supposed person-in-charge out and dispose of them. In order to do so, you need to complete a number of mission. These missions are relatively the same. Sneak or go gun banging in and do/kill/grab something/someone. Then in each area are also some some side quests, well the same side quests like defend an area, flip some switchs, kill someone or steal some vehicle. These are always the same in each area. 

Your character has tonnes of arsenal in your dispose and you are always accompanied by 3 other A.I. They are quite useful in a way as they cannot be detected by the enemies and you can even upgrade them to be more lethal or mark enemies for them to take out simultaneously. Of course, best of all, they never seem to be able to fall in battle, run out of ammo and revive you when you fell.

While steering or piloting a vehicle, your companies are the only attack options as you cannot shoot while driving with the attack copter as an exception. Its the only vehicle you can pilot and attack at the same time. There is a plethora of guns around this time. Each gun is customizable except for the unique variant which comes equipt already with certain parts. Weapons and attachment parts can be unlocked by progressing through the game, completing certain quests, finding collectibles or buying cases through in-game store. Yes, microtransaction exists and you can also purchase certain boosts to add some edge to your game.

Weapons works pretty great in Wildlands. You can feel the difference when handling each weapon and they don't feel so plasticky. Ultimately, you will feel like trying different weapons and find those that you prefer most. Wildlands also has bullet drop so those long range combat is a little more fun.

Enemy A.I. also seem to get an upgrade. At close or far range, they can be quite a threat be cause they take cover pretty well now but most of the time its because their quantity can be overwhelming. 

The open world, at first glance is quite beautiful. Lush vegetation, mountains of jungle and islands. You have villages, enemy bases and towns all around. You also have fixed enemy spawns in certain locations and fortified enemy areas. But, these areas are bare minimal. There is nothing much to do and the buildings are all similar including the collectibles locations. You can find 2 exact same building in 2 similar locations and surroundings. Civilians randomly spawns to make places feel populated and livelier but mostly, they just seem to be zombified A.I. and don't do or react much. There are no animals except for some birds flying around so forget hunting. Not sure if that is a good or bad thing in a Ubisoft game.

The game currency is depicted to be food, salvageable parts, medical supplies and oil rather than actually currency. You can find these things lying around in game. Collecting them allows you to purchase upgrades in addition skill points earned. You will find escorted trucks that you can rob from the enemies. The spawn is random but the location and route is always fixed. They can prove to be a challenge at first but once you find out the way, then it is always the tactic.

That covers Wildlands mostly. Go to a an area, kill a bunch of enemies the way you prefer it. Do some quest and collect some stuff and proceed to the next area and repeat the same thing all over. In order to unlock the locations of collectibles in the map and also missions, you need to interrogate an enemy leader or pick up some intel. You always need to do this 5 times to completely unlock all locations and missions. Best part is, these person/intel are always in the same place. I picked up an intel, quits the game and logon again and the item is right at the same location again.

Wildlands can be fun even when playing solo. Gun fights can be tough. Sneaking and clearing enemy bases can be satisfying but unfortunately, doing the same things over and over without much rewards and just for the sake of progressing the story can be tiring when the story itself is plain, barren and simply. You don't even get introduced to your companions yet alone knowing their story. So much for bonding. 

Vehicles handling is one of the biggest part the game can improve. To be honest, they handle like vehicles in GTA: Vice City. Because you cannot shoot while driving, ultimately, the first thing you do when logging in is finding an attack copter.

Wildlands feels a lot like a white washed Ubisoft game. Wrap with a different paper, tweak it a little and you get this but after you unwrap the paper, it becomes a disappointment quickly.

I disagree with this game being originally advertised as a very multiplayer focused game. Yes, it is enjoyable with multiplayer, but I played the story solo with just me and the three AI you get in your squad and I thoroughly enjoyed it.

The squad AI: The squad AI is actually very good. Occasionally, yes, they can do dumb things when in hectic situations, but overall they are tactical and easily controlled with the in-game orders you can give them.

Enemy AI: The enemy AI is very believable. If you miss a shot from a surpressed weapon, they hear it go past them, and if you aren't quick enough they will shout out and alert everyone else, instead of like in some games where they investigate on their own like idiots.

Enemy Characters: The characters within the cartel are believable, whether they are deluded by the Cartel's religion or in it for the money. If you kidnap someone to interrogate, there isn't any of the ♥♥♥♥ in action films where a simple mercenary will be tortured beyond belief before giving intel. You put a gun to their head and they take it seriously. Death is taken seriously and I definitely appreciate that. Gives it a more realistic feel.

The story: I personally loved the story. It's a very realistic situation with realistic characters done in a fun and tactical way. It is very satisfying working your way through the cartel, ruining their smuggling, security, influence and production wings and seeing it fall apart piece by piece. 

The Stealth: Very fun and very easy to ♥♥♥♥ up, which I liked. It meant you had to think more of what you were doing so that you wouldn't be seen or heard.

All around, a very very good game that i had a tonne of fun with, though it is a little pricey due to it being under the Tom Clancy franchise. If on sale, 100% buy it.

I think this is a very underappreciated game. I've heard that in the past it had a lot of problems, but I think when I played it, the game ran smooth and I only had one minor glitch happen to me.

The story is very good, which is to be expected when you put the original author's name in giant letters on the name of the game. I especially loved the way storytelling was done, I was always eager to get the next briefing video about a cartel boss, and seeing your actions have an effect on the cartel is very nice. Loved the atmosphere of the whole thing being a secret operation, but it was kind of ruined by the fact that suddenly the cartel knows that there are exactly four American agents running around killing people, would've been nice if they were confused by the stuff.

Some people say that the world is empty and dull, which can be true, if you're daft enough to not use helicopters to move around since it is a giant place with a lot of quiet roads. There's a lot to do though and taking out all the bosses is, while in the end a bit arduous, rewarding and enjoyable.

But in the end, the combat is where this game shines. Sneaking is fun and being undetected is rewarding with the sync-shot system and scouting before going in. The rebel scouting also helps a lot to make it more fun to infiltrate places. You're outnumbered in most cases, so it's pretty nice to be shot in the face or forced to retreat if you've put yourself in an awkward situation. 

I definitely recommend the game, I got it on sale myself, but I enjoyed it so much that I could even consider buying it full-price.

REVIEW >>>>> I've really enjoyed this game: it's the best looking game I've played. Bolivia is stunning. The varied provinces, and dynamic weather and day cycle create unique visuals, and the feeling that you're actually there. 

The gameplay is what you expect from a ghost game: you approach a mission area, scout out enemy defenses, and choose how you wish to engage, whether it's stealh, ambush, or full on assault, and you're given a fair amount of tools to do this. The varied geography, enemy bases, encampments, and mission objectives make for interesting play. Also, the open world is great for CO-OP. It's the kind of shooter I used to fantasize about playing when I was a younger.

Also, you're given a lot of options for customizing your avatar, which is a fun little bonus I didn't expect. Makes your avatar really feel like yours.
 
There are problems, but overall it is a good experience; similar, yet different, to MGSV. I hope they make a sequel to this game set in a different location.

COMPLAINT >>>> The micro transactions are really obnoxious: for example, I completed a sidequest to unlock a bigger clip size for my assault rifle, only to find out that it doesn't actually unlock until I spend $15 on the "assault rifle clip package." You're given a clip size of 20 to start, and in order to get "medium" (30 bullets), and "large" (50), you have to spend a significant amount of real money on such a little thing. And that's just for assault rifle clips. You also have to buy the clip packages for other types of weapons if you want them. While this isn't game breaking, it is REALLY petty, and gives an advantage to players at higher difficulties. I hope gamers will refuse to indulge this kind of money grubbing by not spending in the store.

I enjoyed this game. I can see why a lot of people didn't. It's repetitive, simplistic, the AI is terrible, the game can be buggy/glitchy, and the world overall seems a little dead and scripted. Despite all that I enjoyed playing the game for an hour or so between doing other things, racking up almost 70 hours when I completed all the missions. I liked the huge range of customisable weapons. I liked choosing different loadouts for my different play styles. I enjoyed the Predator mission which thereafter gave me the creeps whenever I walked into a jungle. I liked trying to be stealthy then have something go wrong, and have to shoot my way out. 

Ultimately, if they put out future games like this I would keep buying them.

That being said I did buy it on sale for $23 so that's ~33 cents per hour of gameplay - this probably skews my overall view. Had I have paid full price I might have been disappointed by the fundamental weaknesses such as the weak AI and repetitive missions.


Improvements wishlist 

Stronger AI: rebels would be standing around with cartel members and soldiers and not be shooting one another even though we are in the middle of a shootout. AI-Squad members constantly getting hit by trains. Rebels won't free other rebels who are locked up in cages in enemy bases while we're storming said bases - they rely on me to do it.

Enemy mechanics: enemies seem to spot you from far away and have pinpoint accuracy, even with heavy machine guns. 

World seems dead: I'm not saying it has to be GTA V, but it's hard not to compare it to GTA V, a game which you can drive around and just explore the world and watch events unfold between NPCs. Wildlands has nothing like that - it's a beautiful world that you just rush through, either trying to get to a place, or trying to complete a mission.

Missions: more variety. The side/rebel missions being the same convoy tag etc are great and I wouldn't necessarily change these as they're fun and they provide quick side quests when you don't have much time to do an actual mission (though they could add some variety such as convoy destroy, rather than tag). The main missions do need more variety, and not just in what the objectives are (kill/destroy/take/follow etc), but the actual content of the mission and layout. There is certainly some variety but it feels a little cookie-cutter by the end of it. It was fun going through underground facilities or through mansions but there just wasn't enough of these different missions. I think of games like Hitman, where you're following a target through a crowd of civilians and, sure, you can kill the target and his henchmen in front of everyone and risk killing civilians, or you can choose to follow him to a secluded spot, or engage in some kind of distraction. Wildlands doesn't need to be that technical, but there are all kinds of other games the designers could have drawn inspiration from and they didn't. 

Vehicle variety: vehicle models were limited (and people NPCs too for that matter). There was only one type of supercar, a handful of trucks and vans, sedans, 3 differnt helicopters (albeit with different weapons loadouts), a couple of different bikes. Would have been nice to have more variety. Also, this mighting be asking a bit much, but I would have liked to customise my own car and helicopter - they could have added more grind-missions for the player to accumulate points to then spend on vehicle upgrades. (in all honesty though with Bolivia the way it was depicted with long winding roads and an overall crappy driving experience offroad - I stuck to helicopters to get around whenever I could and never drove cars - planes were horrible, bikes were an okay to dash over mountains to get to missions).

Again, despite all this I did thoroughly enjoy the game and recommend it.

The game's  biggest flaw its its repetative nature. Gameplay summed up is photograph a piece of paper 5 times and then do 5 missions that are mostly the same and then kill a boss and then repeat.

But to the point this game had good potential and its map is gorgeous and one of the largest maps in gaming history, but that doesnt make up for the zombie like grinding to get through this game and its way too repatative to play for an extended period of time.

So unfortunately i cant really say i would recommend this game if you are looking for any sort of variation in gameplay because you arent gonna find it in Ghost recon: Wildlands.

Its fun at first, an open world, lots of missions, some simple progression and unlocks. Best part? Its multiplayer, so naturally you get your friends together and have some fun. Unfortunately this game comes with the training wheels bolted on, the target demographic in terms of difficulty for this is most likely kids in the regions of 8 to 15 in age. The content is closer to that of 16 at least. Issue?

So here are the default training wheels:
Enemy clouds - basically you always know the approximate area an enemy is in.
Grenade, missile warnings, enemy markers - everything that poses a slight remote threat to you is highlighted with audio, flashes and clearly marked on the map or your hud.

All of the above can be changed with some tweaking to the options, also these settings are not server enforced. So its entirely possible to have a friend or random join your squad with all of these enabled and effectively be Rambo while the rest of you look like the bob the builder.

Here are the bolted on training wheels:
Ammo abundance - Literally, why does some peasent have enough ammo stashed away in their bedroom that could sort out US ammo needs for the next 10 years?

Health regeneration - Take a shot and within 3 seconds youre back at full hp.

Zero weapon scaling - you may as well run around with the first gun you get. Actually just use the assault rifle and a sniper. Once you have the under barrel grenade launcher you can cover ever conceivable situation this game will ever throw at you. You get this attachment within the first hour of playing the game. So effectively it takes you one hour to get all useful unlocks, not bad.

Infinite bleedtime - You take a lot of damage, fall on the ground and wait till your friends come revive you. You can stay in this bleeding out state forever. So if you need to go have supper, watch a movie, finish your degree there is no stress, your character will faithfully bleed out for as long as he needs to.

Infinite revives - So you hit the ground, bleed out for an hour, get revived, hit the ground, bleed out hour, revive, ground....

Personal Gripes I have with it:
One of the selling points of this game is the massive landmass. Unfortunately this doesnt mean much when almost every third peasent village in this game owns their own helicopter capable of traversing the area within 5 minutes. You can also unlock the ability to spawn a helicopter eventually. Or you can just teleport to where you need to go.

The AI is really stupid for 2018 standards, this would have maybe impressed me when I played CS 1 or Doom 1 back in the 90's. They also have perfect night vision, so lighting means pretty much nothing. 

Hardest difficulty is really just a theme, kind of like changing the background on your Desktop. I mean its really still the same, things just look different.

So here is how I managed to make this game remotely challenging in single player and somewhat live up to the standards of 00's ghost recons.
Turn off all training wheels in the hud as far as possible.
Turn off all enemy audio (they like to tell you when they are coming to stab you, kind of like a general disclaimer)
Turn off all bots (they are gods for some reason)
Highest difficulty.
No under barrel grenade launcher.
No drone.
Selectively choose from talents in the tree (to ensure you dont become a god).

OK so do I recommend this?
For some people, yes: 
If you are highly stressed or just want something to kill 30 mins every other day, great purchase. Its always easy and is very non-commital.
If you are bad at Dota (or games in general) and want to feel like you are winning for a change then yes (totally not the reason i still play this).
Want something simple to play with your kids that is probably not age appropriate? Yea totally, I think...

Otherwise no.

He loved his job. Driving a train had been his dream ever since he was a child. He loved to make the train go as fast as possible. Unfortunately, one day he was a little too reckless and caused a crash. He made it out, but a single person died. Well, needless to say, he went to court over this incident. He was found guilty, and was sentenced to death by electrocution. When the day of the execution came, he requested a single banana as his last meal. After eating the banana, he was strapped into the electric chair. The switch was flown, sparks flew, and smoke filled the air - but nothing happened. The man was perfectly fine.


Well, at the time, there was an old Bulgarian law that said a failed execution was a sign of divine intervention, so the man was allowed to go free. Somehow, he managed to get his old job back driving the train. Having not learned his lesson at all, he went right back to driving the train with reckless abandon. Once again, he caused a train to crash, this time killing two people. The trial went much the same as the first, resulting in a sentence of execution. For his final meal, the man requested two bananas. After eating the bananas, he was strapped into the electric chair. The switch was thrown, sparks flew, smoke filled the room - and the man was once again unharmed.


Well, this of course meant that he was free to go. And once again, he somehow managed to get his old job back. To what should have been the surprise of no one, he crashed yet another train and killed three people. And so he once again found himself being sentenced to death. On the day of his execution, he requested his final meal: three bananas.


"You know what? No," said the executioner. "I've had it with you and your stupid bananas and walking out of here unharmed. I'm not giving you a thing to eat; we're strapping you in and doing this now." Well, it was against protocol, but the man was strapped in to the electric chair without a last meal. The switch was pulled, sparks flew, smoke filled the room - and the man was still unharmed. The executioner was speechless.


The man looked at the executioner and said, "Oh, the bananas had nothing to do with it. I'm just a bad conductor."

CONS
- Extremely repetitive dialogue (both the bad guys, the secarios and the santa blanca, and the ghosts). At first the dialogue is fine, but when you are scouting your seventy-fifth base and hear the AI using the same phrases and bits of dialogue you are pretty fed up.

In reality you can fire an AK at twice the distance with no or very little drop. It would be really fun in this game if you could pull off long shots, but the AI is not even visible (or spawns) at long distances. Also canvas and camo netting is often bullet proof in this game.
- If or when you are detected everyone in the whole world and their grandma knows where you are. And I mean exactly where you are. And they will spare no costs in finding you. :)

I'm gonna give it to you easy: this is a game you should get on sale. While not worth full-price, it's still worth playing. Despite the kinds of negative reviews I've read, don't let them bother you.
For starters, yes, there is a weird issue where this game can crash unexpectedly. Luckily, this game has a frequent autosave feature, along with checkpoints in the missions to help alleviate this problem. And for note, if you're looking for a game that's beautiful and runs well, play this game on low or medium graphics. (Somehow, this game runs better on my gaming laptop while on medium settings than Mirror's Edge on the lowest graphics).
But the gameplay is another story. It has a lot of things going for it. The cover system feels natural, and the overall gameplay feels like it had been set up to support whatever playstyle you preffer. Keep in mind, though, the game itself has an overall gameplay feeling of "go here, kill some guys, beat the boss, move on and repeat." The story is present throughout the game, and is revealed through files collected and videos given to you by Sueno and Bowman. Overall, though, the story just felt like The Division's; minimal character development, a mostly absent antagonist and the only way to progress is to trek across the map and do a bunch of seemingly tedious tasks before reaching the boss of the area and moving on. And there are two ways to play this: do the simple method and just chase down the final boss and only get collectibles that are in your path. Or, you can do the hard way and collect everything then take on the buchon.
The characters are mostly unmemorable, aside from Sueno and a few of the Buchons. The rest don't really have a personality, aside from just "antagonist."
All in all, this game is pretty good. Getting it on sale is likely the best option, considering how it doesn't have much appeal to it. The bright side is that you can go at your own pace and accomplish things in your own way, in any order you want. That said, I'm willing to give it a 7/10. Maybe 7.5.

The Good: The game is gritty, very tactical, has good stealth AI and when it comes to strategy based shooters that are live and not turn based, it does this fairly well.

The Bad: The game has serious programming issues. I have experienced crashes, stuttering, freezes that last 10 seconds (in a gunfight), and other issues. One would think, upgrade hardware, update drivers, check for computer issues... but in hundreds of games, this is literally the only one giving me issues of this degree. Upon research, it isn't hardware related. In other words, I have a great graphics card, sufficient RAM, and processing... it doesn't care.

The combat is clunky. It plays only in third person (I dislike this immensely in shooters), and while it isn't my preference, games like Mass Effect and Gears did this really well. There is no cover button. You frequently take cover facing the wrong direction, and although there is a button to face the other way, you will turn around randomly while aiming and see wall. Lazy.

Control: Fail.

Sound design is really good. 

The world map is huge. Cool. 

The graphics are great.

The story is.... well... acceptable. 

Overall the game didn't feel like it took itself seriously. At all. The leveling system is lazy and not inspiring. 

It feels like this game wanted to shoot like gears, but failed to match it even 50%. It wanted to be a completionist open world like Assassin's Creed, but doesn't satisfy or make you feel like there is much point. 

It wants to be a stealth game, but fails to appease as its control scheme and lack of flush, clear controls makes me only focused on that most of the time. 

I really wanted to enjoy this game with my friend, as he recommended it, but frankly? Save yourself the trouble and frustration. There are 100 better shooters, 100 better stealth games, 100 better open world games, 100 better games for immersion, and a game as clunky as Dark Souls better impress me with its direction and immersion. It didn't at all.

You misheard what your friend said and you might compramise the mission. This isn't a game where you could just rush in all guns blazing, well... you can do that, but from my experience, not so much. As you progress through the world, leveling up, moving to different provinces, enemies get tougher, and so will the difficulty. Pros:
- Gun physics is well done, the ballistics is similar to sniper elite IV without wind.
- There is a good variety of weapons and attatchments to choose from.
- Drones and night/thermal vision work nicely in this game. It is satisfying to learn to use drones to gather information on higher difficulties.
- The plot, albeit generic for some people, is supported by well conceived lore items (audio/video recordings, paper files). They are interesting enough that I (a quite impatient person) will go out of my way to collect them.
- The landscape and open world looks beautiful.
- The co-op has a lot of potential when you increase game difficulty and remove HUD.
- Performance is rather ok. 60fps with 2k resolution on a system with 1060 on medium/high setting.

Cons (there are a ton):
- AIs (friendlies and hostiles) are just awful, awfully awful:
 = Enemies will instantly pinpoint your location if they notice anything bad (see a dead body, hear an explosion, etc.). They are also telepathic.
 = AI squadmates are not a choice in single player, they will follow you anywhere unless you tell them to sit at a location.
 = AI squadmates ignores flanking enemies completely, consistently. This means if you sit on top of a tower reconning with drones, it is entirely likely that your squadmates guarding the stair case will watch enemies running up the tower to shaft you with dispassion. I've watched this happening on my drones too many times.
 = Enemies on all difficulties have ridiculous aim, meaning they can land an uzi burst on you hiding in the tallgrass in the middle of a moonless night while a storm is going on from 300m away. They can make Shroud look like a blind old lady.
- Mild cases of invisible walls, meaning a well aligned shot can hit something along the trajectory with a bigger hitbox than visible. 
- Stealth gameplay is a trainwreck. Most of the missions will make you face overwhelming number of enemies, hence stealth is essential on higher difficulty (due to AI aim prowess). But the mechanic is so poorly done it feels like an added feature on a finished game.
- Some missions are, imo, very poorly designed. One type of mission requires you to defend a radio broadcast in the middle of the street for 3 mins, while enemies pour in from all directions, with your position exposed. Let's say it feels like fighting 30 Shrouds high on coco at the same time, while protecting a truck sized hostage in the open.
- There are a handful of bugs in my 80 something hours of gameplay.

Things you may or may not like:
- Uplay.
- Ubi-grind.
- Ubi dlc items. It means you have to pay $ for certain weapons, so if you are a compulsive hoarder this may upset you.
- Barely existing cover mechanics. People feel differently about cover shooters.
- Certain game mechanics. E.g. the Bolivian popo that works like gta popo that will send unlimited reinforcement unless you run.
- The shooting mechanics (bullet drop, muzzle velocity, ADS etc). I am a huge fan of Sniper Elite IV gunplay and accostomed to rainbow six siege weapon handling, so GRW feels like a watered down hybrid of both (no wind, no leaning, no rapelling). If only they just copied either of the two, if only.
- It's a finished game, so devs won't be changing anything significantly.

In conclusion, GRW is worth the price if you can get it on 50% sale (for average FPS gamers), as it has a good deal of content and is a decent shooting simulator even without it. If you want a polished experience, know that this is a Ubi game, so you will be triggered left and right, and looking elsewhere will save you some torment.

Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands is a good game.
The action takes place in Bolivia, where powerful drug cartels are ruling the land.

As part of a four-man special ops team, you have various missions and side missions to complete.
There are also pieces of intelligence placed around the map (which help you level up), as well as various gun caches (which give you new guns to use).

You don't have to follow the story-line, but can just roam around the map if you like, looking for fights to get into (the drug cartels are happy to oblige).
There are several types of vehicles you can use to get around, with a wide variety of cars, motorbikes, and helicopters (and some boats too).

I've played this both as a single-player (you and three AI guys) and multi-player game (up to four players), and have found that both work well.
I have been able to complete most of the missions in single-player mode, except for one sneak mission (where the AI guys kept on getting the attention of the guards).

All up, it's a good game.
I can recommend Ghost Recon Wildlands for a bit of shooting fun.

 everything stated in this review are my personal experiences and or opinions

SHORT REVIEW:
Ghost recon Wildlands is a game that thrives on immersion and on the overall experience it provides to the player. Some of the individual features of the game might have flaws (the AI, bossfights  and driving most of all) but the overall experience makes up for most of the hiccups the game has. Going from stealthily taking down snipers in enemy camps in a series of coordinated shots with your teammates to chasing a convoy in an helicopter while making bullets rain from a minigun on the armored truck feels smooth, exciting and fun. I often felt like I was a victim to the circumstances the world presented, forced to adapt and freak out a little when the enemy VIP tries to leave the base via helicopter the second an enemy spots me. Still, motocross drifting  through the muddy roads and lush vegetation of one of the (if not the) largest, richest (in biomes and missions) and best looking open world maps I've ever seen in a videogame feels incredible. I'll go as far as saying that for the discounted price, the game is worth picking up solely for the way it looks, it will stress you computer, but the risult is worth every FPS you loose. Jokes aside, the game is just fun. The story and map achieve a great level of immersion, missions (main and secondary both) don’t feel like a waste of time and everything you do is excting, packed with action, useful, and (if you’re into customization) you can look damn good while doing it. To me, if it wasn’t for Uplay and the lootbox thing it would be an 8/10, but honestly, for the discounted price, it’s a must have


DEEPER ANALYSIS AND CONSIDERSIONS:
Aside from my general considerations one very important thing to point out is the quality of story. It is a well written tale analyzing the "drug cartel" topic quite deeply asking a question that is "what if a cartel got so powerful it would end up running a country?". The Santa Blanca cartel isn't just a random evil organization, carachters themselves admit the genius of the corrupt system they have created, the same system you as the main carachter are trying to dismantle. The game provided me with entertaining Intel, recordings, pictures and videos on every single enemy I hunted down, trying to make me understand who the person is, what are his/her motifs, and why I should take him/her out. The focus put on making enemies feel like actual people and not your everyday NPC takes the immersion and the story telling value of the game to a whole other level. The ones who actually end up lacking personalities are the "good guys" who's reasons to even be in Bolivia I found to be very arguable without even touching on points like their oddly blind obedience during morally ambiguous moments and the way they joke about in-game events, theese things kind of mess with the feeling of immersion because I ended up in a situation where the game tells a very detailed and serious story about drug-trade, tradition, poverty, power, culture and corruption while in-game carachter sometimes are like "yeah right LOL". The feeling that the game portrays carachters as actual people but the carachters don't take themselves or events seriously kinda made me scratch my head. 

Regardless, the main protagonist of the game is without any doubt the map. Bolivia is beautiful, alive and filled with things to do and places to explore. From mountain tops to forests, little islands and salt flats, swamps and dry deserts, crop fields and ancient ruins the map really has it all. The quiet, calm moments I sometimes spend resupplying and regrouping with my squad after clearing an enemy camp can feel meditative, leaving me in awe to the beautiful, fictional, world of Wildlands. I often choose to walk or drive rather than fly from place to place just so I can let the view sink in deeper. The map is also the canvas on which the action takes place being filled with all kinds of missions, collectables, military and non-military vehichles that with the aid of the autosave mechanic allow for fun, exciting action moments to which you must adapt (being unable to load a previous save) making the experience feel different at every enemy encounter and genuinely challenging at higher difficulties. The tasks you have to complete hardly ever feel like a waste of time, there are no useless collectables or tedious secondary missions, everything you do or collect feels somewhat useful or it helps progress towards and objective. Honestly, the game is just fun. If you add to the mix things like the chance to join other people in the co-op mode, the surprisingly deep weapons and carachter customization, the fun easter eggs missions, the challenges, ghost mode, the surprising longevity of the story, the amazingly well done gun play, you get a huge game with a tons of content that, most importantly, manages to be FUN basically all the time


However there are low point,  in my opinion they are the driving, AI and bossfights

The driving is arcadey, and there's nothing inherently wrong with it, but driving Humvees, Jeeps and Trucks that feel too fast and weightless doesn't feel right and breaks the immersion, still, bikes, helicopters and boats, feel amazing to drive. A honorable mention must go to the offroad bike driving experience, without any doubt, it was one of the single best in-game driving experiences I’m ever had in any game, ever.

 The AI of enemies is bad but not terrible, point is, sometimes enemies just act dumb; the one of single player allies, on the other hand, is just lacking. Ordering them around simply feels bad, the commands are always too generic both for stealth and guns-blazing and when left alone allies seem to have no idea on how to preserve your and their lives. I also don't understand why can't allies drive when NPCs do and it triggers me a bit having to trash every helicopter I parachute off of because none of my allies can safely land it or fly it away. Honestly, I felt like the only point of NPC teammates was to take out marked enemies

Honestly? I guess it isn't the worst game in the world, but Ghost Recon Wildlands isn't a great game either. There is nothing that has been done in this title that hasn't been better done somewhere else before, and there is a handful of issues that essentially boil down to Ubisoft being a goof that kept this title from reaching it's true potential.

The main problems I see with this game are; Technical issues Ubisoft has failed to fix, boring gameplay and anti-consumer business practices.

Google Ghost Recon Wildlands for technical glitches and compatibility issues and your jaw will drop. These range from the minor and goofy(having your helicopter launched to the top of the map after trying to land) to downright critical gameplay issues, like game crashes. I experienced several random game crashes. Every time i logged in to the game i had to toggle Fullscreen > Windowed > Fullscreen to actually play the game in full screen mode. My Ai teammates were an absolute nuisance as they flat out ignored commands and stood at my feet while i would bleed to death without reviving me. Simple mechanics, like traversing terrain, were awkward and buggy, often leading to comprimising situations you intended to avoid. I flat out gave up on the stealth mechanics in this game, as they were unpolished to the point of being an unviable strategy. I was clearly spotted through walls, tracked by non-alerted enemies through cover as if they were locked on to my character and even got killed by a grenade on the other side of multiple walls. I was reading other reviews where people would have their game file or earned items disappear. This game has been out for far too long, and Ubisoft has had the tools to fix these issues. Instead, they let critical issues interfere with the game experience, to focus on wringing more profit out of the game, like DLC and MTX's.

The gameplay itself, for being an elite team of tier 1 operatives given free range to take out a cartel in Bolivia, is incredibly lackluster. Being a Ubisoft game, about 90% of this game is generic objectives and side missions that supposedly add "depth" to the game. From the first hour to the tenth hour, the gameplay didn't change. I was doing the exact same things in the first area, that I ended up doing in all of the other provinces i conducted operations in. Even the pattern for reaching a Buchon was copy paste throughout the game. Mess with production, put a gun in someones face, capture someone close to the buchon and then capture/kill the HVT in an obvious ambush. "Free to operate your way" feels like a meme the fourth time you're forced to walk into an obvious ambush. In later provinces, the developers tried to modify the missions by simply piling multiple missions you've already done elsewhere into a single missions which gets irritating quickly and seems like a waste of the player's time solely so Ubisoft can proudly exclaim they have "hours and hours of content".

These issues are an adamant deal breaker for me because I know for a fact that Ubisoft can do better. The fact that they had day one paywalled content and continue to release DLC's and microtransactions while there are still critical issues with the game, proves that yet again, Ubisoft is putting profits before the player experience. Ubisoft's development team has all the tools needed for success. They have the money, the creative tools, the manpower and the fanpower to create well polished and cutting edge gameplay experiences.

If Ubisoft put half of their effort into THAT goal, as opposed to finding a way to jam in as many microtransactions as possible, They might have produced a more memorable and reputable title in the past few years. 

Another thing to note too - This game was easily shallow enough to beat on the free weekend if you ignore doing a full clear of the provinces, like me. Despite there being play time left on my account for the free weekend, I only had access to the game for 24 hours so i was unable to finish up the last few missions i would've had to finish the story.

Perhaps Ubisoft knew i was close to knocking off El Sueno and decided to bench me.

Maybe you won't get suckered into having to pay for the base game and all of the DLC's too.

TL;DR:
It's fine. It's a Ubisoft game. Bullet travel time is dope. Everything else is see-sawing between meh and aaight. Decent deal for 20 bucks. Otherwise ignore.

Extended thoughts:
It's a Ubisoft game. With all the good and the bad that comes with that statement. It's got quality in presentation, sure, but it varies very little from other titles released since 2012 onward. 

It's like they managed to mush together both Far Cry 3/4 and The Division to make the best of their mediocre inspirations. Which, unsurprisingly, ends up still pretty mediocre. It's servicable, sure. Plays fine. Looks great. But you've played this game before. Nothing here to merit full price. At 20 bucks I think it's a pretty good deal for what you're getting, it shoots better than the Division at least. But other than that, you could just skip this title and miss nothing of value. A statement that is becoming sadly ever more prominent when relating to Ubisoft titles.

I will say however that I like that the bullets have travel time and bullet drop. This goes for all of your weapons, making you place your shots more carefully. I also like that - contrary to what you might think - that you don't capture outposts and then suddenly control that part of the map forever, á la Far Cry 3/4. This time they have the bad people respawn if you've been away from that particular place/outpost/etc. Which is nice, because you never really run out of things to shoot. I haven't yet felt like I was lacking in progression in the story, but at the same time, it does somewhat invalidate the impact that you're supposed to have. I mean, after you've killed the the Local Villain in Sesame Street Bolivia, nothing much changes it feels like. You just get out of the region and begin the cycle anew, which wears out fairly quickly. Moreso because of the fact that missions are structured very similarly, and never really demand your full attention when you've played enough and realize how every mission will play out. Besides that, the customization is dope. But I then immediately have to retract the statement about customization due to just how much is locked behind lootboxes or other menial nonsense designed to waste your time. And I can already hear the argument of 'But it's just cosmetic' ringing my ears. To which I reply to that strawman: frankly, even the 'just cosmetic' parts are an integral part of the game experience. If you didn't care about looking cool, or we didn't care about graphics at all, we'd be playing with untextured polygons in vague shapes. If only gameplay and merit carried games, we wouldn't have half of the gaming demographic made up of people who play mobile games. But this is starting to sound like a soapbox. The lootboxes in Ubisoft games have always been tolerable, and this title is no exception. But they're still in the game, and just because they're the least obtrusive with implementing them doesn't mean they're void of scrutiny altogether in that respect. 

That'd be like praising a cook because they only put a little bit of dung on top of your meal, which you think is better just because other cooks have a horse directly defecate on top of their meals. In both scenarios, you're still willingly eating dung. In the former case just less of it. My point is that lootboxes are stupid.

Let alone anyone else's. 

In honesty, this is what this game is: 
A content-rich third person shooter with sneak elements and many stats, skills and abilities to combine with just as many weapon, appearance and attatchment options in order to create a Ghost Recon operative that you'll love playing as
The graphics and scenery leaves little to be asked as this game along with a clear majority of Ubisofts' games are above all graphically impressive.

But then we arrive at the second layer... And the fact that this isnt a movie, or a photoshoot. It is a GAME. Which also far too often seem to pass the minds at Ubisoft entertainment by. 
A game needs gameplay. And I do not think that the crew spend even a fraction of their time spent painting the landscape on forming the gameplay itself.

This is sad, but to the point and honest, how the game works:
Your controls of the character you play as are quite varied, your moves are a little bit unrealistic at times, but far within reason (and personally I think they are great).

The game's weakness starts to show. And bugs appear. The alerted NPC's will for a time know exactly where you are are shoot you as soon as it is possible with insane speeds, let alone accuracy if you are playing on a high difficulty. The time it takes an NPC to ready their weapon and shoot you down may be less than 0.5 seconds. Making bot fights as unrealistic as they are annoying to deal with. 

In a game like this the whole idea is to try avoid as many engagements as possible. But you would think that this would be because it is a game about stealth, and not because the actual engagements are tedious and boring.

Interactions with bots is what the mostpart of the game is all about. So why have the dev team put as little effort into this as humanely possible?
Instead all they are adding now are more cosmetics and premade weapons for their microtransaction crates. Lots of content that you will not be able to unlock just by playing. 
Mistake upon mistake will and probably have... Killed yet another game that has and had all it needed to become great.

I got a lot of enjoyment out of this game, but take that with a grain of salt, as this game has a lot of flaws that could very well turn someone off.

But first, what I like:
- Easy to pick up, put down, repeat
- Gorgeous scenery, great graphics
- Huge map with different terrain / climates
- Tons of gun and character modifications earned in-game
- Crossover missions are super cool 
- Satisfying gun mechanics / physics 
- Synch Shot is pretty darn cool
- Drone is a cool gadget
- Story is pretty well done, especially with all the King Slayer files adding details

The Bad:
-  Awful AI. Enemies have eyes in the back of their heads and will shoot you at 150yds, dual-weilding machine pistols. Your AI teammates are clunky to control, will waltz right up to enemies without being noticed (thankfully lol), and other than for sync shot are kind of just spectators excxept to heal me when I get plowed over by a civilian in a truck. 
- Missions can be done out-of-order, but do not account for it. For instance, you will have a current mission / cutscene referencing someone whom you've already dealt with in a prior mission. Def an immersion killer. Either have the main missions follow a set order or make multiple variants to account for people who go a differerent route. 
- Repetition. Side missions are just dozens of the same 5 things in different areas, some story missions are very similar. However, there is no one way to go about any of them as base / hideout layouts and terrain are VERY different. As are the defenses present.

Neutral:
- Driving. Driving fullsize vehicles and helicopters was easy for me to pick up and become adept at. Motorcycles and airplanes were a pain. Motorcycles are unweildy off road (where you want them most), and I dont know what the deal is with the planes, but I was terrible.

MY opinion:
I bought it on sale for $25 and I would absolutely do it again, and would for sure play a sequel that is hopefully more polished.  If you like Far Cry-esque open world military games, I would give it a shot next time its on SALE. You'll know if its right for you within a couple hours.

Hm... Ghost Recon Wildlands? Doesn't ring a bell. At least, that is the reaction to this game being mentioned by most nowadays, because the game was so bland and repetative that I'm pretty sure even Ubisoft forgot about it. Here's the thing about the Ghost Recon franchise Ubi, it was not meant to be an action sandbox game. Waaaaaaaaaay back in the day (the early to mid 2000's) Ghost Recon was a tense tactical shooter with an emphasis on stealth and teamwork over blowing ♥♥♥♥ up. Ubisoft seem to have looked at this idea and thought to themselves "maybe what the fans really want is a boring linear third person cover shooter with some stealth elements?" It was this line of thinking that left us with the snore fest known as Ghost Recon Future Soldier a few years back, but what about Wildlands? Ubisoft threw off the linearity issue by swinging the pendulum so hard the other direction that they lost the point again. Wildlands is an open world action game that is trying to be comparable to Just Cause or Grand Theft Auto, but with none of the freedom offered in those games. You are ostensibly a government agent working on behalf of the United States within Bolivia to take down the Santa Blanca drug cartel. A cool concept but when put into the context of an open world sandbox, it results in the game kneecapping itself to stay consistent. For example, you cannot shoot civilians or you will get a game over. There are also numerous missions that will result in a failure state if you break stealth, which is fine if that's how you want the game to be but there is zero indication based on the available equipment that stealth is the best or even a good option. Yeah, you get suppressors  and a drone but most of the upgrades are combat oriented and many weapons cannot mount suppressors. There are also times where the game just alerts the enemies based on a scripted event, so even if you were running a perfect stealth op it gets ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. The point is that the game never gives you an indication of what to expect so you cannot prepare accordingly. 

How is this a ghost recon game exactly? Yeah, I know your unit is called the "ghosts" but they seem awfully under equipped. Like for example, the ghosts in Future Soldier had futuristic active camo, but our ghosts in Wildlands have hoodies? And don't come at me saying "oh they're trying to blend in" when you can wear a plate carrier and a ghillie suit with three guns strapped to you at all times. 

But none of that matters if the game is fun. Is the game fun? If you have a full squad of friends, and even then only for probably 15-20 hours max. After a while, you realize that the game is one big repetative loop. Your goal in the game is to take out underbosses to get to overbosses to reach the big boss himself, El Sueno. The problem is that all of these steps take the form of 3 things: kill someone, break something, steal something. Now imagine you are expected to do those same 3 things for upwards of 50 hours to beat the game. Sound boring? You're not wrong my friend. 

Look overall, the game is just boring. It's not bad, or broken, or offensive, it's just the gameplay equivelant of plain oatmeal. No variety, no flare, no fun. And what, I ask, is the point of a game if it isn't fun?
