+Difficulty (there's Extreme, and after you reach the "Tier 1", this pretty much adds a whole new difficulty dimension to the game. Did not get there yet, so no idea how it works really, but AFAIK it's just another "layer" to keep the game from becoming too easy.)

[b]CONS:[/b]
-Graphics (need a pretty good machine to run it at ultra. At 4k, it takes NASA's quantum computers to get 60 FPS). I play on i3 6100 3,7ghz, 8GB DDR4 RAM and a GTX 750 TI 2GB DDR5. Medium settings, stable 30 FPS on 1080p. Game still looks great, but not so much at large render distances - and those are, indeed, very, very large.

-COOP. Because you do need to find like-minded players at first, it may be a bit frustrating to join 15 games and find out that all those people are either not communicating at all and playing it like GTA V, or maybe too hardcore for you. In any case, trust me, you WILL find your soul mates. Very soon, probably :)

-Repetitiveness: Just like with any other Ubisoft open world game. The content is repetitive, but you should already know that from games like Far Cry, Assassin's Creed or The Crew.

-Story: I mean, did Ubisoft ever make a good story? It's as good as any other Tom Clancy's game. You play as the good guys ('Murrricaaaa) and kill the bad guys (drug cartels in the South). I am not even paying attention to the cutscenes and stuff. Also, it may get a bit messy, since there is no order to the missions - you can complete late game bosses and whatever, if you have friends with access to those missions, and likewise - your high level friends can re-play starting (or any) missions with you. 

-Price: Very subjective. I would not pay 60 euro for this, but that is because I'm a poor student. I did, however, gladly buy it for 20. If you can spare the 60, go ahead, you will not regret it.

-Loading Screens: SO MANY OF THEM. Despite the game being open world with no loading screen barriers, you get a 2minute loading every time you: join a game, get kicked off a game, go to main menu, start a game, end a game, fail a mission, restart a mission, fast travel, respawn... blah blah. You get the idea. I can get annoying, but not to the point of frustration. There's just much more fun than loadings :) 

[b]-The medical drones - There's a feature that allows your drone to fly to your fallen comrades and ressurect them INSTANTLY. This is also Area of Effect. It's extremely OP, unrealistic and I think should be removed from the game. I suggest you agree with your friends to simply not use it.[/b]

[b]TL;DR: [/b]If you love tactical gameplay but are afraid of PVP games like ARMA (ah the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ campers) get it asap. If you like Splinter Cell games, this one is for you. Vehicles are WAY TOOOOO arcade-ish, but it's not game-breaking. Content is repetitive, but COOP and M A S S I V E open world saves the day. There is also really good 4vs4 PVP with many different game modes, if that's your thing and it's pretty balanced. Graphics are completely awesome, if you have the machine for it.

This game has two sides. One is the single player; here you have a Far Cry type game but in 3rd person and with 3 other AIs (or CO-OP players) tagging along the way. From what I saw, the story is good. You are given an open world to grind but it gets pretty repetitive fast. A good challenge would be the higher difficulty levels but the AI is exploitable, it is easy to draw into ambushes. Gameplay wise, the accent is put on tactical approaches for combat, you can’t really “Rambo” your way through the game. You are given a drone which you can use to scout and plan your moves. You can upgrade your character and weapons in lots of ways.

The other side is the multiplayer where you can play 4v4; here, after the teams are made, you get to vote for the game-mode that you want. Time to kill is relatively low, meaning that a well-placed sniper shot or head shot can take you down, but during the round you can always be “revived” by your team mates. Personally, I didn’t find the (insane) adrenaline rushes that I got from Rainbow 6 Siege, not sure why. You have to gather experience (levels) to unlock classes/perks or buy the season passes. But unless we talk about the new classes from the DLCs, the “old” ones are relatively easy to unlock. You can choose from two weapons for each class and the only customizable things for them are the scopes (not taking into account skins).

In both game modes the accent is put on tactics and balance, not on realism. The shooting mechanics are pretty basic, you can have ADS, there is bullet drop, and some materials are penetrable. On paper, this should be a great game, but in practice, it is not as good as could be. Besides the fact that the game is 3rd person, I can’t really put my finger on what exactly they are doing wrong (or not to my liking).

I’m going to preface this as most Tom Clancy fans would by stating how I played the originals and blah blah blah. I started out playing the original ghost recon for pc. A game that took the tactical cqb of the original r6 and rogue spear, and transferred it into land warfare and special operations. It was an absolute blast, very difficult but very rewarding if you planned out your mission the right way, it was a thrilling and overall great game that is lost to the ages.

Now that doesn’t mean wildlands is  bad, because it is not, it’s just different. Keep in mind I’ll be reviewing single player only as that is all I’ve played.

Wild lands provides an open world playground where you and your 3 ai teammates insert into Bolivia tasked with systematically identifying and eliminating a powerful drug cartel, as well as strengthening the resistance. You will engage in hostage rescues, sabotage, intelligence gathering, and ultimately the killing/capturing of the cartel leaders. 

Now this sounds cool right? In many ways it is, however as I breakdown this review from gameplay, graphics and lasting appeal, you will see some elements work better then others.

Graphics 4.5/5: This is an easy high point of the game, it looks gorgeous, the terrain, lighting, shadows, all of it is stunning. In a pitched firefight, tracers, explosions all create a very immersive environment. I can’t ignore the fact that many have had optimization issues and there are times when viewing long distance I see a drop in frame rate but nothing significant. A lot of these issues have been fixed since it’s release though. Overall if your rig can handle it, it is a gorgeous game. The only negatives here are driving physics. Tare laughable but this isn’t exactly a racing sim.

Gameplay 4/5: This encompasses a lot. I’ll preface by saying I played wild lands for its initial release, stopped for about 8 months, and came back due to the new updates. 

Overall the story will leave you wanting more, it’s nothing that truly grabs you and brings about your moral resolve to stop the cartel, a lot of the missions take on the same repetitive formula with the only difference of switching regions. I find myself not caring at all about the resistance or the bad guys were supposed to be hunting.
Where the game shines is the combat. I’ve been playing on tier one mode, and while many here seem to dislike the 1 shot death, I find it more reminiscent of the ghost recon I remember. The weapon customization is great, the feel, sound and overall gunplay is where this game shines. Executing a well planned mission by stalking and eliminating the enemy is the most enjoyable aspect of this game.

However the biggest detriment here is the ai, both friendly and enemy. Your teammates are absolute tanks, an easy strategy would be to send them directly into the front and pick off enemies from a distance yourself. Your teammates make questionable decisions to say the least, there are times I’ve tried to crawl and stalk an enemy position while my teammates are literally crouch walking in the middle of the street in direct sight of enemies. The enemies at times can have laser accuracy but are not as difficult as other reviews have stated. The advent of your drone and marking targets make for an easy way to plan out how you will carry out a mission. While some other reviews state this forces you into always doing the stealth route, id say this adds more to the realism as a team of 4 will probably not take on a cartel controlled city head on. Which brings me to the realism aspect. 

There are elements that just don’t make sense. Instead of piloting a helicopter by myself, why not have the ability to call in a Blackhawk to transport us anywhere on the map, as would most likely be the case in the real world, or a vehicle drop of high end military spec buggies, bikes, etc. or the ability to call in air support, gunship overwatch, laser guiding bombs instead of just resistance mortar strikes. Or the ability to halo drop with my teammates as opposed to having to get in a helicopter and climb to a high altitude, then jump out leaving the chipper to crash and have my ai team be teleported to me when I land. These things are small but add up and at times are hard to ignore
I know it sounds ridiculous, but the main reason I stopped playing was the lack of customization to my ai teammates, more specifically there outfits. It was an absolute immersion killer for me to be in a full tactical load out, helmet and all, while my teammates were dressed like edgy paramilitary hipsters. The advent of the recent update to change your teammates uniforms has been the reason I came back and have found myself enjoying this game again which is why I give the gameplay a 4/5 now.

Lasting appeal: 3.5/5. I will update this as time goes on, as of now I don’t see myself going through the entire story, why bother? I don’t care about taking out the main bad guy, there is no motivation or reason to really do so, you will get the entirety of the experience by going after the lower level enemies and traversing the map, the splinter cell missions are a great advent and add some variety, but overall many of the missions are the same.

As of now I’d give this game a 4/5.

On a side note, or I should say, here comes a rant from an old gamer. I find the practices of a lot of these AAA game studios to be utterly terrible. The micro transactions are killing this industry, a lot of the cosmetics and weapons require you to simply purchase loot crates or the packs themselves. A lot of these cosmetics and weapons are really cool but instead of including them in the season pass, you are strongly encouraged to spend more money on gambling on crates, or purchasing a pack. On average a cosmetic or weapon pack will cost you $10. Further, and arguably most importantly, the trend in a lot of these developers seems to be releasing an unfinished game, and working on it over the years. This is not to say games shouldn’t be patched over time and have additional content, or even to say season passes are bad, but there is a bare minimal bar that games should meet upon release. A bar that many fail to come close to.

Now wild lands is a good game, now it is relatively optimized, now it is including aspects that arguably should have been in the main game. Now is over a year since it initial release. You would need to buy 2 season passes one for each year, on top of the original game, on top of cosmetic and weapon packs to truly get the full experience that will cost you a couple hundred dollars for a decent game. Ultimately I hope we as gamers push back against this, and support those that do right by their customers. While I purchased this game for the full $60 upon its release, I would’ve been better served waiting a year and buying it on sale.

Oooh yeah, a review to a game I played 96 hours, according to Steam. First of all, I highly recommend this game. I really really like the possibility of different approaches, be it sniping (with bullet drop and stuff, I LOVE that), stealth, or just slapping on a LMG und going full Rambo. Well, the last approach kinda only works on the lower difficulties XD... 

Also, the open world is GORGEOUS. Ubisoft's version of Bolivia under the grip of the Santa Blanca drug cartel is easily among one of the best open worlds I have ever seen, alongside with the world of Horizon Zero Dawn. And its HUGE! With a helicopter, from one end to another you travel round about twenty minutes. It looks beautiful even on the lowest settings, which unfortunately is the only setting my GPU can handle XD.

The story is okay. Four american "Ghosts" are sent to Bolivia to take down the aforementioned Santa Blanca Cartel und kill its boss, "El Sueno". What impressed me are the small videos that introduce each and every region boss. Those are pretty well made and I like to watch them over and over again because I like them so much :). 

The gameplay is also okay. I really love the bullet drop mechanics, the shooter gameplay lets even me rack up some kills. The missions all are kinda the same. Get there, steal or destroy or kill or interrogate and exfiltrate. What makes it good in my opinion is the freedom of approach, like I mentioned before. Additionally, as  I type this, the Splinter Cell crossover mission is out since 6 days, which is short, but a pretty nice because different mission than the others.

BUT. But of course the game has its flaws. I normally oversee minor bugs and glitches, and I do so here, too. But the biggest flaw is the f***ing AI. I honestly stopped counting the times where I was detected through walls or at a distance of  300 (!) meters by some random dude, at night. Plus. on extreme difficulty, the AI kills you in two or three shots. And then you turn on Tier One Mode, where you level down from Tier 50 to 1, while the difficulty increases even more, enemies take more damage and deal more damage. The game simply becomes ridiculous. You HAVE to stay hidden, otherwise you're INSTANTLY dead. Simple as that. The AI snipes you from obscene distances (I once was killed from a distance not shorter than 300 metres LMAO) with akimbo-held SMG's with fire rates that rival that of a gatling gun. Also, the accuracy. Oh boi. I honestly think the AI dreams of 100% acc. IN THEIR NIGHTMARES! Once you are spotted, you may as well restart the mission, it's only a matter of time until you sneak around the corner, you hear the sound of being spotted and then stare at the revive screen to wait for your teammates to revive you. I also had several instances where I had alerted the enemies inside a base and died WITHOUT EVEN HEARING A SHOT! Turned out some unmarked enemy had sneaked their way round the whole base, spotted me in a quarter of a second and dumped what feels like 10.000 rounds into me. (I'm not even kidding here. The AI does that almost all the time. The spotting times are RIDICULOUS, had me ragequit more times than I could count.) 

I could go on here, for a long time, but I want to answer the question why I still recommend this game. It's because if it works the way it should, and there are no major bugs and glitches and you are not spotted, it's SO MUCH FUN. It just feels great to sneak into a heavily fortified base, shoot out light and alarms, turn off gennys and drone jammers and complete the objective without being seen. It's fun to fly around over this beautiful world and jump out the chopper to parachute exactly onto the objective building. It's awesome to lay down with a sniper rifle and kill the enemies spotted by your coop mates from 650+ metres. In these situations, the game is just great. And because these situations form the majority of play time, I can "whole-heartedly endorse this game" (got the reference? XD)

tl;dr An incredibly barebones game with a squad mechanic tacked on. Metal Gear Solid V except without any of the fun stuff. Buy it, try the first hour, and if you don't like it, refund it, knowing it won't get better. 

Honestly, you will see everything this game has to offer in the first 15 minutes. In a way, this is a kind of strength, because you can decide if you want to refund it quite quickly. 

We've all seen the gameplay videos with incredibly awful scripted acting meant to jerk off the developers, but don't fall for the other videos either. 

This is a game where you will literally show up and shoot people and that's it. None of the other "make your own fun" things they throw in the videos are necessary, encouraged, or incentivized in any way. There is no reason to "Place C4 on Cars for a distraction." Why would you do that? There is no need for someone to "provide cover fire" from a mountain half a mile away. There is CERTAINLY no reason to hijack an enemy truck to "Sneak into a camp" when every camp has a back entrance. 

There is absolutely no penalty to just killing everyone with a silenced rifle the minute you see them. It is the most efficient way to deal with everything. Even if their body is found, I ♥♥♥♥ you not, no alarm is raised and nobody does anything other than "Patrol in a slightly angry fashion." 

And, astonishingly, there really is no penalty if you get caught. The game turns into a cover based shooter, until you disappear from sight for more than 2 seconds. Does the game get hard when everyone is alerted? Even at the highest difficulty, this is hardly an issue, and the worst thing that will happen is "reinforcements" will show up (2 cars, tops). 

The bases get harder. Oh, sorry, I meant the game says the bases get harder. I wouldn't know. I went to one of the highest difficulty areas in the first few hours of the game, and just walked through the back door of the hardest places in the game. 

The A.I. is terrible and does nothing more than fill up an "I see you" meter or go to your last known position. That's it. Your squad in single player can literally walk right in front of A.I. and the A.I. won't see them or care. That's because your Squad A.I. is ♥♥♥♥ too, and the devs figured it'd be easier to make them invisible then actually have them move in a stealthy manner. 

"But you are in charge of your own fun!" 

No, you are not. None of those "Make your own fun" things are doing anything special. They are just getting you caught faster or slower, a fact that's irrelevant because getting caught has no stakes whatsoever. 

For a squad based shooter, they are missing some of the most basic ♥♥♥♥ an open world tactical squad shooter needs:

-You cannot individually move your squad: Did you see that one video where one of the squad mates was sniping from a mountain? Not possible in single player. 
-You cannot breach doors, because there are none: They sometimes have a mission that "starts" when you throw a grenade at a door. Most of the time, however, you are running into open buildings like a jackass. 

The most you can do is tell your squad: 1) Everybody go here 2) Everybody Stop Moving 3) Everybody Follow me 4) Everyone start shooting indiscriminately. 

There is also, the sync shot, which is a cool feature in singleplayer: Your squad will execute their target at the time you do. They sometimes do this while superhumanly looking through two solid buildings and a cow, but whatever. This is, of course, a dumb thing in multiplayer, where one person can mark targets to tell everyone else what to do. I'll let you guess how well that goes, whether you're playing with friends or not. 

This game is so unbelievably bare bones I would have thought it was slapped together in under 8 months, and the only reason I don't think that is Bolivia is huge, beautiful, and diverse. It is a very cool place to be, and it's one of the only things the game does right. 

The other thing the game does right, true enough, is the shooting is genuinely fun. Even after the free weekend, I can't say I don't miss the silenced assault rifle. But this is literally all the game has to offer, and you will be doing it again, and again, and again, at every single outpost. 

What this game does not do right is multiplayer, which is one of it's biggest draws. Multiplayer is simply replacing your A.I. squad mates with real ones. And while the A.I. is garbage, playing with another person is even less fun. Remember how easy this game is? Imagine how easy it is with 3 other players. 

"Maybe you can place c4 on cars and cover them from a mountain!"

Yeah, maybe we can draw ♥♥♥♥♥ with bullets and watch the sun rise. What are we doing here? 

These things, like c4, and drone bombs, and a mortar strike every once in a while. None of it would even cross your mind if the devs didn't randomly shove RPG elements into this game. You have a level (you know, like in Iraq). You unlock skill points by finding medals to level things up like your drone battery, or C4 capacity, or how much damage you take from bullets, or something even more boring. None of these things are really worth upgrading. They are just there so you feel like you are unlocking more gameplay, but you aren't. None of it is preferable to just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ shooting everybody. I have never, ever, ever, needed C4, or mines, or even grenades. The only thing I upgraded that felt good was the amount of sync shots I can have. Because, for whatever reason, my squad refuses to shoot somebody when I tell them, unless I find the correct medal in somebody's shack. 

They want you to think this is Far Cry. This is not. You won't be liberating outposts with a variety of mechanics. You won't be unlocking cool things. You will just be showing up places that have enemies, and shooting said enemies. Those enemies will later respawn. 

This is Metal Gear Solid V, but without any of the stuff that made that game cool. That is the dynamic between player and outposts in Wildlands. Genuinely, imagine Metal Gear Solid V where all you can do is shoot people. You can't even pass time in game. Seriously. Night ops are a lot more fun than day ops, but if you want to do them, you just have to ♥♥♥♥ around until it's night time and then get them done. That is how bare bones this game is. 

So, my advice, buy it, play the first hour, and understand that the game will NEVER change or adapt from that point on. That is it. 

If you like that, keep playing. If you don't, refund it. You can't lose.

Held off buying this originally because of some of the negative comments I'd read (also was suspicious of Ubisoft's online-only approach to previous games). After playing the trial, I was really impressed, particularly with the huge open world, authentic-feeling combat and weapons, loads of customisation options, wide range of vehicles, and neat integration of single-player and co-op, with option to play offline. Grateful for the trial because would probably have missed this otherwise. 

Surprised to find this runs fine on my laptop - low settings of course, but still looks pretty good imo - optimisation is a lot better than a lot of other games I've played. Importantly the core combat manages to be fun while at the same time having a feel of realism (the handling of weapons etc feels authentic enough without detracting from playability). As for vehicles, it's nice that there are options to  tweak the handling of the vehicles - after tweaking, ground vehicles handle pretty much as you'd expect - and the helicopters are a joy to fly. This is fortunate as due to the size of the open world, helicopters are the best way to explore imo (can't get the hang of the fixed wing aircraft).

The level of character and weapon customisation is very impressive. It's good that they kept a realistic approach to the weapons instead of just just making early weapons 'bad' and  unlockable ones better. All of the guns, including the early ones, are realistically deadly, but have different characteristics (damage, penetration, accuracy, range, handling and loudness) which can be changed by customising their parts - this actually gives you a real choice of loadouts when you unlock more weapons and parts. The only exceptions to this are named weapons, which are unique and can't be customised.

The game also does a pretty good job of making the world feel alive, with an ongoing conflict between the rebels and the cartel forces. The teamate AI is not the best I've seen, but imo it's good enough to enjoy the game in single player. One thing that did seem a bit off was the speed of escalation when Unidad forces get involved - reminded me a bit of escalating wanted levels in the GTA games.

One major annoyance is that occasionally the game fails to launch, requiring a reboot to fix - I'm guessing that this is Uplay related.

After playing this game a lot more, I have decided to update and change my review as I know a lot more about the game now.

This game is a mixed bag, I'd say that there's more good overall than bad, but I think it's important for me to say that this game is not for everyone. I have read through most of the negative reviews for this game and understand more than ever why some people wont like this game.

I can run this game at 30-40 fps, so the game isn't optimized well for mid range processors. If you're running a mid range PC you may have issue keeping the framerate high. Graphically speaking the game looks wonderful. Screen popping was a rare occurance for me but it does happen.

Ghost Recon Wildlands is a very shallow world with little interaction outside of missions, you'll find that most of the map is wasteland and the occasional town/outpost. That isn't entirely a bad thing though, the map *is* a wasteland, but it's wasteland that's varying in terrain, in climate, and in variety. If you're the kind of person who likes to plan ahead before doing something, you can use the terrain to your advantage. This is the only game I've ever played where I have explored every corner of the map, getting every single last collectible. It was a pleasure crawling through the wastelands of Bolivia trying to sneak up on my enemies.

The guns in Ghost Recon WIldlands look and sound awesome, with silencers and without. You have the option between 3rd person ADS and 1st Person ADS. Sniping is satisfying, and hit markers make your bullets feel powerful. There's a wide variety of weapons to choose from, though you'll have to explore to find them alongside their attachments.

Personally, I play a lot of shooters and my preffered playstyle is to stealth my way though an area if that's possible. So this game is a perfect fit for me. I've played the game on all of the difficulties and now I exclusively play on the hardest setting. Stealth on the hardest setting is the only option. Going loud in this game on the harder settings is a deathwish, the only viable strategy to going loud is to hide in cover and use explosive drones, artillery, rebel support, and your AI team mates to shoot for you. Trading fire is never an option as the enemies will kill you in 2 hits and essentially are aimbotting.

Driving in this game is awful, I'm not an amazing driver in games generally speaking, but I have spent a lot of time driving in GTA 4 and 5 on the PC and in comparison, the handling in this game is awful. Flying on the other hand, alongside riding motorcycles is a far greater experience.

I quite like making an unique look, and you can definetly do that in this game. I have varying outfit presets depending on the terrain I'm in, with camo for every situation. I enjoyed making my character look like a total badass, though I don't see any point in paying for any micro transactions to unlock new weapons/skins, as those that are already in the game are more than what you'll need.

First impressions of this game might push some people away too, because of the fact that guns are locked away and you have to go out into the world to find the ones you want. I hated that at first, but it made me improvise and use different playstlyes until I eventually unlocked every single weapon and modification. You also might get overwhelmed by the HUGE ammount of varying things that you can do, this game isn't set on rails and you can choose whatever order of missions you want to do.

Overall, this is an open world stealth game, I adore this game but I wouldn't recommed it to everybody. Stealth games require patience, and some people don't have the time to patiently wait for that enemy to walk out of sight of his friends.

I would recommend the game, but not at the standard price tag. I tried it out during a free trial weekend and got it for € 20 instead of 60, which is more appropriate for what the game has to offer, in my opinion.

Why do I think so?

The gameplay is fun, gunplay is okay and the AI is a bit dumb, but for someone who doesn't play lots of shooters, like me, it's a nice experience, but not too challenging on normal difficulty. That said, the game is also extremely repetitive, which is why I don't think I would have bought it at the full price. You always do exactly the same thing, which is infiltrating bases, killing goons and stealing/tagging some item. There are four or five side-mission types and they are all the same in every province I've visited so far, which is a bit dull and could definitely have been done better.  That's why I don't see me playing through the entire game in one binge-gaming week, like I'd do with some other outstanding games like GTA or Witcher. Nevertheless, even though it's repetitive, it's also kind of addictive. It does have these "lets do one more quest" moments just because the gameplay itself is quite fun. At least it's still fun to me after maybe 10 hours. 

The story is nice enough, but don't expect something outstanding here. But it does fulfil its purpose and doesn't get boring quickly. However, I want to stress again that everything you actually do in the game is basically the same thing over and over again, which might be a bit boring for someone who wants lots of different mission types or stuff like that. 

Graphics in the game are fine, too and the visual effects are also pleasing, but I think that's to be expected from a modern shooter game. The scenery is also very nice, but don't expect an open world full of interesting things to discover. There's just some towns, villages and military/cartel-bases where you can do missions, but I haven't found anything interesting to discover so far. So the open world aspect could've been done much better, if you ask me. 

What I don't like about the game is the driving of cars and other road vehicles (airborne stuff is fine, imo). You can't switch to an in-car perspective, like you can in GTA V, for instance, which makes it very difficult to maneuver the vehicles on the serpentines in the game. This is generally a bit of a let down. There's only 3rd person perspective throughout the game, which is a bit disappointing in a shooter game. 

Another thing that I would've liked to see in the game is more options to tackle objectives. For instance, there is no grappling hook or anything of the kind. Therefore, even though you're supposed to be the most elite soldier on the planet (or something like that) you can't scale walls or cliffs to get into a base from a different angle and are basically restricted to use the main entrance (or one of the side entrances if there are any). This is kind of lame, since one of the fun things about games like this is finding creative solutions as to how to infiltrate an enemy base. 

To summarise, it's a solid game, but not an outstanding one and there are lots of things that could've been done better. Therefore, if you're interested at all, get it at a discount or try it out at a free trial weekend like the one ongoing as I'm writing these lines. I'd probably have paid 30-40€ and thought the price tag okay, but 60 is definitely too much for it in my opinion.

Like the rest of the Ghost Recon games, you're meant to be stealthy. In WIldlands, however, it's not a huge deal if you mess up, which is good for me since I am terrible with stealth, but may put off some people.

The game world is gorgeous and very detailed, it's obvious a lot of hard work was put in to it, and it runs very well on my GTX 1060 and Intel 17-7700.

The gunplay feels good, the bullets go where you'd expect them to. [strike]But that should be expected from a shooter game[/strike].

There's no jump key, only the ability to vault and climb over things. The lack of a jump key feels a bit restrictive, but hasn't affected my gameplay too greatly.

Enemies can be fairly challenging if you aren't prepared, especially the purple faction. It doesn't take many bullets to put you out of action, but you can revived by a squadmate.

No opinion on the story, I've mostly just been messing around in the free roam taking on enemy bases.

Driving isn't that great, I found it to be very floaty and hard to direct where you're going, plus the vehicles have skyrim-horse syndrome in that you can pretty much drive up the sides of mountains if you try hard enough. This isn't too much of an issue though, I've mostly just gotten around via helicopters and airplanes.

 
The character customization is pretty basic for the actual character. You're able to change your gender, face through specific presets, hair, hair color, beard, and tattoos. However, the outfit customization is decently in depth, being able to change each article of clothing and their color. Only complaint I have is many of the outfit pieces are locked behind the game's lootboxes.

This game has lootboxes, which I'm not a big fan of. As far as I can tell though, they're cosemetic, featuring things like outfit pieces and reskinned guns.

The AI you get when you play without any other human players are pretty much immortal and have pinpoint accuracy when using sync shot, and never mess you up by getting detected or get in your way. Sometimes they mark enemies, but other than that are pretty passive until commanded to do something.

There were some very tense moments where we thought we'd get seen, but it all culminated with us flying out of the stronghold with the Unidad sentries trying to shoot us down.

[b]Overall I'd give it a 7/10.[/b]

[h1](CASUAL REVIEW) Wildlands! Beautiful! Repetitive?[/h1]

[b]Disclaimer:[/b] I am writing this review as a consumer who has not followed the game at launch or it's promotions prior so I am not aware of whether or not Ubisoft had broken any promises regarding this game. Furthermore, I bought this game during a [u]67%[/u] sale so I will be basing off my enjoyment and worth of the game based on that value. I also have yet to complete the game so I will not be writing about the lore and DLCs. TL;DR for the review will also be included at the bottom!

[b]Introduction[/b]: Wildlands is an open world game based in Bolivia. You play as a rebel against the government and authorities as well as dealing with conflict with drug cartels. The game is advertised as a tactical shooter utilizing both a third-person perspective and first-person perspective camera in combat. And for the most part, it stays true to that. I will be writing my review based on the following: [b] Gameplay, Environment, and Content. [/b]

[b]Gameplay[/b]: In Wildlands, the gameplay consist of a few things-- side missions, main missions, and searching for goods (such as weapon parts). These three seperate objectives, while they slightly vary each time, are mostly the same 'rinse and repeat' cycle. You infiltrate a camp or clear out the enemies then proceed to do the objective which can consist of either escorting a hostage/vehicle, killing a target, or gathering information. This can understandably get repetitive after a while and can start to feel stale even after a few hours admittedly depending on the individual. As for gunplay, it does feel very nice and impactful with each gun varying in different damages and bullet drops, similarily to Battlefield or PUBG. However, this game very clearly benefits you taking a [i]stealthy[/i] approach as the mobs hit very hard and you can be downed easily if you are outnumbered.

[b]Environment[/b]: Bolivia, while it may not be so accurately shown (as I am unsure), is beautiful in Wildlands. From deep jungles to flatlands, the game offers a variety of different biomes each giving a distinct aura and look which makes the game feel fresh and new as you progress. The raw detail they put into the game is also nothing to joke about as it almost makes the game feel extremely realistic. Little details such as the lights turning on in the car while exiting and entering it to mud being stuck to your clothes when falling and light reflecting off your wet gear. It's truly a magnificent sight and can only really be appreciated through experience... assuming the specs on your computer are strong enough for it. Haha. For reference for how beautiful this game REALLY is, check out my [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1359939877] screenshot! [/url]

[b]Content[/b]: There is quite a lot to do in Wildlands. Questing, exploration, gear hunting and... oh? What's that? We're practically doing the same thing over and over again? Jokes aside, there is a ♥♥♥♥ ton of things to do in this game and that is a fact. However, a majority of it consist of doing the same things repetitively as mentioned in the gameplay. For some, this may be perfectly fine and they love the grind! Personally, I am also one of those individuals as I found this game to be quite enjoyable with friends to mess around with and the missions are interesting enough for us to feel engrossed into the game. However, it is very understandable why many people would feel ripped off or disappointed in this game if they paid $80 for it... that's crazy!

[b]Conclusion[/b]: Wildlands is a gorgeous game with a huge world to explore and discover filled with thousands of different things to do in the open world but is unfortunately cut short due to the repetitive nature of the gameplay and missions. It is a fun game for those who can put up with this and the experience is greatly enhanced, like with any other game, with your friends! However, I CANNOT recommend this game at a full price tag. Never. If you are interested in getting Wildlands-- buy it during a sale for at least [u]60%[/u] or more and it will be a more promising title for your money. Because of this, the game gets a overall recommendation from me.

[b]TL;DR[/b]: Wildlands is a beautiful game filled with many different environments and thousands of things to do. In three different ways. Missions and gameplay can feel repetitive after only a few hours and is not great for those who do not enjoy grinding. The game is more enjoyable with friends and is ONLY worth buying on sale of [u]60%[/u] or more. Gunplay is also relatively solid which includes bullet travel and drop similarily to Battlefield or PUBG.

As a long time Tom Clancy reader someone who's played Rainbow Six and Ghost Recon when released, and every tatical shooter since, this game is terrible. The story is amazin. The graphics are amazing. The player outfitting and weapon crafting is amazing. The vehicle controls are not good. The mobility of the player is not good, getting into a firing position or quickly getting out of the line of fire is difficult. The thing that makes this game terrible is the friendly AI in single player mode. Let's say you set up in a secure position and have your teammates pulling security while you are hiding operating the drone. Lets say that a bad guy walks into your team while you are in "drone mode." The friendly AI will completely ignore the bad guy while he shoots you in the back while you have your face in the drone video feed.

You cannot control your teammates very well. There are 4 of them but it is pointless. You can tell them to stay, go, fire, or rally, all at once. You can't set one guy up on overwatch, use one guy as a diversion, one guy as an assaulter, and one guy to cut off anyone trying to escape or ambush enemy QRF. You can't set waypoints for your team mates and execute them with go codes. You can try to assign them individual targets with "quickshot" but this results in laughable situations such as the good guy "getting into position to take the shot" by literally walking up to the enemy in his line of sight from 20 feet away. AND the enemy will be staring at good guy not firing or reacting at all to the good guy with a gun pointed at his head in broad daylight.

The friendly AI is terrible, but the enemy combatant AI is actually pretty satisfying at times. Enemies may zerg, they make team up and hunt you down, they may call for a narco QRF over the radio, and your intel guys apparently rigged your comms to eavesdrop on their radio chatter. The only problem with comms in this game is the inability to answer the phone LATER, when you're not in a high speed vehiclular gunfight. Another great example of enemy AI being very good is that on kill/capture missions you don't always have to raid. In fact, you can trip their alarms and simply wait for the target to panic, get in his vic, and come out while you set up ambush on every road waiting for him to come out.

UPDATE: Ghost Mode saves this game and makes it worth while. The friendly AI is still terrible but Ghost Mode forced you to really slow down and account for the weakness, as well as account for many other mission planning and mission execution factors that are more realistic in nature. For example, the slightly clunky movement of your gunfighter can be mitigated with more strategic use of cover, range, overwatch, smarter ingress and egress routes, and a slower assault tempo. After Ghost Mode was implemented, and the ability to change the time of day by waiting at a safe house, I thoroughly enjoyed this story and game. I also discovered that the vehicles can be controlled MUCH better if you use an x-box controller plugged right into the computer.

The inability to use your 3 teammates in specific and varying roles is eventually counteracted by the ability to use indigenous forces in those roles. For example, you can have indigs create a diversion, conduct recon, prvide mortar fire, or reinforce your assault from a flanking direction.

Don't let the wildly overblown rants about loot boxes fool you: Wildlands is a pretty solid cooperative shooter. It may not fit in perfectly thematically for hardcore fans of the Ghost Recon series, but it's a fun game in its own right. Despite the complaints, stealth is very much still a viable playstyle. You just have to actually work for it, instead of having everything telegraphed for you, and the sync shot system is there to help you accomplish that when you're playing solo. There are multiple approaches to every mission, as advertised, whether you want to go loud or quiet, close-quarters or long-range, or whatever else your heart may desire. Sure, there are a few missions now and then where you'll want to tear your hair out after the fourth try because your AI teammates won't listen to you, but the game's real strength isn't in single player anyway. Especially now that I've come back after playing Far Cry 5, I have an even stronger appreciation for the co-op play, because there's no damn invisible distance tether. 

The only time you'll ever see a blatant notification regarding loot boxes is when you have one you haven't opened. Aside from that single notification, when I claimed my two free ones off of Club Rewards, I haven't been reminded once. The loot crates will never contain anything other than skins for vehicles or weapons, or some kind of character customization cosmetic option. If you hear someone yelling about how terrible the game is when it comes to loot crates, they're probably just upset because they didn't get the shiny golden skin they wanted.

Don't fall for the whining. Ghost Recon: Wildlands may not be perfect, but it still deserves recognition.

[h1]==Introduction to the Game==[/h1]
You play as Tier One Operators in bolivia. Take down a cartel which has been running the country for a while now from the shadows. Free hostages, clear outposts, play story missions. You get the idea. However: Most aspects from previous Ghost Recon titles have been stripped down to make the game more suitable for a mainstream market.

Ghost Recon used to be a serious game about top tier soldiers that use lots of technical playthings to fullfill their missions. The games were known to be very tactical and sometimes even hardcore. You had to plan ahead and you were fragile like a real soldier would be. Make a wrong decision and it is game over.

This installment brings multiplayer into the game so you can play the entire story and open world with friends. Open world itself is also a new addition to the series.

Sadly all aspects which made Ghost Recon a unique and interesting game are gone in this title and have been replaced with customization and lots of guns as the main selling point. Basically this game could very well also be a Far Cry title and you would not notice, which is a very saddening fact.

[h1]==Performance and Technical Aspects==[/h1]
The game runs like a piece of crap in 4k regardless of the settings whereas FC5 and The Division, both Ubisoft titles just like this, run steadily and without any problems. Even in 1080p my 1080ti sometimes struggles to keep 60FPS up. From a performance standpoint, this game is a mess.

The driving physics, as well as flying is some of the worst I have seen in recent memory. Helicopters feel like they are on a rail and cars are so slippery you lose control quite often.

Weapons all feel like toy guns, they do not pack any recoil and the overall feedback just lets them seem like I am playing with airsoft guns.

[h1]==The Positive aspects==[/h1]
Giant open world with hours and hours to play, lots of fun with friends but sadly very shallow as it repeats itself quite fast.
Gun and especially character customization is some of the most in-depth possibilities I have seen in any game besides Far Cry 5 and ArmA.
If you can run it on ultra settings it looks very beautiful and stunning.



[h1]==Conclusion==[/h1]
Even with a high end system (Check my group/profile for details) this game runs like a piece of crap. The mechanics of both shooting and driving, which is about everything this game has to offer, feel clunky and badly done.

If you are getting this get ready to not be able to play on ultra settings. I would advice to only buy on a sale and only if you have friends you can play this with.

[list]
[*]Overview - Ghost Recon: Wildlands is a spectacular game in its size and varied locations, and character customization, but everything else is pretty bland and boring. Here's why I think that.
Ps: I didn't finish the game completely.

[*]Gameplay - The gameplay is pretty mediocre, you spend your time taking over outposts, collecting resources to upgrade your character and gadgets. You collect intel and 100% a region, rinse and repeat until you have everything, standard open world stuff that devs made the open world industry today.

Stealth is ok at best, it does some things right, and you do feel like you are being tactical with sync shots and some weapons being loud when shot with a silencer at close range, but otherwise, it's not really anything special. 

I should mention that story missions are just reskins of taking over outposts, or killing a certain target, so story missions feels no different than the core game.

[*]Story - Honestly, there's not much to say, it's awful, characters are forgetable, you don't care about the plot, and the game is trying to be too edgy constantly. I could elaborate some more, but the story is not at all noteworthy.

[*]Co-Op - The reason I got the game was to play with my 2 mates, and we sure did have fun for the first 20 hours maybe, but after that we felt like we experienced what the game had to offer, we did stick around for another 20 before we started to get bored of the repetitiveness.

 It is fun to mess around and such, and try out funny bugs, I remember once my friend did a nose dive and landed on a rock about 6 feet below him, and he died instantly, we died laughing doing that for a little while.

[*]Optimization - Jesus Christ, what happened there? I have a GTX 1080 and an Intel i7 4790K, and I can only barely run the game at highest settings and get a decent frame rate of 60, the problem is I have played better looking games, that have more features that runs way better, unless you can handle PS2 graphics, I would stay clear of this game if you have anything less than a mid range PC.

The game looks fine, but compared to the Witcher 3, it doesn't make sense that it runs way worse when it's on par with that game in graphical terms.

[*]Microtransactions - ... Why? They are just added clothes or guns that should have been in the game already, nothing special like a gladiator armor, but you can get a boring backpack that doesn't look any better than what is currently offered in the game.

[*]Conclusion - The game is fun with friends for a few hours, but it is just so bland, it's a beautiful open world with filler content that are also what takes up the story missions. Mediocre stealth and gunplay with guns that doesn't feel like they have much of an impact most of the time.

A huge, open world, sandbox filler content game. If the game is on sale for 20 bucks or less, go for it if you have some friends to spend the time with, but not if you already have any games you are playing currently.
[/list]

To me Ghost Recon Wildlands is the feel-good summer hit  among tactic shooter games, and loads of fun!
The game offers a huge and diverse open world, great visuals and a lot of freedom how to approach missions:

- You can play stealthy and surgical which is lots of fun, especially with friends in co-op. This way the game does feel kind of realistic and finishing a mission in "ghost mode" can be really challenging, which is awesome.

- You can come up with all kinds of cunning or stupid plans like blowing up nearby gas-stations to create diversions, or drive-by shooting, or trying to parachute drop onto the balcony of the target building..

- And you can go in guns blazing and witness how things escalate to GTA-like over the top action, often hysterically hilarious. Also loads of fun in co-op for having a good laugh.

And just like I fondly remember from SWAT 3 and 4, it's very entertaining if your careful tactical approach fails somehow and everyhing erupts into total chaos, bullets flying left and right, cars exploding starting chain reactions by setting other nearby cars on fire, enemy helicopters swarming the sky above..   and you are left with no choice but to improvise.

pros:
- up to 4 player co-op for the entire campaign!
- a lot of freedom and options to approach missions or simply "do stuff"
- !!!-fantastic-!!! style, graphics and lighting! This goes both for environment and character design!
- dynamic day/night cycle and weather
- awesome character customization! everything between future soldier, cowboy, terrorist and bum is possible
- i totally dig the rugged mercenary look: full beard and a mix of civilian clothes and scavenged military gear
- good stealth and cover mechanics
- top notch voice acting and (almost-) cheese-free dialog
- nice synergy of story and campaign mechanics (gather intel, compromise cartel bosses, control provinces, work your way up the ladder)
- gaining sympathy of local rebels can unlock nice support actions (for example rebels can make diversions, provide vehicles or intel)
- you can use cars, motorcycles, helicopters, LAV's and planes 
- well rounded gameplay experience 
- best parachute jumping EVER, in any game I've played so far
- awesome LOD'ing! even from a heights of 1-2 kilometers the landscapes look amazing (and the cities at night.. wow!)
- customizable drones are fun!
- nice music and sound design, I like the punch of the gun sounds, even with silencers
- huge arsenal of weapons, grenades, mines, c4, etc..
- believable ballistic physics
- adjustable level of difficulty and user interface options (you can turn off UI completly for "hardcore mode")
- very interesting PVP, very tactical and totally different from anything else i've played
- did I mention the diverse and often mind-blowingly beautiful environments?

cons:
- Ai buddies can be really stupid (like in most games), this can be remedied by simply placing them at a safe overwatch spot
- if you play this game for many hours per week it can become repetitive
- playing solo can be kinda dull
- i've often missed a time-advance feature (accelerated wait until dusk or dawn), workaround by fast-travel back and forth is meh..
- PVP matchmaking/player-syncing too slow.. sometimes seemed longer than the actual match (might be fixed in the meantime)


As a side note: I also enjoy ultra realistic tactic shooters like ProjectReality (now "Squad") and ARMA, but Ghost Recon Wildlands is a nice, lighthearted diversion to those. Probably more movie-like than realistic, it offers a lot of opportunities without ever getting complicated.  I hated the first Ghost Recon game for it's clunky, unresponsive controls but I understand a lot of people loved the franchise for it's realism. Maybe Ubi simply shoudn't have made Wildlands part of the franchise, because seeing it for what's -in- the box Wildlands is an absolutely awesome game!

What this game does well:

+Provides a seamless co-op experience for up to four players,
+Provides comically entertaining and/or satisfying moments for said co-op experience,
+Provides a large scale playground that feels substantially larger than any other open world game,
+Some stealth ideas are neat (a silenced pistol can't be heard as easy as a silenced assault rifle),
+Varied environments provide plentiful beautiful locales to explore.
+Plentiful amount of side quests.

What's irritating about this game:

-Story/Narrative is practically non-existent...with what little is there, it's not coherent,
-All AI (enemies and teammates) behave more like AI rather than behavioral driven,
-Despite varied environments, areas will have entire cities that are exactly the same in several regions (you will question if you've been to a particular area despite the map clearly indicating you've never been),
-Despite gun variety, only two gun types are actually useful - and of those two gun types, only a few are worth using,
-An uninspired skill progression system,
-Year 1 Season pass content does not link progression such as weapon unlocks from base game (it's standalone but requires you to own the base game to play it),
-Side quests are bare bones, copy/paste missions that have zero story content (as in no relevance to main story or any other side quest).

What does this mean:

This game has faults, and I wouldn't recommend it for $59.99. As a single player game, avoid it. This game is a different animal single player, and the cons listed will be what will make you not want to play this game in single player. If you're playing with one or up to three other friends, your mileage will vary then.

Get it when it's on sale with a couple of friends. That's when the pros outweigh the cons. Otherwise stay away.

I might continue playing for a while but I can't really imagine getting through this game.
Here are some pros and cons I've concluded in about 90 minutes of playtime:

+ It's Ghost Recon
+ Stealth Shooter (even if it's rather tedious to truly play it as one)
+ Open World with decent graphics
+ Options to skill and customize your character and weapons with parts and if you're into that also skinitems/decals/...

- Ground vehicle controls feel very wonky and you have to use them to get around or you can fly instead, which doesn't feel quite as weird
- Animations (especially speech animations) in occasional cutscenes are terrible
- Weird looking physics interactions (when you fly a helicopter your teammates bounce around from every adjustment)
- Some graphics choices/implementations that don't look like they were done very well (for example shifts in detail when getting closer to vegetation has like 5 steps of changing detail and it looks too restless for my taste)
- Ubisoft collectable-disease (maybe some people like it but since Far Cry and Assassin's Creed it mostly annoys me)
- Bullettravel seems slow (even at 50 meters you have to aim noticeably ahead of walking enemies to hit them with a sniper rifle)
- You can sort of lean up to cover by kind of walking/crouching against it but I much prefer a more solid "cover state" where you have to do something to end and/or initiate taking cover. Mainly so you're not trying to walk to an edge to shoot someone, accidentally press backwards or don't walk to the perfect position at the corner and end up not really leaning beyond the corner because of your positioning or breaking your cover alltogether


Overall it feels like they didn't take enough time to "polish" the game to make the physics feel more grounded, the controls more direct and to iron out things like the speech animations and other small discrepancies.

I grew up playing "Mercenaries: Playground of Destruction" on the PS2 and I've been looking for something to fill the void ever since my PS2 went kaput. Wildlands is the closest thing so far to scratch the itch

Pros:
-- Open world is one of the most gorgeous and immersive I've ever experienced. Particular highlights were the Inca Camina and the Koani regions
-- Story missions are pretty varied and exciting. If you focus purely on story missions, the gameplay rarely feels tired or rehashed
-- high level of character and weapon customization
-- Squad AI is actually useful and responds well to player commands
-- "Legend" collectibles contain a lot of really interesting information about the history and culture of Central and South America (if you're into that sort of thing)

Cons:
-- While you can play in any style you want, the game really REALLY wants you to take it slow and stealthily chiefly for two reasons: One - your character has very little health. Even on lower difficulties you go down very easily which is a problem during "wave defense" missions. Two - the AI is very good at finding you when you're hiding. If you kill someone - even stealthily - while the AI is "on alert" they will zero in on your position. The AI is also way too accurate: there were plenty of times where I was merc'd from 100m away by an enemy dual wielding machine pistols. These problems become even worse on Extreme Difficulty to the point where it feels unplayable

-- despite the high level of customization, lots of the more "desirable" customization options are hidden behind a paywall (probably intentionally)
-- there are six kinds of side missions in the game that are repeated ad nauseam. It's a chore to do them over and over again in order to fully unlock rebel support options: which are a huge help on some of the more frenzied missions

I'd definitely recommend the game to anyone who enjoyed Mercenaries like I did or anyone who's looking for a shooter with solid gameplay and a rich, deep world to run around in.

Ghost Recon... I've been waiting for a long time when Ubisoft will once again remember this series of tactical shooters and I was very happy when on E3 2015 they finally announced the Wildlands. However, the joy was short-lived and that's why.

Firstly, we see the completely redesigned concept of the game. Instead of traditional levels, we are sent to the big open world of virtual Bolivia. On the one hand, this is a plus, with the other negative. Advantage of the open world - we get freedom in the passage of missions, but not every developer can take advantage of this advantage.

In the Wildlands, the minus dominates the plus, as the developers could not think of anything better than filling the game world with the ctrl-c -> ctrl-v principle. This is easy to explain: we have 29 bosses, and to get to 21 of them (the rest will then appear themselves), we need to perform a bunch of monotonous objectives: kill, capture, clean the sector, intercept, destroy and sometimes overhear. I will not deny that in most modern games everything is the same, but these things are not repeated in one game several times.

The secondary objectives are presented with the same monotonous routine: defend the agitation installation, hijack a plane/helicopter with supplies, deactivate relations, intimidate the mercenary leader and all the time. As a bonus, players are invited to collect various documents that make up the history of the Ghost Recon Wildlands, skill upgrade points and weapons with gadgets. The last two things look really stupid, because it seems that Bolivia was not abandoned by special forces, but by regular infantry.

Tactical gameplay, which was the basis of the series ruined. The artificial intelligence of local dudes is even dumber than in Future Soldier, which makes it easy to eliminate them on the stealth, and no one will notice a puddle of blood or a shortage of personnel. The high difficulty only increases the accuracy and damage, as a result of which you will be killed even by firing from Uzi from the sky-high distances. And this is relevant both for the cartel soldiers, and for La Unidad soldiers (local police and army). The latter will be dangerous only at high wanted levels, because we will be regularly chased by helicopters and heavy armored cars.

As for the plot, it's secondary, as if the developers spent on creating live action trailers. I expected the story at least as in Denis Villeneuve's Sicario, but as a result, there was some crumpled narrative with a typical ending. I have long noticed the trend that the theme of Latin American cartels is one of the weakest in video games...

Of course, it's hard to evaluate Ghost Recon Wildlands. In my opinion, the series went in the wrong direction, and the ideal option is the Future Soldier concept, but not the open world. Perhaps, I wouldn't rank it as a flaw, but the game turned into a continuous routine, not to mention the ruined tactical gameplay. It's ridiculous to say, but even in Metal Gear Solid V virtual opponents had more tactical features than here. In Ghost Recon Wildlands, opponents can surprise you only with their stupidity and high accuracy, no more, and the plot is very mediocre. I put thumbs up, because there is no neutral evaluation. The game has potential, but implementation leaves much to be desired.

Hi,

My first review so be gentle.

After playing many Tom Clancy games in the past (including the first...yes I am that OLD!) I was not actually expecting much from this offering since I felt the game series had gone down a slippery slope of "arcade" style.  After watching "The Mighty Jingles" play this on his Casual Saturdays I thought I would give it a shot.

The graphics (if you have a decent spec, I have a Nvidia 1080, quick SSD & i7) are brilliant and I really enjoyed flying/driving/running-like-hell around Bolivia, obviously a beautiful country I have yet to see IRL.  Some bugs do exist but I can appreciate that making an open world, mountainous country without the game occassionally having a bug is pretty hard given the amount of variables.  Some of them can be "mission" breaking but never game breaking in my experience, a quick reset and new approach can sometimes be frustrating and on other occassions be more rewarding.

The sounds can be a tad repetative and the radio is annoying after a few hours of the same messages.  I played with a headset (married with kids so....yeah) with virtual surround active which was fine.  Some variations are noticeable with the weapons but most of the generic "bang/splut/pop" which is unfortunate.  Again, not game breaking but attention to detail would have been great.

The story is a typical "America World Police" but there are some lovely twists dependant on the choices you make.....my femme fatale associate was "right" to do what she did at the end and took the fall in my first play through.

The missions are varied at the start until you realise that they are all pretty much repeated, IMHO the most fun you can have is varying your approach to each.  Go stealth, go snipe, go loud and go balls-deep.....all viable but some work better than others and sometimes you just get lucky!

AI can be stupid beyond reason at some points and absolute Special Forces monsters at others.  It depends what the game feels like it wants to do.  No mission I played ended up with the same outcome....some Unidad patrol overkill and some sneaked, shot, sneaked & complete.  The stealthy ones are the most satisfying but getting a long range silenced sniper kill without alerting anybody is probably the most fun!

The weapons....hmmmm.  You have to "find" the weapons/upgrades that make this game a lot more fun.  Most powerful sniper rifle..head to another zone and pick it up.  Nothing wrong with that but if you read online guides then you will get the most powerful stuff really quickly which takes away some replayability but on my second run through thats exactly what I did.  Still enjoyed the suppressed variation which is accurate IRL (loudest guns are still loud-ish if you have one fitted) and the fact that you can decide what upgrades you use.  Oh, and the worst aspect is the option of buying weapons in the "store"......what a money grabbing act of complete fail.

Co-Op is a lot more fun than I imagined.  3 of us sneaking from different directions, calling out targets, sniping, lobbing grenades, saving each other when we failed massively to sneak around.....huge plus for me and if you have friends who play this then I recommend grouping up and taking the cartel down together. 

Multiplayer....I don't do it due to old age, failing reflexes, poor old man eyesight and just being crap at it.....so I can't comment on it; sorry!

I have played Far Cry etc but being a military man IRL I felt this is so much more fun and allows me to decide what/where/when.  Loved the game despite its obvious flaws!

Hope you have fun.

Kind regards,

Ghost Recon: Wildlands is a big letdown. The idea of the game is neat and a good idea for the Ghost Recon series, but the execution is by any standards not acceptable. It lacks many fundamental things which are a must have for a good shooter.

Pros:
+ Huge and stunning map with different terrains and impressing landmarks.
+ Incredible character and weapons customization. Probably the best I ever saw in a game.
+ Extensive options menu.
+ Good performance.
+ Soundtrack fits nice in the beginning, but gets boring because the amount of tracks is very limited.


Cons:
- The map is littered with the usual random filler content - collectibles, random patrols, resources. No other interaction with your environment than that.
- The story is almost non-existent and offers no memorable moments or characters. While looking nice, the country and especially the villains are very unbelievable. They can afford sports cars, littlebirds with miniguns, and flatscreens, but no doors, proper beds, or paint for their houses. Overall, the world feels like how a 14-year-old Breaking Bad fan might imagine a narco-state.
- Boring, repetitive and overused mission design with zero creativity or innovation.
- Maybe the worst AI I ever saw in an open-world game. Unadaptive, implausible, bugged and no tactics or coordination. Ubisoft said the AI will have realistic behavior with a simulated day-night circle. This means some of the guards will sleep in the night, while others standing on guard at the same spot for the whole day. When in a fight, they usually just run into the player one after the other without any efforts to suppress, to flank or to overwhelm.
- The world is filled by the usual ridiculous and braindead civ-AI which is probably used since Far Cry 3.
- The rebel AI randomly likes to assault an enemy camp which you are trying to infiltrate.
- The AI of your squad-mates is "okay". They benefit from massive cheats so the enemies probably ignore them most of the time. They tend to stand around on rails without any interest for approaching trains.
- Gunplay feels spongy, unsatisfying and unnatural. I especially dislike the soundeffect that you can always hear an impact when hitting an enemy, no matter how far away he is. Maybe this was added to stimulate the player and to whitewash the bad hit-detection.
- Animations tend to be buggy.
- The driving physics are dreadful. The controls for cars and aircraft feel very unintuitive.
- Unnecessary level system. Because every game needs an unnecessary level system.
- One year after release the game is still plagued by bugs, glitches and AI-breaks.
- A gigantic ingame-shop where you can buy all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t one can imagine for hard cash.
- Health regeneration.
- The Santa-Blanca-propaganda radio with this DJ is the most obnoxious radio show I ever had to listen to.
- All that sold by a typical over-hyping, inflated and mendacious marketing campaign.

A smaller map with more focus on the interaction with the enviroment, proper squad-features rather than this pointless level-system and all that wallhack-crap, more love put into the AI and the gunplay, and some more polishing would have been much needed. Instead, we get quantity over quality and a Ubisoft formula game - lacking of inspiration and innovation more than ever.

[h1] Visuals/Graphics [/h1]
This game is the best looking open world game ever and is one of the best looking games in general. The lighting, the terrain, the weather and the distant landscapes are all superb quality. Seriously a visual overload. And your graphics card will suffer. Cranking every setting up to the max stresses your GPU like no other game can. This is the new "Can it run crysis?". There's a price to pay for visual fidelity and it sure is worth it.

[h1] Sounds [/h1]
The sounds in this game are awesome. The gravel under your feet, swimming through one of the many lakes and hiking up a mountain covered in snow all sound spectacular. The environmental sounds are spot on. 

The weapon sounds are great for the most part. The majority of the weapons sound beefy when they're fired (especially the sniper rifles) and the suppressor sounds are good as well. The SMG's can sometimes sound like pea shooters and the pistol sounds can leave a little to be desired but overall the weapon sounds are awesome. The hitmarker sounds are a little too much (COD like?) in my opinion. 

Helicopter and plane sounds are great but car and truck sounds are lacking. Obviously they aren't the main focus of the game but they just sound okay.

The voice acting is good but nothing to write home about.

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]
Is the game repetitive? Yes but I enjoy that. I'm one of those nerds who likes figuring out the best vantage point and turns their HUD off. The game world is huge. Massive. Gargantuan. And extremely detailed. Probably the biggest map in any game ever. The gun play is solid but there is a ton of bullet drop after a certain point; almost exponential. And the vehicle controls are crappy at best. I liked the story and it was fun to play but there wasn't anything new with it. They've fixed the AI so they don't know your position without ever seeing you but them searching your general area still happens.

[h1] Verdict [/h1]
If they ever make a second Wildlands, I hope it's more hardcore and less "mainstream". I feel like that would get rid of a lot of the problems that exist in the game currently due to it being caterted to the more casual gamer. I wouldn't go totally hardcore like Arma but tuning the gunplay and AI would make it near perfect. 

Even with all of it's flaws, this is still one of my favorite games. I've spent hours walking from one waypoint to the next clearing outposts and gazing at the incredible visuals this game offers. It's not perfect but it sure is a ton of fun.

The game is better than I thought it was gonna be. I've never played a Tom Clancy game so I went into this with no real idea of what to expect. From the hours I've played, it feels to me like a mix of Just Cause and Metal Gear. There's a lot of action and some good quality gunplay, but my preferred way to play is using stealth, marking out enemy locations and picking the best way to sneak in undetected. In my opinion its a stronger aspect of the game than the combat itself, but both are good.

The story is decent too, though I haven't progressed very far. It gives you good reasons to travel to each area and there are a lot of videos and documents that go into more depth if you desire it. 

My initial main draw to the game was from the open world itself and I have to say it didn't disappoint. The different regions of Bolivia represented here are very diverse and exploring each new area has always brought surprises. As for how  you can traverse the world, you have your standard ground vehicles like cars and bikes, along with boats, planes and helicopters. The land vehicles seem a bit too floaty for my liking, especially in faster ones like sports cars. The helicopters are definitely my preferred method of travel. They control well and most of them are helpful in combat.

Finally, I want to talk about the AI. If you plan on playing this game solo like myself, you'll have 3 AI teammates who follow you around and provide assistance. But don't worry if you'd rather go it alone; you can always tell them to hold back if you don't want the help. Not that the help they provide is always top-tier anyway. In stealth they're totally fine, mainly because the enemies seem to ignore their presence (I've seen them walk in front of guards countless times with no consequence) but in combat they seem rather awkward. They're fairly accurate on foot, but stick them in a vehicle and they couldn't hit the bronze side of a barn. Trying to take out convoys is nigh impossible with the AI doing the shooting, so you'd better be good at ramming the vehicles off the road. Apart from that though, they're good enough. I make regular use of the "Sync Shot" function they have, allowing you to pick off multiple targets simultaneously.

Overall, I would recommend this game, although I would strongly suggest waiting for a sale. £50 in the UK is a lot of money to throw down on a game, and in my opinion this game isn't fantastic enough to warrant that kind of price tag. Don't get me wrong, it's fun, and I'm probably going to be putting a lot of time into it, but definitely try to get some money off if you can.

[h1]TL;DR[/h1]

Wildlands can't really decide whether it's an action game, stealth game, tactical simulator or a skill based exploration MMO. In the end, it excels at none of those, becomes a fancy shooting gallery instead and falls short in the endgame. One thing it's definitely not, is a Ghost Recon experience.

[h1]Too long part[/h1]

The limited amount of unlockables and gear doesn't really allow for sensible team-oriented builds. You eventuyally unlock all skills and have all of them at your disposal at all times. You're always better off being a one man army which by itself stomps teamwork and public matchmaking into the ground. Not like matchmaking with people who run off hunting llamas is fun anyway.

The extremely vast environment, while nice to look at, provides surprisnigly low variety. Same goes for missions and enemy types. You fight the same dudes for the whole game, you just become a bit more efficient at it by the 30th level.

The combat system obviousy encourages you to be stealthy as you are very easy to kill with a few rounds, very hard to detect by oblivious enemies (who are shooting with great accuracy once they DO detect you), headshots with pretty much anything are a 1-shot kill and the recon tools at your disposal are outright Godlike overpowered. 

You know where everyone is at all times which actually sucks. A fair challenge would be turning on the highest difficulty and disabling all HUD elements, but then it's you against tens of Bolivian clones of John Wick. That's not really fun either!

If only Wildlands got the same after-release care that the Division got, same amount of fine tweaks and additional content, it would have been an amazing game. Unfortunately, it seems abandoned and unfinished in comparison. Fair to say, it's fun for a while, you can mess around with various difficulty settings, unlock new gear and skills, but the will to go on pretty much ends once you reach level 30.

I would recommend getting it on sale if you're just looking for some temporary mindless action-packed fun.

A lot of people mention how repetitive this game is. Well, they're correct. It definitely is. But, I don't mind. I'm a really laid back gamer and I'll take my time on a game until I either finish it or walk away completely. This is one of those games.

The AI can be a bit stupid at times, as in, hold your position clearly means not stay out of sight and shoot the enemy while the player tries to go all ninja and wipe out a base without getting busted, but instead dies repeatedly because of the mentally challenged A-Team you just gave orders to. Oh, and I should mention how members of said team like to belt out how they can see an enemy through mountainous terrain/rocks/trees and buildings five miles away before you even get to where you're going or have a clear vantage point. If I can't see through things, how can they?! Whatever the superpower is called, it's actually pretty helpful, if not unrealistic.

The game looks beautiful. I have a GTX 1080, so I can't say what it'd look like with a lower-end GPU, so this may come off as...bias? Everything is crisp and clear. No complaints in this department. Day and night seems to cycle at a decent rate, unlike other games where day lasts a minute and night goes on until you graduate college.

I've played for about 16 hours or so, now, and within that time they've already done an update and screwed up the way the camera operates. It now pans slower than a sloth on a skateboard, well, if you're using a controller, that is. Keyboard and mouse still function as normal, I assume. They've also changed on-screen button icons that didn't need to be, but I suppose that's not something to whine about, though. Worth a mention, I guess. Someone obviously hasn't heard the phrase "if it ain't broke, don't fix it".

All in all, it's a decent time-killer. I haven't played multiplayer as of yet, but I'm sure it's fun. Most games are in this mode, especially when playing with people who have loud music going in the background or constantly scream obscenities because they lack Jesus. I don't know. I'll eventually get around to it. As of this review/rambling, the game is on sale, so it's worth it at the $20 price point. Stay away if at full price and just be patient for the next sale.

Well, that about wraps things up. I think I'll go drive down a mountain at full speed and keep going because of the realistic way the vehicles have super-strength or, fly a helicopter until it explodes in air, wait to hit the ground and walk away like nothing happened. Yeah, Wildlands for sure.

I won't say this is a bad game, it does have a lot of problems though.  Random crashes, the occasional invisible enemy, stuff like that.

It is not very well optimized, like at all, so if you are using anything under the power of a RX 570 or 1060 then you'll need to play on medium settings or be prepared to run under 30 fps in a lot of areas.

The Story is just the typical generic "America is here to save the day" ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with all sorts of military talk cheese that games like these all seem to have. None of the characters are relatable (I could not ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stand Bowman at all). There is little to no character development.

Gameplay-wise it can be pretty fun, especially with friends. The map is pretty large and has a ♥♥♥♥ load of main and side missions. Overall I'd say wait until its at least on sale for $25 or lower.
