Ghost Recon : Wildlands is a Open World TPS, Created by Ubisoft Paris. (The same studio behind Future Soldier)

[b][u]THE PROS[/u][/b] : 

- The game is huge, at the second you're starting you can clearly see that we're facing something big, the devs really managed to get the Bolivia feeling right, the world is alive, people are living their own lives, interacting with eachother, the wildlife is present.

- Graphics are top-notch level (Not for every rig tho), the Vistas are gorgeous, you won't be surprised if you're taking screenshots all the time, it's beautiful.

- The game has been build around hardcore Co-Op, which is awsome when you got some friends and you're planning a strategy in order to either stealth it or bust your way through, it adds a really deep gameplay to the game. (Some people may say it gets repetitive, which i can agree but get some friend and be serious when doing the job, you'll see that it won't be repetitive at all.)

- Controls feels cluncky at the start but once you've got it (especially if you're used to the olds ghost recon), it's like a second nature and fits well to the gameplay.

- The story overall is nice and well-thinked, what would happen if a drug cartel take over a country? You just need to get into it (and like the Tom Clancy type of stories in general) to like it, especially with such a game, that distilled the whole story throughout the game, get to the story and you'll found out that it's a really good story.

[b][u]THE CON[/u][/b] (Yes, not cons)

- The AI. Oh my god, the AI in the game is HORRIBLE, beyond everything i saw before. They're ruining the gameplay so much in both Stealth and Loud aspects that it will be your nightmare every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ time you'll launch the game, here's why :

- Stealth : The AI is a Hive mind, one is triggered, 2 seconds later every single guy in the base is aware of your presence and managed to pin-point your location like if you were GPS-Tracked. They're not in search mode in the entire base, they're sprinting all the way through like Usain Bolts dopped with steorides, it's even more true when you're playing with a sniper, 500 meters away. That make me laugh once. Also don't even think about being stealthy when they track you because can spot you within 5 seconds from 200 meters without any problem.

- Loud : Bots have Aimbots, Wallhack and locks-on. I don't mind that usually, i mean it's bots, they're dumb by nature, but here it's like the devs knews that their AI's were dumb so they went full power with that. It wasn't that of a problem in Future Soldier since it was a linear game and they managed to balance thoses ones right (yeah, i'm quotting Future Soldier because that's the same AI) but here? a cartel member, topless is taking 3/4 shots to the body, firing with his two Uzis without any recoil, the same gun that fire a lazer-like spray of bullets? do i really to say more?

The AI feels clumsy, dumb and poorly designed and will ruined your fun if you're not super-tolerant about that.

[i]In the end, should i recommand it? if you can by-pass the AI's go for it. But only buy the main game, DLC's are crap[/i].

Firstly, we can all agree that Ubisoft is a **** company that prioritises revenue over good gameplay experience but for this game I think the folks over Ubisoft Paris, Ubisoft Bucharest, Ubisoft Milan and others did a good job at making this game. This is one of the better single player experiences in the current industry today. Now I’m not saying that this is the best game but from the usual Ubisoft suspects, this game does stands out. Though it does have some flaws but ill cover that in a bit more detail later.

 Now the best thing about Ghost Recon Wildlands is the setting, the story of Wildlands is the focal point and main point of the game and all others stuff are add-ons to the base game. The story revolves around hunting down El Sueno who is an all mighty drug lord that rules over all of Bolivia as if it’s his own country. This story echoes the real-life story of Pablo Escobar and his reign of terror and the effort it took to take him down (though Pablo Escobar was in Columbia not Bolivia which is why the Bolivian Government was cheesed off because of where they choose to set this story. I don’t want to get into politics so read the articles about this elsewhere).

 The game does a great job of modelling the entirety of Bolivia and they also place many informational collectables for you to learn the beliefs and stories of the Bolivian people. They also model the power struggle of the cartel very well that if feels like this cartel is held together by strings and the fear of El Sueno. The operators that you play as also have very unique personalities that make the world feel more real (though the amount of dialogue between the 4 operators are very limited and will repeat if you pass by old areas so it can become annoying after a while)

 Now for the game play aspect I won’t praise so highly like I did the previous segments, because though the base gameplay of stealth co-op play is great fun, it becomes repetitive really fast. The game is only a lot more fun is you have friends while playing the game to mess around with or else the game becomes a boring collect-a-thon. This is also not helped by the games second ending that only happens if you defeat 100% of the bosses in the game (I don’t know it you also have to collect 100% of all items because I collected them long before I defeated the bosses). However, the game doesn’t end after defeating El Sueno, because the game is still being updated with special events and the recent Predator event (Which was amazing BTW).

 The gameplay aspect is also hammered by the bad multiplayer connection issues. The multiplayer of this game suffers pretty much like all other Ubisoft titles (It’s like they don’t know how to make a proper multiplayer game). The game will lag a lot when you open up a multiplayer session that the game becomes unplayable for the most part. The only way I was able to make this become less of an issue was to make sure that the friend that host the game must have the steady’s internet connection (that host must also become the driver because the lag will make driving impossible with this game).

 Also, the multiplayer versus mode feels tacked on just because Ubisoft Corporate wanted to turn the game into a multiplayer game because that’s what they do to all games. If Ubisoft Corporate had the chance to change the core game they would have definitely tried to put loot boxes in it, so we are lucky that they didn’t get the chance to do that. The only micro transactions in this game is purely cosmetic and don’t affect the game play at all. The DLC however I can’t say much off because I only played “Fallen Ghost” and that DLC was just a glorified hard mode with extra feature (Fallen Ghost is still good but just way too short and only fun if played with multiplayer since the single player just feels like the same old repetition from the base game). I didn’t buy Narco Road because driving in this game is S*** so good luck trying to race.

 So, in short this is a great single player game with great story and add-on content with mediocre DLC and broken servers for the Multiplayer. Personally, I think the base game is the only worth wild item in the whole series with the rest just options that I wouldn’t really improve much from it unless you want some more missions.

This is certianly the absolute best multiplayer co-op "PVE" style of video game I've played this decade, even topping my previous #1 on the list "Torchlight II".  I play all sorts of games in all sorts of themes and genres, but I'm super picky when it comes to certain aspects, with my #1 priority being the gameplay itself, especially focusing on multiplayer playability.  If the game isn't fun to play as a group, I usually don't care to spend much time on it.  Wildlands does not have this problem.

More good things about the game:
Wildlands is a 10 / 10 on gameplay, environment design, progression systems, multiplayer systems and networking, storyline, and port optimization is pretty good.  The game is BEAUTIFUL.  The game is HARD but scales really nicely with more squad-mates.  Rewards are better for playing on harder difficulties.  The loot grind (for guns, attachments, upgrades, etc) is entirely "optional" and does not significantly interfere with gameplay.  No recurring cost encountered yet and i'm 70 hours in already... I think I've completed about 60-65% of the story missions and still plenty of things to do... expecting to get about 100 hours out of the game first playthrough which I say is pretty good.  Also you don't really have to worry about out-progressing your friends.  All the missions work no matter who is where in the story.  You might not get "storyline" credit for something you haven't unlocked yet, so just watch out for that, but I think about 80% of the missions are available RIGHT AWAY due to the completely open world design.   It's amazing.  Difficulty levels also merge together in co-op mode (I believe your difficulty applies to you personally) though I'm not 100% sure how this works.  I believe the difficulty impacts how enemies can detect you and how much damage they do to you individually (basically, your teammates may have a "handicap" if they play on easier difficulty level).  This system is incredible and way ahead of its time.


What's bad about it:
Uplay is some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.  Had some issues getting the game to run due to Uplay issues and outdated graphics drivers.  I've seen a few glitches here and there.  Price point is a little steep for some people but you're really getting what you pay for here.  (also it goes on sale for $30 semi-frequently)  Single player is really not as much fun.... probably comparable to Farcry series but a little less immersive (less crafting, survival aspects, etc)... but I don't play the SP much at all.  Replayability is also questionable, I haven't beat the game yet but I imagine it will be somewhat like replaying Borderlands 2 or something like that... you can scale up the difficulty to make it more interesting but I dunno if that makes it any more fun.

This game can be both incredibly engaging, and incredibly infuriating. I have been playing at the highest difficulty, with no HUD, and that has required me to play very tactically, forcing me to engage with systems I would have otherwise left untouched. The semi-realistic ballistics (It doesn't appear to take wind into account), adds a subtle level of difficulty as it requires you to understand how your weapon will work in any given situation. I took the time to document the individual characteristics of my favored weapons, things such as bullet drop and travel time, which is something I couldn't say for any other game I've played. My playstyle has been centered around using sniper rifles, and making shots at long range (400+ meters) has proven to be very satisfying. The game is exceptional when playing with friends. Playing spotter for my friend as he infiltrates a base was some of the best gameplay I've experienced this year. The version of Bolivia in the game is beautiful and expansive, with a wide variety of environments, from salt flats to mountain jungles. This combined with the dynamic weather leads to picturesque, almost breathtaking views. There were moments in my playthrough where these vistas lined up with the games soundtrack in a rather sublime way.

 However, the game is not without it's flaws. The story is completely forgettable, serving as little more than an excuse to get to the next mission. The variety among the side missions leaves something to be desired. You will find yourself stealing the same planes and stopping the same convoys over and over again. The AI leaves something to be desired, and I have found myself yelling in frustration at multiple times playing the game. The 3 teammate NPC's are next to worthless outside of there use for sync shot. All to often I find myself being flanked and killed by enemies while my teammates did nothing to help. More often than not they will prioritize reviving you over killing enemies. This has led to situations where they are reviving me in front of the enemy who just took me down, who then proceeds to immediately open fire again, usually resulting in being knocked right back down again. They are constantly repeating the same boring dialog, and telling the same unfunny jokes over and over again. The rebel NPC's that are meant to act as your reinforcements have proven to be more of a hindrance than anything. I have had them show up and engage the enemy while I am trying to infiltrate a base, blowing my cover and getting me killed (cause as soon as the enemy are fighting the rebels, they know exactly where I am as well). The environments have a tendency to be finicky, with many surfaces seeming like they should  be climbable when they were not. There were multiple times where I found myself stuck in some mountain cliff, forcing me to abandon whatever I was doing and fast travel away.

Also, the cars don't have horns. Come on Ubi, it's 2017, put a horn on that car.

Overall, I've really enjoyed my time with Wildlands. I would recommend picking it up either if you have a friend you plan to play it with, or if you happen to see it on sale.

Over all, this is well worth the price tag. Plenty of things to do in game, plenty of regions and weapons. Enough side missions to keep you busy for the most part. Now this isn't Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, which is massive and you can get hundreds of hours of play without ever touching the main quest line in the game, but Wildlands is definitely fun. HOWEVER!!!!!!!!!!! THERE IS NO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ JUMP BUTTON!!!!! Really the only major complaint I have about the game. It's an open world, over the shoulder shooter with RPG elements, whose game is similar in map set up as LoZ Breath of the Wilds, Horizon Zero Dawn, Skyrim and Borderlands. Except without a jump button. I've had to exit the game to the main menu and re-enter just to unstick myself where a JUMP BUTTON would've gotten me out, a lot too. I seriously will take 5 hours explaining why a 3-d openworld, NEXT GEN, RPG-esque game SHOULD HAVE A MOTHER LOVING JUMP BUTTON. 

But anyways, gameplay, world, visuals, content, weaponry, they are all great, very well done. Another small issue, minus the usual complaints about enemies in either direction, and the vehicles being difficult to drive, is that the weapon selection, while large and nice, never really see's new weapons added into the game, except with set versions or some wepons which you don't get the pain skin they use and cannot customize them except maybe putting on a silencer. This and the lack of uniquely different weapons limits the types of players. You're either Long Range, Mid-Range (the all around player), or CQB with SMG's and shotty's, or "Heavy" gunner with a very small number of weapons that would be considered "Heavy" class. I believe you have 4 different shotguns and 5 or 6 different LMG's? while you have over 10 snipers, at least 20 Assault Rifles, and close to, if not more than, 20 SMG's. Only 2 or 3 full auto pistols, and maybe 10 pistols, minus special versions of weapons and DLC's which add some old fashioned weapons (Musket Rifle and Pistol being the most notable). Mission objective, free the rebel prisoners. Landed helicopter close enough to recon the mission objective area to find out that it has a surprisingly solid setup. A massive bowl shaped canyon surrounded on all sides by huge cliff walls. Only one narrow, well-guarded way in. Deploy drone. Crap. Drone jammer. Judging by the red blobs everywhere on the mini map, this was going to be tough without any intel on enemy positions. I dig my binoculars out of my pack and peer down into the canyon the old-fashioned way. I spot combatants everywhere. The canyon walls have multi floored walkways build on to them with prison cells hollowed out in the walls. Four floors high. Must be hundreds of cells. Guards everywhere. Snipers. Alarms. Panel and spot lights. Going to make it difficult even if I wait till night. I spot the generator... with no lights near it. There’s my in. I'll wait till night, parachute in near the generator and shut it down to kill the lights. Without the lights I can just sneak around, silently drop a guard or two and take my time opening cell doors and let the rebels out to occupy the guards. 

I run around and knock out a few supply missions while I wait till night, jump in my chopper and pass directly over the canyon… bail out and carefully aim my chute near the dark spot close to the generator. I’m off a little and quickly go prone, holding my breath and hoping no one saw me. Seconds eek by but feel like an eternity. No alarms. Just as I exhale.. my chopper crashes somewhere nearby and explodes. Crap. I didn’t think about that. Red dots flash everywhere as guards go into high alert. I shoot out some lights and take out three guards that have drawn a bead on me with my MP5. My only hope is to make it to the generator to shut off all the lights and alarms. I shoot out a light panel illuminating the path between me and the generator  and make a run for it. The ground erupts around me in gunfire. I shoot out the lock and dive to the switch to kill the power and go prone behind a concrete barrier surrounding the generator. All the lights die. Also… all the cell doors open. They were rigged to the power system, apparently. Didn’t expect that. 

Green dots appear on the mini map EVERYWHERE. Sweet. The rebels are free. Gunfire erupts all over. All hell breaks loose. As many guards as there are, there are a lot more rebels now. I watch as the red dots wink out. I pop up and take out a few myself. 

A few minutes later, my mission is accomplished and I’m feeling awesome. Not my usual silent, in-and-out without ever being spotted method and it hurt my stealth profile score a bit, but it worked. And it was epic.

Longer review --  the options for this are myriad and they are great.  Customize your character (both male and female),  The guns are highly customizable and brilliantly depicted, with incentive to earn more parts on stand-alone missions.  I had a lot of fun just swapping different guns depending on the mood and needs of the mission.  Bullet trajectory is modeled somewhat, and is enough to keep things interesting yet fun.

Controls are very intuitive, and I found myself using a Xbox-style controller instead of a mouse, and I'm usually a mosue person for FPS's, to the point that I would always use the mouse for combat in GTA V.  In this game, I haven't used the mouse once, so that shows how well things are balanced.  While running around is in 3rd person mode, aimed shots are in first person, and the attention to detail on iron sights and scope options is very much appreciated.  

Sound is an important component to the game, both for the ambience (much like GTA, including radio shows, music on the radio, eetc.) and for the actual special effects for weapons.  Firefights without suppression (and most guns do come with suppressors) are a feast for the ears.

The map itself is huge (someone online said it was 4-5 times the size of the GTA V map) and varied enough to make a difference location to location in terms of the different provinces.

Vehicle simulation is just ok, which makes sense, since this is more of a combat and gun simulator vs. a vehicle simulator.  Thus, GTA V has better driving, but that's because GTA V is about driving.  This game is about combat, so the guns and combat are more exquisitely modeled.

So far the AI seems fine to me.  It is somewhat predictable, but doesn't do anything stupid, and is a challenge enough.  Enemies do show up fast, but given the leeway you have in other dimensions to stay stealthy, it is balanced enough to keep things fair and fun.

I am going to compare this to another game that not many others make the connection but I am sure others wonder about.

Just Cause 3. I was skeptical about jumping into a jungle terrorist shooter because I have already put a solid amount of time into Just Cause and completed each mission base etc. But something I always wanted from the Just cause series is stealth and tactical gameplay. The most tacticle that JC3 can be is sniping from very afar, even melee alerts every soldier.

Now Ghost Recon Wildlands is not the most advanced military simulation but regarding your squad they can be told to open fire on a group, hold back, follow, and of course sync shotting enemies.

To point out the big listed takeaways I'll cut to the chase.



+Wildlands Pros+

+++Giant world. Seriously most games I do not believe in fast traveling because the game is open world and filled with roads and enemies for a reason, but this is a giant country made of 15 or nations. 3-4 nations probably would have been plenty
+++Wide selection of weapons. After 20ish hours I was finally done hunting for favorite personalized parts. This was very enjoyable creating a weapon by finding the pieces I wanted.
+++Useful land mass. In this I mean that in a game like JC3 the jungles and oceans do not contain much of reason to go through, besides seperate the world and make the world big obviously. With Wildlands there are many sites, cocaine farms, hideouts etc to run into. As well as using the treeline and mountains as a sniping position.
+++Variety of landscapes. Snow, mounatin, jungle, swamp, desert, badlands, salt flats, urban warfare, village, mines, worksites, factories.



*Specialty*

***Ultra Realisim. This is an odd pro because it is one that no other game makes me think of. Many many games happen in modern times and have increased bullet damage etc. But Wildlands packages all of its assets into something that feels so realistic that often times I forget that I am playing a video game and am completely pulled into the game world. Obviously JC3 has a arcadey speed action feel. Wildlands is easily one of my favorite games I own, and though it has sold well due to reviews I can see this becoming number 1 on future "hidden gems" lists.



-Common Cons-

---People have called it repetive. But honestly it is in the sense of repeated mission types. The game is all about assassinating leaders, sneaking out of bases with intel, sabataging equipment, through caves, jungle bases, villages, hospitals, chemical labs. HONESTLY these types of mission is all the game is but they do not get old, no one becomes bored of that type of mission!
---Bad driving Controls. I will agree with this the cars are very slidy which after some time just becomes more drifty than it is a hinderance
---Bad team AI. This can be broken down as that as a tac-shooter there really is not many options for utilizing your team.
---Weapon parts are useless. This I will tether back to the realisim factor. Yes there are a ton of parts and you can beat the game without the extra parts, but then again in real life adding a laser pointer, or folded stock is not going to dramatically change the gunplay expierence.
---Respawning Bases and enemies. This complaint confuses me because never would I complain that I can go back to big or my favorite bases to re take down. Instantly makes the game replayable forever if you enjoy the combat.
---Story. The story actually is a con because it is generally devoid of moral, value, and character. You are a very abiding soldier who will do exactly what you are told, the ends justfys the means!

Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon® Wildlands is an open-world tactical shooter video game that takes place in Bolivia, where you play as part of a special forces team, tasked with taking down a powerful drug cartel. The game offers an extensive and immersive experience, allowing players to explore the vast open-world environment while engaging in thrilling tactical combat.

The game's story is engaging and well-crafted, with a variety of missions and objectives that keep you on your toes. The main campaign is divided into multiple regions, each with its own unique terrain, culture, and storylines. The game also features side missions, which offer additional challenges and rewards.

What sets Ghost Recon® Wildlands apart from other games is its emphasis on tactical gameplay. You can choose to take on each mission with a different approach, whether it's through stealth, sniping, or full-on assault. The game rewards players who take a more strategic approach, using gadgets, drones, and teamwork to take down enemies. The game's graphics are impressive, with a realistic depiction of the Bolivian landscape, including mountains, forests, and deserts. The attention to detail is also evident in the character models, weapons, and vehicles, which are all rendered with a high degree of realism.

One of the standout features of Ghost Recon® Wildlands is the cooperative multiplayer mode, which allows up to four players to play together in the open-world environment. This adds a new level of teamwork and strategy to the game, as players can coordinate their tactics and take on the drug cartel as a cohesive unit. While the game does have some minor flaws, such as occasional glitches and AI issues, these do not detract from the overall experience. In conclusion, Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon® Wildlands is a well-designed and immersive tactical shooter that offers hours of engaging gameplay, with its tactical combat, open-world exploration, and cooperative multiplayer mode, making it a must-play for fans of the genre.

Sadly the common complaint that Wildlands becomes repetitive does bear some truth.  Most of the missions are of the "kidnap the VIP" sort, or the basic “Search and Destroy”.  A few of the missions involving the bigger cartel heads are more creative, but it still doesn't make up for that feeling of sameness.  Hell, even the final mission suffers from this problem – once you reach the rendezvous point, it’s basically a speedrun from the ambush point to the Mausoleum, only without Rebel support.  

I think I've narrowed it down to a matter of convenience - particularly, the helicopters.  Having helos available to quickly whisk you from one area to the next make it far too easy to exploit the AI's weaknesses, as well as quickly bypass the enemy's defenses.  One too many a mission (especially the extraction/kidnap missions) could be made trivial by merely getting an armed light chopper, buzzing the few enemies near the target, identifying any major threats, and then swooping in to grab them.  And while the game will try to pursue you with their own choppers at times, they're pretty easy to dodge and out-maneuver.  And yes, even the final mission can be made trivial if you find yourself an armed chopper.  

It’s big enough of a problem that I’ve wondered just how much of a positive impact it would’ve had on the game if Ubisoft either made the choppers extremely rare and expensive to use, or limited them to special scenarios or support calls with no direct player control (basically, the same way Metal Gear Solid V handled Pequod, the extraction chopper).  Certainly would’ve made the extraction missions a lot trickier.

Ok, now that my biggest gripe is out of the way, let’s get to the good part, and why I’ve bothered to spend roughly 85 hours playing it.  For one, the core gameplay loop of finding a target, scouting out the area, silently infiltrating the base, and gradually eliminating the guards is fun, and stays fun even hours into the game.  Collecting the gun mods becomes quickly addictive too, since you’ll begin to try and figure out just where to grab what you need to create the ideal loadout.  The game gives you a clue where to search by telling you which province each weapon mod is located in, but beyond that you’ll have to grab intel to figure out the rest.  Admittedly, there are indeed a few firearms that outshine the rest by a wide margin.  Case in point, the sniper rifles.  The moment you find a high-powered sniper with good range and penetration, there’s little reason to use that weapon slot for anything else.  Doubly so since the game strongly encourages players to snipe targets from long distances, and with little difficulty aside from bullet drop and delay.  And shotguns?  Forget it, aside from El Sueno’s SILENCIO! (a heavily modified Russian Saiga auto-shotgun with a drum barrel), none of them are practical, even when breaching interiors.
But if you manage to find a buddy to play with, oh man, are you in for a treat: this game is a BLAST to play with friends in co-op.  Yeah, you’ll probably constantly screw up the total stealth missions thanks to your bumbling real-life teammates, only to start accusing one another as to whom alerted the guards first, but that’s part of the fun, isn’t it?!

But for the one thing Wildlands does better than almost every other game out there, it's the absolutely GORGEOUS vistas.  It really speaks volumes for how beautiful Ubisoft's virtual rendition of Bolivia is when you constantly feel like stopping for selfies and overview pictures of valleys, mountaintops, canyons and sunsets. Or even just pictures of rebels huddled around a campfire and searchlights in the middle of a midnight rainstorm.  Steam’s built-in image-capturing utility is serviceable, but… personally, I prefer the quality of the pictures that Nvidia’s Ancel option affords, especially since it allows you to shift the angle of the camera, zoom in and out of a scene, change the graphics resolution and overall quality before taking a shot… lots of neat stuff.

Now, for the Ghost War 4vs4 PvP multiplayer.  I don’t really have much to say… got a feeling the other reviewers on Reddit or other forums will help make or break this aspect of the game, but certainly not me.  It reminds me of what the Sniper Elite games were trying to accomplish with their multiplayer, only they somewhat managed to surpass that in the sense that it is genuinely difficult to pick out enemies in this mode from the shrubbery.  If the bullet physics were improved, the sniping in this game would be something beautiful.  Oh, and for the most part, these matchups are truly about the stealth, not run-and-gun 360-no-scope kills.  The loudest, most-trigger happy team will be the first to be spotted and blasted away, whilst the most cautious and patient teams will bring home the bacon, every time.  

In conclusion, Ghost Recon: Wildlands is one solid purchase if you’re into tactical shooters or stealth games like the Metal Gear series, especially with friends to play with. However it will become dull after a point, which is where the addition of the Ghost War mode will make or break the package for you.

I avoided this game when it first came out because the beta was just okay and the reviews killed it. But after a while, I picked this game up on sale and was pleasantly surprised at how much fun it is to play. I play by myself with the AI squad and there are some times where it gets pretty annoying. But all the issues I have with the game could be solved if I had any friends.

OK, so I usually DO NOT buy games right when they come out, and I also usually stay away from big titles because they always end up in failures and money grabs with ridiculous game content and future over-priced DLCs... 

About 2 months ago I bought Tom Clancy's The Division while it was on sale, and I was actually pleasantly surprised by how fun it is. WHen I saw Ghost Recon Wildlands on sale for 50% off I figured, why not give it a try? 

I"ve been playing this since Friday and I absolutely love it! The graphics are gorgeous, even though I can only run this on medium settings... (gotta upgrade my system tremendously). I only have a GTX660, 8GB ram and an i5 processor. 

So how is the game? Its almost like a mixture between Arma III and Skyrim. You have this huge, I mean HUGE open world of Bolivia, ranging from jungle, to salt desert, desert, mountains, plains, forests, lakes and rivers. You can drive and fly everything from bikes to humvees, from helicopters to airplanes. 

You can customize your entire character down to small details, and make the perfect looking operator. During the game you can unlock additional skins.

You also only start with one rifle, an SMG and a pistol, but during the course of the game you can unlock a multitude of weapons, attachments, accessories like different granades, C4 or mines and also weapon skins. Besides this you have a handy little drone that you can upgrade as well. 

You do have a character leveling system in terms of skill points etc. With this you can upgrade many things like rebel support (mortars, cars, troops and diversinos), drone skills, character skills, weapon skills, more items for your etc. 

The game itself in my opinion offers a lot in terms of missions, side quests, random events and treasure hunts (for skills points and different weapons). I don't think it gets boring at all, yes it is repetetive, but what do you expect? You are an operator hunting the cartel. Its not like in real life one day an operator infiltrates with a heli, equipped with an M4, and the next day he infiltrates with a starship and laser guns. I think its actually quiet fun, it definitely is NOT a grind. 

What is better? Single player or multiplayer? I think you should play this with a group of friends because your AI team is dumb sometimes and doesn't really do stealth. So either you have to stealth infil yourself and keep your team behind, or get caught, alert everyone and their mother and get f***ed. 

The random lobby search is alright, but you seldomly find good players. I mean 80% of the time other players don't have mics, are 14 year old kids who enjoy crashing your heli into a mountain or just don't understand more complex "do not shoot" missions. 

I did have some fun pairing up with an American and some guy from India who didn't really speak English, and neither could he fly planes... :D 

Needless to say, get this on sale and play with friends! 

This game is definitely worth $30 and I rate it 9/10, just because the paid DLC is total garbage.

Game is good, the co-op portion of the main story is fantastic. There's still stupid bugs, and if you plan on playing with two people, prepare to be on permanent "hard mode", since the game is designed for single player / 3 AI teammates or 4 human players. The second someone joins your team you'll lose all your AI.

This game suffers from other Tom Clancy annoyances, like how the enemies are all crack-shot snipers even if they can't possibly see you. Even with all your skills maxed out, you are a squishy pincushion compared to the enemy AI. There's no way to "wear" armor, so once you max your bullet resistance, that's it.

Unidad will show up at the worst possible time and ruin any stealth you have. Expect it and you won't be quite as disappointed when it happens.... All. The. Time.

The game also has a terrible habit of respawning you in the middle of disaster instead of in a semi-safe area. We once had a stealth-only mission spawn us 10 times in front of an enemy, and due to loading times (even on an SSD) you would be detected and fail the mission before you even touch a key. Cars and other vehicles when called for will spawn in impossible locations, and Ubisoft is on record as "never going to fix it, don't hold your breath".

It's also incredibly easy to hit level 30 and you will probably do so before you finish the story. It would have been fantastic if the level cap was 50 or higher, with more places to spend the skill points you will inevitably stockpile and become worthless after you cap out the skill trees. Tier 1 mode is a "replacement" for the level system, but it's mostly pointless other than simply bragging rights and a few cosmetic goodies. Once you get down to Tier 35 you'll be forced into "impossible" mode and the game gets infinitely more cheaty against you. You are warned.

I do not play PvP and thus have no use for the ghost war stuff. It appears as the PvP is all Ubisoft cares about now, so know that you're paying for 50% or less of a game if you decide to buy the "gold edition" but don't like PvP.

All this being said, I did have fun playing what little of a campaign mode there is, and the fact it supports co-op  through that main story gives this title a great boost in that department. I only hope they realize there's a huge potential to expand this game for those of us who are "co-op main story only" players.

The singleplayer is still very fun and I have spent a lot of time in it (even if it can get very repetitive), and it is of course more fun in co-op, but the multiplayer is why I have to recommend this game. 
All content updates to the multiplayer are free (like Rainbow Six Siege) and it's a great tactical 4v4 game. At this point in the game, there are only two modes. Elimination, where you just have to kill the enemy team, and Uplink, where you must control an uplink to win the round (of course, killing the enemy team works too).
There are also several amazing classes, a decent variety of weapons, and fantastic customisation. Fans of tactical multiplayer shooters should like it a lot.
The main downside, to me at least, is the lack of players. Because it was released so late, and because the initial learning curve can be rather steep, there aren't a lot of players. But when you do find a match, it's worth it.

Ghost Recon Wildlands really shines when you play it with friends. On its own, it’s a solid open-world shooter, but in co-op it turns into a completely different experience.

The open world of Bolivia is huge and gives you a lot of freedom. You can approach missions however you want. Go in stealthy, take out enemies one by one, or mess things up and start a full firefight. In co-op, this freedom becomes even better. Everyone can take a role, one player scouting, another sniping, others pushing in. When a plan actually works, it feels incredibly satisfying.

The co-op gameplay is where the game really comes alive. Coordinating attacks, calling out enemies, reviving each other when things go wrong, it all feels natural and fun. Even when plans fail, those moments often turn into the most memorable ones. Laughing, improvising and somehow still finishing the mission is a big part of what makes Wildlands special.

The world itself is varied and atmospheric. Mountains, jungles, villages and deserts all feel different, and exploring them together never gets old. There’s a lot to do, plenty of missions, side activities and optional objectives, which makes the game perfect for long co-op sessions.

Ghost Recon Wildlands isn’t about a deep story or complex characters. It’s about teamwork, freedom and shared moments. If you’re looking for a game to play with friends, plan missions together and just have a good time, this is one of the best co-op shooters out there.

You may die really easily in different areas at the beginning due to enemies being stronger, but you can go wherever whenever. You can tackle areas in the map however you want to. Overall I really like this game.

Mercenaries + Metal Gear Solid V = Ghost Recon: Wildlands

I can't think of a better description for thsi game or a better indicator or whether or not you will enjoy it. If you like the Mercenaries series and/or Metal Gear Solid V, this game is right up your alley. [b]I play purely solo[/b] and here's what I think of the game.

[b]What I like: [/b]
[*] Huge open world with wide varieties of terrain.
[*] Progress the plot at your own pace.
[*] No Restrictions. Go out and do what you want, when you want, with whatever gun you want. 
[*] Very few stealth requirement missions and escort missions. It's not going to force you to play stealth all the time. Stealth is very recommended, though. 
[*] No Agenda.
[*] Operate or Obliterate. Tactical combat, or, Schwarzeneggar combat. Your choice. Although tactical combat is the much smarter choice, we can't be smart all the time.
[*] Character customization without affecting stats! You want to operate under the influence of a mustache? GO AHEAD! You want to go full tacti-cool with multicam combat shirts under plate carriers and MOLLE everywhere? Nothing is going to stop you.


[b]What I don't like:[/b]

[*] The Friendly AI. Friendly AI is totally useless and serves only to revive you when you do something stupid. They can be enhanced, but it seems to only increase the damage they can do. 
[*] The Enemy AI. The enemy AI is just as dumb as your squad and to make up for that, they have a hard time missing you with their bullets. Distance and cover don't always guarantee your safety. 
[*] Vehicle handling is wildly inconsistent and atrocious on most vehicles. You are always better off taking a helicopter or fast traveling to get somewhere. 
[*] The post-leveling leveling system, Tier One Mode, offers very little rewards for the challenge it creates. Maybe the reward is conquering the challenge for some. Developing bad habits before you unlock it can hamper you down the road. I wish it were available from the start to counter this. 
[*] There are lots of weapons to choose from but most of them are just the same old weapons from all the other shooters out there. This may be comforting to some but I like odd-ball weapons. 

It scratches the itch left behind by EA's abandonment of the Mercenaries series and Konami's abandonement of MGSV's story content. You're going to get hours out of this game whether it be 20 or 60 or 300. HOWEVER, I feel it's really not worth the $60 price tag unless you have that kind of money to burn. There are still bugs, glitches, and kinks. The controls (mouse and keyboard) sometimes feel clunky. The monotony of the gameplay will wear on you sooner or later. But, $30 is the perfect price for this game. If DLC could be folded seamlessly into the main game without them feeling like a "3 games in 1" scenario, they would be worth the purchase as well.

This could have been a great game, unfortunately the game has three major flaws that make it just an average game.

     Firstly, all of the ai are garbage. The teammates, the friendlies, the civilians, and the enemies. They are worse than ai from 10 years ago. 

     Your teammates can be set to either never fire or to kill everything. If set to never fire then they just aren't helpful and might aswell not exist. If set to kill everything then they either get themselves killed, or leave nothing for you to do and make the game really boring. 

     The friendlies are uncommandable and kill everything when they happen to show up, but usually appear after you have killed everyone. They could be removed from the game and I wouldn't even notice. 

     The civilians only exist to get killed by you accidently, and they're pretty good at it. They will often run straight into your gunfire and because its an Ubisoft game you get penalized for killing them. If you kill three friendlies and civilians in succession then you basically just die, because thats fun.

     The enemy ai would be fine if this were an average shooter or open world game, but this is supposed to be a tactical shooter so then the enemy ai are subpar. They are horrible at searching and give up if you run a quarter mile away.

     Secondly, the engine for this game is by far the worst part of it. Boats and water don't really work and none of the ai can use boats. There are no tanks, only an apc with eight wheels that drives and turns like a car with four wheels and is as well armored as your mom's minivan. 

     I also think it is worth mentioning that the game is not optimized at all so it runs like trash (like all ubisoft games) and that the graphics are...strange. Like if a car back window is cracked alot and you look inside the car through that, then you can see the cracked glass texture sort of moving with the passengers inside. Its hard to describe.

     Lastly there aren't as many tactical cosmetics as anyone would like, just the bare minimum. The devs release a little cosmetic dlc about each month or week and a lot of them look kind of silly and everyone wants more military guns. Also, the teammates dress like hipsters that walked through a military surplus store and there is no way to customize them or their equipment.

     If you want an open world shooter with a military theme that leans towards the casual side then this is your only option so buy it. If you want a good game then do not buy this.

My only real gripes are as follows: The AI can be kinda dumb at times, parts of the game suddenly become overly difficult for no reason, AI banter comes off as super cringy and generic, and the game is entirely too short for what it is; myself and friends only taking roughly 60 hours to 100% it (this also includes just pissing around, and killing ourselves for hours on end for laughs). I would've liked to get to that 100 hour mark in the base game, but, all in all, I really enjoyed Wildlands.

8/10.

So, I played this game initially on a free weekend, and it scratched the open world shooter itch I had. It was fun, there was adventure, there were lots of items to get and play with. 

So I bought the game, and I just 100% completed the base game. I won't be buying the DLCs because the base game experience was... underwhelming. Here's the good and bad:

- the game is pretty expensive for what you get

- it's really repetetive, and assets were clearly reused many times

- load times are SUPER long, especially when respawning after being killed

- the story was good, but not nearly as good as i had hoped

- there are quite a few bugs

- DEAR GOD THE GRENADE LAUNCHER BUG (caused me countless game overs)

- you have to play through ubisoft's uPlay, which caused my rather good computer to only be capable of a stable ~35fps. edit: may have* caused. regardless of the reason i was unable to get more than 35-40fps out of this game on single player, with occasional spikes down to <1fps

- the map is gorgeous, massive landscapes and beautiful scenery

- it seems like the game was definitely designed around playing multiplayer, both PvE and PvP. the single player experience was pretty meh

I can't in good conscience recommend this game at anywhere near full price. If it goes 50-75% off, it's worth the money for sure. But if you're looking for a great single player or even coop experience, you'll be better off looking elsewhere. I kind of wish that the PvP mode was locked into a DLC and the base game was priced much much lower.

I think 50 hours enough time to put into a game to get a proper feel for its mechanics and gameplay, haha.

The game is visually stunning. Bolivia is a beautiful yet terrifying environment to play in. The developers did a great job of incorporating the culture and lore of the country. 

The charcter customaization options feel nearly unlimited. Personalizing a soldier that you're about to spend hours playing as is essential for me in a video game. Weapon customization in terms of parts and camo is phenomnal and all the unique weapons are interesting. Wildlands nails this.

3rd person and over the shoulder shooting takes a bit to get used to if you're not familiar with it, but its essential for the stealth gameplay. The driving mechanics are a bit annoying and clumsy, especially when flying planes.

If it weren't for the captivating storyline and weapon customization, the repetitiveness of the missions and side missions is absolutely mind numbing. It's unbearable. The single player campaign drags on and on if you don't have a group of friends to be Ghost buddies with. It almost makes you want to quit playing the main story and just play online PvP or screw around with friends.

The 4v4 PvP multiplayer is an enjoyable and unique experience most shooters don't have. If you were going to get the game for any reason, it would be for this. It's highly addictive, even if you don't have a group of friends to play with. Each class is customizable in its appearance and each class has a unique ability. A lot of fun.

That being said, I did find the game enjoyable overall and I would recommend it.

[h1]Broken Promises[/h1]
During the Free-Weekend event prior to its sale in celebration of their new tacked-on, last minute PvP add-on, they promised any and all progress made would be saved so you could continue where you left off. As it turns out, many players purchased the game, myself included, to find all of our data deleted. When I confronted Support with my problem, they closed my ticket immediately without any explanation given. As I enjoyed the game, I was actually happy to start fresh and get more playtime in as my save within the 3 days of free-play was more than 75% complete the game.

[h1]Vehicles and Terrain[/h1]

Universal Handling
Many games, like GTA V for example, cause your vehicle to respond instantly to your input. As such, pushing A or D to turn left or right immediately snaps your wheels in the corresponding direction. To change the turn radius of a vehicle or vehicle class, these games usually set a forced limit to the angle the wheels can reach and change the center of gravity, traction, and sometimes even more complex systems like downward force. Wildlands does not perform as such.

Much like the recent Mad Max game, but far worse so, your vehicles do not respond instantly to your input. This means that pushing A or D to turn left or right respectively causes your wheels to turn at a specific rate. If you extend your wheels entirely to the left for a left turn, then attempt to turn right, it will take twice as long to reset the tires to default and then turn right. To account for turn radius, Wildlands changes all of the above features, but also tweaks the rate that wheels turn.

This makes driving feel clunky, though some may in fact prefer it. 

Bikes
They hardly drive, anywhere. Difficult to control, easy to fall off of due to the terrain. Best suited for steady roads and paved streets. Odd for a dirtbike in a game.

Cars, Trucks and SUVs
Squishy as hell, odd to control. Similar problems to the bikes, hard to take off-road. Makes sense to be fair.

Helicopters
They released an update at some point that makes helicopters more usable in a combat scenario, thanks to new controls that offer you more control of your helicopter, but they still feel slow and clunky. Due to enforced aim acceleration for the helicopter, it can be difficult to use your wingmounted weapons to land any killshots, homing missiles included.

Airplanes
Eh, I wouldn't say they fly well at all, but they don't ever get used in combat scenarios. It's a vehicle you use only because a mission will ask you to, such as Supply Raids where the Supply Vessel [i]is[/i] an airplane.


[h1]Bullet Spongebob[/h1]
Enemy Resilience
A classic problem for increasing difficulty. As you increase the difficulty, enemies become more alert, can survive what seems to be up to more than 300% more damage in all scenarios. This wouldn't be much of a problem, however increasing difficulty reduces your bullet resistance. 

Player Resilience
Where in Normal or Easy you can survive entire magazines of bullets from untrained, spraying, panicking sicarios, on Extreme, you can survive roughly 3 bullets without any skillpoints invested in survivability. With full bullet resistance invested, including the Medal you find in the world that adds to your skill, I've survived up to 4 bullets, 5 after regeneration started to kick in. To help drive home why this is a problem I should include the weapons you're up against. M134's, LMGs with up to 175 bullets in its box magazine, dual Mac-11's and Skorpions, assault rifles, sniper rifles and of course helicopters with missile pods, homing missile pods, SAMs, ground vehicles like trucks or SUVs with mounted M134's, APC's with HE cannons, etc. All of these become laser accurate on the highest difficulty. 

Tier One
Once you've activated Tier One mode, the end-game levelling system available after you've maxxed your level, you become locked to a Difficulty level. The higher level Tier you level up to, the higher level you're locked to until you're locked to Max Difficulty.

[h1]Detection[/h1]
Stealth and Guerilla warfare
Another classic in stealth oriented games for Difficulty-Ups. I normally would actually applaud this added difficulty, however it can be rather buggy and has led to many failed stealth missions, and even more failed Loud missions. Adding to the laser accurate dual wielded SMGs at mid-to-long range capable of dropping you in 5 bullets or less, on Extreme enemy detection markers indicating how aware of you they are become very spotty. Often times my detection meter will fill slowly but before it's even halfway filled, the enemy detecting me is already shooting at me fully aware of my position. This makes using cover to get surprise guerilla attacks very risky, and very unreliable. It's more luck based than skill based, regardless of range in many cases.

Overcast
On Advanced and below difficulties, enemies are shown on your minimap as vague red clouds. You can mark them with your drone, or Rebel Spotter Support Skill to remove the cloud and add certainty to enemy positions. This I find is a crutch and can be disabled in the HUD options, +1 points. My friend who had never played Wildlands found that the Detection Clouds were enabled by default. This could be a -10 for a player that gets suddenly floored by Tier One mode disabling their Detection Clouds.

[h1]Busywork[/h1]
Much of this game is simply repetitive busywork, it's a typical checkbox an openworld game would have to tick to offer a low cost, high yield turnout of gameplay for the players to tackle. You'll find yourself stopping convoys all across the country from province to province, hijacking helicopters for supplies, blowing up airplanes 'cause you'd rather not do that Supply Mission and instead see the plane explode.

You'll be collecting your typical collectibles like story tidbits, music, pictures and items. 
Collecting intel to mark important intel such as additional Skill Points and Supplies used to invest in skills such as weapon stability, inventory upgrades such as C4 and capacity, flashbangs, drone upgrades, etc.
I found that the team hiding skillpoints, weapons, weapon parts, skill medals, Rebel Ops, Supply Raids, and so on, did a [i]very[/i] good job building encounters in spite of many of them being random encounters. For many, this can actually be a plus, but a lot of it was added solely as a low-cost means of extending gameplay.

[h1]Uplay[/h1]
You can refer to the massive list of complaints against Uplay that everyone everywhere lists about this wannabe Steam clone. It has launch errors and bugs, often becomes unresponsive and the achievement systems that reward points to allow you to unlock items in-game(as a sneaky way to introduce you to the microtransaction items available for purchase) often don't reward you the item you bought for weeks on end using achievement points. Does not bode well for items you would purchase with cash.

[h1]Launch Issues[/h1]
Tying into the Uplay problems, many programs cause launch errors with Uplay games and many can be hard to identify. I haven't discovered a fail-safe method of detecting programs that prevent Uplay titles from launching, but after buying this game it took me well over 3 hours to figure out how to launch the game. As it turns out recording software, in my case Plays.tv, can prevent the game from launching.

I have still have many more complaints but Steam won't let me extend this review further.

Through multiple hard covers and with no line of sight. The AI generally ignores your squadmates entirely and pretends they don't exist (and the few times they actually try to shoot someone they're almost useful because of this).

The co-op is where this game really shines. The non-existent physics, awkward and braindead helicopter controls, repetitive missions and generic story are completely shoved to the side in the pure fun that happens when you play this game co-op (I'd even say the laughably bad physics occasionally help add to it). There are multiple approaches to any given location, though most of them tend to end with various things exploding and an all-out attack from both sides.

tl;dr bring a friend or three for co-op if you plan to pick this one up. Pubbing it is alright at best, singleplayer is boring as hell. Oh and I guess there's a pvp mode or something.

Pros:

+ Graphics are beautiful looking
+ Sounds are amazing from walking to firing off different weapons
+ Guns and using the Gunsmith
+ Open world and you can do any mission is any order you want to
+ A good story, but based more on investigations and missions rather than just pure dialogue (e.g. RP games).
+ Background information about Bolivia and that a lot of it is based on actual facts
+ Customizations 


Neutral:

*/- Stealth
*/- Camouflage 


Cons:

- AI at times makes you question their intelligence
- Driving a car can feel like you’re constantly playing a drifting simulator
- Crashes that happen once in a while when playing co-op


The story really isn’t a story, but about missions with slight background knowledge about who you need to take out. You hardly know anything about who you are, who your operatives that you work with are, or who your boss is and know very little about even the organization you work for. They made the story more or less to investigation and/or criminal solving shows (Law and Order, Criminal Minds, etc.) in sense where you finish a case and move onto the next case. In the end, you know more about the enemy than you do about yourself and/or your own operatives. They did an excellent job at executing the story in this regard, but don’t expect a big time story from games that relate more around Roleplaying titles. 

The game looks amazing. All my settings are on max and never seen any AA issues; as well never seen any stuttering or FPS drops. The grass and bushes will move or get flatten when moving over them or when in prone position so you can flatten the grass, move back slightly, and snipe people from afar. The different biomes and the weather effects with a day and night cycle makes the game feel realistic and does an accurate job (more or less based on the given Kilometers within the game) of showing off Bolivia’s landscape.

The sounds whether walking on snow, dirt, mud, or diving into the water is very noticeable. It adds to that realism compared to other games where a lot of the footing is the same regardless what biome you’re in. The voice actors do a good job at commenting about missions, syncing shots, cinematics that occur, and just bluntly describing how they’d love to ‘stick it to them’. At times they’ll throw in a joke or give some insight about where they came from and/or who they (not a lot, but at least it’s something). Vehicles in general sound different from one another; whether it’s a four door coup, to a lambo, to a pick-up truck, they all have their distinctive sounds. Both helicopters sound different from one another and the bush plane sounds like a bush plane. 

From firing off a MP5 to a M4A1 to a G28 all sound genuine to their counterparts. Adding a compressor only makes it feel more genuine when doing stealth combat. You have an ample amount of customization for your weapons: scopes, barrels, grips, muzzles, triggers, stocks, and few other options. Each option as dozen or more items that help with accuracy, handling, rate of fire, damage, etc.; you customize your weapon based on your playstyle or how you want the weapon to feel in terms of gun n’ gun, aiming, or hip fire. Depending on how customize your weapons they’ll lean toward one direction or have a recoil higher than other weapons and they feel all very accurate based on how you fit your weapon. Also, you have multiple options to paint your weapons.

This game has kept its word about doing any province in any order you want to. I felt like this was a great aspect of the game and a feature that wasn’t a lie or falsely advertised. I went from one area to another based on certain weapons and gadgets for said weapons early on and finished other zones for pure enjoyment. You have multiple ways of transportation: cars, trucks, diesel trucks; planes, helicopters, boats, motorcycles, and parachutes. You do have to get used to flying, but once you have that in place flying becomes easier that other modern warfare titles. Some of the vehicles are horrendous when driving regardless of how fast or slow one would takes around a curve or eases on the brakes. Some of the vehicles feel like they were imported from an actual drifting game and with a lot of roads being on hills and/or trying to pursuit someone can become an absolute headache at times. 

Customization in general of your character is appealing compared to other titles that fit within this genre. You can wear sunglasses, hat, different vest types, you can wear civilian clothing and/or military clothing; you can mismatch items and numerous color variations regardless how you pick your items. When it comes to using camouflage to hide yourself from enemies, this concept goes entirely out of the window. You could be engulfed in a full ghillie suit and the enemy will still see you a few hundred meters away. This is applied if you’re in full black camouflage and in pitch darkness where they don’t have any Night Vision on and still can see you through the brush when using a compressor. I would like to see some rework on how camouflage works as this is a major factor at times when using stealth against the enemy. 

Most of the times stealth works to a degree; one can sneak up behind an enemy and eliminate them in melee or sniping them well over five hundred meters away. Factors that can hurt your stealth is noise (gunfire, running, explosions, etc.), another guard seeing the corpse of a fallen member, or being noticed because camouflage didn’t do its job. There are traits to help prevent from being detected, which at times makes it too easy (e.g. If you’re about to be spotted and you’re hundred and twenty meters away, just prone and they’ll stop noticing you). There are devices to help distract guards to your location so you can pick them off without someone else spotting their body. I would’ve liked to see an option about picking up the corpse and moving it instead of waiting a few seconds and having it magically disappear. Also, regardless of what weapon you use, you can one shot anyone as long as you’re in stealth mode. I understand this helps in co-op to do sync shots, but I feel like that this method is way too easy. If you’re not in co-op mode, sync shots with your AI counterparts are an amazing feature and it helps clear out majority of the operations you take. 

The AI at times can be the best help or the worst help. They will NOT engage unless you command them to do so or if you are under heavy amounts of fire where you will automatically command your operatives to attack. They will remain in stealth mode for majority of the time and the more you upgrade your sync shots the more use you can get out from your operatives. When they do open fire, they just seem at times not knowing how to eliminate an enemy when it really matters. There really isn’t a middle ground with your AI operatives. I’ve seen them meters away from an enemy and just eating all their bullets instead of turning around and shooting them instead. The AI does need work, but you can finish the game on a higher difficulty – just expect a headache at times dealing with them. 

I did experience some crashes when playing in co-op mode and when I finished the game (both endings). In co-op mode, if one person joins the game, then it’s you two vs Bolivia instead of two people and two AI, or three players and one AI. The AI will still talk even though they aren’t in your squad and it’s to keep the immersion within the game. I never experienced any lag or disconnects when playing with my friends, but the crashes would happen randomly. Co-op needs work, but when it does work it is an amazing experience with friends. 

I recommend buying this title to play with your friends. Unfortunately, I can't add any more information - I exceeded the amount.

Title: Ghost Recon Wildlands - A Thrilling Covert Operation in the Wild
Overall Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5 stars)

Gameplay: ★★★★★ (5/5 stars)
Ghost Recon Wildlands delivers a compelling gameplay experience that combines tactical shooting with open-world exploration. The freedom to approach missions in various ways adds a dynamic element to the gameplay, allowing players to experiment with different strategies. The vast array of weapons and gear, along with customizable characters, cater to diverse playstyles. While the AI can be inconsistent at times, overall, the gameplay remains engaging and enjoyable.

Graphics: ★★★★★ (5/5 stars)
The visuals in Ghost Recon Wildlands are nothing short of breathtaking. Ubisoft Paris has crafted a stunning open-world environment in the lush landscapes of Bolivia. From dense forests to arid deserts, each region is meticulously designed, creating a realistic and immersive world. The attention to detail, day-night cycle, and dynamic weather contribute to the game's stunning graphics, making exploration an awe-inspiring experience.

Sound: ★★★★☆ (4/5 stars)
The sound design in Ghost Recon Wildlands is well-executed, enhancing the overall immersion of the game. The ambient sounds of the environment, gunfire, and explosions create a realistic atmosphere during missions. The voice acting for main characters is commendable, though some supporting NPCs may lack depth. The soundtrack complements the gameplay, adding to the intensity of combat and moments of suspense.

Story and Narrative: ★★★★☆ (4/5 stars)
While the premise of dismantling the Santa Blanca drug cartel sets the stage for an intriguing storyline, Ghost Recon Wildlands falls short in its narrative execution. The plot can feel somewhat predictable and fails to fully engage players emotionally. The character development lacks depth, making it difficult to form strong connections with the protagonists. Despite its potential, the story doesn't reach the same heights as previous entries in the Ghost Recon series.

Multiplayer: ★★★★☆ (4/5 stars)
The cooperative multiplayer mode is where Ghost Recon Wildlands truly shines. Joining forces with friends to tackle missions and take down targets offers a more enjoyable experience compared to playing solo. The seamless transition between single-player and multiplayer modes ensures a smooth and immersive experience. However, the absence of competitive multiplayer options might disappoint players seeking PvP gameplay.

DLCs: ★★★☆☆ (3/5 stars)
Ghost Recon Wildlands' DLCs, "Narco Road" and "Fallen Ghosts," add exciting content to the game, including new missions, weapons, and storylines. "Narco Road" introduces thrilling undercover missions within the Santa Blanca cartel, focusing on daring vehicle-based gameplay. "Fallen Ghosts" ups the challenge with tougher enemy factions and intense survival gameplay. While some DLCs lack impact and suffer from occasional technical issues, overall, they enhance the game's lifespan and offer additional value to fans seeking more adventures in Bolivia.

Bugs and Updates: ★★★☆☆ (3/5 stars)
Ghost Recon Wildlands had its fair share of bugs and technical issues upon release. While Ubisoft Paris addressed many of the early concerns through patches and updates, some issues persisted. The occasional AI glitches and mission bugs could disrupt the gameplay experience. However, the development team's commitment to providing updates and addressing player feedback deserves recognition.

Conclusion: 
Ghost Recon Wildlands successfully blends tactical gameplay with an expansive open-world, offering players the freedom to chart their paths in a visually stunning environment. With solid gameplay mechanics, cooperative multiplayer, and outstanding graphics, it provides hours of enjoyable gameplay. While the story could have been more compelling and certain technical issues lingered, the overall experience remains engaging and satisfying. Whether you're a fan of the series or a newcomer, Ghost Recon Wildlands is a thrilling adventure worth undertaking. if you come here after playing Breakpoint then this is a much better option.

Ghost Recon: Wildlands is a co-op open world game where you and up to three buddies can take on the Santa Blanca Cartel, across a fictionalized version of Bolivia where this massive organization has essentially taken over the country. You and your team of Ghosts can systematically take down piece by piece. All at your own pace, the game doesn't guide you by the hand past the first zone. Recently, the game also includes a PvP component. Ghost War, a 4v4 class based tactical elimination gamemode. Is it worth your time? Well read on to find out.

Pros
-Immersion. Top notch if you let it. Or not, you can ignore the story and just kill these bad dudes.
-You can do this, by blowing up, knocking out, shooting, or stealthily taking down the cartel.
-Some members of the Cartel are actual characters and you can change the outcome of the story based on how you take down the Cartel.
-Loads of firearms and gunsmith to customize your guns. You can carry two large guns, and a pistol on you at all times.
_> Gunsmith: You can make any gun better suit your playstyle with a large amount of attachments.

-The game looks amazing in some spots, and can feel like you are going on a vacation in Bolivia sometimes.
-Both stealth, and brute force are valid tactics.
-Loads of vehicles, super cars, helicopters, planes, jeeps, armored personnel carriers, and trucks with miniguns on them.
-PvP has a role for many play styles. Teamplay can really make or break a team composition.

The game was stunning, which is to be expected from this developer. As such, it took me a small bit of micromanaging within the built in benchmark function to fight the right mix of FPS and graphical enhancement. I'm running an EVGA 970 FTW and was able to play the game easily at 40-50 FPS without sacrificing too much visual eye-candy.

I give this game a thumbs up for first-person-shooter fans, although despite the great mechanics, immense configurable options, and cutting edge graphics-- I could see how someone who already owns a library full of first person shooters might try to claim that this isn't all that innovative compared to it's predessors, contributing to a sense of deju-vu. That said, I imagine that can be said for any fan of any particular genre. I'm a huge fan of RPG and survivor horrors, so it takes a lot to impress me within those genres.

This game is a masterpiece; One of my favorite of the last 10 years. A major departure from most Ubi games, in that all the features feel fully crafted to thrill the player, rather than just left at "good enough." Love almost everything about it, but here are my top three:

1. Realistic in all the ways it needs to be, arcade-y in all the others. Bullet physics are great, and enemies typically die in one hit, driving is really fun. But also, you don't have to practice for two hours to make helicopters fly right.

2. Missions don't force you to run them a specific way; the player is genuinely free to improvise based on a wide spectrum of tactics. Parachute onto a rooftop and blast everyone, or stealth in while your (robot or human) teammates give you sniper cover, or run a rebel assault from above using a drone, strafe with helicopter-mounted mini-guns, et cetera, or any combination. Folks are complaining that missions are all similar, but that's looking at it from the wrong perspective; variety isn't forced on you, it's given to you in a big fat tool kit to use however you want. (If you get bored, it's because you're a boring player)

3. The options menus are rad, which is a weird thing to type. The game allows you to tweak a heap of settings, so everything feels exactly right all the time. Car steering sensitivity is a different setting than helicopter steering sensitivity, which is different from airplane settings, for example. Also, all the graphics tweaks come with a little demo of what that option actually does, and tells you how much it will impact your CPU. A great example of how Wildlands is very consciously-crafted player experience.

The downsides? It's a CryEngine game, so you need a moderately beefy computer to make it look pretty (I get 40~60 fps on moderate/high graphics settings with a GTX 1050Ti). Also, even single-player is dependent upon a server connection, so when they do server maintenance, the game is inaccessible. Not the worst copy-protection Ubisoft has ever implemented, but still irritating.

Full Review:

Ubisoft have had a bit of a troubled past for me. The Assassins Creed series took a nose dive after the first few titles, and it seems they are absolutely flooding the market with game after game and to be honest I can't keep up (nor do I want to anymore).

And while I've played a few of the Tom Clancy titles, I wasn't holding out much hope for Wildlands after reading a significant number of people talking about the famous "rinse and repeat". Then came the play free weekend, topped with a 20% discount if you buy direct from Uplay, and I now own a copy of the game.

It's true, if you play the game mission after mission, I can see why it would feel like the old rinse and repeat is coming back, but that's only seems true to me if you rush through the missions/side missions one after the other eager to complete the game in record time.

I've spent countless hours (19) just wandering around the streets looking at stuff, driving around, collecting items you need to unlock weapons and skills, and I've been in awe of the views and landscapes this has to offer. I've tried all the different settings, and this is packed full of them - from easy/normal/hard/extreme difficulty to a highly customisable HUD (or no HUD at all if you want complete emersion).

The characters are often amusing and your squad cracks jokes when you aren't in combat or just hanging around. The whole feel of the game for me is superb, and a credit to the Ubisoft franchise. And what day doesn't feel a bit rinse and repeat... we do something different to make each day different and I see no reason why this shouldn't be applied here.

If you see this on sale again and appreciate 3rd person shooters (1st person when right mouse button held) then grab yourself a decent shooter. It's definitely one of my more recent favs of Ubisoft's

Thanks for reading - Enjoy!

Ammo capacity and handling also play a big part in how much you can do in a single down sight sitting, and how confident you can be trying to run and gun. Guns that have more ammo are harder to move about, but great at doing things like killing helicopters in a single clip. (Early on, skills may make it obsolete.)

Enemy AI is bittersweet honestly, Foes are mostly difficult because of sheer numbers, vantage points, weapons, backup, helicopters, etc. They seem like they know how much health you have, and gun for you pretty hard. Watching the AI revive me in front of enemies with no consequence whatsoever. I almost never see them throwing grenades. They're more effective than a terrible team who can't keep one survivor, but otherwise, the AI allies are useless for anything aside from cheesing shots with sync.
